column9: My dog loves it! A great help for taking her meds!
column10: Shetland sheepdogs (shelties) and a few other breeds (Poms, Shnauzers) can be genetically inclined to gall bladder rupture due to gall bladder mucocele.  This is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate surgery.  The condition appears suddenly with almost no symptoms other than the vomiting of water.  It is a medical emergency.This terrible ordeal happened to my beloved older sheltie this past April 2012, and, praise God -- who loves us all and all His creation -- she was saved by emergency surgery and a long recovery protocol.Now she must eat low-fat food with a non-prescription-veterinarian-ordered vitamin (a pill) to support the liver.  I buy the pill at 1-800-PetMeds because it isn't available easily at Amazon.com.She loves Natural Balance Original Reduced Calorie Formula Canned Food, which I use to induce her to accept the pill.  She now has a mission every morning:  to take the pill so that she can eat the canned food.  The small can is affordable and practical.I mash up just a bit (half-a-teaspoon-or-less) of the Natural Balance Canned Food and add 1/4 cup or so of water to make a "stew."  I give her the pill followed by the watered-down Natural Balance "stew" so that the pill won't stick in her throat. (She is supposed to have an empty stomach. The pill is taken with just a tiny bit of watery "stew" so that the pill will slide down her throat.)At the end of an hour, she can have the rest of the Natural Balance without diluting it, and she shares it with my younger sheltie so that she doesn't eat too much fat.  Sometimes we stretch the canned food for two days -- sometimes, not.Both of them LOVE this canned dog food.  The younger sheltie's main diet is the dry version of this canned formula; the older sheltie eats a dry Blue Buffalo that has even less fat.Whereas I used to have a terrible struggle to get the older sheltie to accept the pill, she now nudges my arm or hand (just did so, as a matter-of-fact) every morning so that she can take her pill, then her "stew," and, later, the rest of the can of  Natural Balance.I was so relieved when it turned-out that she likes this product.  She previously had refused to eat other canned, low-fat brands.  The pill-in-the-morning-procedure had been a time-consuming "battle" with the pill flung everywhere; now she swallows the pill immediately to get her Natural Balance morning treat.It's fun.  I give praise to God.

column9: Hottest Hot Sauce Known To Human Kind
column10: I kid you not, this is the ultimate bottle of hot sauce.  The smallest of drops will light your food on fire.  If you love spicy foods, this is the sauce for you.  Since so little of the sauce is required to dynamically alter the dish you are preparing, this is a tremendous deal.  I must warn you:  TOO MUCH INSANITY SAUCE WILL BURN YOU.  My older brother once applied this to a sandwich like it was Tobasco sauce and found himself literally crying (in front of his girlfriend).  Start with small amounts and ramp up your tolerance - this is like fire in a bottle.

After I began using and going through Sriracha (and various other supermarket hot sauces) like ketchup, I decided step up the heat and try Dave's Insanity Sauce. I first tried it on a slider sized sandwich- one drop with the mayo. First impression? Taste was good, and it was pretty spicy. So I decided to test the hot sauce (and my limits) to three drops total. Mmmm! This is good! And it tasted awesome, but I paid for it afterwards. My tongue was on fire for about 10 minutes after finishing the sandwich. So the taste tricked me in to using more and more, and then the heat bit me. It wasn't unbearable, but made me uncomfortable. Definitely worth it and can't wait to try more of it.Doing some research, it looks like its rated at 180,000 Scoville Units. Their hottest sauce, Dave's Insanity Jolokia Private Reserve, is rated at 700,000. Sriracha is about 2,400, and Tabasco sauce measures 2,500-5,000 SHU.Quick shipping and processing from vendor, "Miss Fit."

column9: I expected more of this sauce
column10: Let me get this out of the way right now: most of the reviews on Dave's Insanity Sauce exaggerate the greatness of this product. It's hot, but there's not much else good about it. With a few drops on a plate of food, I can get my eyes watering. I was under the impression that this sauce was so hot that you shouldn't even use it on a single serving of food (based on Amazon reviews). But that's only if you're using it on dry meals. If it's blended into a sauce or condiment, it's watered down nicely and palatable. In terms of flavor, this sauce has a plastic-y taste to it. That's the best way I can describe it, and it seems to be a common problem in sauces which use hot pepper extract. I was under the impression that it was flavorless, but no, it actually tastes sorta bad. Because of this, a good use of Dave's Insanity might be to heat up a lesser sauce which happens to taste good. In terms of heat, there are definitely hotter sauces out there. But that doesn't mean this sauce is a pushover. If you dab a little too much, you'll find yourself running to the fridge for milk. One problem with using Dave's Insanity on single food servings is I find that I can never get just one drop. Inevitably, when I pour a drop out, a bit gets on the side of the bottle and I have to swipe it off with my thumb and spread it onto my meal as best I can, then lick the rest off so that it doesn't go to waste. This is a problem because that small amount of sauce is enough to leave my tongue with a light burning sensation, while my nose is on the verge of running (though, this varies depending on how much I can water down the sauce in my serving). That might just be because I exclusively use this on single servings of food (I'm not a cook). Ideally, for me, I just want a bit of a kick, and did it ever give my food a kick. I can handle a few drops of it if I need to, but I prefer not to leave myself tearing after every meal. Overall, it's not bad. This sauce garners a lowly three out of five due to its unique flavor. It's plenty hot, so had it tasted better, it would have gotten a higher score. If you're a huge fan of saucy meals and looking to use this on single food servings, you may want to consider picking this up. If you prefer sauces with rich flavor, look into something without hot pepper extract. Alternatively, if you're looking to use this as a cooking additive, you'll probably want something hotter unless you're a spice novice.

column10: "Dave's Insanity Sauce" is not to be taken casually or even as a way to add heat to individual servings (for most people), this is meant for larger dishes such as a whole pot of chili or a big batch of salsa since one or two drops will make a large amount of food VERY hot. I bought some Powerade and it helped, as long as I held the Powerade in my mouth; once I swallowed the burning pain started again in my mouth. PROCEED WITH CAUTION, indeed.

I got a bottle of Dave's Insanity Sauce from a health food store (?!), brought it home and took about half a teaspoon of it with some salad.  About 15 minutes later, I was writhing in agony on the bathroom floor and semi-conscious.  My husband called an ambulance, and the last thing I remembered was a medic saying, "I can't get a pulse."My husband took the jar of sauce along to the hospital -- the ER doctor said to me later, "My brother eats this stuff, but they make him sign for it when he buys it."  I thought he was kidding, but he assured me he wasn't kidding.There were no permanent after-effects.  My husband said it was the first time he'd ever seen me take anything without reading the label first -- turns out the label said to put only a few drops on the food -- and I took half a teaspoon.  Live and learn. column9: AN EXCELLENT TEA...I AM GLAD I FOUND THIS STUFF HERE AS IT IS DIFFICULT TO FIND IN STORES NOW.
column10: For some reason, known only to the powers that make such decisions, this bland, Twinings Prince of Wales Tea is not longer readily found on supermarket shelves.  You can still find it in variety packs, but It has been sometime since I have been able to find a whole box of the stuff.  That is a pity, but as I am what you might call a "tea hoarder," I had two boxes in my stash and was rationing it slow out.  You can imagine my delight when I found you could purchase this product through Amazon!Prince of Wales tea has a nice robust taste but no bitterness.  It is one of the few teas I can (if I so desire) drink without adding some sort of sweetener.  It never use mild or cream as my wife does, so for me that is a nice factor.  I simply like the flavor of this tea.Twinings has been around (It is based in England) for a bit over 200 years now and there is a reason for this...they provide a fine quality product.  We are constantly trying new teas as we locate them, but it seems that over the years we keep coming back to this brand.  Now as has been noted by another reviewer here, this stuff is NOT packaged in England; it is packaged and distributed here in America.  This does not magically change the flavor of the tea though.  Tea is tea is tea.  Tea is NOT grown in England, so to say that tea that is packaged in England is better than that packaged in America is simply codwollop!  Yes, you might get "stale" tea here, but I doubt it. If you keep your tea under proper storage conditions, i.e. out of the light, no moisture and away from heat, it will last quite some time...I can assure you that the producers do this simply because they want to sell you the best tasting product possible. We in this country may not be as adept to brewing tea as our English brothers, but I doubt it.  No, the difference in the taste is more than likely all in the drinkers head.The biggest problem I have and the biggest problem I have noted in our country when it comes to drinking tea made using tea bags is that we seem to be a very, very impatient people.  We simply do not, generally speaking of course, do not let it steep long enough.  A tea such as the one being reviewed here needs to steep no less that three minutes; preferably at least four.  I find myself getting in a bit of a hurry at times and end up drinking very weak and rather tasteless tea simply because I did not wait long enough.Note:  Cost wise, this is on the rather high end for tea bag tea...in my opinion it is quite worth it though.Anyway, enough of my babbling...this is a good tea.  Is it the only tea I drink or ever will drink?  Of course not.  3/4s of the fun of being a tea drinker is continuing throughout life trying different blends and brands.  I will say though that I most certainly have not grown tired of this stuff...yet.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks

column9: Nice mild tea for non-tea drinkers
column10: About three years ago I was diagnosed with two bleeding ulcers (which fortunately healed quite quickly once I stopped taking all NSAIDs and took the heavy-duty prescription antacid drugs morning and night).  The gastroenterologist did NOT tell me to quit drinking coffee, but although I had been a coffee drinker since high school, all the coffees suddenly seemed much too acid; I HAD been drinking regular coffee until about 3 p.m., then decaf after dinner - but even the decaf just seemed "too much."  However, in the morning especially, I did crave a bit of a caffeine jolt, and I was definitely accustomed to a HOT drink at breakfast.  My parents and my husband were always at least occasional tea drinkers, so we had the major brands of American grocery store tea around the house - I found them all unpalatable, and usually did not even finish the mug after I fixed some.  Then I started trying the "fancier" teas, starting with "assortment" packs.  My husband had warned me that there was SOMETHING in the Earl Grey teas that made them taste really odd - well, that something turned out to be bergamot, and I did not care for it either.  So, at least I had eliminated all types of Earl Grey tea...  Fortunately it did not take me too long to stumble across the Twinings Prince of Wales tea, and it was like Goldilocks and the porridge - just right.  With coffee I always drank it black, but with tea I do use about a teaspoon and half of honey.  As far as I can tell, the Prince of Wales does not come in a decaf version, so in the evening I drink chamomile tea (and that varies a lot from brand to brand!).  Unfortunately the Prince of Wales tea is only available at one grocery store near me, and sometimes they are all sold out.  So, I finally realized that I should sign up for the Amazon "subscribe & save" for this tea.  The tea bags come wrapped in foil packets (as I think all Twinings tea bags do), so it's easy to take them along when traveling, or just to carry one in a purse or wallet.

column9: The Prince of Wales couldn't get enough
column10: TWININGS PRINCE OF WALES tea was originally blended for HRH Prince Edward the Prince of Wales (later King Edward VIII then the Duke of York). It is described as a pure black Chinese tea from Yunnan Province and other southern areas of China.In other words, it approximates green tea. While it is a bit weak for me, I think most tea drinkers will absolutely love this quality tea still enjoyed by the royal family. I myself drink it only occasionally, if brewed together with Twinings Irish Breakfast Tea, Tea Bags, 20-Count Boxes (Pack of 6) or the spectacular Twinings English Afternoon Tea, Tea Bags, 20-Count Boxes (20 Tea Bags) (see my reviews for these).In the event it interests you, Twinings tea bags are designed like Lipton's clever invention, the 'double' tea bag (what they originally named "FLOW-THROUGH") that you can puff apart a bit if you like before steeping it. Twinings does not have any staples anywhere on their teabags, unlike other companies with a staple here and a staple there. You might as well buy staple-flavored tea.Either way, this is one of those teas that is a must for your tea shelf at home.

This Twinings tea formulation results in what might at first seem self-contradictory: a mild, but flavorful, black tea. Many tea lovers like a strong, black tea, and I, too, enjoy these. But sometimes you want something that's not so powerful, perhaps after you've already had a number of cups, or perhaps late in the afternoon or in the evening. This Twinings blend fits the bill perfectly. It is smooth, almost silky to the taste, with a mild black tea flavor that also has a hint of aroma. It's really a welcome addition to any tea-lover's tea set, and when you also consider the more than reasonable price, it's easily a home run.Like most Twinings teas, the bags are individually wrapped to keep freshness using a sealed, moisture resistant paper. The box I just picked up has a freshness code two years from now, so that should more than suffice for most uses, and you don't have to worry about going through an entire box soon after you purchase it because you are worried about the teas going stale.An easy five-star recommendation for flavor, mildness, packaging, and price.

They are a perfect size for getting him to feed himself but they can get messy.  Even when they get stale, he loves them.  It's a good snack for him and definitely a little overpriced, but Amazon has them cheaper than any store in my area. The Puffs tend to go to the back of his tongue and he often coughs and gags on them. They are nutritious, and there may be better snacks out there but for right now these are awesome.

column9: Great Puff alternative to the "Fruity-yogurt" kinds
column10: Our daughter loves these!  She had a lot of trouble transitioning to solid foods, and we had to take her to a specialist. THey can be easily cut into rounds using a serated knife, and to encourage chewing, they are long enough for you to hold them to the one side of the mouth.Also, since our daughter loved puffs of all kinds... we wanted to at least introduce a variety of flavors. Also, we get great flavor addition when pre-soaking black beans in combination with garlic powder and cumin.The company offers a better price for regular shipments.
