I don't dig Genoa or any wimpy greasy stuff.This stuff is hard, hearty, and really well spiced up.Cooked or cold, it kicks ass.I would bring this on a boat, camping, or to the workplace.Sliced nice, it would really compliment cheese, crackers, and vino too.No doubt, one serious real deal of value.
I really didn't care for this product to much. The salami was way to hard to chew. I have had Italian Salami before (other brands ) that were a lot better.

Given the positive reviews posted, I thought I ought to give this sausage a try, particularly given the higher cost of salami I had purchased from other companies (Columbus Salame Company and Fortuna). The Bridgford salami was kind of a disappointment-fibrous and greasy with a somehow duller taste. Kind of like a Slim Jim with less heat and more sawdust (I'm not implying there is really sawdust in it-it just has a different texture that what I'm used to). My wife took a bite out of her slice, then put it aside and didn't nibble on it further... that is actually not a common outcome in encounters between my wife and bits of food. I did bake it with some cheese in some soon to expire canned pizza dough and it was pretty decent-my son really liked it. All in all, I'd say go a little upmarket if you are going to use the salami to snack on with fresh fruit, olives and whatnot but this product is probably fine for cooking.

stumped by a hard to chew review, maybe with no teeth, as this is easy to cut and chew, not like nearly rock hard cured italian meats; taste is slightly spicy- about halfway between sweet and hot sausage for comparison; and a very good deal; ordered a top-rated pepperoni, one stick, was $13 and over $9 for ship+handle (won't do that again); this is 4 chubs, probably 6+ times the weight and size, but only $23 and $6 ship+handle; can't say it very often but a good product that's underpriced

My family loves the Bridgford Italian Salami chubs. You can cut it, slice it, chunk it any way you want. It's very tasty,not too salty or fatty like some other products. Once you taste it, you are hooked. Since it is cured and doesn't need to be refrigerated, it's perfectly safe to order by mail.We had to mailorder, since the supermarkets in this area don't carry it anymore.

Bridgford simply makes the BEST Salami (the HARD variety- we didn't care much for the Italian style) and also their Peperoni sticks are EXCELLENT on Pizza!These 12-ounce salami "chubs" are the perfect size... use a meat slicer or very sharp knife and go THIN. I gave it a FULL FIVE STARS and am a repeat purchaser.

I enjoy the bridgford salami.  I eat a sharp cheddar cheese with french bread or wheat crackers with a slice of salami on top.  I have tried other brands but always return to this selection.The only reason for 4 stars rather than 5 stars is that there maybe another brand I haven't sampled yet.

When they say "hard" salami they really mean it.  Has great texture as a result.  I like to cut mine paper thin and eat it with cheeses and crackers.  I get a workout even with a very sharp knife.  Loads of garlic - a good thing.  Have eaten 2 of the four sticks.  Will definitely buy again. Cheers.

Well, what can I say?  I regret this purchase of Bridgeford Italian salami (I didn't buy the hard salami).  The quality of the salami is just so-so, not terrible but not comparable in quality to slightly more-expensive salamis available at my local grocers.  The taste?  Not bad but not great either, a walk on the mild side (in other words, bland and a bit rubbery-tasting).Stick with Hillshire Farm, Genoa, Gallo, etc...Bridgeford makes good pepperoni but their salami is sub-par and not worth the money.

I just tried Bridgford Hard Salami for the first time. I'm no salami expert, but I have been eating food my whole life, and this tastes really good in my opinion. The texture isn't grainy like some of the more gourmet brands I've wasted my hard earned dollar on. Surprisingly it isn't very greasy, no gristle bits, no bitter aftertaste, and it smells good for a salami. Their use of salt and spices are well balanced. You could eat this with a sweet beverage and there is no conflicting flavors. Overall I rate this 5 stars and will be ordering this from Amazon again.

column9: Other then greasy, an excellent salami
column10: To be fair, I didn't purchase this product.  But I found it outside of someone's home as I was wandering the streets.  What I found to be exact was 3/4ths of one of the salami, in some sort of pet food dish as if left for a pet or some wildlife.  Well, since it was left outside, I decided that the owner might not care if I went ahead and ate it.  So I did, and it was wonderful!  I am only giving this product four stars since like "Mntijo" here with his review it was a bit greasy, and I also had stomach distress after eating it.  But this product is still delicious!  I do hope the owner of the home that placed this salami outside orders more, I'd love to get more free food of this caliber.

column9: Good Salami if you don't compare it to Italian Salami
column10: Good salami compared to other hard salamis you usually get in stores. But nothing close in taste to real italian salami. Bland taste.

This salami was so greasy when opened it, it literary poured out grease. I tried eating on two separate occasions and gave me the runs and cramps so bad, I couldn't even go to sleep. I threw 5 and 3/4 of the salami away. The 3/4 portion I left out for the animals which roam around the neighborhood, they wouldn't even eat it. Save your money don't buy this salami.

Tastes like a rancid dishrag pickled in brine.  No sign of spoilage - just bad tasting.  I bought based on the rave reviews of others here so I thought I'd chime in with my opinion.  I'm comparing this with the Fresh and Easy house brand - scarcely the premium - that costs less and is scrumptious.
I couldn't believe how fresh and soft these cookies were.  It was like they had just been baked and then packed up and sent to me.  I'm very impressed, Thank you!

I was expecting a larger granual suger and am dissapointed in this product. I might as well have used normal grocery store ganular sugar (i.e., Domino).  Not worth returning and I would not buy again. It certainly doesn't fit my description of "sanding" sugar.
This was an addition to my sprinkles for Christmas cookies.  It was fun to use. Made my cutout cookies much prettier than I ever imagined.  No problem with item or seller!! Excellent!!

It's absolutely amazing how adding a simple dab of sugar can make a cupcake pop! The thing about this product is its vibrance, which quite frankly makes the grocery store brand seem dull. It's as if they infused in granule with as much Red-5 that they could pack in. Mind you sugar and artificial coloring aren't the best things for you, but they make for fun times with food. Would I recommend you to buy it, sure would. After all what do you have to lose, the bottle is cheaper then your store brand and with amazon prime there's no trip to be made to the store.
Very pleased. Expensive but worth the cost to me because of the beautiful soft luster it adds to my baked goods. Shaker and pour openings for easy application.  Ordering more.
It's good to have the spices available when I cook. I don't like running out of a spice unexpectantly when cooking.

Well, what can I say. It's oregano and it's a lot of it. I think I'll die of old age before I consume this whole thing. The weight looks like this isn't too much, but it's dried leaves, very light. Oregano is supposed to be very high in antioxidants, so there you have it. I have to say that all these health-related rules of thumbs are confusing, and you can find reports claiming directly opposite things, for example, isolated antioxidants (pills, basically) don't seem to do squat in humans (in petri dishes they do work). But when consumed as food they seem to work, and oregano is very rich in this stuff. And, all else aside, it tastes great, so this option here is clearly recommended, at least because it's cheaper than buying small jars in stores. I'm very satisfied with this product, and I will gladly reorder (assuming I live long enough to need a refill!).

column9: Terrific Coffee...  especially from a Can!
column10: OK, I confess, I'm a coffee junky.... with a budget!  Unfortunately, there are very few of the "affordable" brands that are even drinkable.  The Maxwell House BOLD, however, was a very pleasant surprise.  Great fresh flavor, rich and deep, without tasting burned.  Very nice overall.  I used it for both cone drip and espresso, and liked it for both.  Can't wait 'til they have a good sale on it again!

This is the Sam's Club house brand, available from any Sam's Club for $2 a can (5 cans for about $10 really). Who on earth would buy Sam's Club housed brand canned chicken through Amazon? At $8 a can? Ouch.Vendor is obviously a scammer taking advantage of Amazon Marketplace.

This chicken is amazing. I cooked it at about 340* for 20 minutes and it came out perfect. My children loved it. The hard coating on the outside was a bit rough to get through but the amazing inner-copper veins of the chicken meat really tasted great. A good buy all around.

The discovered the Columbian-blend Starbucks Coffee about a year ago; I've tried ~6-8 different Starbucks blends, but found that the Columbian strikes a perfect balance in flavor and boldness.  Very flavorful but not overwhelmed with that bold espresso bitterness you get in something like French Roast blend.

I no longer have to spend $5 for a cup of coffee at Starbucks at the corner.  I've tried several flavor and this is my favorite.  If you are looking for somewhat strong one, this is it.  Highly recommended.

column9: The Best Colombian Coffee you can get - from Starbucks!
column10: Having tried many Colombian Coffees including Specialties; there just isn't any that comes close to the one that my old Colombian friend who resided here for awhile while attending University and as Hospital Intern before returning back home; having tried Colombian Coffee from her own homeland. I just couldn't find anything that came closest except Starbucks Colombia which is only a Medium Roast Blend but close enough to what I had drank from what she bought over from her own Country in Colombia.I was surprised to learn from her she was disgusted here in "Americas" of what they had deemed as Colombian coffee when it was merely a mixture of this and that, showing me the labels; that was when I began to start reading coffee labels.  Furthermore, she even indicated that while they do grow coffee beans in Colombia, but a small percentage of them are actually pure Colombian. So much did I learn what the Colombians did, With her being gone, no idea if she has returned back to the USA or is stuck in Colombia. But one thing she taught me that I never had forgotten was "READ THE LABELS". I was even surprised by some of the expensive, imported 100% Colombian coffee were not, but rather a mixture of this and that with Colombian coffee being at the very bottom of the list! I guess the saying still rings true, "if it's too good to be true, it prolly is..."Not so with Starbucks Colombia Coffee!Whenever I drink this, I remember her brothers, her families, and of course her - whether I am at Starbucks or at home. To some, might find this rather strong, but I never use the exact dosage, I use less for that reason - for it is so rich and full of flavor, there is no need to waste it. I keep mine sealed, and yes, in a Freezer Zipped Bag to keep its freshness.I also use this for Iced Coffee as well during hot summer dog days of the months, it is refreshing.

This is very good blend nice body and hearty flavor definitely worth a try if you haven't yet. I still prefer Starbucks medium breakfast blend but I will buy this every once in a while for a change of pace.

This coffee variety (Columbia) offers a nice alternative to the Pike Roast which the company uses as its default blend at their coffee shop locations. When traveling thru O'Hare Airport in Chicago I'm usually a customer of the MacDonald's for coffee, since the Starbucks in the United Concourse only dispenses Pike (except at seasonal times with Holiday/Christmas Blend). I keep the unopened bags in the freezer to prevent the ground beans from oxidizing.

I am very pleased with this purchase.  I enjoy Columbian coffee.  I find the flavor to be superior to all others as it's not weak, but it's not overpowering.  It really is perfectly middle ground.  If you want a brew that you can just sip and enjoy, then I would definitely recommend this.

column9: Very Fresh and Good Price On Special
column10: I received this coffee on special.  I was a little worried that it wouldn't be fresh or something because it was on deal, but the coffee was very fresh and the price ended up being cheaper than anywhere I could find it locally.  Thanks again Amazon for saving me a few bucks!!

I have a 4 cup coffee make and I put 5 teaspoons of coffee grinds to be brewed. I love it and it seems to be very strong so far for those intense workouts. Will but another set for work as I work the graveyard shift.I drink it black with two tablespoons of sugar and the flavor is really nutty.

column9: Amazon ships balanced nutty, not what I ordered
column10: I ordered 6 bags of Medium Colombian Coffee, when I started using it I noticed differed taste, then I read carefully the label on bags, it showed balanced nutty Colombian Coffee, this is not what I ordered, I do not like its taste.

We originally purchased this in all places - Ross - on a closeout for cheap.  It was soooooo good I went looking for more.  At that time I couldget it from the vendor, but not any more.  I'm so glad to find it here.  This is just delightful - it has a nice kick  but not hot!  I get heartburn with other hot sauces - but not with this!!  Love it on chicken.  TRY IT!!

Douwe Egbert Classic Blend Decaf Coffee is my favorite flavor ofcoffee in the world. That says a lot. I bought this package choiceinstead of the pods because it was more reasonable. I needed togrind it fine. Before it had no flavor. It was dry and remindedme of the old coffee my mother used to buy. Brazilians calledour coffee chaff. This still does not taste fresh. It is better ground finer,but does not match the pods. I am also disappointed in the Coffee DuckI bought to use this pack in the Senseo.

I love the 4C totally light 2 go drink mixes these give you vitamines and the B12 gives me a pick up later in the day when I need just a little more energy. I also like the energy rush drink mix by the same company. Better than drinking coffee all day and it does not keep me awake at night. Wife likes it too and it is sugar free. $9.00 is a little high of a price so may look for something less expensive.

The quality of this coffee is the first thing one notices. It goes without saying that all Gevalia coffees meet the highest standards and this new one is no exception.  I ordered the whole bean and ground each time right before making a pot.  The flavor reminds one of an AFrican bean (Zimbabwe) but slightly muskier...the only word that comes to mind.  Yet, the sip is crystal clear - a perfect compliment to a morning muffin.

column9: Best taste, best froth, organic, and reasonable cost
column10: This morning I taste-tested 3 top-rated Matcha green teas that I recently purchased on Amazon.1. Serendipi Tea matcha culinary grade organic green tea from Japan, 4 oz. costs $17.43(result: *****)2. Tea Zone matcha green tea powder, 8 oz. costs $16.99 (Amazon sells this as `Matcha Green Tea Powder By Malden Tea', but my black foil packaging label says it's made by Tea Zone)(result: ****)3. Liquid Jade powdered matcha green tea 100% organic, 3 oz. Cost $18.46(result: ***)Recipe:I made 3 different cups of  `green tea latte' with the following method:1 tsp tea powder,mixed with filtered water into a smooth paste,added to 1/3 cup hot soymilk + 1/3 cup boiling water + 1 tsp raw agave nectar,frothed into a Latte-style tea with hand-pump device.NOTE: I am a scientist.  Each cup was clearly labeled.  I tasted the teas side-by-side, taking 3 sips of each before proceeding to next sample.  I tasted in random order until all 3 cups were consumed.  Total time: 15 minutes.  I took lots of notes and drew graphs etc.Result:Serendipi Tea (5+ stars)  won for sweet smooth flavor, amazing long lasting froth bubbles, and the fact it's organic!!  Cost: $4.30/oz but worth it.  Note on the packaging: For those reviewers complaining of the green tea powder leaking, I have to point out that it's hand packed, with a note explaining that you must pack it yourself in an airtight and light-blocking container.  Fine with me, since this is the best tea I've found, and the act of packing it myself is itself a ZEN moment in which I feel a connection to the individual soul who packed the brown bag by hand just for me.  You decide.Tea Zone (Malden Tea) (4+ stars) came in second for a very nice flavor, but the frothy bubbles popped sooner than the Serendipi Tea, making for a lower rating, and plus, it isn't organic.  But it gets extra points for its low cost:  $2.12/oz (can't beat it for a daily tea).Liquid Jade (3 stars) was an O.K. tea, ever-so-slightly more bitter than the other two I taste tested, and almost a chalky feeling (perhaps it was ground into larger particles than the other teas).  Yes it's organic, always a plus, but at a cost of $6.15/oz, no way will I buy this again when I can get TeaZone 4 stars for a third this cost, and Serendipi Tea 5 stars for significantly less money as well.  So long Liquid Jade (though I do love your container and I'll save it.)

column9: Excellent buy for organic culinary grade matcha!!!
column10: This organic matcha is great for everyday use!!!  I will definitely buy this matcha again and again!  I put matcha in smoothies or make tea by the quart with honey.  Ceremonial grade matcha is just too expensive to drink everyday by the quart or to load up smoothies with it.  This tea has a good, clean flavor that is flavorful enough without being overpowering.  I have found it to be delicious in smoothies made with a fresh peach or mango, coconut milk, honey, ice, and a teaspoon of this matcha powder dumped directly into the blender.  It is a great way to enjoy the delicate flavor of matcha and the health benefits never tasted so good!  You are getting many times over the anti-oxidant effects of green tea from a tea bag because you are actually ingesting the tea leaves when you enjoy matcha. When making matcha as a tea by itself, less is more.  I use 1 teaspoon to a whole teapot of steaming (not boiling) water (but I enjoy strong flavors), then I mix in honey after it cools a little.  After my morning cup of matcha, I store the remainder of the tea and honey in the fridge for iced matcha later that day.  The flavor can be strong by itself, especially if you don't enjoy strong flavors, so it might be a good idea to start with smaller amounts (1/8 teaspoon or less per cup water) and work your way up to suit your individual tastes.  Experiment and enjoy!

I drink a lot of tea, and over the years I have done my own research. Inevitably, I discovered matcha, its abundant health benefits and its ease of preparation. Few who are not avid tea enthusiasts or those who don't drink high quality teas for their staggering health benefits, or gift of wellness, might not favor the taste of matcha. However, for the majority, matcha honestly does not taste bad, and if you disagree, just add some sweetness to it, like some agave, honey, lemon, stevia, or sugar. You could even mix up the condiments to create your own nirvana for your taste buds. Anyways, through all my searching for organic matcha, SerendipiTea offers the best price, and consistent availability I've seen yet!Thanks SerendipiTea :)

Matcha is purported to have elevated antioxidant and cognitive benefits above standard green teas and was the reason for the purchase. The price is also correspondingly higher, and this brand was the least expensive with the most favorable reviews available on Amazon. This product was my introduction to matcha, and I was pleasantly surprised. It seems a more potent version of your typical, off-the-shelf green tea in just about every way. As a regular tea drinker, I can definitely see this becoming a frequent addition to the different teas I consume on a regular basis.The reason for the deduction of two stars was the packaging. The small box the tea is shipped in is small and relatively flimsy, but is sealed, which is not a big deal. However, as another reviewer testified, the plastic bag inside that actually contains the ground tea was not only partially unsealed, but I would estimate maybe a half tablespoon of powder escaped the bag's 'seal.' This is absolutely unacceptable. I don't care if you're shipping sand; any powder, let alone tea, let alone a finer grade of tea, needs to be completely sealed with an extraordinarily-high level of confidence that the bag is secure. I fail to believe this cannot be achieved within the boundaries of both successfully cost-effective and green packaging.As a broke university student trying to maximize dietary healthfulness on a restricted budget, I'd very much like to include matcha in my regular tea consumption, but I'm not sure I'll order again from this outfit. The unprofessional feel I experienced from this product was not insignificant.*****UPDATE - 10/13/11*****: I since reordered this product, and I was indeed surprised to find that any packaging concerns have been completely resolved. As in the pictures listed on the product page, the flimsy plastic the tea came in previously has been replaced by a thick, folded, brown bag placed inside a very solid tin - which I'm sure I'll reuse. The tea itself is fantastic and now it comes with killer packaging. Zero complaints about this product now; 5 big stars.

I compared 4 different brands of matcha green teas. Here's how they rate:#1 DO 2nd Harvest, excellent flavor, texture, and color, expensive, organic#2 Serendipi, great flavor, best price for the quality, organic#3 The Tao of Tea, local Portland Oregon company, fair flavor, price slightly lower than DO, organic#4 Maeda-en, available at Uwajimaya. Difficult to dissolve. Less favorable flavor and not organicUwajimaya has best selection of Matcha teas with several others I have not tried yet. Whole Foods carries both DO and Tao of Tea. New Seasons currently does not carry Matcha. Serendipi is available on Amazon for $17/4 oz. box, best tea for your money!

I had high hopes for this, but sadly the bag this tea came in was torn completely opened and the tea inside was spoiled and stale.  I know what stale matcha tastes like, and this product tastes like it has been sitting exposed to air for months. Not only is the tea undrinkable due to the spoiled taste, but it loses its health benefits after being exposed to air. I'm very sad about this, because I have liked other products from this company in the past.DO NOT ORDER. If this company wants to make good, they should refund or replace for anyone who has received a defective product.

I'm not sure why, but I had high hopes for this matcha. The price is wonderful, but the label on the box says it is a "Product of USA". Now, I have nothing against American-made goods, but matcha is something that has a history in Japan, and it's there that it has been perfected.I guess I should have been able to tell from the price that something was amiss, but I just held out hope that the fact that this product is culinary grade was explanation for the price.The taste isn't bad, it's just that it takes about 3 times as much matcha powder than normal to make my lattes. Once I add all the extra in, it's tasty. But if I use that much, then I might as well use the more expensive, authentic powder from Habiki-an.

I haven't tried many brands of matcha, but this seems to be very high quality and it tastes great.  My only problem was that the bag containing the powder (which is contained in the box shown in the picture) must have come open, or been punctured during shipping.  I didn't loose much powder, but then entire shipping box was covered with a fine layer of green dust.Besides the mess, I am happy with my purchase.

Evidently, the company took negative reviews regarding poor packaging to heart.  Despite said reviews, I ordered the product anyway.  The tea arrived in a plastic lined paper sack (the kind used for coffee with folding wire closure, only smaller) tucked in a nice tin, all in good order.  I have been using the tea to make frothy lattes with almond milk in the morning.  After having given up a life-long coffee addiction just a few short weeks ago, these make me very happy!

I'm new to matcha and now I understand why the "grade" matters. Not being a fan of warm/hot drinks, I use matcha for lattes and smoothies.  Initially, I used DoMatcha Organic Matcha (which I purchased here at Amazon)DoMatcha Green Tea, Organic Matcha, 1.06-Ounce Tin and I loved it. I was surprised at how much I liked it because a number of reviews advised that the taste was acquired. When it was time to buy more, I thought I'd try Serendipitea since it was cheaper and the reviews indicated it was tasty enough for lattes and smoothies.I noticed the difference right away when I saw the color.  Not a big deal, just not the same color - or fragrance.  Blending it was difficult.  It stayed clumpy and stuck to the sides of the glass mixing bowl even though I used the same method I'd used previously.  Once I got it blended, I added cold almond milk (I don't use milk), stirred, and added ice.  Blech!  Not a bit like that which I'd grown accustomed.  The flavor was pungent and new clumps sprung up that had gone under the radar when I blending. The really icky part was I inadvertently sucked a clump up my straw before I knew there were unblended bits in there!  Not wanting to waste, I used that failed latte in my smoothie. It was acceptable, but didn't add the taste and zip that the other brand added to my smoothie.I was going to go with 2 stars, but I figured I'd go with 3 since this may just be a matter of taste, rather than an issue with the brand.  As stated previously, I'm new to matcha so I took that to heart in my review.

Just made a Green Tea Latte with this stuff and it is quite good.  This is an excellent price for this quantity of organic tea from Japan.  I don't ever drink matcha traditionally prepared, but I do enjoy it in cooking, sweet beverages, and ice cream.  This particular tea has a very light, green, fresh grassy taste and I'm glad I'll be able to enjoy so much of it at this price.

For all those Green Tea Latte Lovers.......having trouble with clumping matcha?This tea does not clump when prepared correctly..I too got introduced to this drink at starbucks.....and alot of money later I decided to try it on my own, I went through alot of trials....and finally I am getting close to perfection...lol1. Pour as much milk as you are going to use in a small pot, preferably with a handle2. Add one heaping tsp of matcha powder ( or more if desired)3. Add sweetner (if desired--I use 1 tsp brown sugar)4. Whisk vigorously with a small metal whisk until clumps are gone.5. Bring all to a boil and just before it starts to rise poor into your cup.Enjoy!

Wish I read more of the reviews.  The product arrived with then inner package all broken and tea powder everywhere.  What a mess.  Also, when I did get that all cleaned up, the tea tasted stale.  What a waste of money.  Stay away from serendipiTea.SerendipiTea Matcha Culinary Grade, Organic Green Tea, 4-Ounce Box

column9: Opened the box to find matcha powder spilled inside
column10: I opened the box and discovered that the inner bag of matcha powder was opened and spilling all over.  It was a huge mess.  I called the customer service at SerendipiTea and left a message for them to call me back.  Didn't hear from them.  Called them again later in the week and left a message asking if the inner bag was supposed to be sealed and if I should be concerned that it was opened.  Never heard back from them.  I know that this stuff is hand packed and all, but if it is packaged so that the tea won't stay in the bag...

I ordered this tea after reading about the many health benefits of Matcha tea, the healthiest of all Green teas.  I knew it would be dark green and milky- not clear and brownish as regular green teas.  But, I did not know that Matcha tea is actually green tea leaves ground into a very fine powder.  So, you do not need a tea infuser, but instead mix the powder with hot water and drink the actual tea leaves! No wonder Matcha tea boasts more of a health punch than green tea bags.  Now, in my opinion Matcha tea is not a pleasant drink.  It is thick and deep green, looking and tasting very similar to wet grass clippings.  I mixed the tea with honey and could stomach the first two cups, but the third cup made me gag.  Thankfully, this is a tea powder, so now I just put some in the blender with my yummy berry smoothies (yogurt, water, honey, ice, blueberries, other berries) and the grass taste isn't noticeable.  At the Amazon price of 38% off, this is an outstanding value for a whole 4-ounces of tea compared to other brands!  It is organic and comes in a recycled brown paper bag housed in a recycled box, along with an instruction card.  Arrived promptly in 2 business days as always with Amazon Prime!

I wanted to like this matcha because the price is so good. So when it arrived all split open and spilled in the box I told myself that was ok because it was cheap. When I took my first awful bitter sip I told myself just add more sweetener...and maybe some milk. But after a month of drinking this stuff I can't take it anymore! I just can't talk myself into enjoying the bitter taste no matter how cheap it is or how much milk and sweetener I add. I've gotten to the point where I don't even look forward to my morning cup of tea anymore. I'm still giving this 3 stars because it will work fine in smoothies or cooking where the flavor is more hidden (and it is marked as culinary so I guess that makes sense) but they really need to fix that packaging. And really if you're addicted to matcha you almost have to give this a try right? It's SO much cheaper and maybe the flavor won't bother you? As for me? I'm ordering the organic DoMatcha second harvest so I can enjoy my morning tea again.

column9: reasonable quality, good value but 3rd rate packaging
column10: Overall the quality is decent but not in the same league of the DoMatcha products. The tea mixes reasonably well when I use a small hand-held frother though a bit of small and stubborn "clots" do persist. I use stevia to sweeten the brew and like the taste. Given the price point this does seem to be good value. The one big negative is the packaging i.e. the inner foil bag which holds the tea almost always shows up damaged inside the box you seen in the picture. There is definite wastage with the powder all over and around the foil bag. If they fix this one weakness, I would certainly give this product a 4 or 5 star rating.

Like others have mentioned, the packaging of this product needs to be improved.  I have ordered this twice in the last few months.  The first order came in a mylar-type bag inside a sealed box.  The bag had broken open at some point so I had Matcha all over the place!  I decided to give it another try.  This time the mylar-type bag was inside a closed tin inside a sealed box.  I opened the box and Matcha was all over the place.  I opened the tin and bag was broken open inside.  PLEASE change the mylar-type bag to something more durable.  I most likely will not order this product again unless a change is made.  Too much wasted Matcha!

column9: Best deal for a great Matcha, for lattes, anyway!
column10: We have bought this brand of Matcha 3-4 times now and are very satisfied.  It used to be $12 for a 4 ounce box, which is an amazing deal!  Especially for ORGANIC Matcha!  I see the price jumped to over $17.  It is still a fair deal, although, I obviously, liked the $12 price better.  This price jump did cause me to search out other brands.  But, so far, I still like this one the best, for the price.I am not a coffee drinker ...never had any coffee in my life.  So, I had no reason to go into a Starbucks, until my girlfriend got me hooked on their Green Tea Soy Lattes a few years ago.  We don't do dairy, so we get soy instead.  We also don't get their sweetener (melon).  We have found the vanilla flavored soy milk has just enough sweetener to make it addicting.  Anyway, we have been able to make good soy lattes at home with vanilla soy milk and the SerendipiTea Matcha.  It has a nice bright green color and full flavor, which I have found works well in the lattes.  Not all the other matchas had the same full taste.  Maybe that has to do with the type of matcha (i.e. culinary grade, ceremony grade, etc.).  Anyway, the SerendipiTea culinary grade matcha makes a good soy latte and is still very well priced.I just got some Matcha from Malden Tea, from Amazon.  The price was amazing, 4oz for $9.99, although it isn't organic.  It was more of a yellowish green color, not a bright green.  It has a more bitter taste, not as full and isn't working as well in our lattes.  I am going to have to order more SerendipiTea Matcha, and hopefully, they will lower the price again.  I would even buy in bulk if I could save more.  Bottomline, in our Soy Lattes, this Matcha is the best for the price!

I started purchasing matcha about a year after they started selling it at Starbucks and Jamba Juice. live near San Francisco's Japantown and have tried several brands, varying in price from about $6 to $11 for approximately 1 ounce packages. I was happy to find what I thought was a great deal on Amazon, which with the subscription discount works out to less than $4 an ounce.  The package shipped quick, but as others have noted, comes in an unsealed package. I wouldn't freak out about that, but all things being equal, I'd have more confidence if the package was sealed. Bigger complaint is the quality is not up to snuff. It does not mix properly and tastes bitter compared to the matcha that I'm used to. I tried it twice (once with soy milk, another time with non-fat milk), and on both occasions it created a strange mixing effect, with the top half of the glass mixing nicely and the bottom half a murky mess that wouldn't mix properly. Both times the drink left me naueseous.  I don't claim to be a green tea expert, so I'm giving it two stars instead of one, but I've never had these problems with store-bought matcha in Japantown (or at Starbucks and Jamba Juice, for that matter). I would not recommend and have cancelled my subscription.

column9: Great Tea...packaging, as noted , is truly horrific
column10: On openning package, I ended up with fine green powder all over myself, my kitchen counter and the floor. It was completely unbelievable...like a blizzard of green! The tea, itself, is great for the money....I'm already trying to figure out a better way to open it next time...oh yes, there will be a next time as the risk/reward makes it a "go."

column9: Very high quality compared to most teas, easy to prepare, makes a great gift.
column10: I bought this item for my mom for Christmas. It comes packed in a little 3"x3" cardboard box, sealed in a plastic bag. It arrived in the mail within a week to the DC area. It is a fine powder of deveined green tea leaves. Before I bought the tea, I read that this brand is mediocre (mediocre, not poor) as far as matcha goes. However, it is the best green tea I've ever tasted, and it's in a realm way above your average teabags you get at a coffee shop or grocery store. It's also relatively cheap: we made eight or ten cups of thick, frothy tea, and it barely put a dent in the box. The box cost about $12 when I bought it. Way cheaper than a coffee shop.This tea is easy to make. Just pour a spoonful of powder directly into a cup of hot water, and stir it in for a thick, frothy cup of tea. It's easier than tea bags.Overall, it is an excellent product and makes a great Christmas or birthday gift. I was very impressed.
When I subscribed to this product 6 months ago it cost $19 and now it's $25. This price increase seems pretty ridiculous so I'm looking elsewhere for a replacement.
Dr Oz recommended this tea to try with my skin care routine so I have not tasted it.  Dont use to much tea on your skin.  Its powerful.

This stuff is powerful! I have not experienced problems with packaging like the other reviewer(s), it came tight sealed. The tea itself is very, very potent, but I feel so awake right now, stronger than cofee. I wasn't too keen on the flavor, but I downed it anyway because of the monstorous health benefits this stuff has. I see myself drinking this stuff for a while now, great product.

A number of reviewers have complained about the matcha packaging. serendipiTea apparently listens to their customers, when I received mine the matcha came in a bag inside a green tin box which prevented any spilling. So don't let the negative packaging reviews stop you from buying this product.For first time matcha brewers, don't add too much matcha and don't use boiling water, unless you like your tea extra bitter. One level teaspoon per cup is more than enough.Delicious matcha for a low price, no more needs to be said.

I was hesitant to purchase this brand because the price was so much lower than others listed. But I am very happy with the tea. Mind you I am comparing it with Starbucks "Green Tea Latte".....never been to Japan or had this served properly. So as a make-at-home green tea latte, I love it.

Dont expect Perfect cup foamy matcha TEA with this,  Its Mainly for cooking in foods... If you want Drinking Grade Go with Ceremonial grade  Worth the extra price trust me. I bought this because a reviwer said it was smooth in drink, It wasnt. It was chalky... But excellent for cooking, I made Green Tea Cake!
First, I am only using this matcha for smoothies and iced soy-lattes. The bag fully closed inside the tin when it arrived. The flavor is great, no bitterness. I fully recommended this product.

As a fan of matcha and chanoyu, I've bought and tried all grades of matcha both in and out of Japan.  This matcha is a terrific value--four times cheaper than the lowest-grade matcha from Nara--and it tastes wonderful.  I highly recommend it!(For the record, I've had no problems with the packaging.)

I just received my SerendipiTea Matcha Green Tea and immediately prepared a Vanilla Soy Green Tea Latte.  The tea was easily made into a paste and blended with the soy.  The flavor is outstanding.  It was beautifully packaged and well sealed.

I received the box and opened it up and green powder was everywhere! The bag inside the tin seemed sealed but there was powder caked on the directions. I brewed a cup and compared it to the Organic Eden brand I usually drink, which is a lot more expensive. The SerendipiTea Matcha was a bit bitter. The color and froth was fine but it had a very bitter taste. It's a bit messier to use than the Eden brand because the powder seems finer. As long as it gives me the health benefits of green tea, I'll drink it but I'm not sure I'd order it again.

Since the reviews for this tea were generally good, I was hoping for my usual cup of sweet green tea. Unfortunately, this tea turned out to be very bitter.  The packaging is very thin and was also split open, as other reviewers had also reported.  Very disappointing...
Awful, awful packaging. As soon as my mother opened the box the powder spilled all over the place because the bag was ripped opened. Flimsy piece of thin thin foil.

This matcha is not good enough for drinking straight. It doesn't have the bright green color and good aroma that a good quality matcha should. However, it IS labelled as culinary grade, which really means for adding to ice cream, smoothies etc. And for that, it's OK. Don't expect anything more!

Other reviewers have complained of the packaging.  A card inside the tea box stated the following:"SerendipiTea packaging is 100% post-consumer-recycled material Kraft; the inner bag is sustainably-sourced compostable plant-derived material (Nature-Flex).  All packing is done by hand on SerendipiTea premises in New York.  For optimal storage, we strongly recommend that contents be transferred to an air-tight, opaque ceramic or tin container kept away from heat and moisture."Just to clarify the above statement, the exterior packaging looks like a cardboard box.  On the inside is a brown paper bag containing a sealed cellophane-looking bag which holds the tea.  It isn't possible for the tea to leak out of the bag or box unless the entire package is crushed.  My product arrived in perfect condition.  The tea tastes great and the packaging is earth-friendly.  I also like the fact that it's packed in the USA.

column9: Decent matcha for a decent price!
column10: This matcha appears to be a good balance between price and quality.  I'm not a matcha expert but I have a couple months and several ounces worth of experience.  The matcha I was drinking before was $10/ounce which had good full flavor and was not bitter even when made strong.  I admit I've only used matcha to make lattes which is one reason for switching to something less expensive.  I've made about a dozen lattes with this matcha and I'm overall pleased with it. The flavor is comparable if not the same as the more expensive matcha I had but it is definitely bitter but if you're making latte with this it isn't a big deal since the additives almost ompletely overcome the bitterness.  I do have a somewhat weak stomach when it comes to green teas and the first couple lattes made me a little queasy (less than nauseous).  If you're the same way it might take a few to get used to it or enjoy it with a little snake.  This stuff is the way to go if you want to enjoy matcha daily without breaking the bank.

I was a little apprehensive in purchasing this product due to some reviews. However, I am so glad I took a chance, this is the best MATCHA. Excellent packaging, it's in the box shown, double bagged in plastic and paper. I will purchase again.

After enjoying DoMatcha Green Tea, Organic Matcha, 1.06-Ounce Tin as my first foray into matcha and deciding to drink matcha each morning, I figured it was time to find a less-expensive alternative and chose SerendipiTea's matcha.  Organic, cheaper price, larger quantity, and positive reviews all seemed to indicate that it was a smart purchase.PACKAGING:  There's been some discussion as to the packaging of the SerendipiTea's matcha.  Inside a thin cardboard box is a heavy paper bag with the top rolled up.  Inside the bag is a thin foil bag containing the tea.  The box and paper bag are decent, but the foil used is extremely thin, and mine had several holes and tears that allowed a powdery dust to accumulate.TEA:  There's definitely a difference in color compared to the DoMatcha tea.  While DoMatcha was a bright, vibrant green, SerendipiTea resembled olive drab and looked sickly in comparison.  It tastes far more bitter compared to DoMatcha's smooth flavor...I kind of had to choke down the rest of my cup.On the bottom of the box it notes that this is CULINARY grade tea, not ceremonial grade.  I do not know if this accounts for the difference in color vibrancy and flavor, but I'm willing to bet it might.If you're planning on cooking with matcha or making ice cream/smoothies then SerendipiTea's matcha provides more bang for your buck.  However, if you're simply looking for a tasty brewed cup this might not be the most delicious option.  While DoMatcha was definitely more expensive, I think I'd prefer to pay the extra to get the quality and taste that's best for me, and in the meantime I'm off to find some good matcha recipes to use up the rest of my SeredipiTea!

While this is not the best matcha I have tried it is a good deal for the money. Compared to Domatcha brand the green is a little lighter and a bit more bitter so the quality is not quite up there with the other I mentioned. However, if you are looking for a cheaper matcha than this is good stuff for the price and by no means is it junk. This is a lot better than some of the practically yellow matchas I have tried in the past for not much cheaper. I have allergies and use green tea to control them and Domatcha brand is a little better but costs more.
I do really like green tea, it has an after taste, But this tea was smooth and mild. I can drink it even on an empty stomach. It makes me feel good. I will order this tea again.

I like this Matcha for Green Tea Latte recipe, with soymilk. For tea alone,a little bit of bitter taste is present, but depends on your taste, you might like it even so. For latte recipe it is great !!!

This is a culinary grade matcha and I have used it to make doughnuts, blondies, cookies, ice cream and candies. A couple of tablespoons mixed with a bit of powdered sugar gives desserts a nice green tea flavor. I have only drank it as a tea once and it was a bit bitter. The product comes in a tin with a tightly closed paper bag which made it hard to use, so I transferred it into a plastic bag for easier access. Overall I would recommend this product if you are interested in making green tea desserts.Update: I have tried this again as a hot tea, this time using the correct temperature and method and it was not bitter. Although it was not the best matcha tea I've ever had, it was quite good once I learned how to prepare it properly.

I wanted to try Match Tea and I wanted something organic. I researched and decided on SerendipiTea. Glad I did! It's really great! There were some photos that indicated the packaging could be messy but I had no issue with the packaging. It tastes incredible. I recommend this product!

I researched the various green tea powders available for purchase and found this one to be the best price for the quality.  Many others are not grown in Japan and are far more expensive.  I highly recommend this product for taste and quality!

Shipped very fast , and packaging was fine .  I have tried several matcha teas .  For the price this is excellent quality .  Of course it is not as sweet as ceremonial matcha.  Ceremonial matcha is $50-$70 per ounce , this is $5 per ounce , less than 1/10 the price .  Having said that , the quality for the price is excellent and its organic , which is nice as even some ceremonial is not organic.  The main difference is that this is more bitter than ceremonial.  I enjoy bitter and sour tastes so this is great for me.  Same health benefits as ceremonial , and thats the main thing for me , but I also very much enjoy the taste.

column9: a decent culinary-grade matcha meant for smoothies or cooking
column10: i bought this culinary-grade matcha specifically for mixing it into my smoothies.  the packaging is acceptable although it could be improved by sealing it some sort of air-tight foil bag to keep it fresh.  i transferred mine into an air-tight container (see pic i posted of a close-up view of the matcha) and store it in the fridge to keep it as fresh as possible.  i prepared a hot cup of tea to drink by itself so i could test and taste it in its true form, but it is not meant for that purpose.  organic is a plus, and the price versus amount is reasonable.  kudos to the seller for providing us with an accurate product description.  i would purchase this matcha again.
Does not taste good.  Only meant for smoothies or cooking.  I have experienced matcha green tea that tastes good. I wish I remember the brand.

My kids and I like this,its WAY milder than the brand I tried before this,The other brand was 8 oz and a good deal,But it was a bit bitter.Once I tried this,there was no going back to the other.This is so mild compare to the other one we had

column9: Delicious and new packaging is very sturdy!
column10: This matcha tea taste delicious and smooth, plus it mixes really well. I use it for smoothies and lattes and it taste fantastic. No issues with the packaging or shipping. The inner paper bag is a sturdy, reusable gusted bag with a fold down top with a tin-tie.
[a.]  Received sooner than expected[b]  Product was good quality for the price; a little bitter but,[c]  I will buy this again

I bought this to use in some homemade green tea ice-cream and absolutely love it!  Using this in the recipe gave me the delicious green tea ice-cream you get out in the restaurants.  Getting it to dissolve took a little time but not so bad.  Only complaint I had was when I first opened up the box, the inside packaging was unraveled and there was powder everywhere in the box.  That made for a mess to try and scoop some out.  Other than that I think was a great high quality product.
You get more of this product than other teas that I have tried.  I have used it in my French Press also, which does a fine job.

I drink green tea every morning instead of coffee, but I've always been a bit leery of trying the Matcha. However, after hearing about its many health benefits, I finally broke down and gave it a try. Delicious! The dark green color threw me when I was whisking it, but I was a convert from the first sip.  It's very smooth and flavorful -- and, it may just be the power of suggestion, but I feel a huge difference in energy levels and alertness during the day. I haven't tried using it in any recipes yet, but I think this would be awesome in an iced green tea chai soy latte, too.One word of advice: Make sure you whisk it thoroughly, or you'll have a little bit of sludge at the bottom where the undissolved powder settles.

I finally decided to get this tea instead of other brands because of the price, even though I'd read some very negative reviews mixed in with the positive ones that made me wary. I made my first cup of this today and couldn't be happier. Some reviewers complained about the packaging. Mine came in perfect condition and was easy to transfer to an airtight zip-lock bag. Some reviewers complained about a bitter aftertaste. I found the flavor to be rich, fresh, and smooth, with not even a hint of a bitter aftertaste. I dissolved 1 tablespoon of sugar in 1/2 cup of water, heated it in the microwave and then whisked in 1 teaspoon of matcha. Then I heated 1/2 cup of milk in the microwave and frothed it and slowly added the tea to the mug of milk for an absolutely perfect latte. I haven't bought my own matcha powder before, but I have had green tea lattes from Starbucks and other such places and this is every bit as good as those. Especially for the price, I'd say you can't beat SerendipiTea's matcha powder!

Tea tastes great.  I first started drinking this type of tea at Starbucks.  I then ordered some matcha from Nutsonline.com but didn't realize it had additives in it...but it did tasted EXACTLY like the Starbucks Green Tea Latte (they use matcha powder) except I wanted it all natural without any flavorings.I tried this and even though it tastes fantastic, it clumps...gotta find a way to make without the clumping.If I can get rid of the clumping then it's 5 stars.

I did not have any of the packaging problemsthat a few others had.  My tea was sealed insidea dark green plastic bag that was inside a tinand it did not leak inside the tin.  I also tookthe bag out and weighed it on a digital scaleand it was exactly 4 oz. just as they stated.All in all, a VERY GOOD price forORGANIC green matcha tea.  I am very happy with it(it tastes very good too.)

column9: Good flavor, poor packaging, will never order again
column10: The package is terrible! My bag was split open and green tea powder was spilled everywhere! I lost 4-6 cups worth. It was a pain cleaning up that tea powder. I had to put it in my own plastic container. For $80/lb I expect better. Will never order this brand again! Not worth the trouble. It also took over a week to arrive, when I paid for regular shipping.I tried this plain, with only water, and it was smooth enough to drink. Normally I drink it in lattes. With Culinary Teas brand, I had to add vanilla and sugar to the latte to make it palatable. Even though this costs more than Culinary Teas, it is worth it. I still add a bit of sugar to the latte though. The packaging is terrible, some form of hippie foil bag inside a cardboard box. Every time you spoon out some tea, it spills and powder gets everywhere. The inner bag is not resealable neither. I wish they came in larger sizes, with a resealable container.

column9: Nutritional value and flavor vs price
column10: Without a CSI lab, I don't know if the paler green of the culinary grade means less nutritive properties than the higher 1st & 2nd harvest brilliant green teas, but my money is on using less of the higher quality grades to compete with the value of this culinary grade.For culinary grade, it is a little more bitter than the higher grades, but is declicious in coooking and frappes.At the subrscription rate, it really is a good bargain.  Then again, if the higher priced brilliant green ryu-mei 1st and 2nd havest (grade 4 is good enough to drink as plain tea), means the nutrients are higher, I find myself using less quantity and feeling I'm getting the same benefits.Depending on how much I use, I will keep the Serendipiti Tea coming as a subscription, because it's affordable and I won't have to worry about running out of it.

column9: Great Cafe Grade Matcha Tea - Worth the money!
column10: So many good things about this tea -1. Tastes good (and tastes like Matcha!)2. Organic3. Eco-friendly packaging4. 4 ounce box for approximately $15 (AND GOOD QUALITY!)I was buying Matcha green tea for the first time and was unsure of whether to spend a lot or whether I'd like the taste of tea (in smoothies or in the traditional japanese style). I read reviews about DoMatcha, Matcha Tea from Matcha Source, Imperial Grade Matcha from Teavana but finally settled on SerendipiTea. This turned out to be a pretty good deal.When I'm ready to spend more, I might buy one of teas I mentioned above (pretty expensive compared to Serendipitea) and will buy those only for drinking 'Koicha'or 'Usucha'. I might also stock up on Serendipitea for smoothies.The first smoothie I tried was a simple one - milk, ice, 1tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp Matcha green tea all blended together and it tasted very good. It's my favorite now - for health reasons and for the taste. I'd definitely recommend this tea. If you opt in for the subscription, you'll save some more.P.S. In some reviews, I read about complaints with the packaging. However, it was not a big issue for me as I usually prefer to store tea and coffee in airtight containers. It is also not advisable to use Green Tea from its original packaging if the contents are not used within a month. Although I'm using the tea out of the original packaging and it's only been two weeks now, I intend on buying a beautiful, semi-transparent, decorative canister to store my green tea in.

This matcha tea is comparable to others I've tried, a little bit more bitter. Packaging is horrible. It arrived in a foil package inside a box, the foil was ripped in several places so I had a green powder mess all over the place, and a lot was wasted. Come on, they can do better than that considering what it cost.

This is a nice matcha tea to buy. I don't think the grade is what is claimed as the taste isn't consistently smooth. It is quite good quality though for the price, and I recommend that others buy this if a higher quality matcha is not withing price range. I think this matcha is better than others I have tried in this price range.

I'm no matcha expert, however do enjoy this tea. I can tell it's good quality, not some cheap pretend-green tea. It has mucho flavor, whether I'm making a latte or just plain hot green tea like you drink with sushi. packaging could be better but for the price and quality, I don't really care.
I really like this. The powder is very fine, and it tastes great when blended with ice cream. Lowering the price wouldn't hurt, but I guess you get what you pay for.

I know some reviews said that the packaging wasn't adequate, however I think they have changed the packaging. The tea comes in a sealed foil bag, in a paper bag in the box shown. There was no spillage of the tea. The tea flavor was great in a smoothie that I made. I was very happy with the tea.

I'm no tea expert, but I am a Starbucks Green Tea Latte addict. I decided to cut back on the cost and make my own latte at home. This tastes virtually the same as the Starbucks matcha to me. The price per ounce is a bargain for an organic tea. Only downside is that you need to pack it in your own opaque airtight container after opening. The box is as shown in the picture, and inside you'll find a small brown paper bag with a thick twist tie thing to open an close it. And inside the paper bag is a small sealed thin foil bag with the tea.I add a teaspoon to my haagen daz vanilla,  make a green tea smoothies/shakes, Cakes/pastries, etc it's pretty versatile in it's uses other than for just your daily tea.
I've never had bad matcha but this is very nice. I mix it in lemon ginger soup. Very nom nom.

column9: This company makes GREAT fruit teas, however
column10: Did not care for their organic green tea at all, but their fruit teas are the best.

I've been adding Matcha to my morning "smoothie" for several months now but have been looking for something a bit cheaper than what I've been using.  A search here at Amazon pointed me toward SerendipiTea Matcha, Culinary Grade.  It is perfect for my needs.When the box arrives, I open it immediately and put the contents into a canning jar--a rubber gasket-ed "Fido" style jar.  This does two things for me:  it gets it out of the shipping packaging but it also makes it easier to access on the fly.The flavor of this Matcha is as good as the non-culinary Matcha that I have tasted--at least for my "smoothies."  I have yet to try it in hot form.My only complaint about this tea is that it is not available for Subscribe & Save ordering.  In fact, as I write this, there is none is stock--a condition I hope is temporary.03/06/10 Addendum:Amazon has just added this to Subscribe and Save and I could not be happier.

column9: Definately culinary grade, but a decent buy
column10: I bought this because I just couldn't see putting my good matcha into smoothies. To my surprise, it's not terrible to drink (and most of the organic matcha I've tried in the US has been). It's still mostly for smoothies and cookies, but also for off mornings when I won't appreciate the good stuff. (I certainly appreciate the good stuff more after one of those.)
Excellent product, good price and awesome turn around time.  I received this in 2 days !
If you have had the pleasure of drinking a bright green, smooth, mellow matcha...this is not for you! *Eek* *Cough-cough* *Hack!* *Whooo!* *Uncle!* tears roll* I'm speechless.

I bought this Culinary grade Matcha powder based on many good reviews but was very disappointed! I like to bake green tea cookies and cakes but unfortunately the bitter after taste just makes my baked goods very unpalatable (using 1-3 tsp per batch). I previously used a store bought Matcha from Japan which cost twice as much and was not specified "culinary grade" and compared the two. My store bought brand had a slightly lighter green color and a nice balance of flavor with no bitter after taste compared to SerendipiTea Matcha which blows you away. I will stick with the store bought brand in the future.
This came as described.  Good price and packaging.  Be aware it can be messy since the particles are so fine.  Not your bagged tea but fun to try something different and so good for you, too!!

I didn't like this tea at all.  I prepared it according to package directions but it was very, very green and kind of thick.  I didn't like the taste but I will admit I didn't drink much of it.  I think I'll stick to the regular white, green and oolong tea.  I thought of making the tea "weaker" but didn't....I don't think I would have liked it any better :)

I purchased one of these for my girlfriend while I was in Afghanistan and she loved it.  She took pictures and sent them too me, It looks exactly as pictured.  she said everything inside was great. The yogurt pretzels were here favorite, she said they were outstanding.  however, the box she received did not have chocolate covered cherries in the top, instead they had been substituted with chocolate covered peanuts of a different kind than the others already included.  If you're away, you won't be disappointed sending this gift, it is very large and reasonably priced.  The only reason I give this four stars, instead of five, is that I feel as a substitute for chocolate covered cherries, she should have received something more akin to that category; perhaps a chocolate covered fruit of another kind.  Anyway, a great gift idea.

This item was extremely disappointing.The boxes were damaged. The boxes were filled with filler (paper, styrofoam, etc) to make them look full and therefore there were very little sweets in the boxes! Not worth the price for the amount of goodies. Would have returned it if I had received it earlier, but unfortunately I didn't and had to give it as a birthday present anyway. It was embarassing! Don't waste your money on this.

I purchased this as an Anniversary gift. They said it was great they loved that it was a variety of  items as well as great packaging. The box is shipped as a tower.Each item is individually wrapped . Overall it will make any special holiday or birthday, very special. The candy was great as well.

This product is a huge rip-off. The chocolate chip cookies were almost like astronaut food as far as consistency. I counted a total of 8 half-dollar size cookies in the package and 4 of which had only 1 chocolate chip each. The other food was of similar quality, appearing to be cheap processed junk food. For the price of this package and the amount of snacks received and quality, I say completely avoid this rip-off.

Talk about false advertising!! This is what you will get if you order this. From the website it looks like you are getting a nice gift. Boy did I get fooled. It makes me mad to know that there are companies like this that do people this way. And to think of what I am having to pay for something that is really not worth it. I think they should be made to repay us what we are paying for this gift basket since they are promoting false advertising. I will have to "cherish" every bite of these tiny treats. I want my money back!!! I will be glad to send it back to you. I have not opened it.

Not as described! When ordering, the picture shows box's over-flowing.In all actuality,the contents barely covered the bottom of each box!There were no pistachio's as promised and there was no gift card,(TO:/FROM: CARD), Very Disappointing! I would not recommend thisproduct to anyone! My views could possibly change, if they were toredeem themselves. I will update this post at a later date.*****This item was originally purchased through Amazon.com, so they handledany problems with this order. Since this item was a grocery item, returningit was not an option. Never the less, Amazon handled my complaints in atruly professional and very courteous manner! Amazon is my go to placefor all my online purchases! A+!******

I purchased this for my grandmother's birthday. She wrote back and stated that this was such a nice gift. She also stated that the boxes were stacked nicely, well packaged with "ice bricks" keeping the package cool and preventing the chocolate from melting, and it had lots of treats in each box.She really enjoyed this product. An absolute great gift! Bravo!!!

I ordered and paid for a Broadway Basketeers Gift Tower of Sweets as a birthday gift and what showed up was Coffee Mate Creamer and Murine Ear cleanser..... Really???? How embarrassing!!! Who packs this stuff???? I want my money back !!!
This was sent as a gift to hosppital staff for caring for my husband.  They said they loved it! I have received similar items myself and enjoyed all the contents.
wasn,t sure what to get for a friend of my sons, so i got him some gourmet treats. i hope he likes it, it is nicely packaged.

column9: Simply the Best Tea in the World
column10: Years ago,I was introduced to Barry's Gold Blend Tea by a priest from Ireland. Members of his family would ship it to him and he made some for me. It is simply the best tea in the world. This was before you could get a lot of products online and when I went off to college I had to live without it. I am delighted to now be able to have it shipped right to my door.
This is the best tea that there is. I'm totally addicted, starting from a visit to Ireland years ago. It's smooth, never bitter, and absolutely perfect!

Like so many others, I had this tea on my first visit to Ireland.After my first cup, I thought, "this is pretty good!"After my second cup later, I thought, "this is pretty darn good."The next day I bought a box to take home.Then I started asking friends and co-workers to bring an extra suitcase on their trips to Ireland...Over the next 20 years I heard the same story from many others here, "I asked a friend to bring an extra suitcase..."I'm really happy that this tea is available here now, and my wife and I travel nowhere without bringing a sufficient supply of Barry's, as it really brightens our day in a way that is unmatched by any other tea (or coffee for that matter).This is the "tea bag" version, so some loose leaf tea drinkers may suspect that the bags are filled with floor sweepings, as seems to be the case with many other tea bags.Not so, this is the good stuff (although if you want the hassle, you can get this in loose-leaf).I prepare it in a Krups coffee maker (this and a few others have the correct water temperature), set a timer for 6 minutes in good water (Brita faucet filtered, which beats bottled Mountain Spring water for taste, really, and costs $0.10 per gallon).Don't follow my example and be led into a life-long addiction, stay away from this tea!:O)

We had some at home, but I don't know where it came from, but on a whim I tried it for making a quick glass of ice tea (instead of a Lipton bag).  In a rush, I made a mug of tea, let it cool a while then poured it into a big cup of ice.  I am overwhelmed at how good it was.  Not bitter at all (like the Lipton usually is) and a sort of natural sweetness (I take my ice tea unsweetened).  What a treat! I am going to get more of Barry's for my ice tea and will try it as a morning hot tea as well.
Barry's tea has a wonderful rich but not bitter flavor.  I drink it every morning.

A pleasure to read the glowing reviews here for this truly fine brand of tay. On an average day stretched to include morning, noon and night I can honestly say I must drink upwards of fourteen or fifteen scalding hot mugs of Barry's Gold Blend and not a bit of a bother on me neither during the entire length of the duration. Milk and a lump of sugar too, of course, black tea being something of a Paddy Kavanagh-like penance for the homegrown likes of me. Barry's tea is blended in the fabled city of Cork, me old stomping ground as a matter of fact, having being blended meself as a fat wee babby in nearly the exact same whereabouts some two score and seven years ago. Cork incidentally is also home to The Butter Museum, a revered if not indeed wholly sacred institution whose existence is quite properly the pride of Shandon. It hardly needs repeating I suppose that Barry's tea and butter are big news in Ireland although to be honest I myself never ever tire of repeating it. Lookit now and this is no lie but there I was just the other day watching John Huston's The MacKintosh Man from 1973 and sure weren't bits of it filmed in the west of Ireland and anyway along comes this bus at one point and here's what was written in giant green letters along the full length of it: BUTTER IS THE CREAM. Begob but I froze that frame instamatically for to stand up and larf and hoot in a befitting manner. Ah memories! I heard tell of a relation of mine once, batty as a barm brack by all accounts, who on discovering he was out of milk one morning promptly dolloped a spoon of butter into his breakfast tea instead. Like I said nutty as a fruitcake but how's that for country cute, eh? Only in Eire although our Sasanach friends across the puddle do be drinking more tea than even us betimes and to prove it I'll leave yiz all with the following ditty from that very great Englishman Ray Davies, entitled appropriately enough:HAVE A CUPPA TEAGranny's always ravin' and rantin',And she's always puffin' and pantin',And she's always screaming and shouting,And she's always brewing up tea.Grandpappy's never late for his dinner,Cos he loves his leg of beefAnd he washes it down with a brandy,And a fresh made pot of tea.Chorus:Have a cuppa tea, have a cuppa tea,have a cuppa tea, have a cuppa tea,Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah, Rosie LeaHallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah, Rosie Lea.If you feel a bit under the weather,If you feel a little bit peeved,Take granny's stand-by potionFor any old cough or wheeze.It's a cure for hepatitis, it's a cure for chronic insomnia,It's a cure for tonsillitis and for water on the knee.ChorusTea in the morning, tea in the evening, tea at supper time,You get tea when it's raining, tea when it's snowing,Tea when the weather's fine.You get tea as a mid-day stimulantYou get tea with your afternoon teaFor any old ailment or diseaseFor Christ sake have a cuppa tea.ChorusWhatever the situation, whatever the race or creed,Tea knows no segregation, no class nor pedigreeIt knows no motivations, no sect or organisation,It knows no one religion,Nor political belief.ChorusGood that, innit? You should hear the rest of the album too that that smashing little song is on, Muswell Hillbillies, bleeding masterpiece so it is. The Kinks, wha'? Right then, I'm off to put the kettle on.

My poor husband can't find a decent tea 'in the States'. Our local grocery stopped importing from Ireland some time ago. My Mom bought Barry's as part of a gift basket for him and he's never looked back. I can only hope that there is enough in stock to keep him happy!
This tea is simply the best. My sister brought some back from a foreign exchange trip, and when we had finished the box I had to have more. It's nothing fancy, just really good tea.

If you want a quality tea that is the daily choice of the Irish, this is for you.  It is bold. Drink like the Irish do with sugar and milk.  I got so used to my daily "fix" while working in Dublin for a month that I was delighted to find it online when I had depleted the supply brought back with me.
Ever since my husband and I went to Ireland we love Barry's tea.  It has a really nice flavor.

Acceptable tea, with a light gold colouring, and weighty single bags.  Despite the amount of tea per bag, the tea is not very strong, even with a long 5+min soaking. As such, it will not accept too much cream or sugar either. This is fine in itself, as the tea has a nice flavour, a blend of Assam and Kenyan teas. Its taste and strength are similar to PG Tips or more closely Typhoo.  Makes a pleasant, late evening tea, but was expecting more out of this popular Irish blend. For those preferring a much stronger, darker tea you may want to find another brand.

Having never heard of Barry's tea and learning it's an Irish tea, I decided to check it out with a friend who has visited his wife's aunts and uncles and cousins in Ireland very, very often.  Had he ever had Barry's tea?  Indeed, he had.  Every day, in fact, that he'd spent in Ireland.  And was the tea good?  Indeed, it was.  He always had some on hand back here in the states.And then he told me that he liked tea strong with nothing added. One of his wife's aunts didn't approve.  She gave him his cuppa and then offered him sugar and milk.  When he declined, she exclaimed, "No milk!  No sugar!  Never heard of such a thing.  Why, it's not Ash Wednesday, Lent, or Good Friday."I plan to buy Barry's when I find some shelf space to store it.  And, I will drink it with milk and sugar if it's not Ash Wednesday, Lent, or Good Friday.Amazon,  your reviewers are a hoot.

This tea would be worth traveling to Ireland if it weren't available in the US.  I drink only tea and have tried all of the major brands and this is the perfect one.  I use one tea bag in a pot and it makes six cups off medium strong tea.  At work, a partners and I have switched and we get five travel mugs (16oz) from a two bag pot.  I can't praise it enough!
Barry's is the best tea I've had, then again I'm not a tea expert. I like it and will buy more.

column9: Black tea with a nice punch
column10: This is a great black tea and a must in my kitchen.  I like boxes of tea with at least 40 per box.  I don't buy overpriced specialty teas that cost 4 bucks for 16 to 20 bags.  That said, my kitchen tea essentials are:  Tetley Classic, Tetley British Blend, PG Tips, and Barry's Gold Blend Tea.  Barry's may be similar to these other teas, but is definitely the very strongest of these teas.  The Irish Blend in the green box is even stronger.  Barry's is great tea in a generous 80 bag count box.

Barry's Gold is top of the line Irish tea.  It is a great beverage anytime of the day but my favorite times start after a.m. coffee gets to be old tasting. After supper is another great time to enjoy this distinctly, deep flavored tea.  A lovely warm, dark, brown with a hint of gold, it even looks good.  Oops, I have made myself thirsty for a cup of this fine tea right now, putting the kettle on the boil.  Try some.

column9: Great Tea at a Great Price
column10: This is a great tasting tea that anyone one, Irish or American will apppreciate. It comes from Ireland and tastes like the kitchen back home. With milk and sugar added, we call it Irish Pennicillian when one of the family has a cold.You can't forget it and you can't beat the taste or quality... Enjoy mate!

I drink tea daily and have for over fifty years. When I first tried Barry's Tea, I knew I had found my favorite brand. It's flavor is bold, but very yummy at the same time. I will not be without it again! I have even given it and the decaf as Christmas gifts with a tea pot to a few friends. They also thought it was outstanding tea.

This truly is the best "real tea"-- just a golden cup of pure flavor--and a pretty color it is! You must try it to know----I was introduced to it at an Irish festival in Pittsburgh, PA about 12 years ago !!

Barrys Gold Blend Tea is the finest cup of tea that one can buy. To Traveler who only gave it 4 stars I say it probably did not taste right because your water was crap. Real tea does not have a string attached to the bag. You just need boiling water, leave it to stew for a minute or so, sugar and milk to taste.A that reminds me, it's time for a cup of Barrys.

In an age of flowery herby teas we have Barry Tea Gold Blend.  I drink a lot of tea and this consistently is my favorite.  There are numerous great green teas but for traditional black tea drinkers this is as good as it gets for me.  And, the Irish really do drink it,  at least in Cork.

column9: Great Irish Tea... All Day Long
column10: I love this tea!  Add boiling water to the teapot, wait a few minutes and the best tasting tea is the result.  No matter how long the bag is in the pot, the tea is always perfect; it doesn't get over-strong or bitter.  Such a smooth blending of flavors.  Truly, no better tea than this Irish Gold.

Barry's Irish Tea, Gold Blend (The red box) is an absolute 5 star, must try for the serious tea drinker.  As a traditional Continental tea it is much stronger, and better than the black teas typically available to us here in the states.  One tea bag of Barry's is much heavier and aromatic than what you are probably used to.  You can make two strong cups from a single bag.  Pickwick Finest English is my hands down favorite, but Barry's Gold Blend is a close second and a must have essential to my stock of tea.  If you are looking for a fine, heavy tea to get you started in the morning or to share a cozy Sunday morning with, give this traditional tea a try.  Barry's is a nice alternative to morning coffee.  Try it the English way with cream and sugar.

column9: The BEST bagged tea I've ever had
column10: My friend brought me back a box of this stuff from Ireland. I loved it so much I actually switched from being a morning coffee drinker to a morning tea drinker (Barry's ONLY!).  Strong, but not bitter at all. Great flavor. A little milk & honey and I'm in heaven. I absolutely love it.

While visiting Ireland we had the most delicious tea, Barrys Gold.I ordered this tea thinking it was the same, but it is not.The Barrys Gold in Ireland was a beautiful light golden color with a different taste.Don't know if the word 'blend' on the box had anything to do with the difference??This was a very good tea, but not what I had in Ireland. Are there different Barrys Gold teas??The tea I ordered is better than what I've bought at the store so would recommend it to others.

column9: every sip relaxes your soul and revives your spirit
column10: When I feel a need for something that soothes me, I like to make myself a cup of Barry'ws tea.  It does not have that harsh aftertaste, but is so smooth.  Every sip relaxs your soul and revives your spirit. Barry's tea is a friend.
My wife had purchased some of this tea when we were out east.. When she ran out no one in our area carried it and we were very happy to find it on-line

When I went shopping for a baby cereal, I only wanted pure organic ingredeints! No pesticide residue for my baby! I found HappyBellies and not only does it have ORGANIC ingredients, but uses brown rice (no bleached white rice) and has DHA (brain and eye development) and probiotics (immunity support) too! Plus, vitamins and minerals! Mixed with my breastmilk, my baby gobbles it up!

I was disappointed that Santo Tomas Paella Rice had a high percentage of broken rice pieces. Broken rice cooks faster than intact rice, so this offering of Santo Tomas Paella Rice resulted in a mushy consistency. At first Santo Tomas seems a bargain, but add in shipping costs and you'll get better for the same price. You can find alternative rice for Paella on Amazon for $2.95 (16 oz.). C & F Arroz Valencia Short Grain Rice for Paella, 1 lb. Or look at your supermarket for Arroz Valenciano or Arroz Perla from Iberia or Goya. Both offer a better quality of rice than Santo Tomas.

I made paella for first time and this rice cooked perfectly. After shopping around online and in a couple of grocery stores, I found rice that was overpriced. This rice seemed authentic so I decided to give it a try.For anyone who wants to find a rice that holds up to long cooking time without becoming mealy or starchy-tasting, this is it.

column9: Russell Stover Assorted Fine Chocolates - 12 oz.
column10: Outstanding!  I don't know what Russell Stover has done in the past 5 years, but there is certainly an excellent change in the quality and recipe of this variety of chocolates.This 12 oz box of handcrafted chocolates are stated as being made in small batches--delicious every bite!  I paid about $7.00 for this box on sale at a local drug store chain.The box contains a variety of flavors and textures wrapped in milk chocolate.
