And even when she doesn't eat much else, I'm happy knowing this is simply chicken, nothing more.  I wish they came in bigger sized bottles!(This is indeed the best online price too.)

Sodium phosphate is a preservative.  So these are not chemical and preservative free.  That's the part I read, but I should have read more carefully.  I didn't realize it was in there when I ordered these for my cats.  One cat ignores them, but my other one loves them.  But sodium phosphate causes me terrible migraines so I stay away from it in my foods and medicines.  Even a little bit has a bad effect on me.  This makes me very wary about giving it to my cat.  The salmon has no marinade and therefore no sodium phosphate, so I'll get that one again.  I wish the chicken was more pure.  I don't do many reviews but I thought I should point this out in case it makes a difference to anyone else. I'm always looking for healthy food for my cats and dog.  Not sure this is, with that chemical in it.

column9: Liv - A  - Littles whole chicken treats for Cats & Dogs
column10: This treat is excellent for cats and dogs. It is pure dehydrated chicken, with no unhealthy additives, chicken parts or fillers. I have two Abyssinian cats who are crazy about it (the breeder from whom I bought the cats told me about this product). It's a healthy treat for them. Every night at 10 pm my cats let me know it's their chicken treat time, and they gobble it up.It's a wonderful product and I highly recommend it to anyone who cares about their pets.
Our geriatric cat, 17 yrs, loves these and when she won't eat anything else she'll tear these up and eat 'em in a most carnivorous fashion.  Pure protein- yum.

Had just about given up on ever finding a treat for my kitty Zummy ~ I tried them all ... everything from the cheapy supermarket brands to the ones that come from Whole Foods andare organic ... then a close friend gave me a few (from her cat Travis's stash), to let Zummy have a taste ... well, she devoured them, inhaled them and wanted more. We are on our first container, and everytime I head toward the refrigerator Zumis at my heals waiting for more! I wouldn't have believed it until I saw it with my own eyes. Not cheap tho ~ but Amazon definitely has the best price! Guaranteed to please for sure... if Zummy loves it, your cat will to!!!

We ordered these recently because we used to get them at Whole Foods in Louisville or at Krogers.  But there is no Whole Foods where we live now and Krogers runs out for long periods.  Our cats love them.  One of the cats eats these treats about 90% of the time.  They're expensive but he's just so healthy and playful. (We break them up a little smaller)They came in just a couple of days, too.  Great service and packaged up nicely.Update--The first few times the product came in 2-3 days.  This time I ordered it June 26th thinking it would come by the following Tuesday but it's now July 6th and they are giving me a goal date of July 8th. To me, this is just too long. I've ordered things from East Coast before with standard shipping and gotten them in 3 days, so I don't know why it has to be 11-12 days for this.Barbara, Larry, and Cats

I'm not quite sure why this product listing is for the chicken variety yet in the product description it speaks of how the beef version is made. That's a little confusing and makes me wonder about the chicken version...which is what I'm here to review. Trust me, the chicken variety is where it's at!This potent, endlessly pleasing box of feline ambrosia is the closest thing to opium I could imagine rewarding my cats with, without travelling over to the Middle East to get the real deal. Be warned: your kitty will take to this treat like the most ravenous furry addict you have ever seen, never missing an opportunity to spy on you as you open the refrigerator to once in a while (when you're not spending inordinate amounts of time with your cat) get sustenance for yourself. If you've never wondered what it is like to marvel at a cat trying to open a refrigerator door, don't buy this stuff. Don't even think of returning to simple store-bought crunchy treats after this stuff. Your cat will look at you like you are trying to replace sushi with a gold fish cracker! "C'mon, human, give me the goods; give me the white lines, I mean CRUMBS!"If you drop a little piece on the floor, your animals will race to lap it up and transport themselves into "Blissful." It is the ultimate reward with very few negative side effects as far as I can tell (other than unbridled, but functional addiction!)This stuff is a magical, mysterious little concoction that puts an instant smile on your feline and makes her your friend for life. It will slowly start wrecking your monthly budget, of course, but you will find justification after justification for purchasing it ad infinitum.I believe that William S. Burroughs, in the seminal novel Naked Lunch, spoke of the "algebra of need." As soon as your fluffy little angel hits this chicken-laced pleasure pipe, she'll be hooked for life!

The concept is good, the snack is nutritious, but in ordering from Amazon, there was practically nothing but dust in the bag.  The couple of treats that were left uncrushed were practically air and my 71 pound dog looked at me as if I were playing a joke on her.

My cat adores these.  I crumble some over his (Halo salmon) dry food and he is in cat heaven.  He loves the salmon version, too.  These can also be "reconstituted" by adding a little water, as an alternative to wet food.  I love that the ingredient list contains a single item:  Freeze-dried chicken breast.  Simple and perfect.

These are just terrific!!  If I can't find my cats, all I have to do is shake the container and they come running from where ever they were hiding out!!  These are great training snack for the puppies as well!  I have had a hard time finding these in the stores, so this is the BEST place to get them!!

Our cat Max has a morning routine.  He goes into the kitchen and stands by the counter where these chicken treats are kept, and stares up at it until one of us gives him some.  Then he dances around while he devours the morsels.  If we don't come into the kitchen quick enough, say on a weekend, he'll come and find us and meow unitl we stand up, walk into the other room with him, and give him some.My wife and I have no idea why this is so addictive.  It has no particular smell, no special ingredients that we can figure.  My wife even tasted one of them, and found it to be very bland.But the kitsers LOVE it!  Dunno why, but we keep it handy.  And by the way, other flavors don't seem to have the same addictive appeal.  Only the chicken.We have a lot of fun giving them to our cat, and you probably will too.
All of our cats love them!!!!! Some times they chew through the container to get to the treats.

column4: Valerie J. Wood "Author and Sports Journalist"
column9: This is Kitty Crack...the cats LOVE this stuff...
column10: I was skeptical when a friend raved about this treat for our cats, but she was absolutely right!! They love all the flavors--we mostly use chicken, salmon & cod. Great enticement to crumble over their canned food when they think you're giving them inferior food not worthy of their little palates (even when you're feeding the good stuff!). If I could rate this stuff 10 Stars on behalf of my Abyssinians, I would do so!!! They think this stuff is manna from the heavens.

I have not yet met a cat (or dog) who didn't love these treats, unless they had a cold (they seem to be almost odorless, and most cats need to smell what they eat). We can generally get our cats to do anything/go anywhere if we shake the jar.Sorry, Amazon, but your price is high. I buy 3-6 jars at a time from With six cats (never again), we go through too many jars to pay retail.

I don't normally bother to write reviews, but I had to put in a plug for these.  We adopted a mother cat and two 5 week old kittens a few weeks ago.  The mom had been a stray and is really skinny, so we wanted to get her to eat something extra.  We went to a cat show and one of the participants was feeding these to her cat as a treat.  She said all cats love them so I ordered a jar.  The mom and the kittens all love them.  The only problem is that we keep them in the refrigerator and every time we open the door the mom cat comes running hoping for one and the kittens soon follow if they are awake.

I first learned about this product a year ago, and I've been giving it to my cats ever since. They get it once a day as a treat, and they love it. If there is a flavor of food that they may not be too crazy about, and I have nothing better to give them at a moment, then this will do the trick. I sprinkle it on top and they will eat it all no matter what. Also, when I clip their nails they get it for putting up with it, as well as if there is some special occassion. In overall, this is the best treat that I've ran accross, safe, apparently tasty, and one box can last me over a month, for two cats. I wish I could find it in local pet food stores.

This is the first treat I have found that my cat with "discerning taste" (aka "finicky") will eat! My other cat and my dog absolutely love them too (but they aren't as hard to please). I am thrilled to find a treat Snows is excited about eating. Only wish they cost a bit less....A note for older pets or pets who can't chew hard treats - the Halo freeze dried chicken is very light and soft, so if you are having a hard time finding a good treat, I recommend giving these a try.

I had not been buying treats at the store for my cat because the ingredients lists are full of things that are bad for her.  For Christmas she got some freeze dried salmon treats and she liked them but then she broke out like she always does when she has seafood.  So I came to Amazon to find a similar treat that was not made of fish.  These chicken treats are just right.  I do have to break most of them in half for her, otherwise it seems she can't get a hold on them.  But they are easy to break, airy and light, not dense and hard.  It's nice to have treats in the cupboard for her again, the giving of a treat now and then is highly pleasurable.  Update - I can not open "the" cupboard door or even a Gladware container now without Miss Kiki rushing into the kitchen hoping for some of these treats.  The only downside to them is the cost.  Maybe Amazon will add them to the Subscribe and Save program, that would help.

I bought Halo because I was looking for a healthy way to help me transition my 3 cats from dry food to canned.My cats were kibble addicts, which the vet said was bad for them, and I wasn't having much luck trying to entice them to switch to canned food.I bought Halo chicken and I crumbled some over the canned food and my cats started gobbling it up.It is a little pricey but I like that it is purely dehydrated chicken with no additives.

column9: Cats go crazy over this stuff
column10: This treat is the cat wonder treat.  Cats love it.  We've been able to teach our cats (limited) tricks using these treats as rewards.  They will do almost anything for them.One of our cats is, sadly, dying from heart and kidney failure.  Her appetite is very poor.  These treats are some of the only things she will eat.  You can break them up and sprinkle them on less expensive food to stretch out their use.

Halo Liv-A-Littles® White Meat Chicken Protein Treats, 2.2 oz.These are the only treats my two cats really like, and one cat is crazy about them.  I have tried giving them many other less expensive treats, to no avail.  Following the truism "Dogs have masters; cats have slaves" I buy Chicken Liv-A-Littles for them as often as I can.
These treats are awesome!!! My cats know where the treats are throughout the house and do not hesitate to sit beside them until they are served! Great tool for training too.

This potent, endlessly pleasing box of feline ambrosia is the closest thing to opium I could imagine rewarding my cats with, without travelling over to the Middle East to get the real deal. Be warned: your kitty will take to this treat like the most ravenous furry addict you have ever seen, never missing an opportunity to spy on you as you open the refrigerator to once in a while (when you're not spending inordinate amounts of time with your cat) get sustenance for yourself. If you've never wondered what it is like to marvel at a cat trying to open a refrigerator door, don't buy this stuff. Don't even think of returning to simple store-bought crunchy treats after this stuff. Your cat will look at you like you are trying to replace sushi with a gold fish cracker! "C'mon, human, give me the goods; give me the white lines, I mean CRUMBS!"If you drop a little piece on the floor, your animals will race to lap it up and transport themselves into "Blissful." It is the ultimate reward with very few negative side effects as far as I can tell (other than unbridled, but functional addiction!)This stuff is a magical, mysterious little concoction that puts an instant smile on your feline and makes her your friend for life. It will slowly start wrecking your monthly budget, of course, but you will find justification after justification for purchasing it ad infinitum.I believe that William S. Burroughs, in the seminal novel Naked Lunch, spoke of the "algebra of need." As soon as your fluffy little angel hits this chicken-laced pleasure pipe, she'll be hooked for life!
the treats were simply fantastic, Fur & LuLu have just about eaten them all up.  They need some more, they have only one left, down to using the powder.  Thank you, much.

column9: Really, really small container of dog treats
column10: My dog is ho-hum about these treats.  Don't be fooled by the picture - the package is very small and the treats themselves look like and have the consistency of styrafoam packaging peanuts.  I love Halo's other dog treats, especially the little baked snacks.  For $9.95, I really don't feel this is a good value at all.  Disappointed.

column9: My cats go nuts for these treats
column10: My cats are giving this one an all-paws-up, quite literally. The Liv-a-Littles freeze-dried chicken pieces are the only treats that they will stand on their back legs for and beg. One of my cats thinks it's not really worth THAT much attention and begs in a bit more restrained fashion, but the others positively go nuts for this. Even my most picky and skittish treat-refusing kitty will take these eagerly and come back for more and doesn't even mind getting petted if there's a piece of freeze-dried chicken to have in return. That makes rattling this box of treats the best tool to "call" them when the times comes to go to the vet etc.One word of caution though: These are very rich and essentially concentrated dehydrated protein (80%). They really are meant to be an occasional treat only. I have to be careful to feed just a few pieces at a time and usually just give my cats 2-3 small pieces each and then put the box safely away again. If I offer more, they will eagerly overeat and at least one of my cats will eventually throw it all up again once it rehydrates in his stomach. Also, if you keep the box in an accessible place, they may try to break into it.
Pretty expensive, given how quickly my pets go through these, but they freakin LOVE them!!  So it's worth it once in a while.

I never write reviews, but had to on this product. I bought every cat treat ever made and my cats wouldn't touch them. Pretty much gave up, but then tried this one. They can't get enough of this treat. They go crazy for it and love it. Thank you Halo!

My cat and dogs LOVE these, in a sort of sick drug addicted way.  They are pricey, and you have to store them in the fridge, but my pets seem to think they are wonderful.  If you are trying to train a pet to do something, these would work very well because my non-food driven pets would do probably just about anything for these things.  I don't buy them often because they are expensive for such a little container, but they are nice for Christmas or some special time.

I buy these on a regular basis for my 22 year old cat. He loves them. They are kind of expensive, but he is worth it. And he does not get them all the time, but when we go to bed. My dogs love them as well, but they don't get them as often. They are freeze dried chicken (I have tried the other ones:beef, liver: cod, with less good results). Every once in awhile one of the treats is a bit hard, and those I give to the dogs. Some containers have more hard treats than others (about every fourth in some), but most are pretty good. I have also tried other brands and they are not as well liked by my cat as Halo. When the container gets low, I sometimes sprinkle the crumbs on his food. He loves it.I bought them from this seller because I was running low. I typically buy them at Whole Foods Market in Texas, but have been out of state a bit and needed some. I tried this seller and they were very quick and the treats were about the same price at the ones at WFM. My cat is happy. When he is happy, I am happy.
My cat deemed these treats fit for hockey games only.  He wouldn't eat them, but had no problems shooting them under my couch.

Yes, these are expensive cat treats but Amazon is the best value and I think they're worth it.  My cat has had some digestive issues and these treats are very high quality.  I did buy the salmon and beef varieties also but these are the only ones she eats.  We will keep buying as they do last quite awhile.
Cats go crazy for Halo chicken treats. They act like it's kitten crack. All of mine love it.Cheaper to buy from Amazon than anywhere else.

Man, my cat loves these treats. As soon as he gets eats a piece, he looks around frantically for another.I've tried out these treats on three other cats. One didn't know it was food, but the other two went frantic over the treats also.One note though, this is the first time I've used them and just now, probably 3 weeks after I've opened the package, I saw the "Must refrigerate after opening". I feel bad giving my cat what might have become spoiled treats, but he never cared. I threw out what little I had left and am buying more.
My cats LOVE these and they can never get enough of them.  We love them because it's natural and high protein so better for a carnivore diet.
My dog was always so finicky with his food until I started sprinkling it with Liv-A-Littles.  It is a lifesaver!

column9: Cat loves it, but it is fragile for shipping
column10: My cat flipped out the first time I fed him the treat.  He acted like it was miracle from the heavens and was so excited.  They seem to be good quality and tasty.  The only issue is the fact that it is freeze dried means it doesn't ship well.  There are a few big pieces but a lot of the pieces have been smashed to dust.  I am not sure if there is a way around this, but it is sad to throw away the dust at the bottom which I am sure is equal to a few treats.

column9: A treat you can feel good about
column10: My cat absolutely loves these treats.  Knowing that it comes from Halo and that it is freeze dried whole chicken breasts, I can give it without worrying about my cat's health being jeopardized.  I cannot praise these enough.  Thanks Halo!

I've been feeding Halo freeze dried chicken treats since 2002. I won't give them anything else because these are simply the best. All I have to do is call out "treat" and they all come running because they know they will get these. This packaging is new but I like the new package because it no longer takes up as much space as the cartons did and also that I can squeeze all the air out. The treat itself is still the same as it's always been and I've never had an issue with quality control.

column9: My cat would walk over hot coals for these!
column10: My cat, Gigi, would walk over hot coals to get to "liv-a-littles".  She loves her other treats....but these are a special thing.  Although she is 10 years old, she does amazing tricks for liv-a-littles.  (She even asks for them by name!  In cat speak...."mmr-a-mmmrr".  She now does about 6 tricks, including jumping through hoops, rolling over coming back to a sit, blah blah blah....video to come on youtube soon.  Search for "Gigi" .  In the meantime...get your cat's these treats!  My cat goes INSANE for them!!!  Worth every penny!  I used to buy them at Petco, but they stopped carrying them.  Amazon has a great price.  Trust me.  If you want a bond with your cat (tricks or no tricks)...get them these liv-a-littles.  You will be amazed!  And they will be soooooooo happy!!!!  (Plus, they are all protein and incredibly healthy!)
All three of my cats love this chicken treat, and one thinks it is the very best thing in the whole world!

Bought these treats for my diabetic cat, as he can't have any treats with "stuff" added to them. These are completly natural and high in protein. They do have sodium added however, so I use them sparingly. My cat inhales them!!! The chunks are a little too big for a cat's mouth, but very easy to break into smaller pieces. Overall, great natural treat.

These treats are great! Both my dog and cat love them. When they hear my shake the container they both come running. It's the only time they will willingly sit next to each other and not fight. I'm very happy to have a treat I can feed both my cat and dog. Totally worth buying even though the price is high for the amount of treats you get in each container.
My cats absolutely love these freeze dried chicken treats.  They come out of the woodwork as soon as they hear me open the jar.  Highly recommend them!Melissa[...]
Greatest cat treats on the planet!! They'll do anything for them! And they're all natural and healthy! Amazing!

My cat is totally addicted to this product.  He LOVES them.  I wish I could buy them locally, but for now it looks like I will have to keep finding good vendors like this one and get them online.  Because trust me, he can't live without them!! :)

Who'd have thought plain freeze-dried chicken would be so irresistible to cats? I also call this stuff 'Kitty Krack' - all my six cats love it.The healthful part is also a very big concern for me since one of my cats is diabetic. Halo's is one of the very few treats around that's low carb enough that I can give them as a reward for him cooperating with blood testing. It works great. The diabetic guy heads right to his testing spot on the sofa as soon as I get the jar of Liv-a-Littles out of the fridge and give it a shake. The other kitties follow us and wait for their share of the treat action.It's not cheap, but I give them each a small chunk and a little extra for the one getting blood-tested, and a jar usually lasts for five days or so. Well worth it.

column9: HER FAVORITE HIGH QUALITY TREAT!! AND SHE'S TRIED THEM ALL
column10: Wow this stuff is A-M-A-Z-I-N-G...my dog is on the ground trying to find CRUMBS of this stuff from our last training session. I know its a HIGH HIGH PRICE compared to other traditional items for what seems like a small canister of it, but really its worth it. Its healthy. And really two regular sized chunks of this (maybe theres 30 chunks in the jar), anyways just a few chunks broken up are perfect for a training session for a puppy. One chunk is about an inch to an inch and a half and I break it up between 3 and 4 pieces...today is the first day she's tried it. It's cheaper to get it in the store (petco) if you're getting just one jar (due to the shipping you will have to pay)...however if you and your dog like the stuff it's worth spending a hundred on the larger quantity, and then breaking it down you're only paying $8.00 a jar (and thats including shipping) when you order up. ALL I CAN SAY IS WOW WOW WOW... and after she stopped looking for crumbs, she did a little cute wimper wanting more, and then came over to me a few minutes later (As I was typing this review) and came over to do some more 'playing'...hehe I petted her and left her alone for a bit now she's chewing on a rib bone from last night. Anyways this stuff is amazing!! You should try it...Sandra and Lilly [the dog =]

My little Yorkie would not eat her dry food but just sprinkle some of these crushed chicken treats on the food and she goobles everything up...thank you so much for a great product. The Halo dry food is the best size for little dogs too.

This is an outstanding product.I have 2 cats, and I am very conscious about what I feed them. They are like my children, and I only want to feed them the best. I heard about Ellen DeGeneres' company, Halo, and their products for pets. I respect Ellen and her deep love of animals. The treats are all natural, just freeze dried pure white chicken meat. I bought them, and gave each of my cats a small piece, and WOW, you would have thought it was catnip. They both started purring and rubbing up against me for more.Now, it is a nightly treat. At around 9:30, they both let me know they want their chicken, and I feel happy knowing I'm giving them something safe, and healthy.I will admit that they are expensive. It is not a very big jar, but I break apart the large pieces, and give them each 2 small treat size pieces a night, so the jar lasts a long time. Once you open them, they do have to be stored in the refidge. The only problem that I have is that everytime I open my refidge, one of my cats tries to con me into giving her an extra treat. This rarely happens, but you have to be careful not to shut the door on a tail.I have recommended this product to several friends, all of whom have had the same result with their cats.*****
My cat's love this product but only the chicken breast one. I highly recommend this protein treat. It is made for cats or smaller dogs. I do have one bengal and one savannah cat.

column9: Liv-a-Littles are a sure hit with my cat
column10: I've been buying the freeze dried chicken treats for my cat for years.  She loves it!

I have had cats for years but, honestly, I have never seen a response like this with any treat!  These are basically freeze dried chicken breast chunks, space food for cats. So expensive but so very delicious ...

If you expect to ever open the freezer in our house without being surrounded by five sharks, er, cats, you have another think coming. The freezer is where we keep these treats and their dry food (to kill storage mites, which will infest even airtight containers at room temperature or the fridge. The freezer will kill them), and any time the door is opened I am swarmed by kitties you'd think haven't eaten in a week. T turns into "Godzilla Cat," an 11-pound sleek black DSH with round, golden eyes who loses his mind at the mere mention of these treats. Noisily demanding satisfaction, it is a task to distribute the Liv-A-Littles to the maddening crowd with any degree of fairness. They are also extremely useful to use as a reward when administering medicine. I pretty much have no problem giving any medication that I've previously tried (and failed) with Pill Pockets. Happy cats = happy people  >^..^<
These treats are great for cats, I call it Kitty Crack......great product, great price, fast delivery.
my dog liked these but you get very little amount of treats for the cost. my only other complaint is that they do break up and can be very powdery in the jar.

My cats LUV these treats! So much so that, when I open the fridge, they all come running - Every time! I do recommend, however, that you search for the best/lowest price for them. Several places sell them for much more than Amazon does.

Halo makes great products, my cats love them.  They especially love the Liv-a-Littles White Meat Chicken Protein Treats.  The only issue I have is that lately they seem to contain more pieces that are so hard I can't even break them apart.  Obviously, if I can't break them, my 6 month old kittens don't stand a chance.  I keep buying them because they are superior to everything else on the market (in my opinion), but given the cost, it does get a bit pricey.

I can throw away my clocks because at exactly 12 noon every day my cats tell me the time.  They start meowing and weaving around my legs for their Chicken Halo treat.  They have never responded to any treat before as they do to Halo.  And I know they aren't getting fillers and other "stuff" that isn't good for them.  Good product!

My cats go nuts for these treats.  They are soft enough to break into smaller pieces for piggy kitties that don't chew.  They would also be good for a cat (or dog) who is sick and not doing so well eating.  You could crumble them up on top of some food, or maybe coax them into eating a few plain.  They are basically pure protein, which is fantastic since most house cats tend to be a bit portly, my two included. And as we all know, protein is one of the main nutrients, especially for cats.  These are my cats second fav, but it's a very close race.  I've got my friends' cats all hooked too!  Even the super finicky ones!
Our cat LOVES these things.  The best treat ever.  And a very good price.

column9: My cats go crazy for this!
column10: My two cats have been receiving these 'chicken treats' for over eight years and STILL beg for them every night before bed!  It's really great to see them so excited about this healthy snack.
This company has excellent products, good communication and ships promptly. What more could you ask?

I hope you never discontinue these! They are like gold to me! I crumble these up on top of my cats raw meat to get them to eat it. They LOVE LOVE LOVE these chicken treats! I like them b/c they are 100% real natural freeze dried chicken with no by products or chemicals or additives! Just pure protein which is what cats are designed to eat! Please do not discontinue these! Me and my cats would be crushed!!
Halo Freeze dried chicken is my cat's favorite thing to eat hands down..It only lasts about a week in my house.

column9: "Give me my "chickie bites" says my Japanese Chin!
column10: I would never have guessed that the liv-a-littles chicken treats would make such a hit with my 2 yr. old Japanese Chin.....All I have to do is say "chickie bites" and he comes running.  I give them to him every evenig as a "treat" and I am so glad that I found the product.  I ordered them the first time as a "trial" but now wouldn't dare be without them. I feel that they are much better for my dog than the "store bought" biscuits that he wasn't crazy about.
My cats go crazy for these chicken treats. The fact that they are just pure chicken is great - no chemicals or additives. I've never met a cat that didn't love these!

If you're looking for a yummy treat for your cat, try these.  After trying both the chicken and salmon flavors, my cats greatly preferred the chicken.  In fact, they love them.  These treats are 100% white-meat chicken, so you'll be giving your cat a truly healthy treat instead of one that's loaded with carbs and fat.  I will definitely buy these again.

My cat is not what I'd consider a treat cat.  You cannot bribe her with food and she's rather picky.  So when my friends gave my cat these chicken treats for Christmas, I was a bit skeptical.To my surprise and utter disbelief, she goes crazy for these treats! I ordered them online and had to wait four-weeks since they were on backorder.  Maybe all kitties are liking this treat!The backorder issue is my reason for four stars...Otherwise, I'd give it five stars.  In my panic to find more treats in the interim, I found that Whole Foods carries it for ~$10/container.

This is a fabulous treat with no nasty carbohydrates or preservatives.  My cats absolutely love them and have eaten them since kittenhood.  We use Halo as a reward at medication time, and to tempt cats who are feeling under the weather.  A little "chicken dust" on their food, and the appetite is back.  For ill or elderly cats, this product is a must-have.  I do wish the chicken was organic, and I would be willing to pay a little more for that benefit.  Yes, these are expensive, but a little goes a long way.  We just don't feed the regular grocery store junk any more.

column9: Even Morris would go for this!!
column10: This is an amazing cat treat -- and all natural.  It works on the pickiest eaters.  You can also moisten it with water to tempt a sick kitty.
My cats would kill for this!!  Can't live without it.  GREAT price!!!

Both cats love Halo's Liv a Littles Freeze Dried Chicken Breast. My youngest cat wanted nothing to do with these treats for a long time then one day changed her mind and now is the biggest fan in the house. I haven't tried the Beef or Salmon. Chicken is king around here.I reserve these for once in a while treats or to entice eating by sprinkling it atop newly introduced wet/raw foods. The Halo website says the chicken is made in a marinade broth of sodium phosphate, salt, and carrageenan before it's freeze dried. I trust Halo's practices but do wonder how much salt is used in the process and wish the amount was on the label.I also have a tube of Thrive Freeze Dried Chicken from a UK company that has been very popular at holistic pet retailers lately. Their claim is that it's 100% freeze dried chicken and nothing else. I can't garner any more information than that from the tube or the manufacturer website, but my cats go nuts for Thrive just like they do Halo.These are expensive little treats but the cool thing about them is they can be served as solid chunks or broken into dust like particles, or wet by adding a little water. I have to think that with so many cats out there who have lost teeth, this is probably a superior treat to have once in awhile.

A brief glimpse into the world of Cinnamon, the Chihuahua Princess of Midtown Manhattan:"My Daddy not only does all the typing for me (I'm preserving a manicure, naturally), he also caters to my desire for home-cooked meals. I know, I know: whatever complaints may thus ensue about me being spoiled and finicky are completely his fault, but Daddy knew that when he decided that both nutritionally and economically (not to mention emotionally) this worked out best for both of us.That said, I've lately become a bit fussy -- even when it comes to really, really good meals like freshly cooked pork or beef or chicken with the vegetables that Dad insists I eat. You might understand if I were to turn my cute little nose up at, say, Alpo... or even Grade-B ground beef; but I'm summarily rejecting the good stuff that my old man tastes and actually enjoys as he's preparing it for me. I think it's a phase, because I feel just fine, but I'm trying this whole new "I am not amused or pleased" routine to see how far it'll get me with him. I'm holding out for a mink hoodie and a pony to ride in the country this summer."OK, now on to Dad's own story:"I saw these on Amazon as I was searching for the desiccated beef treats my girl likes. These were about a third the price and one of the few brands in the price range that was actually just MEAT and not some sort of dehydrated hodgepodge of gunk.I figured I'd give them a shot. I opened the container when they were delivered, and tasted it myself after reading the ingredients (which are "chicken" and "marinade", basically). Dried chicken. What's not to approve?The princess was given a piece. She turned her nose up at it and returned to her faux-nap.But as soon as I'd turned my back I heard the chewing and within moments she was at my feet looking for more.I was still waiting for her to eat the plate of delicious food I'd slaved over an hour or so earlier, so I wasn't giving in. Test complete. Treats would be saved for a time when they were actually deserved.And then I read the label as I pretended not to notice her neediness. "...as a tasty incentive at mealtime."Hmm...I took out another chunk, crumbled it on her food, and watched as she sniffed, licked, walked away, reconsidered, and returned to the scene of what she HAD considered my culinary crime.Incentive indeed. Her plate was clean about two minutes later. She was fed, I was vilified, and these chicken treats elevated in both our opinions to the level of 'Heroic.'"From both Cinnamon and Daddy;"Thank You, Halo Liv-A-Littles."

I have returned this! There are some hard pieces that will not allow me to crumble to put on pets' food so they had to be thrown out. What are they? Wood? Not acceptable! Returned and will not order again!!

column9: May have made our kitty sick
column10: We try to feed our cats wholesome healthy foods, so we thought these treats would be a great alternative to the kitty junk food they had been eating.Our 12yo girl cat sniffed these and turned up her nose. She is superrrrr picky, and lots of times will not consume something the first time you offer it to her, so no biggie.Our 2yo boy cat, as other reviewers described, went nuts. We gave him a few small bits (maybe the equivalent of 3 regular cat treats in size) and were delighted that we had found a treat he enjoys (he does not like the treats typically found in supermarkets and such).About 24 hours later around 11pm we noticed he was straining to urinate, unproductive, and jumped in and out of the boxes about 15 times in 30minutes, growling and hissing at the box, and hissing at us when we tried to pet him or pick him up. He urinated on our bed, on his bed, on his pillow, and on the couch. This cat never urinated outside the box before (except during car rides in his carrier) and had never hissed before (even at his evil, manipulative, bullying "older sister" cat that loves him dearly).We called the vet, who squeezes him in first thing in the morning, he had a uti. Several hundred dollars in medicine, overnight hospitalization, and aftercare, he is better.The only thing we changed in his diet (or, for that matter, in his life) in the two months leading up to his illness were these treats. After the vet told us UTIs were usually related to diet, we threw these out. We will probably never know exactly what caused his illness, but we have a sneaking suspicion...

column9: This is not a review of the product, rather just a thought on Venezuela's situation
column10: I read the product specifications and I couldn't help but feel a pang of pain at reading "Product from Colombia". Harina PAN is originally a product from Venezuela, and it has a lot of history. As a matter of fact, it was the first corn flour industrially produced, and at the time it was akin to the effect Henry Ford had when he created his production line. Before Harina PAN, women all over the country had to produce the dough for arepas single handedly. The creation of Harina Pan was really revolutionary and allowed for the arepa to survive the changing times. And now, thanks to that person in power whose name we all know, I see that product, which is almost synonymous with Venezuelan identity, identified as "from Colombia". It really does hurt.So, if you are reading this you are probably a Venezuelan expatriate or someone interested in Venezuelan cuisine. This product is, as a matter of fact, fabulous. It's so great even though it's hard to find in Venezuela (again, thanks to our economy), people bend over themselves to buy it when it finally arrives at any given supermarket. Even people who work with the government do this. I recommend it very highly. Cheers.
