I had an opportunity to try them, in addition to the flavors in this sample box and they are exploding with flavor! Like nothing else out there.So if you're looking for a delicious new candy with natural ingredients, I highly recommend these newDavid's Signature Beyond Gourmet Jelly Beans. I am not only thrilled to have been able to try these out for reviewing purposes, but I plan to place several orders for more in the very new future!

column9: Delectable jelly beans with 100% natural flavors & colors.
column10: This new line of jelly beans by David Klein, the creator of Jelly Belly jelly beans, is made with 100% natural flavors and colors. That will be great news to those with allergies to food colorants as well as to those who prefer to keep the amount of chemicals in their snacks to a minimum.  In addition to this "taste of everything" sampler, the beans are sold in several different mixes (like the 5-alarm spicy Man Mix or the fruity Soda Fountain Mix) as well as individually, so you can really create the bean collection that works for you!This sampler includes 16 flavors. Among people I know who have tasted these beans, there is a great divide in likes and dislikes--some that I hated, others loved and vice versa. Every person is different, so just because I hated something doesn't mean you will.  That said, following are my personal impressions on each flavor in the sampler:*****My Favorites--Could eat them again and again (and already have!).Grape: Tastes like Nehi grape soda from my childhood, sweet but delicious.Strawberry:  Bright, sweet flavor with a nice finish. Reminiscent of strawberry preserves.Root Beer:  Sweet and tangy, addictive and satisfying. Maybe my #1 fave.Pomegranate: Sweet and tangy, but in a totally different way than root beer. Yum!Cranberry:  Sweet and tart; like dried cranberries vs. fresh.Orange Punch: DELISH! Very sweet, bright flavor. Can almost taste the carbonation as if it was orange soda vs. orange punch.****My Liked-but-not-Loved List--Enjoyed, but don't crave them like the faves.Coconut: Very distinct, spot-on flavor, but pretty strong. Best in combination with other beans. Not something I could eat again and again by itself.Vanilla bean: Same reaction as coconut. Good in combo, not in volume alone.Green apple: Could have been more tart.  Tasty but a bit bland.Peach: Quite intense. More like peach nectar than a fresh peach. Didn't love the finish.Lemon: Expected it to be a fave, but it wasn't. It has the tartness of a fresh lemon, but would have preferred a sweeter taste, as was done with grape and orange (like lemonade).Black Cherry: Also expected to be a fave, but wasn't. I am liking it more and more as I try it, though. Better alone than combined with other flavors and better with 2 or more of the same flavor at once. Wish it had a deeper flavor.Blueberry:  I liked the inside but didn't care as much for the shell. Tastes more like a blueberry muffin than a fresh blueberry, but that is a good thing in my eyes. :)Ginger:  Powerful! Very spicy, like biting into fresh ginger. The flavor is beautifully reproduced, but was a bit overpowering for me to want to eat many.**Least Favorites--Flavors I have no desire to eat again.Bacon: Man, I WANTED to love this! I love bacon! But I didn't love this bean.  I didn't even like it.  It tastes more like Liquid Smoke than bacon. Yuck. Don't suggest you mix it with any of the sweeter beans.Himalayan sea salt:  Strange/alien on the tongue at first, but kind of interesting while chewing. This one was originally on my Liked-but-don't-Love List, but then I realized I had no desire to ever eat another one. Also tastes worse when eaten with other beans, esp. the sweeter ones.I wish there had been more mixable flavors in the sampler, like back in the days when Jelly Bellies were new and my colleagues and I were always thinking of new pairings to make delicious flavor combinations.  I did some combining in this sampler.  Can't say there was anything that really stood out as a great combo, though I would say if you don't like super sweet, you may want to eat the super sweet ones with something with a little tartness like the cranberry, pomegranate or lemon beans.Finally, the packaging was a little flimsy and my beans were intermingled when they arrived.  This was a bummer, since there are flavors that share a color and are hard to differentiate (like lemon and ginger, and the black cherry, cranberry and pomegranate) so if there was a flavor I disliked, it was hard to avoid it until I learned to distinguish the slight color or textural variations.  Some of the confusion could have been avoided by not putting like-colored beans in the "cubby" right next to one another, as lemon and ginger.All in all, a delectable bean with some very interesting flavors and natural coloringflavoring!

I have an almost insatiable sweet tooth.  Left to my own devices, I could snack myself into a coffin.  This Gourmet Jelly Bean sampler is just right for a guy like me who struggles with impulse control.The flavors of these jelly beans are so amazing that you really only need a few to feel like you've had a more substantial snack.  The flavors stay with you (in a good way) for a very long time, so you really only need two or three of these jelly beans to satisfy your craving.  And since the calories are pretty low, you won't get into too much trouble if you don't stop at two or three beans.This sampler has turned out to be a fun social activity too.  My family has had a lot of fun trying out different flavors and seeing who likes which ones better.  We've all pretty much agreed that we don't like the Bacon, which is surprising for a family like mine.  My son said that it's worse than his bacon lip balm.  But that's the only clunker in the pack.I seem to be the only one in the family who likes the Ginger.  That's OK.  More Ginger for me.I've also had a lot of fun seeing which flavors pair well with each other.  Vanilla Bean goes great with just about anything.  Himalayan Sea Salt is nice with some of the more sour flavors, like Cranberry--it adds kind of a margarita cocktail flavor.  Lemon and Ginger both pair well with a lot of the flavors.I've also tried some of the flavors that weren't part of this sampler.  The Chipotle and Thai Chile are both out of this world.  I can't believe how delicious they are.  I paired Wasabi with Sea Salt and that was really good.  I even like the Habenero; it's a good flavor without overdoing the pain.I'm very impressed with this sampler.  I typically don't feel like sample packs are a good value for me, because there are always flavors that I don't like as much as other ones, so those go uneaten.  This sampler has really defied the odds:  There has been something for everyone in my family.  Only the bacon is left behind.I was provided this sampler for review.

column9: The Rolls Royce of jelly beans
column10: These are awesome. Lots of flavor and its honestly unlike anything I've ever tasted before. These have truly shattered the mold!!!!! Cranberry is my favorite!!

column9: These jelly beans are meant to be savored
column10: These aren't the kind of jelly beans where you stuff a handful into your mouth.  These are meant to be savored and enjoyed one at a time.  Each has a vibrant, distinctive flavor, the kind you want savor, one at a time.  And this sampler is the perfect way to try a variety of David's Signature Beyond Gourmet Jelly Beans.  It provides a nice variety including bacon, black cherry, blueberry, coconut, cranberry, ginger, grape, green apple, Himalayan sea salt, lemon, orange punch, peach, pomegranite, root beer, strawberry and vanilla bean.  All of them were very good, but my personal favorites were strawberry, lemon, coconut and bacon.  I have to admit that the bacon was a strange flavor for a jelly bean.  Maybe that's why I liked it.  It had sort of a burnt flavor, like bacon when it's crispy.These jelly beans use natural flavors that are quite intense.  One of these small beans fills your whole mouth with flavor.  If you are really adventuresome you could try a pack of David's Signature Beyond Gourmet Jelly Beans Man Mix.  The bacon, ginger and Himilayan Sea salt flavors from this sampler are included, but there is also a chipotle, Thai chili, wasabi and a habanero jelly bean that is three-alarm hot!  If you like unusual flavors you have to give them a try too.From what I understand David Klein created the first gourmet jelly beans some 35 years ago, so he's quite accomplished when it comes to unique flavors that are fun to taste.  Wouldn't this be the perfect thing for the Easter Bunny to leave for the adult jelly bean fans on your list?The manufacturer supplied me with this sampler for review.

column9: The Best Jelly Beans On The Planet
column10: These jelly beans are from the creator of the Jelly Belly jelly beans. The difference is in the quality. Dave's Signature jelly beans are made with all natural flavors and ingredients. These beans redefine the jelly bean. The flavors are like nothing you have ever tasted. The Orange Punch is simply delicious. The coconut is decadent. The Habanero, well, have a glass of water handy. My Son's classmates LOVED the Habanero jelly beans. Thai Chili, Wasabi are simply amazing. Yes, there is a Chipotle bean as well. The blueberry tastes like biting into a blueberry pie. You savor each bite of these amazing beans. My Son loves the Sea Salt bean. My Husband LOVES the bacon flavored. Not only are the beans the best you will ever taste, the creator is a kind and amazing person in his own right. David Klein is a one of a kind soul. He is as kind as he is creative. Once you try them I guarantee you will want no other bean again. I am sitting here munching on his Chipotle bean creation as I type this review and am enjoying every one of them. Oh, and don't forget to combine them to make even more amazing flavor bursts to enjoy. I will not buy any other jelly beans because they just do not compete with David's Creations! I highly recommend you give them a try. You will NOT be sorry.

David's Jelly Bean sampler has a little something for everybody. From root beer to Himalayan sea salt, the flavor range is well represented.These are really nice jelly beans. Some of the flavors are just slightly intense and others are subtle. The great news, they all taste like the genuine article without a strong chemical flavor.All the jelly beans are tender and have a light outer coating. The outer coating is much thinner than other jelly beans, so the full flavor jumps out a lot faster in the mouth. These are fun jelly beans; they aren't perfectly formed and have a more artisanal look to them. The flavor guide on the box top threw me for a loop, in my brain, it is the mirror image of the compartment arrangement. Bacon is at the top of the picture, but the bacon compartment is closest to the top hinge, or bottom of the picture.Overall, I like this box a lot. The flavor mix is unusual. My favorite by far is root beer - it tastes just like eating a glass of root beer. My least favorite by far is bacon. No, that just flat out doesn't work. I love bacon and maple syrup (so sweet and bacon is not a problem to me), but this is just way too weird. My 15 year old son actually spit it out, he disliked it so much. Frankly, that is the only loser in the box. The big love flavors with three of us trying out the box were pomegranate, root beer, orange punch, green apple, and strawberry. The middle pack was cranberry, lemon, ginger (spicy flavor, strong fresh ginger flavor, like a really good ginger beer, not Canada Dry ginger ale - too strong to eat a lot of them), black cherry (not enough cherry flavor), blueberry, grape, strawberry, and peach. Bringing up the rear, Himalayan sea salt (just a little too weird, not bad, but weird), vanilla bean (a little too sweet and the vanilla wasn't sharp enough), and coconut (maybe it seemed a little too much like Coppertone sun block).These are an indulgence. They are superior to other brands of jelly beans. The flavors are a lot cleaner, the beans softer, and the after taste is more pleasant.The great news about these beans, the ingredient line, not 100% all natural, but super minimal chemicals. No high fructose corn syrup.Here's the ingredient line:sugar, corn syrup, cornstarch, dextrose, fruit concentrates (apple, lemon, tangerine, peach, strawberry, blueberry, raspberry, black cherry, grape, cherry, pomegranate), citric acid, pectin, color added (fruit and vegetable extracts, annatto, turmeric, saffron, caramel color, titanium dioxide), natural flavors, sodium citrate, ascorbic acid, bees wax, carnauba wax, confectioners glaze. The last three ingredients are great to note - most beans use thick carnauba wax for the outer coating. David's chose to use three ingredients that make the shell thinner and easier to eat.The manufacturer supplied me with a box for review.

column9: Great Selection of High End Jelly Beans - Highly Recommended
column10: This David's Signature "Beyond Gourmet Jelly Beans Flavor Sampler" contains an eclectic mix of delicious jelly beans. These flavors are from David Klein, the creator of the famous "Jelly Belly" jelly beans, so I was thrilled to be offered this sampler to review since my family loves jelly beans. Here are my opinions of the included flavors, in order of my favorites:* Coconut - Very strong natural coconut flavor, my favorite one* Vanilla Bean - Very good tasting, natural vanilla flavor* Pomegranate - Totally nailed this one! So good!* Ginger - Crisp natural ginger flavor, every bit as good as the fresh ginger candy we get locally* Cranberry - Really very good and natural tasting* Root Beer - Amazing, can almost feel the fizz!* Green Apple - So good! Very natural apple flavor!* Peach - Very good juicy peach flavor* Strawberry - Very good, reminds me of strawberry and cream* Lemon - A little milder than expected, very good "clean" flavor* Black Cherry - Very natural tasting but a tad bit over sweet* Grape - Great grape flavor, not quite as strong as expected* Orange Punch - Good flavor, not overpowering* Blueberry - Good, but somewhat understated* Himalayan Sea Salt - Very odd choice for a jelly bean, but it is a surprisingly enjoyable flavor* Bacon - Does indeed taste like sweet smokey bacon, a fun novelty flavor but not one I'm going to eat all the timeMy list of favorites differs a little in order from other members of my family, as might be expected since everyone has different tastes, but every one of these rates higher than any other manufacturers similar jelly bean flavor we have tried. Combining some of these flavors is also fun with ginger and lemon being my favorite, producing a very clean and refreshing sensation.I also really like that these jelly beans are made with 100% natural flavors and colors, and includes an impressive list of fruit concentrates fairly high up in ingredients list.Highly Recommended!CFH

column9: THE BEST jelly beans in the world!!!!
column10: A few weeks ago, the Lenny and John Show was contacted by an associate of David Klein's asking us if we would have David on as a guest on our show as he was the inventor of the Jelly Belly.  Of course we jumped at the chance simply because, who doesn't love Jelly Bellies?  What we later learned was the incredible story of how David Klein came to invent the Jelly Belly in 1976 and then got forced out only four years later for only a tiny fraction of what the value actually was.  Don't take our word for it, you can see it all in the documentary that was made about him, Candyman: The David Klein Story.That was some background to tell you how we got introduced to this product.  Prior to David appearing on our show, we received 10 packs of David's Signature Beyond Gourmet Jelly Beans in unmarked plastic bags.  They were unmarked so that when we tasted them on the air for the first time David could get a true reaction from us for not just the taste of the jelly beans but also how authentic the flavor was.We interviewed David over a three hour period.  I know that seems like a long time, but it actually flew by - he is a fascinating man with a wealth of knowledge about the candy business and the world in general.  Anyway, periodically, David would pick a number for us to try and we would try a jelly bean from that numbered bag.These beans were amazing.  The flavor was incrediblly strong and the taste was like actually eating the fruit or other food that they were patterned after.  We received no money or any other form of payment from David - our reactions were completely unbiased and honest, even down to the moment when I spit out the habanero flavored bean because it was too hot.  If you would like to listen to the show and hear our unedited reactions, you will get the next best thing to tasting them for yourselves.If you love Jelly Bellies, these will blow you away.  They are a little pricey compared to other jelly beans, but honestly they are a level above all others.  The flavor is so intense you don't find yourself eating them by the handful either.  One bean can be savored and enjoyed which may save your waistline too.  To hear the interview, go to [...]

column9: How real Jelly Beans should taste
column10: I was recently given a box of these gourmet jelly beans by a friend, and don't think I'll be eating any other jelly beans for quite some time. I love the fact that they're created by David Klein, the inventor of Jelly Belly (which David is no longer affiliated with).A few of my favorites:Coconut: Just the right amount of creaminess and tropical flavor. David needs to make a Pina Colada based off of this!Blueberry: All the berries in this box were wonderful. The blueberry is particularly tasty.Cranberry: Love the tartness. Balances out all the sweetness.Peach: I'm just a sucker for peaches.Pomegranate: Made with real pomegranate juice! Really does taste like it - not overly tart, just right.Root Beer: I felt like I needed to put a few ice cubes in my mouth to make it like a real root beer. Classic.Looking forward to seeing what David does with these flavors - I know there's a lot more from where these came from!

If you are looking for a treat with a high flavor-to-calorie ratio, the concentrated, natural flavors of David's Signature Beyond Gourmet Jelly Beans will get your full attention.  They are noticeably fresher and slightly softer in texture than other tiny jelly beans.I was fortunate to receive a sampler pack that included the sixteen flavors in this sampler plus the four spicy hot ones that are included only in the savory Man Mix.  There are also other mixes available such as Fruit and Soda Fountain.Vanilla bean has visible flecks and the unmistakable flavor of vanilla beans that you would expect from a carriage-trade jelly bean.  I suggest that you try these first to really enjoy the full effect.  They are good with almost any of the fruit flavors but especially with orange punch, strawberry, and coconut.The root beer beans are fantastic.  If you have ever bought the little hard root-beer flavored candies and been disappointed, try these; they taste like a whole bottle of natural root beer in one little bite.  Add half a vanilla bean jelly bean and you have a float.The coconut has a dense, creamy coconut flavor and it's one of my favorites.  It combines well, too.The strawberry ones have a flavor that is so intense, like strawberry preserves, that it is hard to believe it is natural.  Same for the peach ones, which don't really taste like fresh peaches but more like peach jam.  If you like peach Jolly Ranchers or peach Nehi but not that artificial aftertaste, you will really enjoy these.  The green apple ones are also similar to Jolly Ranchers but with a clean flavor that increases as you chew.Grape tastes more like purple grape juice than grapes.  The blueberry is also very concentrated, like dried blueberries.The lemon ones are tart, almost like a little lemon explosion on the tip of your tongue.  The other citrus flavor, orange punch, was a bit of a surprise.  It tastes more like mandarin orange than a juice orange, a very good choice.Pomegranate has become a popular flavor but I haven't had it in candy before.  After tasting these, I have no idea why it is not even more popular.  The cranberry ones are a little milder and less tart than I expected after trying some of the other ones.  Black cherry is also on the subtle side but would you expect to be able to distinguish their black cherry taste from that of tart cherries?  You can.The Himalayan sea salt jelly bean is instantly recognizable because of the distinctive mineral flavor.  I was impressed that they are not unpleasantly salty.  How did they do that?  It must have been difficult to get this one right but I like the results.  These are also good as a palate cleanser after some of the more assertive flavors.The bacon jelly bean reminds me more of cured country ham than bacon, with roughly equal notes of pork, salt, smoke, and sweet.  I don't eat much meat and at first I didn't particularly care for their intensity, similar to ham base, but when I started combining them with half of a spicy bean from the Man Mix, I enjoyed them much more and was very sorry when they were all gone.  They are also good with half of a black cherry jelly bean.The ginger ones have a very explosive flavor much like crystallized ginger but without the chewy fibers.I tried to pick a favorite flavor but kept changing my mind because they are all so good.  The only downside is that after eating these, you will be spoiled for other jelly beans because of the overall quality and concentrated, non-artificial flavors.  You may also decide not to share and experience a little guilt.  They really are that good.I will be excited to try new flavors from David's Signature Beyond Gourmet.  Here are my suggestions:  pineapple, passion fruit, cassis, pear, mango, clove, Earl Grey, lemon verbena, carrot pudding, kumquat, blood orange, and cherry cola.

column9: I really wanted to like these...really.
column10: After watching the documentary (Candyman) I really wanted to like these. I waited until they showed up on Amazon and promptly ordered a box.They shipped quickly, and arrived well packaged. A few of the beans spilled over into other sections, but that was easily remedied.I couldn't wait so I started right away. The box smells like scratch and sniff stickers, or those smelly markers, which honestly surprised me because of their commitment to natural flavorings. Very off putting.Here goes:Texture: I don't know if it's just a personal thing, but the textures are all off. A few are a little chalky, while the rest are way to soft. They stick to your teeth way too much. Somehow they are grainy also. Again, I'm used to the chewy texture of Jelly Bellies...Flavors:The fruity flavors have a weird salt flavor. Almost like energy gel or the Jelly Belly Sport beans. It's a little strange...Bacon: I tried. I couldn't finish it. It tastes like a cup of sugar with a fat piece of bacon in it. Good if you like your bacon drowned in sugar.Black Cherry: It tastes like sugar and not much else. I tried it several times to see if I had gotten a dud, but they don't taste like anything...none of them.Blueberry: It tastes way too salty with some granola overtones and a sour finish...weird, but not so bad.Coconut: If it weren't for the texture this would be awesome. Great coconut flavor.Cranberry: It almost tastes like sour raisins...weird. It has a cranberry juice aftertaste...I really wanted this one to be awesome.Ginger: Awesome. Awesome...very strong ginger flavor.Grape: So salty...almost a little like grape, but it really tastes way too salty with some chemically background flavors. Not good.Green Apple: So bad...it tastes nothing like apple at all. So bad.Himalayan Sea Salt: Really weird, salty, but also off puttingly sweet.Lemon: Tastes like lemon Pledge.Orange Punch: Totally Sunkist. Awesome.Peach: It totally tastes like Peach rings. If you eat it quickly to avoid the chemical smell, this is totally one of the best flavors. Eat it quickly though.Pomegranate: Tastes more like Cherry, but it isn't too bad. Doesn't taste like Pomegranate though.Root Beer: The best flavor. Without a doubt.Strawberry: One of the best. Not bad.Vanilla: Tastes like vanilla bean. Kind of like melted vanilla ice cream.If it weren't for the inconsistent textures, the chemical smell, and the bad fruit flavors these could be good. Which is really a shame since the fruit flavors are usually my favorite jelly bean flavors. Personally, for now, I'm sticking with Jelly Bellies. Dang.

Chipotle, habenaro,  bacon, and sea salt top the list of favorites besides the jelly beans we enjoyed at our party.  Serving this  fun candy was trumped only by the arrival of the Travelocity gnome.

column9: Too Hot For Me - I'm a wimp
column10: OK, I'll admit it, label me a wimp. No, I could not eat one of these beans. I managed to bite into the bean and lick the inside. My brain took over and told me, that is too spicy to eat, don't chew the rest. My wife agreed and could not eat a bean either.My 15 year old son decided to man up and ate one. He said they weren't too spicy (he says that about anything I say is too spicy), but the heat got trapped under his tongue so it hung around for a while. I have to agree with his assessment; the spice flavor is really good. They are hot, but not stupid hot (nothing but heat with no flavor).These are darn good jelly beans. I've tasted the other jelly bean flavors in this new product line; habanero and bacon are the only two I don't care for. All the others have a nice clean flavor in a tender jelly bean.Well if somebody that is going to eat these beans cares about ingredients - these don't have high fructose corn syrup in them. They aren't 100% natural, missing that label with a few minor ingredients. Sugar, corn syrup, starch, and fruit juice are the major ingredients.If I loved habaneros and wasn't such a whim, I'm confident I would love these.

He's reached the point where he can eat cheese and bread right around the pill you are trying to get him to swallow, and the "force him to swallow" method hasn't worked with him for a while.A family member recommended these as something she'd heard works, and it really does!The small size works great for a single small pill (think benadryl tablet or capsule size).  The Medium/Large size will hold two small pills, and would hold a single "medium" sized pill well.  The treat itself is very soft, and easy to mash around a pill that is a little larger than the hole allows for (or oblong, like a capsule).If your dog is on medication long-term, like mine, shop around and look for a good price, because there is quite a range out there.

Unfortunately I couldn't find this variety of popcorn on Newman's Own Web site. Perhaps it's been discontinued; I wouldn't be the least bit surprised.

Please DO NOT BUY THE CANNED FORMULA.  IT CONTAINS BPA!  The BPA is in the inner coating of the metal cans.  According to Similac/Abbott Laboratories, the larger RTF plastic container is BPA Free - just AVOID THE CANS!!!I wanted to pass this information along to other moms/dads.  I am not an activist or someone who believes my child will never come in contact with a dangerous toxin.  But geez, as a society we go out of our way to make sure BPA is not in our baby bottles only to find out the my son is drinking the stuff!If you are like me, I was desperate to find a formula that would not cause my child pain to digest (like my breast milk & other formulas).  Sleep deprived and desperate to get out of the house, I thought the can RTF was a god send.  (Especially b/c my child didn't like the powder.)  I can't believe I have been using this product for 5 months.  SHAME ON SIMILAC!  Words cannot describe how truly angry I am.Every other RTF they sell is in BPA free plastic.  I feel like as parents of children with special dietary needs, we have been prayed on b/c we are desperate & could not use our power of the free market to purchase another BPA free brand.  I am just disgusted.  As a mom, I felt I needed to warn other parents of SIMILAC REPULSIVE AND UNNECESSARY PRACTICE.I wanted to post Similac's website just so you don't think I am some nut.  They conveniently don't list the metal can formula in their list of BPA free products. [...].

Based on the previous review, I explored the website and talked with their customer service to find more information. First, they are working on making it BPA free, but for right now there is some BPA in these cans - according to Abbotts 50 times less than regulated limits, but it is not BPA free. We are keeping these for emergencies but primarily relying on the 32 oz container, since we do not want to take any risks with BPA.

column9: delicious and healthy--when enjoyed in moderation, of course
column10: The packaging label may indicate that both Kirkland Signature and Sunsweet made these "pitted dried plums;" but rest assured that these are the same delicious prunes as the ones you can buy from Sunsweet. (The name is sometimes changed from "prunes" to "dried plums" so that they would sell better!) The main advantage here is the size of the container; you get 50 ounces and that should last you a while longer than smaller sized packages. They are delicious, sweet and tasty; and if I didn't know I have to watch how many I eat to avoid stomach problems, I could eat these all day.If you eat these pitted dried plums routinely to keep "regular," I would suggest that you buy them in this size. They won't go bad unless you open the container and let them sit for months; this won't happen though since you'll have finished eating these well before then.In addition, these contain the same wonderful antioxidants, fiber and potassium as any other brand of dried pitted plums or prunes; and that's a huge plus. However, they do contain a fair amount of sugar; if you're diabetic you might want to check with your doctor or dietician before you eat too many of these.Overall, I highly recommend these dried pitted plums; they are healthy and make a terrific snack. They contain sugar for a relatively quick, short-term energy boost in addition to the health benefits and they are always fresh and tasty.

These chocolates seemed like a REALLY good deal. I love Lindor, but the store near me was out of the assorted kind. I wanted some for my sister's birthday party. I got on Amazon and found these, cheap price and free shipping! Wow! So I ordered some.First, they came, and I opened one, and immediately got suspicious. They looked melted, and they were soft. I had read some reviews that people got melted ones, but I ordered mine in April, a cold april, and the temperatures hadn't been over 55 degrees. It hasn't been hot enough to melt them! I've had chocolate melt on me before, and then harden back up. It looks a little glossy, sometimes white on the surfaces, and is usually denser (not lighter/softer/greasier), but I've never seen or tasted "melted" chocolate like this.Second, they tasted, well, cheap. I still had some of the milk chocolate variety, and I tasted them, bite of one, bite of the other. And there is a big difference. Also, the chocolate in the center of the Amazon one was LOW. Not NEARLY as much as the store bought one.Third, I stuck them in the fridge, thinking that would stiffen them up. I was hoping the off/cheap taste and the softness was from somehow being melted (though even then I had my doubts). They've been in the fridge for two days. I opened one this morning, and they are still as soft and cheap tasting as the one I had before. Also, this one has a poke hole in one side and a "plug" that had fallen out. This plug was big and light colored and soft. It seems obvious that its not the same qulity of chocolate and that the process that poked the hole in the side and "plugged" it was not the regular Lindor method! I compared it to one of the store bought ones, and it looked NOTHING like the storebought ones. It just looks terrible.I am not a chocolate expert, and can't say for sure that this is not because of them being melted, but they look ALTERED to me, and taste CHEAP and OILY - GREASY like they were cut with much cheaper chocolate. I don't know how the packaging and wrappers would be Lindor while the chocolate isn't, but that's how they looked and tasted - different. Can melting change the density, texture and taste of cholocate? Maybe, but, in my experience, not like this.I am beyond suspicious and into nervous. I ATE these, and I don't know what they are! They don't look or taste real! It makes me sick to my stomach to think they might have been altered or cut or faked.I am very disappointed, and am sticking to the more expensive store bought. My sister and her friends are just going to have to deal with a plain old one flavor bowl full.I really hope I'm wrong, but buyer beware. If they look funny, feel soft and have fishy looking poke holes/plugs, think twice. Eat them if you want to, but mine went in the garbage.

In a world where canned chili is usually filled with fat, salt, and preservatives, Amy's chili is a welcome relief to those of us who are trying to eat healthier.  Chili is a favorite in our family but I can't seem to make it very well for some reason. It's just not my forté. However, other commercially-made chilis are so very high in sodium and fat that we just had to go without chili for a while. When we tried this, we weren't sure what to expect.The results were delicious!  It's just the right amount of spicy, you don't miss the salt, and it's bursting with flavor. This chili is even good straight-out-of-the-can so if you live in a hurricane area, this is a must for your hurricane kit. I highly recommend this for chili-lovers who are trying to have a healthier diet.

I find that this is nice and filling and, being an Amy's product, gives me greater peace of mind about quality ingredients.However, let's be honest--this is still a rather bland chili offering. And I don't mean bland in the spicy-level way. I mean bland in the flavor way.YET..it's a very, very good base to customize. You got the nice ingredients, the plentiful beans, the tofu for protein (if you don't mind that). I add tomatoes, peppers, onions, and hot sauce or some sort of salsa, plus onion powder, to give it more flavor and texture. I will add some organic or low-fat shredded Mexican or cheddar on top for fun, too. I find once I tweak it, I really like it for lunch with some brown rice or organic tortillas.It works very nicely in a layer dip with chips, too.I appreciate the lower sodium levels, as I have high BP.I recommend this if you don't mind customizing your canned chili. Or, if you're used to bland canned food, then it could suit you "as is" from the can.Either way, if you're looking for a convenience food that's as wholesome as prepackaged stuff of this sort can be, this is a good bet. Give it a try. Play with it. It might become a staple for you.And if you like canned convenience foods, try Amy's Low-Sodium cream of tomato soup. I find that one very nice--comfort food. (The cream of mushroom is nice if you add more of your own fresh organic mushrooms and some spices--garlic powder, onion powder, a pinch of thyme, black pepper, otherwise it also is rather bland.)Enjoy.Mir
