This kit contains everything except the meat, so it is nice for someone like me who forgets to buy a can of coconut milk or can't find one at the store when I want to make this type of curry.  I substituted sirloin for the beef tenderloin.  I was surprised that the copy on the box read that this curry was used at one time to disguise not so great beef, only to add a very expensive cut of meat to their preparing recipe.  Being that my boyfriend and I have bought 28 oz or so beef tenderloins for two dinner parties in the last three months, we weren't up to blowing another $30 on a meal.  The $8 pound and a half of sirloin worked just as well in this dish, even though it was less meat.I prepared it a bit differently than how they say.  I had a few hours so I cooked the sirloin to medium rare in cubes and then blended the rendang sauce packet into the meat and let that marinate and cool before adding the coconut milk packet about 30 minutes later.  I feel the old method of making curry and then cooking it for a while and then letting it sit, makes a better curry.  I didn't think I could do this with the coconut milk, so I added it a half hour before I thought I would serve it.  But before I added it to the sauce and beef, I heated up boiling water and dissolved the coconut premix into it, getting the lumps out of it.Of course, the boyfriend was held at work an extra hour, but no matter, I still cooked the meat and sauce on low, for an extra hour, making the sauce thicker and even more tasty.  I didn't add the 4/5 cup of water as they said to do, more like 1/2 cup and then I had to cook it for a long time in order for it to get thick. I did this on low or 2 on my stove top.  I don't believe in cooking curry too high because it can scorch.  When my boyfriend got home, we decided to stir fry some vegetables like onion, red pepper and carrot to add to the sauce and I cooked it 5 more minutes.  So it had been cooking for a total of two hours.  I served it with rice and it was really good.  The extra cooking bought out the spices and made the sauce more gravy-like.  I find this curry to be spicy in the tasty sense, more than in the hot chili pepper sense.  It's a good combo of ginger, lime leaves, nuts, chili pepper and other warming spices. I tastes similar to curries I have had in restaurants. I think for all the ingredients you'd have to get fresh to make this yourself, like candlenuts and lime leaves, it's most likely worth the $6.63 in price to make.  Some items in the ingredients list for this box are hard to come by at times and I don't normally stock them in my kitchen.  So buying this kit, even though it is pricey, would save me a lot of time trying to find the ingredients or ending up empty handed with most of the items used, but not all.  My boyfriend did dig out the tiny lemongrass stems from the sauce, at least we thought they were either sugar cane or lemongrass stems.  I ate mine, I didn't mind the extra texture and taste they gave the meal.One package makes about four big servings, even more if you wanted smaller servings and more still if you added more veggies.  You could probably feed eight people off of one box if you proportioned it right.  My boyfriend and I get to eat this for lunch tomorrow as well, so with the meat and veggies it was roughly $4 or so a serving, which beats going to a restaurant for the same thing.  Or see could add more veggies and only pay $2 a serving and have four meals a piece.  I might consider buying a pack of these in the future to have on hand if I want to make a coconut based curry, since sometimes it is iffy if I will find coconut milk in stock at my local store at a decant price.  Sometimes a can is $3 and that seems, with buying all the other items in this curry, fair that the kit is at the price point it is.

column9: Surprisingly similar to a restaurant dish, and very easy
column10: The Prima Taste rendang curry was very easy to make.  All you add is beef, or whatever else you like.  There is plenty for four people.  The moderate spicy flavor will satisfy most taste buds.  The heat is mild but flavorful, like a 2.5 on a 1-10 scale (10 being hottest).  The color is great, and it looks indistinguishable from most restaurants.Please note that each box is one meal.  Also, there are 110 calories per serving (80 from fat), but 15 servings per box.  Two tablespoons equal one serving, and that's excluding the protein.  It's not a health dish and it's not intended to be, but it is hard to see how a box could be 15 servings.Overall, it meets all the criterion for a great easy meal.  I would recommend it.

column9: Easy to make and tastes good too
column10: I'm not a big fan of curry. I have to be in the mood for it and usually I never make it. Mostly because I'm not the best cook.But this was easy to make. It thickened faster than I expected but I added some water and it smoothed it out. I used beef as instructed but I also added carrots, celery, onion and potatoes for a curry stew.It was also spicier than I expected but I like spicy foods because it makes me watch my portions better.It definitely made a good size amount and that surprised me. I had enough for two more meals so I felt like I got a good bang for the buck.

This kit has everything you need to make a delicious curry dish. Although it is labeled for beef, we used chicken and it was quite good. The flavor is strong, spicy and a little sweet. Everything you need is in the box. You simply brown your beef (or chicken, lamb, whatever) and add the two packets (one is a dried coconut mix and the other is the spices mix) and finish cooking your meat. This could also be done in a crockpot. The total prep time was less than 20 minutes. The only thing I did not like were the large leaves in the spice mix. I also don't really like the smell of curry and it does linger.

column9: Amazing taste & perfect flavor combination-just WOW!
column10: We generally are fans of Indian and Thai curries, and like to experiment with different flavors/ethnic cuisines. Unfortunately, many of the pre-mixed curry sauces win up providing a decent 'base' but often require additional 'enhancements' based on our tastes. This 'Prima Taste Rendang Curry' needed absolutely nothing to enhance the flavor. We could not believe how perfectly balanced, smooth, savory and sweet/spicey this combination tasted. While 'beef' was the listed ingredient to be added, we already had chicken thawed out, so we used that instead. This was literally the perfect weeknight 'quick and easy meal' that provided for a surprise ethnic burst, without a lot of fuss. We cooked the whole meal, including rice, and the chicken/sauce in a very short amount of time-the rice in the rice cooker took longer than the chicken/sauce. I would DEFINITELY keep this in the cabinet to prepare again for ourselves and for guests...and soon! Highly recommended and yummy!

I have been a curry fan ever since I lived for a few years in England. Now that I'm back in the US, I make it at home probably at least once a month. I like the curry recipe Jamie Oliver makes to music on YouTube but I have also found a few other recipes here and there on the web which are also simple, tasty and reliable. Most curries seem to have a base of either yogurt, tomatoes, or coconut milk. This one is based on coconut milk.As to this Rendang Curry Sauce mix, I have mixed feeling but mostly positive ones. First, the flavor is pleasant with a little heat from the peppers but not too much. It's very easy to make. There is a package of curry paste and a package of powdered coconut milk in the box. Just brown your meat or whatever you are currying, then add the two packages and some water. Bring to a boil and then simmer till the everything is cooked through. If you use a tender meat it will be ready really quickly, though rendang is often made with tougher cuts of beef which are simmered a long time in order to become tender and to soak up the flavor of the sauce. When its ready, serve it over rice or with naan bread.Though I liked the taste and found it easy to make I am only giving it four stars for a couple of reasons. First is because of the instant coconut milk. I think it would have been nicer if I'd used a can of real coconut milk instead. That would also give the option to use low fat coconut milk if preferred, because the one that comes in the package is very high in calories. The second reason is price. Though I enjoyed it, I found it a little expensive for what you get. I typically buy a small can of Mae Ploy curry paste in one of a variety of flavors along with a can of coconut milk at my local Asian grocery and then do almost exactly the same preparation with similar results for about half of what this costs. Still, if you don't live near an Asian grocery, and you feel like making something which is quick, easy, and a little out of the ordinary, this could be an agreable choice.

Spicy and zesty, this sauce kit makes up in a few minutes.We found it to be delicious served over rice, which makes for a hearty meal.The instructions are easy, but it would've been nice if they hadincluded the conversion of 4/5 cup of water on the package.And it's interesting that the original purpose of rendang is to disguisetough cuts of meat, yet the ingredients call for beef tenderloin = fillet.None-the-less we used N.Y. strip steak and it was a delicious.This is definitely an enjoyable dish to add to our menu.

This turned out to be a very tasty dish. It says just add beef, but you will also need to supply the rice or potatoes for it to go over, there is quite a bit of sauce. It has a thick spicy curry flavor and I found the longer the rice sat in it the better the taste, so you might want to add the cooked rice right to the pan instead of over the top. Very good, will make this again.

column9: easy to make, tastes very good -- but definitely decadent
column10: I quite liked the flavor of this Rendang Curry Sauce.  I used part of the kit to make a beef curry and the other part to make a chicken curry, and both were delicious.  Though I believe beef is the more traditional choice, I actually preferred this sauce on boneless, skinless chicken breasts.I have had Rendang curry in a few restaurants and found this kit to be close to restaurant quality.  My major complaint is that instead of using coconut milk this uses dehydrated coconut in a separate pouch, and the resulting curry sauce has a little bit of a gritty consistency because of this.  My only other issue is the amount of oil in the curry mix.  If you have leftovers (like I did), you'll definitely notice the oil since some of it separates out during refrigeration.  While the nutritional information here and on the box make it seem like this product isn't that decadent, the serving sized used is unrealistically small.  It's more reasonable to double the values listed, meaning that each serving of meat will have an additional 200+ calories from the sauce.  Because of this, I would suggest that this makes a better treat for a rare occasion than something to be eaten frequently.

This is some seriously good curry sauce. I made it at around 3 p.m. and left it cooking in the crockpot. Six hours later my family and some neighbors attacked it, and every single one of the seven who tried it gave it 5/5 stars for taste.There are two packets to mix into your browned beef cubes -- the first one is a dried coconut milk powder and the second one has all the seasonings: chili, galangal, palm sugar, onion, shallot, sugar, pandan leaf, garlic, candlenut, lemongrass, soy sauce, fennel, coriander, cumin, kaffir lime leaf, cloves, turmeric, white pepper and cinnamon. The box says it contains wheat, too, but I can't see evidence of that in the ingredient list.You simply brown the beef or chicken, add in the contents of both packets, mix well and cook it all until the meat's done. I highly recommend the crockpot method; you can throw it together pretty quickly in the morning and then just steam some rice with it for dinner. Our meat was beautifully easy to shred and spread out the flavor even more.The taste the mix brings to the curry is not your usual/expected taste -- it's a mild, slightly sweet, slightly spicy and extremely flavorful blend. I appreciated the fact that it had no chemical-sounding ingredients, but there is a warning on the label that it in manufactured on equipment that also processes seafood, peanuts, sesame and egg products.The box says a serving size is two tablespoons (15 servings altogether). I highly doubt that would work for US portions, but we still got a good 7 servings out of it. I'm definitely going to order some more.

column9: Better if it were just the curry paste, and not a kit
column10: I love curry. Thai curry.  Indian curry.  Japanese curry.  But I have never had curry from Singapore before.  This was my first taste of rendang, and I loved it.  But I didn't really love this sauce kit.The kit is easy to make, if all you want to do is follow instructions.  Just brown some meat of your choice--the box recommends beef but anything will do--then boil up the curry paste and coconut milk powder with some water, and the browned meat and simmer, and you are done.  Made directly this way, it is easy, if not a little boring.Whenever I try something new, I try to follow the instructions explicitly to see how it turns out, which is what I did this with this curry sauce kit.  The results were nice.  The curry has a good flavor, with nice lemongrass and a good blend of spicy and sweet.  I generally like my curries a bit more fierce, so I would probably add something to give it more of a kick, but it wasn't too wimpy.This was my first time experiencing powdered coconut milk--normally when I make curry I buy it by the can.  I really didn't like it, and don't much see the point of it.  I suppose there was a time and place when canned coconut milk was hard to come by, and a package of powdered coconut milk would be a necessary addition to a curry spice paste, but those days are behind us.Eating this has gotten me interested in trying to make some rendang myself, but I probably wouldn't buy this sauce kit again.  Because making curry paste from scratch can be time consuming, I often buy premade Thai and Indian curry pastes, then prepare everything else myself.  I would be more interested in this if it were just a premixed rendang paste, but I really don't need the powdered coconut milk.

This stuff was amazing. It is very simple to use and the flavor was just fantastic. We used it on chicken instead of beef and it was some of the most delicious curry I've had. And I've spent a lot of time working and living in the Middle East and Asia. I was very impressed with how good it was, but also how easy it is to prepare. If you can make Hamburger Helper you can use this, and the results are much better. I will be buying more in the future for sure.

column9: A very tasty curry - easy to prepare
column10: I really wasn't sure how this was going to turn out when I received the sauce kit. The recipe calls for beef - I used lamb as I prefer it - I think the overall effect was the same.Bottom line up front - The curry sauce kit is easy to make, very tasty, with simple instructions.Pros:- The directions are straight forward and simple. Total prep and cook time was approximately 20 minutes.- Flavors are excellent and reminiscent of going to an curry restauarant and asking for the coconut curry. The flavors were very nice, if a little sweet. Perhaps a bit too much coconut - personal taste for that one.- makes a LOT of curry. I used two pounds of cubed lamb and made two cups of rice to go with it. There was MORE than enough. I would actually recommend making three cups of rice and perhaps up to three pounds of meat.Cons:- The coconut powder was a little bit challenging to get completely dissolved. Once everything started boiling, this was fairly well taken care of.- I would have liked to have known the amount of curry to expect. I think the recommendation was OK - yet as stated above, it made a LOT.Overall - quite tasty, simple to make, good quality.

column9: Yum! Just as tasty with chicken!
column10: I've had Japanese, Indian, Thai and Jamaican curry, but I don't think I've ever tried rendang before, which Wikipedia describes as "West Sumatran caramelized beef curry". This stuff made me want to hop on a plane to Singapore.The box contains two large packets, one with curry-spice paste and one with coconut powder. The directions say to brown 28 oz of beef, remove it from the pan, add the contents of the 2 packets and 4/5 cup water, heat to boiling, add the browned beef and heat through. I took the advice given by reviewers and mixed the coconut powder with 1 cup (easier to measure!) water in a large bowl before adding it and the spice paste to the pan. Then I added browned white meat chicken bits, chopped caramelized onion and chopped sauteed green pepper and let it cook at low heat for about 30 minutes before serving it on hot steamed Japanese rice.I almost added extra red curry paste after reading complaints that it was too mild, but I'm so glad I didn't! My husband loves 5-alarm hot food, and we both agreed that this is JUST right in spiciness. It's hot enough without overwhelming the flavors. It's different from any curry I've had before, and hard for me to describe - I guess it's like Thai panang curry but without the dominating coconut or peanut flavors. We all loved it! Just watch out for the little unchewable green leaves in the spice mixture.

column9: Almost perfect with a few tweaks
column10: After having been in Singapore for a while, I miss the regional cuisine. Making fresh spice pastes every time I'm cooking is just not practical, which means that I don't get to make the dishes as often as I might like, so I jumped at the opportunity to try a pre-packaged version of a dish that typically takes several hours to make.Rendang is usually a slow cooking dish. The directions here make it easy to make on a weeknight at home. Overall, the sauce makes a generous portion. While the "safety information" (allergy alert) mentions "crustacean", the ingredient list doesn't include belechan (shrimp paste), which is typically used for rendang. I also didn't taste it in the packaged sauce, so it is lacking a bit of authentic taste. However, that's easy enough to rememdy by adding your own when heating the spice paste. It was not as spicy as I would've liked, or as I expected.For the record, I also tried it as a slow cooker with beef stew pieces. That makes the taste slightly more authentic, as the beef was more thoroughly infused with the rendang flavor. I'd definitely substitute the coconut milk powder with a can (I used two) of coconut milk. I also added some more oelek sambal (chili) to give it more kick and some belechan. Those changes produced something that was almost perfection.As another reviewer said, I'd prefer for this to be sold as a paste packet or  similar to Mae Ploy/Aroy-D/Asian Home Gourmet  so that I can add my own milk (and belechan). However, for the ease of making the dish and for relatively authentic flavor, I give this four stars.

I enjoy cooking meals from scratch, but I understand that curry can be somewhat of a hassle because it often requires a lot of specialty spices like white pepper and candlenut. So it makes a lot of sense to prepackage these ingredients into a simple curry kit like this Prima Taste product, and they've definitely done a good job of making it easy.The box includes a rendering paste and a coconut premix, and the only extra ingredients you need is beef (they suggest 28oz of sliced beef tenderloin) and water. After cooking the beef, you just need to bring the water, with included rendering paste and coconut premix, to a boil. Add the beef, then serve - you'll need to supply your own side of rice. Pretty simple.Looking at the ingredient list, I was also pleasantly surprised. The rendering paste doesn't seem to have any additives at all. The coconut pre-mix, on the other hand, does contain maltodextrin and sodium caseinate, but it mostly just seems to be powdered coconut milk - if this is a problem, I suppose you substitute some canned (or homemade) coconut milk (though you'd probably want to nix the water too).I'm no expert on curry, but it smells and tastes very much like I'd expected. Perhaps somebody who grew up eating curry all their life might be able to tell the difference, but I sure wasn't. It had a nice coconut flavor and wasn't very spicy. If I were to make this again, I would probably add some fresh vegetables - maybe onion, garlic, and peppers - but overall I was very happy with this product.

column9: Prima Taste Rendang Curry Sauce Kit
column10: Just made this tonight and it tastes great. Very quick and simple. I cooked some chicken thighs in a pan. Put some water and the sauce kit packet ingredients into a sauce pan. Added the finished chicken to the sauce, served over white rice and had a great meal. This is about as easy as it gets. I'm used to a beef rendang served at a local Malaysian restaurant and their version is a very thick paste. This is more of medium thickness sauce and the kit makes quite a bit. I had enough left over to save for lunch the next day. If you need a quick meal this will do quite nicely. My one complaint is that either the onion shallots or pandan leaf that is in the mix (not sure which) is a little chewy/tough. I would purchase this again.

I love this and will buy it again!  I had beef stew meat in my freezer, so that's what I used and it worked fabulously.  I cooked the beef to about 2/3 done, then added it to the curry mix when it was ready.  Because it was stew meat, I turned the heat down and covered it and let it simmer for awhile so the meat would get more tender.  When it was ready, the stew meat was VERY tender.  The curry has a wonderful flavor and there is plenty of sauce so that you could add veggies if you wanted to.  I added peas.  Next time I may add potatoes and onions as well.I have never had Singapore curry before, but it really made me think of Thai curry, which I love.  I thought the lime leaves in the curry could have been smaller as they are a bit chewy, but they impart such a fantastic flavor!  It is delicious and I'm guessing, since I just made it last night, that it will be even better today when I have it for lunch!

This is a great tasting Rendang with the flavors of the spices coming through. First some comments to earlier reviews. Usually the amount of lemon grass is more pronounced, with some chefs preferring to include a lot more pieces than this mix has in it. If you wish to cut the sweetness or have a stronger lemon bite, I suggest that you add some lemon juice.To add volume and vegetables to the dish without changing the flavor, I chunked up a can of whole bamboo shoots and cut a whole red bell pepper into chunks. This tasted great on a full plate of rice and made 6 large servings- creating an all-in-one dish and cost effective. If you want something crunchy, small pieces of celery would do fine. If you would prefer something soft, you can use a can of straw mushrooms.I prefer to cut vegetables into 1/3" cubes and meat into 3/4" strips so that every forkful has all the ingredients when the sauce is potent like this one. I did use a full cup of water and mixed the coconut before adding the seasoning. After reaching boiling, I added the vegetables and meat.

I fancy myself as a pretty gosh darned good cook, but I don't think I've ever made a curry sauce as good as this. I've used this as recommend with both beef and chicken and both are mouth-watering delicious. I don't know how else to say it. I don't know what more to say. I was flabbergasted, this was so good. Tasty to the extreme. We love it at our house, you'll love it at yours, too.

The flavor is strong curry with a bit of spicy hot. I decided to try the Prima Taste Rendang Curry Sauce with venison instead of beef. We primarily eat venison and elk so I felt this would be a better test for us. Following the very simple directions,I started by cutting the roast into thin strips and some chunks, nothing bigger than a silver dollar. I then stir fried the venison in oil in a steel wok until done since my wife does not care for any pink in her meat. The recipe calls for frying the meat in a pan until half done. As I finished the meat I put in the 4/5 cup of water into a pan and added the two sauce packets. One held a solid and liquid while the other a white power. (no MSG) A french whip was required to mix the white power into the water. A semi-soft material that looked like very small pieces of green corn husk were present in the sauce. I am not at all familiar with food from Singapore and have no idea what this was. My wife and I both remarked that this was the only thing we didn't like about the sauce, but it was not bad just unusual for us. When the sauce came to a boil I added the venison and let it cook as I prepared the rice and a salad. We both found the dish very tasty, my wife found it to be almost at the limit for her in "hot" taste. We had the leftovers  the next day, I found it even more delicious. She found it hotter. We both decided that we would buy it again since it was a big change of pace for our usual venison dishes. It was very easy to make and was good with rice though I would like it with noodles as well. If you like the taste of curry this is your dish.

column9: Great flavor and easy to make
column10: This curry is on the high end of mild, just enough heat to make it interesting.  It depends much more on a rich mix of flavors, which are well-balanced and delicious.  Only a couple things to keep in mind.  The coconut mix got a little lumpy when prepared as described.  You probably want to mix it alone with a small amount of water to make a smooth paste before adding it.  Also, I prefer to remove the leaves before eating.  Those are minor issues compared to the great taste, and I will definitely be getting this again.

I almost thought that I'd made this myself as it was so good!  That such flavor came not from my chopping up galanga, lime leaf, turmeric, etc., all of which are part of my pantry, but from a pouch, well, I was really impressed.  I do have one complaint, however.  The instructions on the box said to add 4/5 cup of water to the mixture.  At first, I thought my eyes were deceiving me as I'd never heard of a 4/5 cup measure.  Google to the rescue.  4/5 cup is the equivalent of 2/3 cup minus three tablespoons. though I doubt that I'll ever see that measure again until I order more of this curry.

column9: Wow, smells like restaurant quality food!
column10: Was very pleased to see the ingredients list was all natural, no MSG that I could recollect.  Just mix the two packets together, and add some water.  The coconut powder clumped together after adding water, even with stirring, but dissipated once I added into my proteins.  I used coarsely cut chicken breast instead of beef, and it turned out excellent.  My stomach growled mightily while stirring it, smelled like restaurant quality food.  They really nailed the coconut curry flavor, in a good, natural smelling way.Minus one star because of the pandan leaves; I appreciated that the manufacturer included pandan, BUT, they appeared to be hard and inedible, and were difficult to fish out of the sauce.  I had some whole pandan leaves that I used instead; these were much easier to work with and remove post-cooking.  I ended up straining my sauce, but more trouble than necessary.  Perhaps Prima Taste can make a bouquet garni with the pandan next time.Now I'm eager to check out Prima's other tasty products.

I've never had much food from Singapore, so I can't say whether or not this was authentic.  But I liked it, and it seemed to taste "exotic" anyway.  Not your standard burger and fries at the very least.It was extremely easy to prepare.  All you do is mix the two pouches with water, and add in some beef chunks that you've been cooking.  And pour on top or rice (or mashed potatoes the box suggests).  Its that simple.  I think in total, with cooking the meat, it took maybe a half hour, and most of that was just it simmering on the stove while I was cooking the rice.  Sure I probably could have added some veggies, but the box didn't say that you really needed to, and there were some green things in the sauce, so hey, its all good.  The sauce itself was kind of an orangey-brown color and it was thicker like a gravy.The taste was a little bit spicy, but I just threw some plain yogurt on top and that cooled it down.  The coconut came threw quite strongly and that was the dominant taste for the dish.  The chili was also quite strong and that was probably the second most dominant taste.  There were other flavors of course, but they all melded together and to be honest I couldn't really distinguish what precisely they were.  Except maybe the lime leaf, I did taste a bit of lime.  But it was tasty, and with the exception of one in the household, not too spicy.I like that the ingredients didn't have preservatives or coloring though.  It seemed somewhat healthy.  And while there are a lot of ingredients, they all seem to be fairly normal and pronounceable.  So that's good.  The fat content could be considered a little high, but I do think that its probably healthy fats considering most of it is from the coconut.I liked it, and I'll probably eat it again.  I might even try some of their other flavors as well.Review by M. Reynard 2012

This was so simple to make and the ingredients pretty exotic to me. I wasn't sure if it would be something I'd really like.  It turned out a really flavorful sauce which had kaffir lime leaves, coriander, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and many other spices.  The coconut powders that you mix in are rich and smooth..and that's the way the sauce turns out.  I used chicken breast instead of beef and it was just fine.  The package says serve with rice or mashed potatoes..do the rice..mashed potatoes would be too weird with this.  Everything included but yr meat and it really is something different to serve and tastes good!

column9: A very nice, flavorful, mild curry
column10: Having had Rendang curry only a couple of times (and then at Indonesian restaurants) I did not know what to expect when I tried this curry paste, looking at it as something of a culinary adventure.  I love curry, and, time permitting,  make my own paste (for Indian curries).  I also *love* Patak's pastes, particularly the Patak's Vindaloo Curry Paste, Hot, 10-Ounce Glass Jars (Pack of 6) and Pataks Korma Paste 10oz and have become very fond of Kitchens of India Paste for Butter Chicken Curry, 3.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6) (so I know that you can make a very nice curry with prepared pastes).  All of the above take minutes to prepare and are very flavorful.  As someone who has tried many many prepared curry pastes, I'd say that the Prima taste Rendang is among the very best i have tried!  It makes a very rich, mild, coconut-based curry which tastes very fresh.  The "kit" I received contained a good deal more paste than any of thee Kitchens of India varieties (the Pataks come in jars, and so you can very the amount you use).  I believe there was more bulk because the ingredients aren't dried (most of the other pastes I have used require the addition of tomatoes or coconut milk).  The Rendang is complete.  In fact, my whole family enjoyed this! (My 14 year old tends not to eat things as hot as I, so he is less enthused about the vindaloo, for example).It is quick and easy to prepare, BUT, I believe they compromised when it came to directions.  This is a beef-based curry, and beef gets tough when it is sir fried or simmered in a pan for a short time.  This is the first time I have seen a curry paste specify tenderloin! and, I believe it was for the sake of keeping cooking time low.  Curry is more or less a stew, and beef curries are usually slow cooked (braised) for a long time at a low simmer.  When I make stew, and sometimes when I make curry, I will use a pressure cooker if I do not have the time to cook it for an hour or more.  I would recommend the same when using this paste.  That is, you may opt to use tenderloin as the directions on the box specify, *OR* if you are using a lesser cut of meat (and honestly, I have never had curry based on filet mingnon!) then gently brown the meat, coat with paste and either cooks at a low simmer (for an hour or more) in a tightly covered pot, or for a quicker version, prepare in a pressure cooker.You should know before ordering that the directions specify tenderloin.  Go ahead and make it that way if it is a realistic option for you, but know that it can be prepared with round, or ? another cut.  It just requires a more traditional slow braise if you are using a lesser cut of meat, or it can be sped with the use of a pressure cooker.The paste itself, though, is very very good, and I will be ordering more :)  In fact, I'd say this is already among my favorite (along with Patak's Vindaloo, and Kitchens of India Butter curry), not too spicy, but very very flavorful.  Highly recommended!

column4: Glenda Boozer "Live, live, live! Life is a ba...
column9: Very good flavor; a bit mild, but it's easier to add heat than to subtract it.
column10: I have regular cravings for coconut-base curries, and this one is delicious. I let it simmer in my crockery cooker for a while, and the fragrance filled the whole house. It is pretty mild, but I can easily at hot seasonings, but not so easily take them away; I'd rather have a milder product and then add my own heat to taste. It was easy to brown the meat and add the contents of the two packets, and then we had everything but the rice. I would definitely recommend this for people who crave curries but aren't always up to making them from scratch.

column9: Try it vegetarian - the right amount of savory/spicy/sweet
column10: This was a breeze to make.  I added a very large boneless chicken breast in bite-sized pieces (much less in quantity than the recommended amount of beef) and added diced onions, sliced carrots, peas, and diced sweet potato.  I was tempted to make it a totally vegetarian meal, because my husband will not eat beef, and he really does not like meat much at all.  but for flavor, and to cut fat, I cooked the chicken and veggies in a bit of coconut oil.  Delicious.  It's true that the coconut powder gets lumpy, but I followed some advice to whisk it up prior to adding it.  Tasted similar to the veggie curry I make with curry paste and coconut milk, but not quite as creamy.  The added crunchiness of some of the ingredients (peanuts, coconut) added to that made it even more appealing.I just love coconut curry.  There is something about the savory/spicy/sweetness that is appealing to me.  I added more chili from a spice bottle.  I don't have experience with the "real thing", as I don't travel to other countries, or try many ethnic restaurants.  I just knew this was a coconut curry, and that is how I prepare it.  The chicken was so flavorful, as were the vegetables. (the sweet potato -- WOW!) The sauce permeates everything.  Very fragrant.I have been going back and forth in my mind about the price.  I decided that since I am the only curry lover in this house, it just doesn't pay to get the curry paste jars and store them.  Coconut milk, which IS creamier, I do buy the premium brand.  So, it is costly to buy the ingredients to make it by scratch if you aren't going to use the rest of the curry paste before it goes bad.  If you add the peanuts and such to the cost per package, you are talking bucks!So, for a novelty, I believe the price is justified.  This package makes quite a bit, so after two people eating, there are leftovers, and I froze them immediately after cooling.  Heated back up, the consistency isn't as good, but passable.I would buy this, but just not in a case.  I have no room.  The only cases I buy from Amazon (and I shop here a lot) are of bottles of a name brand jalapeno sauce.  I go through that fast!  But if you want a good curry, and you eat it a lot, I recommend buying it from Amazon.

Rendang Curry by Prima Taste is a Dry Beef Curry sauce kit. The box says Best Singapore Favorites. Lately I've been trying out a couple of exotic food kits, this one piqued my interest. Although 28 oz of beef tenderloins  were required, I'm not a beef person and decided to try using tofu instead. I invited two other people to join me for this experience. All of us like rich, spicy food and all the better if it is restaurant quality at home.To start, I took two packages of extra firm tofu (packaged in water) and sliced each into eight or nine slabs like a loaf of bread. I laid these between clean dishtowels to drain off excess moisture which aids in absorbing the flavors of the sauce.Choosing toasted sesame oil, I coated the bottom of an iron skillet until the oil was fragrant. I cut each slab of tofu in to eight chunks and laid them in the pan, letting them brown slightly. Then took those out and set aside until all of the tofu was browned.Meanwhile, basmati rice (not part of the kit) simmered in another pan. The box says it also goes well with mashed potatoes, something I'd like to try next time.One of two enormous packets contained a slightly oily red paste that upon first inspection looks like tomatoes, but turns out to be an exotic blend of Galangal, Palm Sugar, Pandan Leaf, Candlenut, Ginger Salt and Lemon grass to name a few. The minute it hit the hot skillet a pleasing, fragrant aroma wafted through the house. Each of the guests commented about it.The second packet held a dry, powdered mix of coconut milk and solids. I hadn't seen coconut processed this way before, but after adding the required amount of water, the sauce began to look much more like a curry. After following the cooking instructions on the box, I added the tofu to the sauce. When it was heated through, I served it over rice. Each of us had a small plate, and there was enough left over for each of us to have 2 more meals.It made an abundance of sauce as well. We were all satisfied with the flavor and talked about having seconds, but were full.I found it a bit on the sweet side, as mentioned above palm sugar contributed to this. I'm not a fan of sweet curries. Although the taste was sensational, the spicy kick was surprising but not overwhelming. For a bit of variation, the addition of baby green beans, julienned carrots, or sautéed onions would be welcome.All in all, we found Rendang Curry very tasty, and everyone enjoyed it. I'll be looking for this on store shelves.

column9: Not quite rendang taste, but good
column10: Taste : 4 starsConvenience : 4 starsAuthenticity : 2.5 starsHealthiness : 1 star!Rendang is an Indonesian style meat curry. I've eaten the dish in restaurants in Singapore (though never in Indonesia), and I've also tried this exact sauce mix a few years ago, and I thought it turned out better the last time. For rendang, it was too wet, and too sweet. However, if you don't try to compare it for authenticity, it does taste very good.The coconut power was a bit difficult to mix well. I should have tried what another reviewer suggested - to whisk it with water separately before mixing it. Perhaps I should have tried cooking it longer to allow more of the liquid to evaporate. The instructions only said to cook till it reached the desired doneness.You can substitute the beef with lamb as well if that's your preference. It doesn't make it any healthier, but it gives it a different flavor.I wish I can eat this more often, but one look at the nutritional information will tell you why that's not a good idea. It doesn't look too bad, until you reach "Servings per container : 15"! A previous reviewer mentioned that it is impossible to eat the entire packet in one sitting. I agree, but I can eat half a packet without too much effort, which should be enough saturated fat and cholesterol to last me through a week.

This is fast and good. If you like curry this works. It is like a lot of the bottled Indian and Asian sauces, which sure makes for fast cooking. If you like it hotter go add red pepper paste or dry spice flakes. I think frozen peas go well with curry and naturally work with a white rice base.

My husband and I agreed that this is one of the best curries we've had in a long time. Curries vary greatly and so does individual taste. We particularly liked Prima Taste's Rendang Curry because it was not very hot, but had just enough heat to make it interesting, and the subtle coconut flavor. The spices blend well together and nothing overpowers the others. And, it smells wonderful when cooking! It tasted fresh, probably since it was not just a dry mix.Making this was super easy. Using a whisk, I mixed the paste and dry coconut packages together along with the water, then added the browned meat. I did have to add water every so often as the meat simmered in the mix, but, I was using 2 lbs of big chunks of meat. If you use smaller cuts that cook to tender more quickly or less meat, you might not have to. I liked the large pieces of spices in the sauce, but others might prefer to pick them out. We added green peas to the dish just before serving it over rice. Chopped peanuts might make a nice topping, and you can use your imagination for other additions.

column9: Fastest way to great beef curry
column10: I love curries and I was anxious to try the Rendang Curry that promoted itself as quick and easy. When I read through the instructions, I was somewhat surprised that the type of beef called for in this recipe was 28oz of pricey beef tenderloin (think filet mignon). Although I'm trying to watch my family's cholesterol levels, I wanted to stay true to the recipe and use beef, but felt I could substitute chuck steak at $4/lb on sale. When stir-frying chuck, the secret is to cut across the grain and to not overcook, meaning I could still see the pink in the meat when I remove it from the pan. The result: my family loved it! Admittedly, my end product does not look like the photo on the box because I have more gravy which is probably due to the excess moisture that the beef produced when I pan-fried it. I did simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to reduce it. After the sauce was reduced, I turned off the stove and added the beef. Next time, the part I might change is to measure the juice that the beef produces and add water to make 4/5 of a cup of liquid that the recipe calls for. Actually, I liked having the gravy with my rice. At $7/box plus $10 for the beef, the entrée with rice would serve about 6-7 people and not the 15 that the box states, unless you have other dishes, of course. My family would love for me to make this curry again.

column9: Not exactly *dry* rendang, but wow, is this good!
column10: I've wanted to try dry rendang for a long time.  I've heard it's wonderful.  This wasn't dry, but that's OK--it left me lots of sauce to pour over rice.  If I licked the bowl when I was done, I would never admit it here.I didn't follow the instructions.  (I'm terrible at following instructions.)  I started at the supermarket, while choosing the beef.  This calls for thin slices of beef tenderloin, but that's not exactly in my budget.  I went with chunks of a fairly tough cut of beef.  That meant long simmering, which is not what the instructions call for.I lightly browned the beef and set it aside. (The instructions tell you to pan-fry until medium-done.)  I added the paste and coconut and brought it to a boil.  (Hey, I got something right!)  The "coconut premix" was a powder that clumped pretty badly.  I think next time I'll add the coconut premix and the water, so I can see the clumps to break them up, then add the paste.I added the beef back to the pan and covered (which you're not supposed to do,) and let it cook for about an hour and a half.  With tenderloin it would be ready in a few minutes, but if you're broke like me, the sauce holds up well to cheap beef and a long slow simmer.The smell in the house was absolutely wonderful.  The flavor was wonderful as well.  It was a good blend of spices, with no one spice stealing the show.  I know that rendang is supposed to have hot peppers, but I don't know exactly how hot it's supposed to be.  This was extremely mild.  Leftovers may meet a little Sriracha to warm things up a bit.  Next time I make this I may introduce some hot peppers before simmering.But oh yes, there will be a next time.

Having once been a twenty one year old student on a budget living in Tokyo Japan, I've eaten my share (and more )of wholesome, filling curry. From the two hundred yen plates under the railroad tracks, to twenty-two hundred yen plates at posh Tops Saxon, I know good curry (and bad curry) when I taste it. In general, when making curry at home, I tend to stick with Japanese brands (like S&B - Golden Curry Sauce Mix - Mild 3.5 Oz.) that require a big pot and lots of cooking time, so Prima Taste's rendang offering looked interesting to me, not only because I'm partial to southeast Asian curries that use fruit, coconut, and such, but also because it looked like it would not be hard to cook. And it wasn't. I browned about a pound and a half of cut up top broil and steak (mixed) and just for kicks threw in two small potatoes and two small carrots. This rendang comes with two pouches. One is a super fine coconut powder, and the other is a traditional red chili based curry paste. Mix the two with a little water, bring to a boil, add the meat, and you're ready to throw it over noodles, rice, potatoes, whatever. I added some extra water and cooked mine for a little over an hour, and the meat got very tender and tasty. The potatoes and carrots were good and soft too. The flavor of the curry is just right. It's punchy but not scorchingly hot, and the coconut adds just the right consistency and flavorful edge. Over rice, it had the perfect balance of flavor and sauciness, and with the extra tender meat, a smooth and satisfying mouth feel. I think what helps make this curry so good is the ingredients are kept separate, vacuum packed, and the paste itself is not dried. It makes for easy prep and a very tasty meal. At $6.50 a box or so, it seems a little pricey, but it makes enough to feed a family of four, or a couple for one night with microwavable lunches for two the next day. I'm definitely going to pick up some more of this stuff at the first opportunity. It's really good.

Even people who aren't crazy about curry may like this. I myself love curry, but I lean toward the Madras type, so this Rendang curry from Singapore is pretty mild for my taste. Overall, the flavor reminds me of certain Thai curries, probably due to the coconut. What you actually get here are two foil envelopes of curry mixture and coconut powder. Chile peppers are certainly there, but hot pepper fans will want to add more. Officially, this kit is for Rendang Curry with beef, but the back of the box states that chicken or lamb would be equally appropriate. I used beef, and made only half of the recipe, as I was the only one eating...the package says that the opened envelopes will keep for three days, so I froze the remainder for future use.  The full recipe calls for nearly two pounds of meat and no added vegetables; if you choose to add vegetables you will have enough curry to feed a small family, so I'd advise that. In any case, this dish can be prepared very quickly, and has a pleasant flavor served with rice. Whether or not the Prima Taste is worth its price is a judgment call, but I probably wouldn't get it again, just because I like to make my own curry. But you can prepare a quick, easy and tasty meal with this product. Prima Taste offers several such sauce kits, and they may be worth a try as well.

I am probably one of the few people on earth who has not had curry before.This being my first face to face meeting of it AND having to be the one toput this kit together...well, I did pretty good and it did too.  I was a bitwary but all in all it was tasty and a new item for me to try.  The onlything I was not wild about is that the serving size is only 2 tablespoons(says that there are 15 servings per sauce kit) and for those 2 tablespoonsyou get 110 calories and 9 gm. of fat (7 of those are saturated) and 5 gm.of carb's...now, ALL that is kind of high for only 2 tablespoons, but Isuppose for something different now and then it won't kill anyone...but Icouldn't quite give this 4 stars.  Interesting new to me product.

As packaged curries go, this one isn't bad.  And in fact if I was rating it against most curry mixes, it'd rate pretty high. (As it is, I'd probably give it 3.5 stars, but Amazon doesn't let us do that.)  It has a nice amount of heat, a reasonable amount of flavor and it's easy to make.  It does, however, have a couple of problems, at least as far as my tastes run.First, the coconut mix is a kind of coconut flour affair, which blends easily but tastes a little chalky, so there's always a bit of a dry, dusty quality to each bite.  Second, one of the ingredients is a leaf or piece of grass that simply doesn't soften up very well.  Getting a bit of hard, fibrous plant material in a bite of curry isn't high on my list of tasty treats.  Still, these are fairly minor problems, and working on different methods of preparation might help alleviate them.  I honestly think the company would be better off selling this in a jar, straining out the leafy bits and using whole coconut and coconut oil instead of that coconut flour packet.The recipe calls for beef tenderloin which is odd because the box explains that Rendang curry was originally developed to disguise tough cuts of meat.  I chose to use ground beef, which has more flavor, and I sauteed it in coconut oil instead of something neutral like canola. Both choices upped the flavor ante.  The box does say that it's also good for lamb or chicken, and it's good enough that I might try it again with chicken, or even use it as the base for a vegetable curry.I think if you're going to make curry at home and not make it from scratch, this is a good option.

I've never cooked with curry, although I have eaten various items with curry at restaurants. This kit made it very easy to make the sauce. Add water and cook the Rendang Paste and Prima Coconut until it comes to a boil. The taste is a little spicy, but too sweet for my likening. The packets that the sauce mixtures come in did nothing to make me confident about trying the sauce. They reminded me of the packets you get when you buy wet cat food. It was very unappealing to squeeze out the Rendang Paste. Once everything was mixed together it didn't seem too bad, but the overall taste and appearance (before cooking) were poor.

See that disclaimer on the product page that says the actual ingredients may differ from what's listed? Apparently, the manufacturer thinks it's OK to switch to using the "Big 8" allergens; there's no milk listed in the published ingredients, but there it is on the side of the box.Two differences that will seem trivial to anyone who doesn't care about milk products: the ingredients list online says, "coconut milk solids," and the list on the box reads, "coconut, milk solids." The allergen statement on the box clearly indicates it contains milk products.Since I am allergic to milk, I couldn't try the actual product; I have no opinion of its quality.:( And I love curry!!

This curry was awesome. It made a big batch, easily enough for four adults. It was tasty, spicy enough, and not too sweet. We added beef and some veggies and it made a great dinner. Rich flavor, utterly delicious. This isn't a curry I've had before but it's similar to a penang. At any rate, we all loved it and it was super easy.The thing is, it's like $9 per meal, not including meat or veggies. For nine bucks, I can get a jar of curry paste and three cans of coconut milk and make 3 meals of curry once I add meat and veggies. And, using the paste isn't really any harder. Is this more delicious than curry paste? It's better than most that I've used, but no better than some. To me it isn't a good value unless you were traveling and needed self contained meals.

Its incredible how Thai seasonings can make food taste.... this is restaurant quality seasoning that is simple to prepare, comes in two separate packs...I follows simple directions, and it was fabulous....  several different flavors, I will try them all...

This is the fourth attempt to post this review, I can only assume I mentioned a country or person or something, so I'll keep it simple.I like curry, any curry (no countries or ethnic groups mentioned)This curry is: -The exact recipe calls for Beef, if you prefer chicken go for it.Cook the meat (whichever you choose) shallow fry, or wok flash fry until cooked through, rare is OK for beef, but obviously not for pork or chicken, cook these thoroughly.Second stage is mix paste and spices with fluid, cook on their own until simmered.Finally add meat, and simmer to taste? That could mean 20 minutes, or 6 hours - I know when I make curry I prefer slow cooked soft meat that has had plenty of time to absorb all he spices, so longer is better. But if you're in a hurry that's fine, it just won't be as fully flavored.So taste?Well that's subjective and personal but I found it hot (spicy) in a white pepper way, and top heavy on the cumin flavor, but this is not uncommon for that part of the World.I guess I was disappointed, I used one mix on three pounds of meat (not the 1-2 pound as suggested) and it was still pretty fiery.

I used this product with chicken, Bell peppers, broccoli, mushrooms and zucchini squash. Sauté the mixture and to this add the sauce and coconut milk which comes in two separate pouches. First mix them together and heat it to gentle boil and then add to the cooked chicken and veggies. Serve with rice or pita bread. You could also use this with just vegetables, if you are vegetarian. I found this stuff to be too sweet for a curry. Generally I prefer Indian curries but I recommend this product if you like mild curries.1. Kitchens of India Paste for Butter Chicken Curry, 3.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)2. Sukhi's Gourmet Indian Foods Gluten-Free Classic Indian Curry Sauce, 3-Ounce Packets  (Pack of 6)3. Patak's Rogan Josh Curry Sauce 283g

This Redang Curry sauce tastes really good. Either Missus 1rude or I would have been pleased with a restaurant dish that delivered the flavor this box did.We were amazed at the high sugar, fat and sodium content of just the contents of the package. We prepared a veggie version that worked really well to try and mitigate that (try it with tofu instead of beef, the Missus sauteed it with onions, cabbage and carrots - yum!), but that and cost would be the reasons why we wouldn't make this a regular pantry item.

I am a curry FIEND, if it's curry I almost always like it. My fridge has just about every Mae Ploy I could find at our local store. When I saw the Prima Rendang, I was anxious to try it, as I've made this before from recipes I found online.If I found a restaurant that served this, I would buy it, weekly. It's SO tasty, a nice fresh bright clean tasting curry, flavorful without tasting like it has too much salt or sugary sweetness. It tastes like I ground the spices and made the paste myself, it's THAT fresh. I have never made a curry this good at home before.PRO*Easy to make (see tips below) with a payout that is restaurant-quality. You could serve this to guests and they would want to marry you!*The sauce is generous enough that you could easily feed 4 people or a little more if you put in some extra veggies. I sliced up some green onions and I think peas would be good in it, or some grated radish or even a little potato if that's your thing.*Prep time is very fast*Everything you need for the sauce is in the box*All the spices and chilies are so perfectly balanced, you get a total experience of the curry and not just a few spices standing out more than others. It was honestly hard for me to pick out separate flavors, such was the harmonious balance. If I had to guess what spices were in it, that would be hard to do. Wonderful blend. They are listed on the box as: Chili, galangal, onion, shallot, pandan leaf, garlic, candlenut, ginger, lemon grass, fennel, coriander, cumin, kaffir lime leaf, cloves, turmeric, white pepper, cinnamon. I think they forgot to add "crack" into their list, I'm already jonesing for another bowl of this.CONS*The bits of leaves in the sauce kept interfering with my enjoyment of the dish. I know they are important to impart that fresh bright taste, but I felt like I was chewing my cud. It was like having bits of lawn clippings in my food and was annoying. I think this could be offset by using more veggies than I did.*The coconut powder can be lumpy and grainy, see tips belowCOOKING TIPS*The sauce thickens quickly and wants to stick to bottom of pan, I'd cook the meat to ALMOST done and then combine with the sauce.*Mix the coconut powder and water together, and then whisk in the paste. My coconut powder was lumpy as heck and left a grainy texture and bits in my gravy. Or, save the coconut powder for another use and just sub in a can of your favorite coconut milk. Eliminate or drastically reduce the water if you do this, try the can of coconut milk first and if you need more moisture add in a little water.*Use coconut oil to cook the meat in, it adds a nice flavor to the sauce.*this makes a LOT of food. Especially if you add more than just meat, you could easily feed over 4 people with it. I froze an extra serving to see how it stood up to the process, and it didn't separate. Package your leftovers into lunches or future dinnersNUTRITION INFO: Typically I see coconut powder with sugar of some kind added, but this only lists maltodextrin. The Rendang Paste does have palm sugar and sugar listed in the first few ingredients. Just the box ingredients have 75 grams of carbohydrate, with 45 grams of that coming from sugar. That's a lot of sugar bang for the buck.  The entire box also has 1650 calories, 135 g. of fat, with 105 of that being non-animal saturated fat from the coconut. The entire box also has 3450 mg of sodium. Let's face it though folks, no one is going to sit and eat the entire box. (I know, I tried!)If the sauce weren't grainy from the bits of coconut powder, I would give this a 5-star rating. I would love to see this sold as a paste packet or jar, so that I could use my own coconut milk brand. This curry paste is SO amazing, I would love to be able to buy it by the jar and use it on ribs, burgers, chicken, etc.UPDATE: Using the tips to preblend the coconut powder, my second batch was smooth. This also does work with a can of coconut milk, omit the water. This product is available on Subscribe and Save, and it was so good that I signed up to get regular shipments of it. When I have bad bad food cravings and am tempted to go drive out to get something, now I always have this on hand and it is so satisfying! It's good with chicken, beef, and pork. I haven't tried any other meats. But d*mn, you gotta try this.

column9: Restauraunt Quality Beef Rendang - Easy to make
column10: I lived in Asia for 3 years and one of my favorite cuisines was Indonesian/Malaysian.  Both countries serve-up slightly different versions of Beef Rendang, which is one of my all-time favorites.  When I first moved back to Chicago I didn't know of any restaurants that served this dish (I've since found two) so I attempted to make my own sauce, from scratch, following a recipe I'd found on-line.  I don't know what I did wrong, but what came out didn't very closely resemble true Beef Rendang.  A little later on I purchased a sauce packet in an asian grocery. No... it didn't quite have the same flavor either.  Well,  it's been 6 or 7 years since those failed attempts and low and behold, I stumbled upon the Prima Rendang Curry.  De-licious! I followed the simple instructions and ... I have to say. It's pretty darn good!

I agree with the review above. It's really difficult to find this type of authentic flavor in the US. This box is ready to cook and is super easy to work with. I like to use two boxes, throw my own fresh meat/veggies in it. The results are restaurant quality. I will be trying the rest of the Prima Taste Curries now.

The cuisine of Singapore/Malaysia is my favorite in the world. And rendang is one of my favorite foods. This was pretty tasty, and very easy to make. It was hard to empty the packets, but I just rinsed them out with some of the cooking water. The kit is very large, though, I wish it came in a smaller size. It was just mildly spicy, not hot at all. The ingredients are authentic. I found it a bit on the sweet side. It's not as good as my daughter's (who is married to an Indonesian, and lived there for years...rendang is both Malay and Indonesian). But as I live in an area where I can't possibly get even half of the ingredients required, it was a treat to have this again.

column9: Tasty, fast and easy- what more can you ask for?
column10: Was not sure what to expect, as the box was a little basic and the instructions were pretty short.  Just brown your beef in oil, remove, and then add the coconut powder, water and the solid curry paste and then stir.  Once the mix was boiling, I reduced the heat and added the beef back in.  Very simple and easy.But, surprise of surprises-- its really good.  I served it up over brown rice and green beans, and received rave reviews on the meal.  The curry and coconut milk flavors are strong, and the big chucks of spices really pay off in the taste of the curry.  If I had been served this in a restaurant I would have been happy.  To make it at home in about 20-30 minutes was really nice.  I think the sauce kit also would have been good with chicken or pork as well.I am looking forward to trying more Prima Taste stuff based on how good this was.  Highly Recommended!

column9: Easy to prepare and makes a tasty meal
column10: I have made beef rendang from scratch in the past, but very rarely-I don't have the 6+ hours it takes to make the dish.  That said, this is an adequate substitute for a quicker version.Following the instructions, I first seared the beef, then removed it from the pan before putting in the paste packet (difficult to get out of the foil envelope), coconut powder and water, brought it to a boil before adding in the beef.  Whisking out the lumps of coconut powder took a minute or two, but other than that the process of preparing the meal was simple.  I used stew meat (just like I do for homemade rendang), and cooked it for about 45 minutes on a low simmer.  The sauce was thick and tasted good, not as spicy as I make it (but it suits my children's palates), with a nice heat and a decent coconut taste.  The meal would likely come together a lot faster if tenderloin is used, as suggested on the packet.

I am a pescetarian, have been for a long time. I don't eat meat, ever, however on occasion I'll eat fish. I've been on that diet for years and it suits me. Not eating meat and not drinking alcohol or soft drinks has turned out to be a terrific way to keep myself slim and looking good.So when I got this curry mix, naturally I made it with fish instead of beef. I used a cheap white fish from Vietnam that I bought frozen. The fish was okay, pan friend with nothing but butter and lemon, nothing extraordinary, but when used with this sauce, it was delicious. I'd swear I was eating off the street in Thailand or at an expensive Thai restaurant in the States.Yes, it's a tiny bit pricy and yes I could make up a curry sauce just as good from scratch, but not in the small amount of time it took me to make up a meal using this. And this, cooked with fish in it and served over a bed of rice, is truly delicious. I will have this curry mix in my house forever and will use it on a regular basis.

column9: Delicious Spicy and best of all Easy!
column10: So you're having company or want to impress a special person with a nice meal, if you're cooking-challenged like me this Rendang Curry makes a great impression. The box contains the sauce and spices that you will need. All you must provide is the beef and rice.The instructions are so easy even I made a great meal! After cooking the meat, simply add the packets to boiling water. Add the beef. Serve over rice.The coconut flavor is subtle. I would say the curry is a medium level of spicy hot. The sauce is tasty and would be delicious simply over rice and would work well with alternative ingredients such as tofu or even lamb. The only part of the mix that my dinner companion didn't like was the lime leaves: within the spice packet there are quarter inch pieces of leaf. They have a particular, distinct flavor. I thought the leaves were fine, but they do have a distinct flavor and texture that some people may not like.This curry mix is not exactly healthy. Two tablespoons are listed at 110 calories, 7 grams of saturated fat, and 230mg of sodium.  However for a delicious tasty spicy treat that can be prepared from start to finish in 15min I rate this as a 5-star product. It was as delicious as going out to a restaurant and a whole lot more affordable.

I live in the sticks and good curry is impossible to get here.  Theoretically I could make it but I don't.  I often purchase packaged curries and sauces since I just don't want to cook them.This was quick and easy to whip up.  It made a lot more than I thought it would.  I ended up cooking 2 whole round steaks for the sauce.  The coconut powder took a minute to whisk in but other than that it was fine.  It tastes great and the price is comparable to the other package curries and sauces I but regularly.My only complaint is that it is pretty oily.  Fully cooked, there were still little pools of oil across the top of the dish.

Great product.I'm a lousy cook.So this product saved my diner. It's easy to prepare and delicious.I followed the instructions and used some prime beef.Everybody loved it! The coconut NUT and the coconut flavor seemed very fresh and rich. I do not like peanuts... but I could hardly feel it.Great if you want to have something different. So go for it!Suggestion: I like a thicker sauce. So it all depends on how you prepare it. And I like onions, so I put some in it too. Loved it.

column9: 9 grams  fat in 2 Tablespoons...and lots of sugar. This is mostly palm oil and seasonings.
column10: Ah, it's the old rule that things that taste good are rarely good for you...well, they can be made healthier but the nutritional label on this one is sketchy.I think it's highly misleading to say a serving size it 2 Tablespoons. You couldn't do anything with 2 Tablespoons of sauce except for put it atop one baby red potato.  However, in just that small of serving size you are already weighing it at 7 grams SATURATED fat and 9 grams total fat.  In those 2 tablespoons you also have 100 calories...this is without the protein and rice you might add as a consumer. Tack on 230 mg of sodium in those two tiny spoonfuls and 3 grams sugar and you are likely to finish this meal wondering why you didn't have a Big Mac.The label says it's "family size" and you'd best have a big family who plans on cooking other dishes for dinner if everyone is only supposed to eat 2 Tablespoons.This rates a D minus on the health websites.That said, until you add meat, it has no cholesterol.  There is some good. Unless you, of course, do plan to add meat...then you are consuming basically a Big Mac and fries if you eat normal portions.For me that's just too much. Taste isn't everything...I believe in everything in moderation, but even in moderation with two spoonfuls of sauce you just have too much saturated fat here from the oil.So let's look at the ingredients. Normally coconut milk is used in curry which is a good fat...instead they used PALM OIL (vegetable oil: bad fat) as the main ingredients and then added in the flavor of coconut as a spice:ngredientsRendang Paste (heat sterilized) Vegetable Oil (palm olein), Chili, Galangal, Palm Sugar, Onion,Shallot, Sugar,Pandan Leaf (Pandanus Amaryllifolius), Garlic, Salt, Lemon Grass, Soya Sauce (extract of soya bean, wheat, salt, sugar, carmel color), Fennel, Coriander, Cumin, Kaffer Lime Leaf, Cloves, Turmeric, white Pepper, Cinnamon Prima Coconut Premix (dehydrated) Coconut Milk Powder (coconut milk solids, maltodextrin, sodium caseinate), maltodextrinSo basically this is a big ol' packet of vegetable oil with seasonings to make it taste more like a regular curry...and a whole lotta sugar to make ya love it.Not my thing.

column9: Hot?  Not for me, but for my guest it was...
column10: I LOVE cooking with new flavors, and pride myself on being an adventurous cook.  I don't do beef much (a few times a year), but happened to have some primo beef that was perfect for this.I seared my beef in a cast iron skillet on all sides, then cooked partway through.I mixed the coconut powder, water, and oil in a Pyrex measuring cup, and added it to the pan, then added the paste.  It blended together perfectly!  No lumps or issues.  *BUT, I am not a fan of the dehydrated vegetable pieces--those were a distraction and we picked them out in the end.*I cooked the meat through with the lid on, at a med-low heat, stirring every few minutes, and turning the beef.To go with it, I made a mixture of different colors of quinoa and a side of lightly sauteed asparagus with garlic.The beef took on the color of the sauce (all the way through the meat).  I found this interesting.The flavor, I thought, was VERY good, especially with the quinoa.  I actually could have just eaten it with the vegetables and quinoa, and opted out of the beef altogether.  My guest, on the other hand, found it spicy (hot-spicy) and although he liked the flavor of the dish, said he would not order it for himself due to how his particular tastebuds perceived that hot-ness.  My mother and her husband would have found it altogether inedible, because they cannot handle any "spice" in their foods.  Just an FYI, in case you have sensitive people to feed.It made a LOT of food.  We two adults ate about 1/3 of the dish.I personally would order this for me, but since he can't enjoy it, it puts a damper on my recommendation.  I hate making a dinner that ends up too spicy for my guest(s).  I know that I have a system that loves spicy foods, so I tend to overlook this part of creating a menu.  It's not like you can opt out of that sauce with this dinner.  ;)I guess I'll just order similar dishes for myself when we go out to eat ;)

I had never eaten Rendang curry before, but I love curry so I thought I'd try it. It very tasty and felt like a restaurant quality dish. I had some left over slow cooked beef that I simply heated up and added to the sauce (tip: mix the coconut powder and water together before adding the curry paste) and let it heat a bit more. It took me less than ten minutes to throw together, certainly the quickest dinner I've ever made. I cooked for two and we had enough leftovers for another dinner. Note: keep an eye out for the kaffer lime leaves, they are not meant to be eaten.The reason I demote this kit to 4 stars, is that I really don't see it as all that great a deal. Its about $7 a box and all you are really making is a sauce. I would much rather buy the curry paste and coconut milk separately. On Amazon you can get a set of 12 Rendang curry paste packages for $25. Coconut milk ranges from about $2-3. So about $4-5 a meal instead of $7. Plus you have the advantage of the less processed coconut milk.

column9: Quick and easy to make; bit too much on the sweet side
column10: Overall this was an OK curry. On the plus side, it's very easy to make - basically cook the beef, then add in the curry mix (2 pouches), simmer and serve.  I added in some vegetables and served it over Jasmine rice.My complaints are that it had more of a sweet taste than I was expecting or cared for. It's a bit oily as well, and could also use a somewhat greater kick with regard to spices. It also had larger pieces of leaves that were not all that appealing.Although I made this with beef, I think it would be as good, and perhaps better, with lamb or pork. The sauce alone is workable over rice and veggies should you prefer not to eat meat.It made for an interesting dish that everyone ate, but I probably would not get this again. I prefer the taste of Indian curries (ideally from scratch, but in a pinch the Taste of India pouches are pretty good).

I have never tried a rendang curry dish before.  Preparation was easy - just mix the curry sauce paste and the powdered coconut in a sauce pan, add 4/5 cup of water, and bring to a boil.  Add slightly browned beef and serve over rice.  In my case, I used seasoned soy strips.  The sauce is spicy and very sweet - too sweet for my taste, in fact.  It was an interesting culinary experience but once is enough for me.

column9: Love it, but don't have a comparison
column10: I have never been anywhere to eat native curries.  I have ate a few Indian restaurants that my immigrant friends told me were GREAT.  So, just saying, I cannot compare this to 'authentic.'  I'm a Kitchen's of India fan.  This is a lot like those packs, in my opinion.It said to use beef loin.  I wasn't sure about that, so I got top sirlion.  I cubed it. I used olive oil to brown it because I always do.  It's an incredibly easy dish to make.  I served mine with mashed potatoes.  I usually serve curries with rice, but it was on the box and I thought what the heck.  It was good, and offered my non-curry eating child something he liked too.It's good and well balanced.  It tastes fairly bright.  It's spicy hot without being painful.  Like perhaps a medium salsa.  The smooth creaminess of the coconut gives it just a hint of sweetness, without seeming at all sugary.  I can tell the turmeric in it is potent - I have chronic hives and after a big bowl they went away, so it must have a fair bit of good strong turmeric in it.  Kitchens of India's curries also has that effect.One tip is to use a pair of scissors to open the pouches - the coconut is powdery and it will go everywhere if you aren't careful, and the pouches do not tear easily at all.  I tried to grab a knife to open mine- that was a messy mistake.The only thing I didn't like was the lemon grass.  The flavor was great but the pieces were just particular stem-y and dry.  They are easy to avoid though.I like it and would eat it again.  I'd add green peppers and onions next time.  I usually put those in my curries.  I don't know about traditional or whatever, I just know what I like.It was *really* good with top sirlion.  I'm sure it would be great with round steak or mock tenderloin as well.

This is my first venture into trying Prima Taste Rendang Curry.ProsVery easy to prepareInstructions were simpleSauce was very goodOnly need to add water and beefConsAlthough the flavor was wonderful, I had more than my share of leaves (?)/spice chunks in my portion as did my dinner partner.The coconut powder was a bit lumpy, but I see another reviewer suggested mixing coconut powder and water first and whisk in the paste.  Probably a good idea.I did cook my beef until almost done (rather than to medium done as the directions suggest)and then added to the sauce because the sauce thickens very quickly.All in all, I thought this was easy and good.

This is a nice pack of dried coconut milk (that mixes very easily) and a generous packet of curry (curry is simply the word for "sauce" in Tamil).  This is typical redang curry, flavored with cinnamon, coriander, cumin, onion, fennel, cloves, ginger, and tumeric.In my opinion, it tastes great.  None of the flavors dominate, but the coconut, lime, tumeric, and cinnamon are the most evident (and in that order) aside from the flavor of the meat (they say mix beef, and it really does complement beef much better than it would duck or pork).  I used a relatively lean cut of roast, and it really helped tenderize the meat while enhancing its flavor.In my opinion, the difference between good curry and great curry is the gravy's consistency.  You want just the right thickness.  It helps to add a little more water than seems right, and then cook in a reduction pan until it's just right.  Patience pays off, as does keeping the heat on the low side after you detect boiling.I want to note that I was impressed with the quality of the product.  When I order a box of food mix over the internet, my expectations are quite low, but apparently I was mistaken.  This is probably not restaurant quality per se, but it's much better curry than I'm used to at restaurants.  I love it, and I'll buy it.I used two pounds of beef, and this fed six people.  I snapped a photo and I'll add it to the product page.

column9: Not bad for a 30 minute meal prep time
column10: Preparation: very easy, but the authentic method requires the meat to be stewed for at least 2 hours; hence if you follow the instructions, chicken would be a better choice otherwise use a good cut of meat; otherwise stew the red meat until it is tender.  All it requires is to pre-cook the meat and then part two is mixing the two packages (curry paste and refined coconut milk powder with a cup of water and then bring the meat back into the fold.End product: quite a thick consistency and I added another 1/3 cup of water to thin it out a bitTaste and texture: not sure about the green lemon grass as that was a distraction, but the curry delivered a good heat and taste, and if you prefer it hotter then add a few flakes of red chilies.Authentic: as close as you could cooking it from scratch, but nothing beats the real fresh ingredients.  But as a 30 minute preparation for a busy work night: it was not bad, and I would substitute a softer meat than using beef.

column9: I wish I could give this more stars. Truly delish!
column10: I love curry dishes. This one from Prima is terrific. It's a little spicy hot, has a nice coconut flavor, and is fairly sweet, which I love. I have a sweet tooth and cook a lot of main dishes with a little sugar and/or splenda. Keep this in mind because if you don't like sweet food, you might find this too sweet.I prepared this with an inexpensive cut of beef, cooked it longer than the instructions called for to tenderize the beef, and put it over rice. One thing I did was to put a little more water than called for -- 1-1/2 cups instead of 4/5's. This way you get a less pasty sauce that pours more easily over rice. I also think if you made this with chicken it would be just as good.The leaves? I guess I'm a little unusual but I actually liked them. I like crunchy foods such as soft shell crabs. So I had no issue with the leaves. If you don't like them, take them out after cooking but before serving.I would say this is enough to serve about 4 hearty eaters, or 2 with leftovers. The suggestion on the box that this serves 15 is unreasonable.I often buy curry and Indian meals prepackaged by Kitchens of India. I love those for the convenience, low cost, and taste ... but the Prima Rendang Curry is significantly better tasting. I think Prima is more restaurant quality whereas Kitchens of India is more akin to fast food.  That's a good way to compare them.  Kitchens of India is a lot cheaper but you get more product with Prima and the taste is considerably better. I would not hesitate to serve Prima to dinner guests but I wouldn't with Kitchens of India unless it was the most casual of circumstances.I will definitely be buying this in the future and can't wait to have it again.
