column9: Prepared in under a half hour: it tastes great!
column10: My wife and I love many kinds of curries. We either make our own or eat out for curries at least once a month. Rendang style was new to us as was the broad concept of "dry curry." I have since learned that Indonesian style Rendang curries are prepared across a scale ranging from wet and juicy to ultra-dry. Among dry styles, in the very driest form all the moisture in an Indonesian Rendang Curry is absorbed into the hunks of beef, with no remaining sauce for rice to soak up.I watched and kibitzed as my wife first cut two boneless, skinless chicken breasts (approximately one pound) into one inch cubes, then followed the instructions on the box for beef. The quantity of water to be added was 4/5 cup.First she cooked the chicken cubes till about 90% done -- sauteed in a frying pan using pan spray. She then set the chicken aside. She next mixed inside the same still hot pan the full content of the two pouches (paste and dried coconut powder) enclosed inside the cardboard box labeled as Ready-to-Cook Sauce Kit for Rendang Curry as well as the recommended 4/5 cup of water. She then mixed it all very thoroughly and without haste into a finished sauce and then added the chicken back into the frying pan. She cooked the whole combined brew for another ten minutes. Then she served us both the Rendang curry over brown rice. My wife added no other ingredients beyond what the instructions on the box called for.We both enjoyed the resulting product very much. Each of us easily detected and distinguished a variety of delicious ingredients. Striking was the size and texture of some of the larger leaves (which, however, had little detectable flavor). The quantity of sauce that my wife mixed left far more sauce than the chicken absorbed. At table we added, if we cared to, yogurt and shredded coconut.My wife and I have since tried the warmed up leftover curry twice (adding peas and onions) and it tasted just as good as when first made. There was definitely a "fresh" homemade feel both to the first prepared final mix and, surprisingly, to the leftovers as well. The "heat" from pepper perceived by tongue and palate was toward the low to mid level on any  spectrum of hot peppers. I found Rendang curry just a tiny bit sweeter than I prefer. To my wife, however, it was perfect.There was nothing "dry" about our our curry chicken. But it tasted great! And we look forward to buying more.-OOO-

column4: Ursula K. Raphael "AstraDaemon of The Zombiep...
column10: I love curry dishes...my mom has shared a lot of recipes that she learned while she was in Cyprus (I know that's not Indonesia, but that's where she learned a lot of Thai, Indonesian & other exotic dishes), so I thought I would give this a try.It will never be as good as making your own from scratch, but if you prefer to keep cooking fairly simple, this is pretty decent.My mom was one of the ones who I shared this dish with, so I could have her opinion too...she thought it was a bit oily, a little too sweet for her liking, and we both would have preferred it to be spicier.I might try this again with different meat...lamb instead of beef, for instance. I think the meat's absorption of the flavor is what makes a difference.

column9: Winning Taste and Easy to Make
column10: If you are a fan of Thai food, you will love this. The taste is robust with just the right amount of heat.Not so hot that it overpowers the flavor. This product has healthy ingredients, which made it a big plus for me.No trans-fats and only a few grams of sugar per serving. Low carb. Highly recommend!

I wasn't expecting much from this product but I was very happy after I tasted it.  I make my own curries since I live out in the sticks but sometimes I don't want to go to all that work. I added a bunch of veggies, chopped small Thai chile, and chicken to the mix.  My husband loved it too. I couldn't find how much water to add but cup and a half did the job. I have already ordered more.

column9: Great "authentic" flavor, a bit too sweet
column10: In the box are two envelopes: the curry paste and coconut powder. There is enough to make quite a lot of curry sauce. You can add stuff like fresh bananas, peppers, spinach, chickpeas, raisins, apple chunks, etc. to make enough for more than 6 people. Adding more veggies will make the result more of a stew with more liquid than the picture on the box. I served this curry on top of a mix of brown and wild rice and with sambals (cashew nuts, chutney, mango slices...) on the side. I adjusted the sweetness by adding a bit of cayenne, ginger... whatever spices you like.The box said it's a beef curry but I used lamb instead. You can use any meat or fish that will stand up to the strong flavor of the curry. The flavor is very 'authentic' but it should be because it's a product of Singapore. Singaporeans are proud to be a nation of Foodies.The illustrated instructions are very clear, easy to follow, only 2 steps: saute the meat, mix water with the paste and coconut, put on top of the meat.The two reasons I did not give this curry sauce 5 stars are it's hard to get all the paste out of the envelope. I squeezed out as much as I can, then squeezed the envelope between two chopsticks to squeeze out the rest. The coconut powder was easy. The other reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is it's too sweet for my taste.My guests loved the flavor so the flavor is 5 stars.Oh the nutritional value given on the box is 110 calories for 2 tablespoons presumably of the sauce alone, without meat, etc. Coconut is what makes it so high in calories. Remember that a single serving of the 'final' curry probably doesn't have more than 2 tablespoons of sauce on it.

I had high hopes for this product.  Having spent a fair bit of time in Singapore & Malaysia I have come to love the regional cuisine.  Especially Beef Redang which if you have never had it is a very tasty (muslim) dry style curry.  It is a process to make at home - lots of ingredients and slow cooking to yield a savory curry of tender beef.  When prepared correctly it is a knockout dish.  When I saw this product and the great reviews I thought it might be a good way to make a quicker version when the mood strikes.  Having said that  I cannot recommend this to anyone who has had this great dish nor anyone who would like to try it for the first time.  The kit is easy enough - stir fry beef and then add spice paste, coconut milk powder and water.  Simmer until tender and then voila beef redang.  If only - the mix gave off a faintly chemical odor which i found disturbing and off putting.  Beef Redang usually (like many dishes of the region) has a funky (good) smell from the use of fermented shrimp paste or belachan. its strong but pleasant - this in no way smelled of that.  putting aside the off smell I tried the curry and found it to be not just mild but flavorless.  Maybe this was an issue with this batch but I could no way recommend this product to anyone.

column9: The Curry Doesn't Burn You As Much As The Price Does
column10: I love curry.  Any kind of curry.  Red, yellow, brown.  Indian, Japanese, Thai. It's all good and delicious.  So I was savoring this dish.  And guess what?  It's great.  I love the flavor, and the texture is nice too.It does have a couple issues.  The heat was a little light for me.  I want my curry hot, and this was too weak for me.  I did appreciate that the curry taste wasn't too light.  Some of that curry powder you buy in the store forces you to use a pound of it because it has very little flavor.  But this was a good pack.So why the low star rating then?  The price!  I think this is outrageous!  There is no way it's worth what it lists for.  It's good, but not that good!  I'll stick with my "have-to-use-a-pound-in-it" powder.  Thanks.

column9: Decent, a tad pricey but way too sweet for me!
column10: The Prima Taste Rendance Curry kit, is a bit pricey at about $4-5 a kit - you add your meat (chicken, beef, lamb, etc)...the flavor is decent, it's tasty but I was wishing for a bit more bite or kick in a curry sauce, and it was too overwhelmingly sweet for someone like me, who doesn't eat a lot of sugar...I mostly eat fruit sugars or some honey or raw sugar, and in normal quantities: I tasted an awful lot of sugar in this sauce, so it just isn't the sauce for me.  This may be someone's choice, but it's not mine...decent flavor, great that the spices and sauce are all together and easy to make, but it's a tad pricey for what you get...

I found this curry sauce kit to be really tasty and able to create a large amount of sauce from one kit.Instead of using the recommended beef I used oven roasted chicken thighs and about 3 lbs of sauteed vegetables.  My veggie mix consisted of yellow onion, cauliflower, broccoli, pasilla chile peppers, and jalepeno peppers.  All cut into 1" - 1.5" pieces except for the chiles which were sliced into 0.25" rings.I roasted the chicken and removed the skin.  I then sauteed the veggies in a large wok with some olive oil.  Once the veggies were near done I added the large bag of Rendang curry sauce, the packet of dried coconut milk powder, and a cup of water.  The sauce mixed with the ingredients well and when all the veggies were thoroughly coated I added the chicken thighs and gently mixed to coated them as well.  Although I did not have rice on my plates there would have been enough sauce to drizzle on the rice without the sauce being watery.  A pasta would have worked well in place of rice.The sauce came out very flavorful without overwhelming the the vegetables or chicken.  The coconut powder -- of which I had some reservations -- added a rich coconut flavor without any chemical or chalkiness.This curry sauce kit made a delicious curry stir-fry dinner last night that was good enough to have again for lunch today.  I would certainly buy this curry kit in the future.

column9: Too mild and sweet, but not bad
column10: I received a single box of Prima Taste Rendang Curry Sauce Kit free from the Amazon Vine program, in exchange for writing a review of the product.We lived in Malaysia and India, so we love curry and enjoy it at home on a regular basis.  I usually use lamb or chicken, but this time I used beef as directed on the box.  We enjoyed the flavors of lemongrass and coconut in this sauce, although it wasn't quite spicy enough for us.  I actually added some extra curry powder to it before it was done cooking.  We all thought it was a little too sweet, but overall was very tasty when served over rice.The current price for this product is around $6.50 per box.  That seems a little on the expensive side when I am adding my own meat, vegetables and rice.  The box made six very small servings (we have six in our family).  If you're looking for an authentic tasting and less expensive curry mix, try Kitchens of India Paste for Butter Chicken Curry.This was nice to try just for the experience, but I will continue to make my own curries because I can do it much cheaper without the mix.

Technically, I'm giving this a 3.5 star rating (my husband is the Indian cook in the family and gave this 3 stars to my four).  The blend of spices is at least on par with other brands and quite tasty.  The flavors seem to be a bit on the sweet side, though those liking the spicier flavors should be pleased.  Preparation was easy and all made for a quick and good meal.

For full disclosure, I am nearly an idiot in the kitchen.  I can short-order cook some stuff on a griddle and boil water but that's about it.  Mercifully, that's pretty much the skill set needed to make a really tasty dish with this kit!If you're a fan of coconut curries, this one will be a hit.  The flavors are bold and complex, far more tasty than any boxed dinner I've ever eaten.  It's got a little zip in the sauce but certainly isn't "Thai hot".  If you can handle "medium" at most far eastern restaurants, it won't pose any problems for you, as it would certainly be considered less than "medium".Two tips:  1)  Do make sure you pick up (or make) some favorite fried rice or noodles to serve with your curry.2)  The recipe calls for beef tenderloin.  Don't skimp here if you want the "WOW" factor.  I used a cheaper cut of beef on my first try and while it remained tasty was chewier than intended.3)  If you're lactose intolerant, this product may cause you some issues.  One family member (possibly even yours truly) didn't think to take his Lactaid ahead of time and had some minor tummy trouble later.  I wouldn't let that dissuade you from trying, just be aware.I've got another box on my "Wish List" already and can't wait to order it again.  ENJOY!

I'd never had Indonesian or Malaysian food and was eager to try a curry from a new region.This slightly sweet, fairly mild curry was terrific on vegetables and rice, unlike any Thai or Indian curry and very fresh tasting. From a texture standpoint, I wasn't fond of the tiny leaf pieces in the mix, but I can look beyond that because the flavor was so good and it was easy to prepare. This was more than enough curry for a family of three (probably ideal for four people) and a great introduction to Indonesian/Malaysian cuisine. This will occasionally be on my shopping list. Recommended.

Rendang is a Malay curry dish not easily found in the US so I was surprised to see it offered on Amazon. This package mix is easy to make and produces a lot of flavor. The sauce mix (after adding in the coconut mix) is so concentrated and flavorful that I was able to mix in almost twice as much beef as required and still get good flavor through out. One package definitely produces a lot. There was a bit too much coconut 'milk' in the package so I reduced it when cooking this. The green 'grass' like pieces in the mix are pandan leaves. This ingredient is actually uncommon for this dish, as pandan generally gets added to desserts, like vanilla. Interestingly, I wouldn't have noticed it if I hadn't seen it on the ingredient list. All in all, this is a good mix and with S&S, it's less than $6 per pack. That's not a bad deal at all for this hard to find dish.

column9: It's like getting Asian food to-go but without worrying about the pick up...
column10: I love Thai curries but have never had a curry from Singapore so I wasn't sure what to expect.  It was very similar (extremely delicious!!!) to the Thai curries I am addicted to but without having to pay as much and with the added bonus of picking what veggies I want (no cabbage!).  I thinly sliced and sauteed chicken, frozen yellow squash, frozen crinkle carrots and frozen crinkle zucchini and I would not change a thing!  It makes a ton so I invited family over and they all asked for the recipe.  I had to admit that it required no work as I just pulled stuff out of the freezer and used a box curry. No one could believe it and they ended up ordering the curry for themselves.  I didn't share the leftovers and ate them all week at work.  That is saying something as I don't like leftovers!I whisked together the coconut powder, water and paste in a separate bowl before adding it to the meat.  No lumps and a beautiful, and amazing, "homemade" curry! Next time I want to try it with shrimp and bay scallops.  Great.. now I'm hungry.

This was so delicious, and has such a great taste! I really like Kitchens of India products, but this Prima Taste curry is even better. I think that the reason is that there are two packets that you use in preparation instead of just one. It tasted just like nice curry in a nice restaurant.You could make this with anything besides beef, also, but I just tried it with beef.Pros:+Very delicious taste+Makes a good amount of curry+Very versatileCons:-Not extremely spicy (I like my curry hot)-Takes more preparation time than Kitchens of India, even though it's still pretty simple to prepare

column9: Absolutely Delicious - Comparable to a Good Restaurant
column10: I am a big fan of curry and have not been able to find something easy to make at home that matches the curry dishes I can get at some of our local favorite restaurants.  This comes pretty darn close.  The main advantage I see to this is that the sauce is quite easy to make (even for someone like me who brings very few skills to the kitchen).  The aroma that permeated the house as I prepared this was wonderful.  The only drawback I see to this product is the slightly high price.  However, when compared to a comparable meal at a quality restaurant, it is definitely worth it.  Enjoy!

column9: makes a restaurant quality dish with lots of flavor
column10: This was my first time cooking with a Prima Taste kit and was impressed by the full flavor when making curry.  I opted to use shrimp since I didn't have beef on hand and it still came out very delicious.  The flavors are complex and remind me of Thai and Malay foods I've eaten at restaurants.  For those who don't like spicy foods, this does pack quite a punch but not too over the top.  Only slight negatives - there are a bunch of little leaves (keffir lime leaves, I believe) which need to be picked out before serving or while eating as they are not really chewable.  Also, when mixing in the coconut powder blend which comes in a paper pouch, it can be messy.  It left a bit of powder around the stovetop so take extra care to open slowly and/or over the pot/pan where you are mixing the curry to avoid the extra cleanup.  Bon appetit!

What can I say?  This is a delicious curry sauce that is easy to use so makes a great addition to the pantry.  Who isn't busy these days?  With running kids to sports practices, school events and music lessons, it feels like we are always on the go and I don't often (okay, never) have time to spend hours cooking.  Having a kit like this in the pantry really does make it easier to feed my family good food in a short space of time.To use it, I get some rice going in the rice cooker, then grab a pack of seafood mix from the freezer.  The seafood thaws quite quickly in a bowl of water so when the rice is almost done, I can add a little oil to the frypan, saute the seafood, add the curry mix....and serve.  The entire meal is ready in the time it takes the rice cooker to cook the rice - couldn't be easier, and the meal is enjoyed by all.

I am lucky to live in an area with a large Asian community, and we have an excellent Malaysian restaurant that we visit frequently, and many Asian groceries.  Therefore, I've been able to try several varieties of randang curry, from both of these types of places.  This is the best version of homemade that I have ever tried.  I'm sure that the addition of several of the traditional spices of the region (pandan leaf, lemongrass, and kafir lime leaf, among others) is what gives it that restaurant quality taste. What is also similar to a restaurant version, unfortunately is the calorie and fat content...and this doesn't even include the meat, approximately 1600 per box, so take that into consideration when determining portion size.  I would suggest you stretch it with some vegetables, potatoes, peas or broccoli would all go well with this.  Also read the allergy  advisory on the packaging if you have any issues with nuts, shellfish, fish sesame , eggs, soy or mik.  I am pleased that they do not add MSG to this high quality product.  Enjoy, but not too much~

column9: Gave it to my Mother in Law to try
column10: And this was her report:We ate the Rendang Curry last night and it was delicious.  My only negative was a dark leaf in the sauce which was a little tough to eat.  I added chicken instead of beef and also added green peppers and onions to give it more substance, then served it with rice.  I would buy this product.I dock one star fir the tough green leaf, but sounds like a winner!

column9: The Bad Out Weighs the Good
column10: Yes, I have to conclude that the bad wins here.But first the good. It was very easy to make, quick and tasted quite good, surprisingly. Just a little hot..you can always make it hotter if you wish...but very flavorful, very tasty.But the bad..First, this is not going to be a cheap meal. One box would cost about $7. Then you need the meat. 28 ozs. of beef tenderloin, as they suggest, at what, $15-20 a pound and you would be looking at $30-$40-$50 dollars. It is good, but not that good. I used maybe half that amount of beef, because that is what I had on hand and added a lot of veggies, but it still would not be cheap.Then, there is the nutritional values. The box contains almost 1700 calories. Add in meat and serve with rice..Of course they get around that, in their minds but listing the box as containing 15 serving! Really? Well, that would be one very, very small serving. Realistically it contains 4-5 serving. Calculate 20% of the 135g of fat, 20% of the 3450mg of salt..and that is without the fat to cook the meat and/or veggies in or the meat itself...and this is not a healthy dish.

I have tried other Indian food kits in the past, and have been underwhelmed, to say the least. Not so with "Prima Taste Rendang Curry Sauce Kit, 12.7-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4)", which was a real surprise for me. Easy to prepare as directed, the taste is comparable to that of restaurant-quality Indian food. The spices are well balanced, while the taste and texture of the meat when prepared in this kit is both rich and succulent.For Indian food lovers, "Prima Taste Rendang Curry Sauce Kit" is a real treat and well worth snapping up.

First time I have tried using a packet for curry sauce; will definitely be using it again! I used Flank steak for the meat and added onions. I mixed the coconut powder with water before combining it; was afraid it might not blend well (has a tendency to do so). Otherwise, all very easy and a great meal served with fresh pita.The flavor is bright and full of zip. If you simply take the time to savor each bite, you will find it is a true sensory experience in taste and textures.

This is an excellent curry sauce and makes for a quick dinner with rice and vegetables.  The intention of this curry sauce kit is to make dry beef curry.  The original idea is for the traditional Singapore dry curry to tenderize tough cuts of meat.  Included in this kit is the Rendang paste and premium coconut mix which is dry.  You are to provide 28oz of sliced beef, chicken or lamb and cook it, then make the gravy and put them together and serve with rice or mashed potatoes.  Since we are vegetarians, I substituted sliced soy meat.  The kit makes a plentiful amount of gravy.  The curry gravy is full of flavor since it contains so many spices and not too hot for our taste.

I found Prima Taste Rendang Curry to be absolutely delicious! The taste is very authentic, rich with spices and complex flavors. It is super simple to prepare. I added not only meat, but some fresh veggies as well. You just won't believe how fresh this curry tastes!

I have never eaten or tasted Singaporean food, but I have tried Thai coconut curry, and this is somewhat Singaporean coconut curry is somewhat similar.A box has enough curry for 4 people (about 2 adults, and 2 children). I recommend using all the curry in one setting, as the curry is in plastic bags and therefore hard to refrigerate unless you put them in plastic container.Ingredients: Chili, galangal, onion, shallot, pandan leaf, garlic, candlenut, ginger, lemon grass, fennel, coriander, cumin, kaffir lime leaf, cloves, turmeric, white pepper, cinnamon.Preparation: Cut open the two plastic bags into a pan with some water (4/5 cup of water), mix it well, and bring it to a boil.If you dont like your curry too sweet, just add less of the coconut part (the coconut curry is separated from the spicy curry)Like how another reviewer mentioned, this curry is high in fat and sugar, so it should not be the main part of your meal but more like to coat your meats and veggies in something delicious.It was very tasty and I really did enjoy it!The package says there is no added MSG, artificial coloring, or added preservatives.For those with allergens, it contains: soybeans, wheat, tree nuts, and milk products

My experience is that I have never been able to get a tasty dish from a box. This product proved me wrong. It was easy to make and very tasty.The coconut taste was smooth and very tasty. I did mix it well before adding it in because I prefer to add liquids without lumps (I followed the advice from one of the reviewers).I also used stew meat which was easily available. Next time I do this dish, I will be using lamb.I highly recommend this product for anyone who likes curry and has little time to cook.

I admit it, I am a huge of fan of easy-to-use curry kits.  Yes, it is not as authentic, as starting from curry spices, coconut milk, etc.  But, when all you need to do is cook some meat (and vegetables), reconstitute the curry, cook a little longer, and enjoy, what's not to like.  Although the instructions call for beef, the Rendang Curry Sauce kit is very flexible.  You can use any meat you want, add vegetables, tofu, you choose it.  There are 2 packets, the Rendang Curry paste and dried coconut milk powder.  Besides the meat and vegetables, you need to add some water.  It is a little on the sweet side, and for those fans of flaming curry, not hot at all, but that is easy to remedy.If you want a flavorful, simple curry kit, look no further.

column9: A Tasty Alternative to Making Beef Rendang from Scratch
column10: WHAT IS BEEF RENDANG?Beef Rendang, or Daging Rendang in bahasa, is a "dry curry" from Sumatra, Indonesia. It may be popular in Singapore, but they did not invent it. According to wikipedia, the Minangkabau migrated from Sumatra to the Malay peninsula, bringing this recipe with them, and now it is popular all the way up into southern Thailand. If you have never had it, the flavors are reminiscent of a Thai curry, especially Masaman curry, which wikipedia says is a Thai version of a Sumatran recipe, quite likely this one. In fact, the name "Masaman" could well be derived from "Muslim".While this dish can be called a curry, it won't taste like anything you'll find in most Indian restaurants. It has some of the same ingredients as South India, and a number of others that are more commonly used in Southeast Asia. The dish is called "dry" because the practice is to cook it down until the sauce no longer flows, instead clinging to the chunks of meat.YOU COULD MAKE IT FROM SCRATCH...Beef rendang is a reasonably easy dish to make from scratch - IF you have access to the ingredients. Cities like Boston, New York, and many others have groceries that carry things like fresh lemongrass, galanga, kaffir lime leaf, pandan leaf, and palm sugar. There is a wealth of recipes available on the Web by searching for "rendang recipe" (without quotes), and with a modest amount of prep time, you could easily do this from scratch and make something that tastes very close to what your average Indonesian cook would make. That is, it would be "authentic," whatever that means....BUT YOU BUY THIS MIX IS FOR CONVENIENCE.But maybe you don't have access to the ingredients. Maybe you don't want to take the time to mince all the various ingredients into a spice paste. Or make coconut milk from a whole coconut (something few people do these days, anyway). But you still like the spicy and unique flavor, or just want to try something new.This mix has two envelopes inside. One is a pre-made spice paste mix that has most of the strong flavors. The other is a powdered coconut milk. Buy some beef, and with some water and vegetable oil, and this mix, you're in business.COMMENTS ON THE PREPARATIONThe recipe is an odd translation from Singaporean measurements. It tells you to buy 28 ounces of beef tenderloin, but then tells you to cut it into pieces 1 cm thick, and requires 4/5 cup of water, measures that are uncommon in an American kitchen. So here is MY version of the recipe, which is basically what is on the box but with some adjustments to the directions, not just the measurements, but also the procedure.Cut the beef into bite-sized pieces, a bit less than 1/2" thick, but it is not critical. Fry it in a wide pan or a wok in some vegetable oil (they say 2 1/2 Tbsp) until it is brown all over. I found that in doing this, there was a fair amount of water in the wok that came from the beef while it was cooking.Now mix in the rendang paste. When you open the coconut milk powder envelope, and you'll see that it has lumps. The easiest path to a smooth sauce is to put it into a sieve or use a strainer with a spoon, shaking the dust and crushing the lumps until it all goes through. The water needed is close to 3/4 cup, but I suggest you start with about half of that, and add more later only if you need to. Stir it well.The package says to cook to the desired doneness. If you want it authentic, you'll need to cook it for a good while, especially if you added as much water as they suggest, in order to get the sauce to dry out. Perhaps you can add less water and save some time. You need to stir it at least every 5 minutes, scraping the bottom to keep it from burning on. Of course, if you get tired of waiting, or too hungry, you can also eat it "wet."An instant mix is supposed to save time and effort. This one does that, but in truth most of the time in making this dish is waiting for it to cook down to thicken, and you have to do that with the mix version, too.You could use stew beef instead of the expensive steak they suggest. That would be a reason to use the full amount of liquid, then slow-cook to make the beef tender and the sauce thick. After all, curries are really a kind of stew.While this mix calls for beef, rendang is commonly made with chicken and lamb, too. I think the original probably used for tougher beef, and perhaps less choice parts than the tenderloin; the long cooking time makes it more tender. You could even make it vegetarian if you like; it would be good that way too. It normally is not made with pork, at least not in Indonesian or Malaysia, because it is a Muslim recipe.HOW DOES IT TASTE?Very good. Not as good as my Indonesian friend Rosita makes it from scratch, or as good as the ones I've had in Indonesia, but very good. My only complaint is that it is a bit too sweet for my taste. The ingredients list both palm sugar and "sugar", presumably the white kind. I could have done without some of the white sugar; you could taste it and perhaps add some lemon juice. The dish could be spicier, but usually Indonesian food is not that out of the pot; instead they have spicy condiments (sambal) on the table for those who like it hot.The box says to serve it with rice (authentic) or mashed potatoes (not authentic, but sounds like a nice idea).BOTTOM LINE4 stars. It's a bit too sweet, in my opinion. And the recipe isn't perfect, such as the odd measurements and a bit too much water.ABOUT MEI am a Vine reviewer and got this mix free for reviewing it. My reviews are my own opinions and are not influenced by getting it for free. I taught a Southeast Asian cooking class for 10 years, and have spent a lot of time all over Southeast Asia studying foods first hand.

column9: Okay, yes.  I want more.  Happy now?
column10: I think I must agree with the reviewer who opined that they forgot to include some kind of opiate in the list of ingredients.  Not literally, but boy, the one family sized serving of this got eaten up fast, even by a teenager who is perversely focused on moving the food on the plate around, more than eating it - usually.I am a huge fan of asian cuisine: Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Vietnamese, Korean, Indian... but have to admit that I'm less conversant with the cuisines of Singapore and Malaysia.  So I didn't bring many expectation to this Rendang curry, other than a vague recollection of a few Malay restaurants years and years ago.  To me, the sauce tasted vaguely Satay-sauce like, but with a gentler peanut flavor and far more complexity in the spicing.  Yes, the lemon grass and other leafy herbs tend to clump up a bit and be overly "chewy", but that's to a Western palate. Asian cultures, which prize such "challenging" textures as beef tendons, would call it authentic, and in any case, there's only a little of that to contend with.The coconut wasn't grainy at all for my family, but then I did cook the pork -- which substituted deliciously for beef -- for 25 to 30 minutes in the sauce, and stirred very thoroughly. (This makes the dish more authentic, as I understand that Rendang curry is suppposed to poach the meat, then fry it as the liquid boils off at the end.)Being cheap, I'd be thrilled actually to be able to buy the sauce packets alone and provide my own can of coconut milk.  I cook mostly from scratch and a near-entree price just for the stuff that goes ON the meal is a little rich for my family's budget.  On the other hand, it's dead simple to make the meal with the sauce so perfectly seasoned - I could see spicing it up to taste, but am kind of glad I didn't succumb to the temptation to add a bit of fresh grated ginger or lime or whatever else I had on hand to "brighten" it - for once, here's a prepared food brand that actually tastes like it hasn't been sitting on a shelf since the last Presidential election.  Convenience and not being tempted to take the family out for a (much more expensive) dinner of the same quality are pretty good arguments for this little kit.If you aren't near Asian Markets, here's your fix.  A bit costly but oh-my-gosh-I-want-some-right-NOW good.

Having spent a decent amount on time in SE Asia (and Singapore specifically) during my childhood, I frequently get cravings for Singaporean-style curry, hawker food and snacks.  As a result I am constantly on a hunt for fresh and authentic ingredients when and where I can get them to attempt to reproduce those dishes at home.  I even have friends send spice mixes and tinned pastes  from Singapore when the markets here fail me.What makes this curry-in-a-packet so good is that it has 2 separate pouches for the spice mix and for the coconut mix. This ensures freshness and authentic flavour when the coconut is added to the mix at the correct moment during the cooking process.  Also, other Singaporean brands do not include the coconut  mixture (requiring additional purchases) or the coconut is already added (affecting flavour).  Prima Taste is one of many curry packets available in Singapore and has a loyal following for its authentic spices.  This is one of the brands that I am sent if my Singaporean friends don't use it all up first!Needless to say, I am really happy that Prima Taste is now available in N. America and through Amazon.To sum:+ Authentic spices in a vacuum-packed pouch+ Pouch of correct amount of coconut mixture (coconut milk plus fresh shredded coconut). So there is no need to buy a separate can of coconut milk and shredded coconut to be partially used.+ All-in-one - just add meat+ No need to hunt down separate ingredients.The only CON is that the prices are double that of Singapore but hopefully should come down as more people discover Prima Taste.

column9: Fairly simple, very mild, quite pleasant
column10: This curry kit is simple to prepare - just one level of complexity up from simply using a jar of curry paste.  You mix the coconut powder with water (not easy to get it lump-free) add the curry paste and bring to the boil.  Add fried beef.  Stir and simmer.The result is far too bland for my taste.  I fried some onions with the beef and chomped on some jalapeño peppers when I ate the meal, to add some kick to it.  If you like very mild curries, this one may suit you.I had it with steamed white rice and a nan bread.  The sauce is creamy and delicately flavored.  It was runnier than it should have been.  If you try it, I suggest using less water than recommended - perhaps half as much - because you can always add more if it threatens to boil dry.  It does after all describe itself as a 'dry beef curry'.

column9: Redolent of kaffir lime and coconut.  Pretty good, but not spectacular
column10: I am a big fan of Thai and Indian curries, and even like that curious yellowy-brown curry that can be found at some Japanese restaurants.  Therefore, my eyes lit up when I spied this curry sauce mix on the list of items that I could obtain free through the Amazon Vine program.  "Ah!" I thought. "A new taste adventure."Sadly, it was not to be so. This sauce is strongly fragrant of kaffir lime leaves and coconut.  The lime turned out to be the dominant flavor.  While I do like kaffir lime, I have come to expect a complexity of flavors in a good curry sauce, and that's where this mix fell short. I was waiting for that "Ahhh...curry....mmmmm..." moment, but it didn't come.  The flavor was oddly pedestrian, almost (but not quite) flat.  While it was a satisfactory dinner for me on an ordinary night, it's certainly not one that I will put on my short list to serve to guests.  Or even my long list, for that matter.To be fair, sometimes dishes with a blend of spices require a bit of time for the flavors to come out.  I let it sit overnight in the refrigerator, reheated it, tasted it with hope in my heart, but detected little appreciable change in the flavor.The recipe called for beef tenderloin, but I used regular old stew meat, and it came out fine.Singles, take note:  Although it yields less than the 15 servings promised by the nutritional label, the recipe makes a generous amount of sauce. It calls for 28 oz of beef, so be prepared for leftovers.  Dividing the contents of the envelopes in half would probably be messy.Amazon does carry some very good curry mixes.  I highly recommend Kitchens of India Paste for Butter Chicken Curry, 3.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6) and Kitchens Of India Curry Paste For Chicken Curry, 3.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6).  Both of these pastes are on the greasy side (I skim the grease off the top before serving), but dang are they good!

column9: Heat it up a bit for a treat
column10: I'm not sure I've ever had Singapore Rendang Curry,  but I love lots of curries, and I liked this, especially when I added a little cayenne or hot sauce to cut the sweetness and brighten the flavors.  The powdered coconut was an interesting ingredient.  Not everybody likes super spicy food, so it's undoubtedly made to appeal to a broader audience, since it's easy to add heat.  It's probably sacrilege, but I liked it better with seafood (scallops!) and chicken than with beef, and I added vegetables, too.  Authenticity is not my main concern; I'm just looking for easy ways to make interesting-tasting food.  I'd definitely get it again.

This mix reminds me of the foods in Singapore.  Very rich coconut and lemon grass flavor.  The preparation was also very easy - just saute the cubed meat (we used London Broil) and add the mix to have a delicious meal shortly.  I am a bit wimpy when it comes to spicy/hot so if you are like me, just use less of the mix or add more meat to reduce the hot flavor.

This curry sauce mix from Singapore makes for an easy-to-prepare dinner that's nice for weekday evenings. The directions call for you to pan-fry beef with vegetable oil and cook it until it's nearly done. In a saucepan, you mix the contents of the two packets included with the mix with water and bring the mixture to a boil. Then you simply add the beef to the sauce and simmer it until it's done. It was easy to make and did not require additional ingredients other than the meat, cooking oil, and water. One thing I did notice was that the coconut power was very lumpy. Of course, I added it to the water so I had to spend some time squishing the lumps before I added the curry sauce. You might want to put the powder in the saucepan first and whisk the water into it before adding the sauce. Anyway, it mixed up well and I didn't have lumps in the final product.The kit contains two packets: one is a powdered coconut mix and the other is the curry sauce mix. The ingredients are fairly basic, although the coconut mix contains sodium caseinate, which I find tends to dry me out when I encounter it in coffee creamer. I did not notice any ill effects from it in the curry, so perhaps it's a matter of how much sodium caseinate is in the products.The flavor was very nice and the curry was more sweet than hot. On a scale of 1 to 10 I'd rate it about a 3, so if your tastebuds aren't up to the heat I think you'd still enjoy this. It's not bland by any means, but it's not overwhelming, and I think most children would probably eat it, too. There are pandan leaves in the sauce, which had a very mild flavor (not oniony or anything like that). I made plain rice to go with this and just put the meat and sauce over the rice.This makes a nice one-dish meal and would keep well for leftovers if you can avoid eating all of it at once. I used three small steaks, or about 12 ounces of meat, to go with this. Of course you can stretch this out if you want with more meat, or you could substitute chicken for the beef. Also, using quinoa or barley or some other grain instead the rice would bump up the versatility of the mix.

column9: Sweet after taste, easy to make
column10: We're a house of curry eaters, no doubt. What I learned with this Rendang Curry mix is that I prefer Japanese and Indian curries. This Rendang was too sweet for me and there is NO heat in this at all. My parents both liked it and said it was correct compared to rendang style sauce they have had elsewhere over the years. Preparation was very easy and pretty fast. I used very thin sliced top round steak and browned it in canola oil per the directions. The sauce and coconut milk come in seperate pouches and mix together to a boil before you add the meat. In less than 30 minutes we had everything and rice on the dinner table. The only other complaint was from my Mother who felt the dried green onion pieces were bitter and took away from the overall taste of the curry sauce. If you perfer more "savory" than "sweet" in your curry, this is probably not for you. Otherwise, our family enjoyed this product.

I've never tasted curry, and my only venture into Asian food has been at the local Chinese buffet.I liked this a lot! Enough spiciness but could have had a little more--when compared to salsa, this is mild, and the coconut is a nice balance to the spicy flavor. I didn't notice this being overly sweet.I used 2 lbs. of extra lean stew meat; I'm lazy when it comes to cooking and also don't like to touch raw meat (I know, it's just the "dead animal thing" I have going on in my head). The package said to serve with either rice or mashed potatoes.  I boiled some small red potatoes, and mashed those up with their skins on.  Some of the "gravy" was good on top of the mashed taters. This box made 5 adult-sized servings, plenty to go around, and we were all stuffed.This is a dish I wouldn't be ashamed to serve to company, and I plan on ordering more.

column9: I'm just a mom, and don't know what Rendang Curry is "supposed to" taste like.  We loved this...
column10: I'm just a mom, have never been to Asia, and know nothing about how Beef Rendang is "supposed to" taste.  So whether this is authentic, frankly, I have no idea.But... I made this for my family (me & hubby and five kids ages 5-14) and everyone absolutely loved it and begged me to make it again.This was easy to make.  The box contains two packets of stuff, with nice easy-to-rip-open notches.  I prepared it exactly following the instructions (something I rarely do!), and that required:*1 3/4 pounds of beef (okay, I used round steak instead of the beef tenderloin called for)*vegetable oil*waterThat's it.  Sliced up the beef, cooked it until at least browned, then set aside.Added the contents of the two packages and the water... one odd thing is that it calls for 4/5 a cup of water.  I used something close to a full cup-- but I like to have more sauce than most recipes seem to make.  At this point, you have to be sure to stir it well... the coconut powder clumped up a bit, but giving it a good stir in the hot water and just being sure to pay attention, and I didn't have any problems.Then you add the beef back and cook until the meat is done.They recommend serving with rice or mashed potatoes.  I made a whole lot of rice, and served this over the rice.  We had a side veggie as well, and for 7 of us (including two teen boys) we actually had enough left over for my husband to take to work for lunch the next day.It smelled amazing.  And it tasted even better.  The flavors combined wonderfully, so it just tasted rich.  I have family members who "don't like" coconut, and nobody even noticed -- it just blended so nicely.An added bonus is that the package claims that there is no added MSG, nor artificial colors, and no added preservatives.I will make this again.  In the future, I might try adding a bit of veggies.  But serving it with a full pot of rice served to stretch it for my family.

According to the box, Rendang Curry is a food served in Saigon. I now officially love love love Saigon food. One box would easily serve 4, and takes mere minutes to put together. I served it over couscous, which was a perfect accompaniment because it didn't fight the huge flavors of the sauce. The curry is a unique combination of flavors - spicy with a bit of heat but that same heat disappears quickly in your mouth as the sweetness of the coconut milk kicks in. It really was spectacular flavors that were new to me.A downside. The box calls for 28 ounces of beef tenderloin. Where I live, that's about $35 worth of beef. I talked with my local butcher and he suggested I use sirloin cut up for stir fry (labelled as "stir fry beef" in my grocery store). That cut the cost of the meat down to about $6.00. Because the meat cooks in the sauce for several minutes, the meet was very tender and I see no drawback from the substitution.I would definitely buy this product again. In fact, I will be looking for other Prima Taste products to try! If you like to try new international foods, definitely put this one on your list.(The four star review instead of 5 stars was due to the recipe calling for Beef Tenderloin. Flavor-wise, this is a 5 star product.)

We tried this last night and it is really delicious.  We love asian food and it was great to be able to "make" such a delicious curry at home, and so easily.I would like to purchase this in SMALLER servings. We are a family of 3 (and our daughter won't eat this anyway) and the calorie count in the provided mixes is QUITE high.  I would have liked to only use part of the pouches but that wouldn't work.If I see smaller packets in the supermarket I will buy!

This is very tasty and makes such a quick and easy meal.  I've never had rendang so I can't say if it's authentic, but it did remind me of coconut curry with a bit of green curry taste.  Very clean and fresh.  I actually used pork tenderloin because it's what I had and it worked out very well and the meal came together very quickly.  I slightly browned the meat and then followed the directions, but added a bit more water than called for.  It still thickened up very nicely.There is plenty of sauce so adding veggies would work out well.  It comes with two packs, the curry paste/seasoning and the dehydrated coconut powder.  When I added the powder to the pot I figured it would clump up, but it mixed very smooth and perfectly.  It is a bit sweet, but it's also pretty spicy (at least for me).  I think if you find it too sweet you could add less of the coconut powder.I'm definitely going to buy this again.  So tasty. My whole family just loved it.

column9: Not great.  .. and a bit expensive
column10: Though I doubt this item will be liked my most American palates, I think overall the product is okay.  This is a product of Singapore.  If you're not all that fond of Thai curry, then you probably won't care for this either.  Personally, I LOVE Thai curry a lot more than this.I do have a few "issues" with this product.  First, there are "leaves" in the sauce, and they can be quite "tough".  You might want to strain them out.  Next, the sauce is quite "oily".  The first ingredient in the sauce is vegetable oil.One totally ridiculous thing is what they show as the serving size and servings per package.  They show that the package serves 15 people and a serving size is two tablespoons.  Totally outrageous.  The reason they do this is so that it makes the calories look low (110 per serving).  The directions show to add 28oz of beef tenderloin, which is also crazy.  One would NEVER use such an expensive meat for a box mix such as this.  Beef stew meat works just fine. But based upon what the box shows as a serving size, then you would have less than 2oz per-person.I also think this item is quite expensive for what it is.  Also, I don't think I'd be interested in making this 4-times before the product expires.

I used to live in Malaysia and am always looking for dishes to replicate the amazing food I had in KL. This beef rendang has great flavor - that's for sure.I only gave it 4 stars because I found it overly sweet and a little too mild in heat.  Plus, there were hard bits of leaves that were somewhat distracting.I wonder....would using a can of coconut milk cut the sweetness?But....the flavor was so good and the preparation was so darn easy, that I'm ordering more boxes to have on hand.And yes - I would serve this at Supper Club . I just wouldn't tell anyone how easy it was to make!I wonder....would using a can of coconut milk cut the sweetness?

I am in no way an authority on Indian food. I do enjoy eating it and am famiar with the spice palate, but I have not tried this dish before. I can't say whether it is authentic or not. I can say I didn't like it. I followed directions exactly but the taste was just odd to me. Too bitter and no I didn't burn any ingredients. The texture of the sauce was off too. It had an unpleasant mouth feel, slightly grainy. We had a LOT of leftovers (no one cared much for it) so I tried it again the next day thinning out the sauce in an attempt to make it smokther. Nope, still didn't care for it. But that's just my (our) opinion.

column9: Pretty good, but I wouldn't get it again.
column10: Having only tried Thai food fairly recently (within the last couple of years), I was eager to try this kit out at home.  I knew it was likely that it would be out of my diet comfort zone, and it really was, but I decided to try it anyway.We made it with lean beef, but if I were to make it again I might try it with bison, chicken, or maybe even tofu.  I thought it had a nice balance of flavors, but it could use a little more spice for my taste.  I realize that to make it marketable to the masses, they can't make it too spicy - I'm just saying that if you do like your food spicy, you should anticipate using a little hot sauce; and if you don't like it too spicy you should be okay.  All in all, I'd recommend this to someone who likes curries and doesn't really care about fat intake.  The fact that it's a bit pricey and I do care about fat intake is what makes me say I wouldn't get this again, but it's just a bad product for most curry lovers.

First I cannot compare this to other brands because it was a new taste adventure for me. I wish I could say I loved it but... it was just ok. Not horrid, not wonderful. So it may be just fine if your taste tunsd to it often but for a beginner exploring I can't give it either a great or an 'avoid' It is ok. That is how it tasted to me.

I very much enjoyed this entree kit. I love all sorts of Asian cuisine, but never tend to have the staples of cooking it in my kitchen. Because I'm on a budget, it never seems worth buying a whole pantry full of ingredients for one meal. (Of course, I aspire to gather those ingredients.)I found this mix to be a perfect way to prepare my own curry at home without buying all the specialty ingredients. I found the instructions easy to follow, and the meal easy to prepare. Until I get the Asian pantry going in my own home, I'll be looking to this brand to satisfy a craving.

I was looking for something that tasted similar to the restaurants that I love to frequent, but are expensive.  I think the seasoning blend is different than what most restaurants here in Connecticut/Northeast use because this had a foreign taste to me that I did not like. I consider myself to be a very "open" eater and will try lots of tastes but this one just didn't do it for us.  It was very easy to make following the directions, but again just not my thing.  Gave it three stars because it was easy to make.

The title said, all things in moderation right?  You don't have to pig out on the foods and flavors you love but we often do, just keep moderation in mind.  The ingredients aren't all that bad, they are good ingredients but not an item you go to for losing weight if that is your goal.I prepared mine with mock duck meat, a vegan product and it turned out wonderfully.  The package is good for 15 servings, correlate that how you will. She never gave me the recipe so I tried for years to  get the ingredients just right to make that wonderful dish only to fail.  I had forgotten all about that dish until I tried the Rendang curry sauce kit.  Being a vegetarian, I substituted the meat for vegetables and was immediately impressed.  The curry has a mild spicy-sweet  flavor with  a moderate amount of coconut undertone.  It is similar to Thai curry but a little less spicy and has more coconut flavor. column9: Hard to believe this is pre-packaged food, and my Chinese wife and Thai friend agree
column10: I was expecting this to be really salty, like most prepackaged food, but was pleasantly surprised. Albeit not as surprised as my wife (who grew up in Beijing and generally hates prepackaged food) or our friend from Bangkok! Along with the recommended beef, we added potatoes, veggies, sausage, and just a little sugar, and it tasted like homemade. Our friend didn't even realize that it was packaged food until we showed him the box -- he just assumed that my wife made it from scratch.Also, the small box made a pretty good amount of sauce. Often times with these kinds of things, one or two people can easily finish off a package that claims to have 6 or 8 servings so they can water down the "nutrition" information. Along with some rice, this made enough for three adults with one small serving left over.The only negative is the leaves -- there are a TON of them. I ended up chewing up and swallowing a lot of them just because it got to be a hassle picking around them. I would have preferred fewer, larger pieces. I wouldn't want to change the taste, though! It's a bit expensive, too, but considering how much food it makes (despite the small box), it's not too bad.

I am a huge fan of curry dishes, so I was excited to try this. I was not disappointed. The curry was flavorful, reminiscent of something you would get at a restaurant. Importantly, the curry was super easy to make. I suggest trying the mix with various other items than just beef. I tried it with noodles. It was delicious but ended up being heavy after a few bites.The only negative with sauce kit are the leaves in the mix. It becomes frustrating to remove leaves as you try to eat the main meal.

column9: From a box, this is tops
column10: I've never had a Rendang Curry, but I am generally familiar with South Asian cuisine, and I have no doubt that this is a good rendition. If I had this at a restaurant, I'd be pleased. Having this from a box is a delight.The package notes that Rendang Curry was originally developed to tenderize and mask tough cuts of meat, so I went to my grocer and got a cheap package of stew beef. Following the instructions I browned my stew beef, although I tossed in some onion which isn't in the recipe. Remove the beef from the pot to start the curry, and here's where it gets interesting. The dish is basically a gravy in two parts. The first is a curry paste which you add some water to, which is pretty standard. To this you add a sizable package of ground coconut, which turns the reddish curry into a deep orange-brown gravy. This portion of the process smells heavenly. Throw in your beef (and in my case, onions), and simmer until tender.I served my curry straight (normally you'd spoon it over rice, although the box also suggests mashed potatoes), and used a baguette for my starch and for dipping. The beef was tender from stewing, and the sauce complements a good stew beef wonderfully. The flavors are complex, creamy, and just a hint of spicy. This is not authentic South Asia heat, but it was spicy enough that I got a case of sniffles.I can only come up with two negatives. One is that the powdered coconut should really be added to the water first, because if it's added to the curry paste it tends to form lumps. This is nothing that really detracts from the taste, but the texture is a little odd, so I'd suggest a slight revision to the directions. Two is that the dish includes large chunks of herb leaves, and while they are authentic to the cuisine, they don't reconstitute well and again affect texture. I highly suggest tossing in some onion with the beef as I did, which is an authentic touch and will help to mask the texture issues- in fact some raw onion wouldn't be out of place either.This is restaurant-quality curry in a box. Pick some up today.

I recently made this for my parents, who were born and raised in Singapore. They grew up eating things like rendang curry, and Prima Taste is a Singaporean brand that my mom has relied on many times to make laksa at home. This curry was exceptionally easy to make -- I added about a pound and a half of beef, browned it in a dutch oven and put it aside. In the same pot I added the curry paste, coconut powder, and 4/5 cup of water, brought it to a low boil, and then added the beef to finish cooking. From start to finish, including the time it took to cut and trim the beef, the entire process took just about 20-25 minutes.. not time-consuming by any means.The sauce is thick and plentiful with a strong coconut flavor. We all thought that the curry was overly sweet and needed the kick of added heat. I served this with rice that I soaked in coconut cream and pandan leaves, ikan bilis (fried anchovies), and a fried egg. With a side of vegetables, this box can easily serve 6 people, at least in my family, or 4 people very generously. My parents and I ate about half for dinner, with plenty of leftovers.

column9: Great Tasting Kit To Spice Up Your Dinner
column10: This curry sauce kit is good on all sorts of meet.  Everything is in the box, except for utensils and the meat of your choice.  The whole process wasn't messy at all as I thought it would be, even for a non-expert cook like myself.  This was very sweet-spicy, but not too overwhelming.  If its too spicy for your liking, simply add less spices.  The only downer for me was that I choose not to ingest the thyme leaves and there were several along the way that I had to pick through.  Other than that, Prima Taste delivered the great spice that I was looking for.

Actually this curry sauce was really good. A lot better than I expected from a box. The kit is full of ingredients to make a sauce - it has a packet of paste (the sauce base) and a packet of coconut "premix" (a powder made from dehydrated coconut milk and bits of coconut). You just add water and you have delicious curry sauce.Instructions said to brown 28 oz of beef for this. But I think you could use any meat and / or veggies and it would taste good.It's not very spicy though. If you like spicy, you'll have to add some. It's also quite high in sugar and fat.One tip: the coconut premix has a texture like sugar. It comes in a packet and has some lumps in it (also like sugar). You don't want the lumps. Mush the packet with your fingers to squash the lumps back into powder. This will make it easier to mix the sauce into a nice smooth texture.It was easy, tasty, and made quite a lot of food. Probably 4 servings at least.I'd buy this again, and I'd try this brand's other sauce kits too.
I grew up on S&B Golden Curry but over time I found my tastes broadening as I traveled other parts of Asia. This delicious curry is as good as many you would find in restaurants.

We really enjoyed the dish that this sauce mix made. Instead of beef I used dark meat chicken and broccoli. The easy-to-make coconut curry gravy was rich and very tasty! The rewarmed leftovers were just as good if not better.

column4: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
column10: I've never had curry until today. Not even a taste. But I was offered this product on Amazon Vine and thought to myself, "Self, this could be interesting. Get it and eat it. Also, don't refer to yourself as 'self,' because it's a bit pretentious." And so I got it and finally got around to cooking it today. What are my thoughts?First off, I followed the suggestion of another reviewer and mixed the coconut powder separately. Then I cooked up everything and dumped it over some rice. The end result was...well, interesting. It tasted good, but not excellent. I'd expected a bit more, starting with it being a little more spicy. I was also taken aback by how much "grass" there was inside the spice-paste pouch. I thought it was going to be little bits, but no, it was good sized bits. Beyond that, I did find the paste pouch to be interesting. It seemed like a good way of doing things.Anyhow, I can't really compare this with any other forms of curry, since I've never had any, but it was ok. Not great. But ok. I'll probably never rush out to buy it, but if I get my hands on some more, I'd be willing to eat it.

I am a "Indian food" kind of a guy, but still, this curry was surprisingly good. It tasted more Thai-ish than anything else, and if you dig Thai food, even better. On my second go, I left out the coconut curry, and it didn't taste as genuine. So, experiment with it a little. In the end, you will really like the curry.

Lots of yummy sauce.  Has just a slight touch of spiciness that kept my  young kids (3 & 5) from eating a full serving but they did like it and had a few bites. I would be tempted to try the mix with chicken in the future.

column9: Tasty though hardly a revelation, and rather expensive
column10: After reading the other reviews here I was expecting some sort of curry revelation from this Rendang. But dang, Ren and Stimpy, it was merely quite good, maybe very good for a packaged curry. It's got some layers of taste but nothing approaching a freshly home-made curry, and miles from a serious restaurant. And at almost 7 per package, if you buy four, this is hardly a bargain.First problem: it's barely spicy. I don't need nuclear but I do want heat from a curry. This has little if any. Second issue for me was the packaging. Squeeeezing this paste out of the army-rations-type foil pouch made me feel like my unit was going to be deployed at any second. Maybe that's just me...but it also made it hard to get all the contents out without serious rolling and some mess on the hands. Far from ideal. Plus the bay leaves were kind of a hassle to deal with; they certainly are key to the taste but while the full leaves are easy to find, the smaller pieces make for some weird chewy moments. Don't swallow...From a pure taste perspective, it's a good Rendang but if you've ever had a truly fresh one made with fresh spices, not just a paste, then you know the difference. At seven clams for less than two servings, I'd say go to your local gourmet Indian or Thai place and get the real deal.But, if there is no such option nearby and you love Rendang, then this is certainly a decent alternative. I just don't think it's that far beyond Mae Ploy or the other packaged curry stalwarts, and they cost literally a third or so what this does, plus you can use fresh coconut, and you won't need to add more spices on your own to get it close to real curry heat.

column9: good taste but deceptive packaging description
column10: Frist, Nirmala's blend is lovely.Second, the information about the amount you will receive is deceptive and that ticks me off. It is a small and extremely spicy member of the capsicum plant genus.Piri-piri, peri-peri or peli-peli is the name used in Portuguese and a number of African languages to describe the African bird's-eye chili. The variations in spelling derive from the various pronunciations of the word in parts of Africa, although "piri-piri" is the correct spelling in Portuguese.In Portuguese cuisine, piri-piri is often used in preparing sauces and marinades for roast and grilled dishes, especially chicken and various fish.

I am a Lapsang Souchong fan.  This variety has a good, strong smokey flavor.  This tea is not for the faint of heart but if you truly enjoy Lapsang Souchong taste this one.  If you prefer a tea with less smoke, try Taylors of Harrogate Taylors of Harrogate Lapsang Souchong Leaf Tea, Loose Leaf, 4.41-Ounce Tins (Pack of 2).

You'll either love this tea or hate it. If you like barbecue or smoked meats of any kind, chances are you'll like this tea. I have to disagree about drinking it pale. The proper way to drink this tea is by pouring boiling water on it and steeping for 5 minutes, which usually make it fairly dark. Unlike other teas, it seems to stay smooth-tasting even when you make it strong and has a nice reddish color to it. I can't get enough of this tea. On the other hand, my wife absolutely hates the flavor.

I first heard about Lapsang Souchong while reading The Story of Tea: A Cultural History and Drinking Guide, where they described the history and manufacturing process for the unique tea, as well as saying that it's strong smoky flavor had a "love it or hate it" reputation amongst tea drinkers. Well, my favorite beverage in the world is the Islay whisky Laphroaig, and I have heard those exact same terms used to describe its flavor many, many times.  I knew I had to give Lapsang Souchong a try.Of course, there are many Lapsang Souchong's available, and it was really just a gamble to decide which one to chose.  I wanted a loose-leaf tea, since they tend to be of superior quality to tea bags.  I had heard the Taylors of Harrogate Lapsang Souchong Loose Leaf described as a "beginner's Lapsang Souchong," with a less-intense smokiness and I knew I didn't want that.  If "less-intense" was what my palette demanded I wouldn't reach for a bottle of Laphroaig!  Another reviewer recommended this China Mist product (sold under the name of their imprint company "Leaves Pure Tea") as being a good example of Lapsang Souchong.  The price and quantity were just right so this is what I picked.I am extraordinarily pleased with this purchase, and now am a dedicated fan of Lapsang Souchong.  The aroma is an intense smokiness, although the flavor is much more delicate.  I went with the recommended steeping time of five minutes in under-boiled water, and that seemed just about right.  If this tea is "love it or hate it," I definitely fall into the "love it" category.The tea comes packed in an air-tight package with an oxygen-eater insert so it is as fresh as modern technology can make it.  The zip-lock bag is re-sealable, which is nice. I can't find any details on the grade of the tea, or where is was processed but I assume for the price we are not dealing with a  top-quality first-flush product, but for something that has been smoked over pinewood for so long you don't really need the most delicate leaves!Aside from enjoying a glass of Lapsang Souchong, it is really wonderful for cooking.  "The Story of Tea" has a Lapsang Souchong ice cream recipe that I want to try out, and I recently used some in a soup I was making as a replacement for liquid smoke.  It turned out fantastic, with the tea lending a complex smokiness to the dish.

Lapsang Souchong tea comes from the mist-enshrouded Wuyi Mountains in the northwestern corner of China's Fujian Province (north of Guangdong [Canton] Province), whose greatest tourist draw besides its mountains is its coast line on the Taiwan Straits.This tea has an unmistakeably smokey note, which for years made it a particular favorite with the "single malt and cigars" crowd of English clubs and drawing rooms. That aroma is created during the tea's smoking process, which involves the withering of the tea leaves in bamboo baskets hung on racks over cypress or pine wood fires, after they have been rolled and placed into wooden barrels until they emit their own aroma. The finished tea leaves are characteristically thick and black. Legend has it that this smoking process was discovered by accident during the Quing Dynasty (1644 - 1911), when an army unit camping out in a tea factory interrupted the processing of the recently-arrived leaves and the workers then resulted to drying the leaves over pine fires to make up for the disruption and get to the market in time, creating an instant sensation there.Because of its potent aroma, Lapsang Souchong should not steep very long. The rule of thumb is that the paler its color, the more likely you'll truly enjoy it.

Lapsang Souchong is a great tea - when brewed properly - it drinks very easily and leaves one with a nice warm, refreshed, and relaxed feeling - when steeped too long - it becomes to strong though, so brew it carefully.

column9: I'm no tea expert, but this is pretty cool
column10: "In American author James A. Michener's 1974 historical novel Centennial, Rocky Mountain fur trapper Alexander McKeag describes lapsang souchong as "a man's tea, deep and subtle and blended in some rugged place," ... "better even than whisky." " --WikipediaBy some arcane internet subject that led to another, and another, I ended up having read that Wikipedia line the other night.  I ask you - how in the hell was I supposed to pass that up?So I went and bought a mesh tea ball, and bought this tea.  Yeah, I read the great write-ups here that spoke about the nuances of different brands, and that encouraged the decision to try it as authentic as possible (because so many brands of tea sold at Wal-Mart these days really don't do much for me ... in fact, hot tea in general never did much for me...).After steeping it for a few minutes I'd say the aroma was that of 50% smoke and 50% black tea. The black tea aroma came after the initial smoky smell, and I found this both pleasing - then reassuring.Initial tastes is that of just less than 50% smoke - unless you inhale before or during the intake ... then you get a boat-load more smoke.  The ability to change-up one's experience with each sip is isn't a bad thing; quite the contrary.  The rest is some mix of tea and sweetness.  I don't really have a clue where the sweetness is coming from as I haven't read about it here, but there doesn't seem to be any need to add anything to it to sweeten it up (not that I'd adulterate a good tea or coffee anyway).  Perhaps I'm confusing smokiness with sweetness, but truth be told they seem intermingled here - no unpleasantries abound.Lastly, without having a good way of describing what it really is, I don't find it something that should be seen as either "love it or hate it."  This brand's version of it, at least, is first and foremost a tasty tea (well, 50.1% of the flavor is, anyway, give or take 10%), so someone looking for a black tea experience probably won't hate it, but that isn't to say that people who mix stuff into their beverages will find it mixes well.  It would seem that it's the delicate balance of the far ends of this tea that is the prize, so putting something else into it may ruin that which you're trying to improve.

column9: Tastes great + strengthens and rebuilds enamel
column10: I and my 7 and 9 year old daughters like the taste of this gum, but the main reason we buy it is because it has calcium in a form that can be directly absorbed from your saliva into your teeth, and utilized to strengthen and rebuild weak spots in your tooth enamel. The specific chemical is calcium casein peptone-calcium phosphate, a lactose-free milk derivative.Natural saliva has calcium in it; this will give it a boost, especially important if you have dry mouth. A decade ago I had the idea of rinsing my teeth with a liquid calcium supplement, thinking it would boost my saliva's calcium, but after a couple wasted years, I read that the calcium in your saliva has to be bound to other, specific chemicals in order to be absorbed and used by your teeth.  This product fits the bill.I also use ACT enamel-restoring rinse. The ACT rinse has a similar calcium product but also has fluoride.  Too much fluoride can be have negative effects on teeth, so I use the rinse twice a day, as directed, and chew the gum during the day to promote salivation (with its own calcium) and boost calcium levels without overdoing the fluoride.Individual packs can be expensive, so I used to get boxes at Sam's Club. Unfortunately, Sams discontinued the product. Now I save on shipping by having the boxes delivered from Amazon every month as a recurring order.

Let me first say that this is my absolute favorite gum of all time. I am a gum ADDICT, and this feeds my addiction just fine! The fact that this gum has calcium is a great selling point for me. The extra minerals that this gum provides is supposed to help strengthen teeth and enamel. If this gum is any help at all for preventing cavities, then it has paid for itself many times over.Not to mention, it tastes delicious. The only downside-- once people learn you have this gum, you might have to share!

This is my favorite gum. It's has a pleasant sweet mint flavor that isn't overpowering and it's not cloyingly sweet. It just has a easy taste. But I think the real reason I like it so much is because I feel it's really helping my teeth. My dentist actually told me about it. So it's dentist recommended, no kidding. I find that this gum is really hard to find. They don't sell it at most gas stations, grocery stores and costco. So I was really happy when I found I could order it from Amazon. Happy chewing!

column9: Great food to keep an older dog healthy!
column10: Our dog is very healthy and happy on this food! He has no digestive or skin issues and he is never sick. He's an 8 year old American Eskimo Dog. We walk him a LOT, but he still doesn't need to eat as much as the package indicates. He eats the "weight loss" amount, but he's not losing weight, he's maintaining his weight. This isn't a complaint at all, but if you're going to feed this food to an older dog or a dog with a slower metabolism, monitor their weight carefully and make sure you're not feeding too much!

A grain free diet is the best you can do for your pet. Wellness Core has a great ocean recipe that I would highly recommend if you have a terrier because they do better on ocean based diets. I have a yorkshire terrier and she loves this food. Her coat and digestion have improved dramatically. Something else to note is the quality of the ingredients. Overall great food!

I have a portly beagle, who is beyond cute but 2 lbs over weight. However, keeping her weight down as she gets older was very important. We'd been using the normal Wellness Healthy Weight and she seemed to enjoy that. We changed her to the CORE after she started to get red skin on her belly. After switching, which had no effects on her GI, the redness went away. She also had has no tendency to want to eat this after it was digested (if you know what I mean!) which can be an issue with many weight management foods.I did my homework online and read a lot of online sites before switching. I can say hands down, Wellness CORE is a great food and if you can afford the small increase in price, I think you and your furry friend will enjoy its benefits.

I got this at a great price and fast free shipping. My miniature schnauzer is liking it ok so far, not as  well as she liked the other flavors of Wellness CORE. Would definitely recommend Wellness CORE to anyone, especially if your dog has a sensitive stomach and has skin issues/allergies.

Search no more for high quality dog food.This high in protein dog food and is among the best there is on the market.  My 1.5 year old papillon loves it.  I feed him about a small cup per day to keep him full while keeping the fat down.What's the selling point for me?**Contains no meat by-products, wheat, corn, soy, artificial colors, flavors or preservatives**Buy the 12 pound bag and save your money.

I have two golden retrievers with hearty appetites.  Feeding them regular dog food makes them overweight.  I switched to Core Reduced Fat when I began to worry about the quality of the food I was feeding my dogs.  I had fed my dogs expensive dog foods which I got at the grocery store.  When I read the ingredients, I decied to look for something better quality.  From my research I learned that high quality dog foods prevent illness and disease and increase life-span.  Core is made with ingredients like real chicken--not chicken by-products or lots of grain.  Afterall, dogs are carnivores.  Since my dogs have been on Core they have not had the usual ear infections, skin allergies and irritations; their coats are beautiful; they have lots of energy and are overall very healthy.  The extra money I pay for this high quality dog food I definitely save at the vet!

column9: Great food for a great price!
column10: This food works for my dog.  She has some serious gas (boston terrier), and this food helps.  Granted, she still has gas, but it isn't as, well, stinky.  Two thumbs up!

column9: My dog loves the food and I love the price!
column10: We have small dog (Pug/ Boston Terrier)and his weight got a little out of control, so we switched him to this. He loves the taste of the food and he can be pretty picky. column9: Wise switch from Iams Low Residue Formula
column10: When my Rhodesian Ridgeback-mix developed mild pancreatitis two years ago at age three, my vet suggested Iams Low Residue food.  Over the last year, however, she's also developed severe skin allergies (but mostly air-borne, I think)and was losing hair in small patches so, after some research I added MSM to her diet and decided to eliminate grain. Wellness CORE Grain-Free food was the perfect choice because it is also low-fat (too much fat aggrevating her pancreas).  In the month she's been on it--both dry and wet formula--her coat has improved and she even seems perkier!
I love that I no longer have to haul big bags of dog food home from the pet store.  This is the only food that seems to agree with my westie's digestive system.

column9: Great dog food. Palatable & good ingredients!
column10: Few things good about this product:1. Made by Wellness. No recalls of any kind thus far. I am really paranoid about having a sick pet with a 3-4 figured vet bill, so that is something I look out for a lot.2. Ingredients is a lot better than most foods.3. Palatable. My dog kinda hates Wellness but would eat down Wellness Core products literally right away.4. High Fiber. 7% if I am not wrong. What made me try this food was that my dog had constantly soft stools at one point in time. So I saw the high fiber percentage, and I decided to try this out. My dog had really solid poop after that!
