I won't purchase again on-line but will wait to find it in stores.  Even the color of the hot sauce was more orange than usual.

I was very excited to purchase Mom Made Foods after reading about them on their website. I was unfortunately, very disappointed in the products. They came "iced" over like they had been in the freezer forever. The taste of each indvidual food was very bland. My 2 year old wouldn't touch them. For the price I paid, the food should look attractive and taste good. I don't think I would have been too disappointed had the price point been a little lower. The pictures on the boxes look 10x better than the actual food itself. I will not purchase from them again. And, I was so excited! Maybe my expectations were too high?
While they may be healthier than your standard fare this is not the 'finally a quick meal' that I hoped it would be.  Our daughter did not like one type and we tried them all twice just in case.

column9: Perfect when I walk in the door and hear "Mom, I'm hungry!"
column10: My kids love this stuff and it is perfect for when I get home from work and the kids are already complaining that they want dinner.  I personally thought the Cheesy Mac was delicious and the chicken munchie was a great alternative to the super sodium Hot Pockets that I used to feed them.

column9: Great healthy option for busy nights
column10: I was very pleased with both the munchies and the meals.  I do not cook, so the ease of this product was a godsend and the fact that my kids actually ate it was even better.  I like that there are veggies in everything so I'm not just throwing a pizza in front of them.  They loved the fiesta rice and bean burritos and it made for a healthy mexican night at our house.  I would definitely recommend this product to busy parents who also want healthy stuff for their kids.

I found this product to be delicious! My husband and I both tried it first and thought it was super easy to prepare and really yummy!  We loved that you could recognize all the ingredients and eat "convenience" food without all the added junk!  The crust was flaky and delish and the mac and cheese was the perfect size.  I am definitely planning on reordering!  Great on babysitter nights for the kids!

I am a longtime fan of horseradish, for its aromatic effect on my sinuses and palatable taste. This product does not have the same effects, but welcome complements of flavors are realized here. This is a very welcome surprise. Heinz got this one right, a winner from start to finish.

Excellent product with just the right kick from the horseradish. Creamy in texture, heinz has managed to put two wonderful items together and create an addicting product. This is great on just about anything !
The best I've tasted this is my second purchase as I can't find in the stores where I live.  Tasted it in FL and had to have..

Note that this product is labeled "Horseradish Sauce" versus prepared horseradish. As Gioacco's review noted, Horseradish is the third ingredient, so this should not be confused with prepared horseradish which would include horseradish as the first ingredient. The actual flavor and texture is like horseradish flavored mayonnaise with added flavors. Egg yolks are listed in the ingredients. Definitely include this condiment however with Ketchup, Mustard, Relish and Mayonnaise for barbecue, sandwich making and tabletop use. For finer beef steak preparation I would recommend prepared horseradish although this product could be a reasonable stand-in. Excellent product and I plan to order another 6-pack when available through Amazon Subscribe & Save again. Saves me about 40% compared to buying locally. Aloha,  John
The only problem I found was I had 3 bottles with splits in them.  I had to throw them out.

The main thing that I liked about this Horseradish Sauce is that Horseradish is third on the list of ingredients, behind soybean oil, and distilled white vinegar. It has a lot more ingredients (flavorings, preservatives, thickening agents). It does taste good, and even looks more "natural". Horseradish is a main ingredient though. I hope this helps. Thanks.

My Miniature Dachshund really likes all the Beneful Prepared Meal varieties. He recognizes the container when I take it out of the pantry and he knows it is dinner time. I like knowing that I am giving my pet a food that has the nutrients he needs. The product is easy to store and  serve and feeding while traveling is super easy. My husband gets the empty containers and lids for his shop. An added bonus is the money I save by buying in bulk at amazon.com and having it delivered to my door.
Our Jack Russell loves this food.The containers make it easy to serve a portion and refrigerate the remainder.This food looks like people food, not the typical dog food mush.
At $1.88 a tub, this runs more that what I find in most grocery stores as well as W*l M*rt and T*rget.Having said that, my dogs LOVE this food!!!
Whether you buy one container or a 16 pack container, the price still averages $ 1.885. Where are the bargains?
My Shih Tzu can be quite picky over his food, but digs right in when served Beneful. I can see why.  It smells more like people food than any of the others we've bought.
The Dogs like it, the container is re sealable, the price is better than my Publix Supermarket and with Amazon Prime it gets here in 2 days with no shipping,....What more would you want????

I have been feeding TOTW to my Italian Greyhound-Terrier mix for over a year now and I have nothing but good things to say about it. First, for all of those wanting to feed their dog grain-free, but struggling to pay Orijen prices, TOTW is the solution. TOTW is definitely the most cost-effective grain-free food I've been able to find.For all of those fearful of the use of fish meal and the possible threat of ethoxyquin, it appears that TOTW customer service have confirmed that the particular ocean fish meal used in TOTW is, in fact, ethoxyquin-free. Here is the link to that information and a step-by-step analysis of the ingredient list.[...]After getting my dog from a rescue, feeding him TOTW has helped him reach a healthy weight and an active lifestyle. The vet has repeatedly noted how good his weight is, how great his coat looks and how well muscled he is.TOTW, with its high protein and fat content (fat is an essential part of a healthy diet for our four-legged friends) is a great, cost-effective grain-free option. However, those switching from grain kibbles need to be slow about switching their dogs to this kibble. TOTW and other grain-free foods are much richer and a 5 to 7 days slow transition will yield the best result.Is TOTW for every dog? Probably not, every dog reacts differently to different food and if you have a small breed, I would tend to focus on the lower protein content of the Pacific Stream formula rather than the High Prairie or Wetlands Formulas. I do, however, think TOTW can be a great option for a lot of dog owners. If you're interested in starting to feed grain-free and holistic dog food, TOTW has worked great for me and my dog.

I have been feeding this food for several months to my 9-year old "allergy" Lab.  He is doing wonderfully on it.  Shiny coat, good muscle... and best of all... no more ear infections!  He seems to love the taste.  I would highly recommend this food to people whose dogs have allergies to grains, peas, chicken, beef, ...etc.  Actually, I think it's a great food for dogs without allergies, too.  My non-allergic bullmastiff is doing very well on it.

column9: Great food but makes our dog smell a little fishy
column10: We usually feed our dog the High Prairie version of Taste of the Wild but we sometime like to buy a bag of a different version of TOTW (Wetlands or Pacific Stream) to provide him with some variety. Whenever we change foods we are sure to mix the two formulas for a few days to avoid an upset stomach, and while this works with the Wetlands version it has not with the Pacific Stream food which doesn't seem to agree with our dog too well.  He loves the flavor, but when we give him the Pacific Stream formula we notice that he tends to have bad breath with strong hints of fish and that he to get loose stools.While we think that Taste of the Wild is outstanding food, the Pacific Stream formula is not for us and we will stick with their High Plains version with the occasional bag of Wild Fowl to mix it up.

***For the person with 1 star It states quite clearly on their site FAQ:DOES THIS FOOD CONTAIN ETHOXYQUIN?Taste of the Wild Pet Foods sources all protein meals (chicken meal, fish meal, etc) from vendors that do not use ethoxyquin. As always, only natural preservatives are used in our manufacturing process to preserve the foods.So why someone would review this and give it 1 star is beyond me! I started to use this after my smooth coat chihuahua Herbie seemed a little sickly. I didnt realize soy and grain is not a good thing for our animals. I previously used Royal Canin.  He's full of energy and his coat is darker and shiny! We also augment his food with the Tast Of The Wild Wetlands food and he loves that also.  The high protein content means the animal will be less hungry and consume less food in the long run.  Think about it if you eat chicken or steak your less hungry than if you ate a bunch of rice because carbs get burned quickly. BUY this food your doggy will thank you for it!

column9: Still Too Much Fat, But Less Than Some Flavors...
column10: Tried this, recently, (in all dry flavors) for my German Shepherd Dog. At first, he wouldn't touch it, but after about a week, he decided he absolutely loves it. The biggest problem is within the first month, he had gained 3 pounds, even though he was eating less than the recommended amount and less than he was previously used to eating. Also, he had soft, oily looking stools while eating this. He is an active, very healthy, well-exercised, older dog. He did seem to be more "chipper" and health-wise, he seemed to do fine, except for the softer stools and weight gain, but reluctantly, we had to stop feeding this, exclusively, as we were feeding less and less and he was still gaining weight AND seemed hungry all the time, looking for any other food to eat. Since he loves the taste so much, we have decided to give him only a cup or so a day, in his Kong, with his other food or as training treats and have switched him to another food. I'm not sure I agree with the "good for all life stages" philosophy either. In the old days, that was what one did, but now that we know much more about nutrition, I believe that different life stages do require different nutrient levels. Much as humans do. Sadly, for our dog, this can not be the only food he eats, but it will remain a part of his daily diet, since he loves it and did well, except for the fat content. Hope this helps!

I have shih tzu's (a few to be exact) and I have to say this is the best food I have ever fed them.  I only purchase the pacific stream because it has 25% protien vs 32% that a couple of the other formula's have.  One other one also has 25% protien which is a good amount for small dogs.  Anyways...I had one girl that seemed itchy and would get hot spots periodically.  After switching to this food the itchyness is completely gone and no hotspots since. They have nice firm poops and I really can't say enough about it. They are all used to high end dog food as I have in the past fed Innova, canidae and was feeding blue buffalo...all of which were good dog foods and for the most part worked really well.  I have always been a fan of grain free food, but most has too high of protien for tiny dogs. Hi quality and certain meat or fish products keep the protien levels in check for small dogs that do not need the high amounts (work dogs and bigger dogs it is fine)...I was so excited to find a grain free food with perfect protien levels (IMO)and it has been wonderful. It is definately a 5* rating in my book.

I've been feeding Taste of the Wild for over a year and all 3 of my dogs are doing very well on it.  My german shepherd has a lot of allergies and so far this is the only food I've tried that she hasn't had problems with.  Its a good moderately priced dog food and much better than the grocery store brands.

column9: Excellent quality grain-free food at a good price
column10: I've done hours and hours of homework on high quality, grain-free dog foods.  From product analysis, kcal analysis, ingredients, customer reviews, professional reviews, company recalls - all of it... I have become a mini-expert in the field.I was pushed into becoming an expert because my yellow Lab kept having seizures and I couldn't figure out the source.  I finally learned it was her food, which was the most expensive store bought brand my local Sams Warehouse carries.  I thought I was giving her the best, it looked fresh and rich, but it turns out it was just absolutely terrible food.  My black Lab also had terrible skin allergies, to the point where I would get a small rash on my skin if he laid next to me on the couch for more than 5 minutes at a time.  I had no clue it was because of the food.  But it was!Since having that epiphany and learning so much about dog food, I've always made sure to feed them the highest quality grain free food I can buy.  This Taste of the Wild (TOTW) fits the bill very nicely, and they love it.  Since switching to a grain free diet, the yellow lab has not had any more seizures in over a year, and the black lab has the silkiest coat you've ever seen and his skin allergies are completely gone.They are on 2/3rds dry and 1/3rd wet combination.  Contrary to what I had previously been raised to believe, a wet diet is not bad for dogs but in fact is superior!  I use the combination to save money while providing them the best I can.Before deciding on TOTW, I had also tried Blue Buffalo, Wellness Core, and Orijen.  Briefly: they are all good foods, but my labs were happiest on TOTW and my wallet is also happiest on TOTW.  I also believe TOTW has a better formulation for them and their life style (some of the products, like Orijen, are simply too rich for the average household dog, despite being made of the best ingredients available).Enter TOTW.  The dry food is dark and rich, with no sign of crumbling.  The kibble is a good average size.  The wet food has nice chunks of meat and the right amount of gravy.  I use the wet food as a topper to mix the 2/3rd dry and 1/3rd wet together for their meals.  I use one whole can of wet per meal with my pack, which is convinient so I don't have to store it in the refrigerator - btw, never store canned dog food in the fridge in the original aluminum container!I still wish I could find a less expensive product with the same quality, but in the mean time, TOTW is the best choice for my pack.

column9: Food production plant has a lot of issues & my dog is sick
column10: One of the three plants that makes Taste of the Wild in South Carolina has had some quality control issues. Two other brands made at the plant have been recalled for Salmonella. My dog happens to be very sick with Salmonella symptoms. I spent over $800 at the vet and he almost died.  Is it a coincidence that there is a Salmonella issue at the plant and my dog is very ill with similar symptoms? I'm not sure, but I don't trust them anymore.

This is absolutely the best dog food I've ever used. We have both a Boxer and an English Bulldog. Before this food, they both had sensitive stomachs and even more sensitive, acne prone skin. Now they poo only twice a day. They shed less, their coats and skin are both flawless. Honestly!!!!  I absolutely cannot tell you how much of a positive change we've realized since finding Taste of the Wild Salmon formula.

column9: Beware:  Gulf of Mexico products (oil spill & chemical concern) in this food.
column10: I loved the idea of this product until I saw the film "The Big Fix" and learned that the fish from the Gulf of Mexico is probably not actually safe to eat (despite what our government wants us to believe).The 2nd ingredient in this food (which I've been feeding my beloved pets) is "ocean fish meal."  I wrote and phoned Diamond Pet Foods (maker of Taste of the Wild) and confirmed that their "ocean fish meal" indeed comes from the Gulf of Mexico.  I then did my own research and confirmed online that today (April 2012) there are major concerns with the fish and seafood coming from the gulf.  Fish are showing up with black and bright red 'lesions' and crustaceans are showing up with blackened body parts.  This was in some video taken by a journalist and posted on the web.If you watch The Big Fix you'll learn not only about the oil that is likely sitting on the bottom of the gulf, but you'll also learn about toxic chemical dispersant branded as COREXIT, which has been used extensively in the gulf to hide the oil.  This is what's REALLY going on with the fish in the gulf and you can probably assume that pet food is considered a great way to "dispose" of food products within the commerce chain.I'm stopping feeding my pet this food immediately because despite what the bag depicts (wolves and bears in the wild) one of the major ingredients ("ocean fish meal") doesn't come from the pacific northwest at all, but actually comes from the gulf of Mexico which is a suspect source of food for both humans and pets according to the alternative press.For reference check out the following articles.  Amazon won't let me post links so you must google these as key words:1.  Lauran Neergaard's 4/25/12 gruesome photo for AP of fish in a Gainsburg FL paper.  She's a medical writer.2.  Amy Goodman's Due Diligence On Gulf Oil Spill 4/24/123.  4/23/12 Crustacean biologist Darryl Felder of University of Louisana reports "finding crab and lobster, etc., that had black gills, that had appendages falling off" plus "parasites and other illnesses" setting in.4.  "Gulf Aquatic Wildlife Deformities Alarm Scientists" 4/21/12, Dr. Jim Cowan of Louisiana State University5.  Same article as #4:  Dr Wilma Subra, a chemist and Macarthur Fellow, has conducted tests on seafood and sediment samples along the Gulf for chemicals present in BP's crude oil and toxic dispersants."Tests have shown significant levels of oil pollution in oysters and crabs along the Louisiana coastline," per Subra.
Great dog food my dog has been on this food since she was a puppy and her coat has been always so beautiful and her energy level is out the roof. I recommend you give this food a try!

I rescued a 14 week old puppy the first week of December. They fed him purina puppy at the rescue (who can blame them). After two days he came down with K9 influenza and was on all sorts of medicine. We had to give him water with a turkey baster. After almost a month of pills and force feeding him canned food, he kicked his virus, but because his body was still recovering and he was growing, he needed the best food he could get. I read about Taste of the Wild on a dog food review site and found it at a specialty store near my work. I got him a bag and he went CRAZY! I swear he could smell it through the bag! He now gobbles it down, then drags his dish across the kitchen begging for more! I swear, he can't get enough! This food increased not only his health, but his coat is beautiful, his energy level is back and he is finally acting like the puppy he didn't get to be! I truly believe this food helped him incredible. No fillers, no byproduct, it has everything he needs. Boomer gives it two paws up!

column9: Finally a food he will eat!
column10: I adopted a 10 month old boxer from the pound and learned the hard way just how picky of eaters they can be! When I got him, he was underweight, his coat was just so-so, and his stools were soft-liquid at times. I tried several different brands of food that we had luck with previously, but he just wouldn't eat them. I also discovered that boxers are prone to sensitive stomachs and allergies, especially when it comes to grains. After lots of research, I decided to try TOTW since it was a grain free product with lots of great reviews on multiple sites. After starting him on TOTW, he is finally eating and starting to look healthy! His coat is shiny and soft, his stools are well formed, and he seems to love the food!

When we rescued our shelter dog (a Golden Ret/Border Collie mix), we found he had terrible diarrhea and chewed on himself frequently.  It seemed to be allergies and a sensitive stomach, and he began taking antihistamines and steriods twice a day.  Not knowing whether his allergies were food or environment related, I began to try different foods.  It was more of a challenge because our other dog is a VERY picky eater, and I had been through the food trials with her previously to find a food she would eat, but I had to help the new guy.  After trying a few foods recommended for dogs with allergies, my poor guy broke out in sores, had urinary & anal gland problems, gas, and on-and-off diarrhea.  I went to our local pet food store & spent a couple hours reading tons of ingredients labels & decided to try Taste of the Wild Wetlands formula.  It helped tremendously! The sores he had gotten from lamb, bison, etc. finally started to clear up, he didn't scratch or chew as much, and after about a week, his stomach adjusted and he had the most normal potties he had yet.  I found that he still did chew on himself here and there, so after a month or so, I switched to the Pacific Stream formula and now he's pretty much chew free since then.  During the process, I gradually lessened his medications & stopped them entirely since he's been on this food.  And the bonus is, the picky eater LOVES it and eats a whole bowl every day.  Even better yet, I found this to be very reasonably priced than many other foods, and I would check your local pet store before buying anywhere online;  mine is quite a bit cheaper.

I have used this dog food for several years and think that the quality is great being that it is grain-free and uses actual meat for protein.  It is also reasonably priced for the high quality of the food.  My dogs are large breed (90 plus lbs), have great energy levels, shiny coats, and not only smaller stools, but also perfectly formed.  This variety worked especially well for my bulldog who had runny eyes, pretty bad skin allergies on his face and a sensitive stomach which led to runny stools.  While this food did not eliminate his skin allergies completely--it helped enormously with all issues previously mentioned. As for shedding, I did not notice any more or any less shedding using this food compared to others.  Dogs shed and there isn't a complete cure for that:) None of the dogs gained excess weight, keeping in mind that I feed each dog measured quantities per day and usually a touch under the recommended feeding amount on the bag.Love that this food is delivered to my house!

We adopted a 5 year old black lab who was a walking snowstorm of dandruff when we got him.  He had no hair on his belly and a lot missing from the rest of him due to severe untreated allergies.  We started him on this food practically as soon as we got him (less than a month later after seeing our wonderful vet).  First off, he loved this stuff.Otherwise, I could not recommend this more strongly.  My dogs will never eat anything but this again.  We've now had him for almost two years and his hair has returned (he has a bald patch on his belly still, but it is a huge improvement).  His skin is great now and his coat is shiny, he gets compliments all the time.When we were staying with my parents for a while they tried their chihuahua on it, and although the pieces were a little big for him, he seemed to like it more than most foods.Overall, this is a fantastic product at a more expensive price, but I firmly believe it is worth it and that this helped him recover from his allergies (along with proper treatment).  But our dog who was allergic to 33 of the scratch samples no longer requires steroids or any major medication to be our happy and healthy puppy!

column9: Very good dog food for the price!
column10: I know nobody wants to read a wall of text on how good or bad this dog food is, so here is a very brief summary:Pros:1. Price per pound is very economical. Price is actually much cheaper than lower quality foods such as Eukanuba, Purina, etc. It isn't cheaper than Pedigree, but at the same time it isn't filled with garbage like Pedigree is.2. Dog likes the taste. A lot of my friends feed this to their dogs. I fed it to one of my dogs before. He likes it. My other dog doesn't but he doesn't like any kibble anyways, so it isn't this food's fault.3. Food quality is good. No by-products or corn or any other garbage (like unknown sources of bone and meat meals, etc).4. No more ethoxyquin in any taste of the wild products!Cons:1. Dogs seem to poop more on this food than other brands such as Orijen or Wellness. Not a lot more though so this isn't really a biggie.2. Made by diamond Pet foods. Not really a biggie either, but diamond pet foods had been plagued with pet recalls problems in the past. Taste of the Wild hasn't had any recalls that I know of, but you're still running a risk, just a really small one.Compared to other brands, this is probably 4 out of 5, but it would be unfair because this brand is much cheaper. Orijen costs almost 2x of what taste of the wild cost.

column9: Perfect all natural Dog Food - we pay only $47.00 + tax!
column10: Priced too high!!!We buy this food at a Feed store and pay $47.00 + tax!Our 6 dogs love this food. We have 3 Chihuahua's 2 Labs and 1 Shepherd mix and they have all done well with it since we discovered about 2 years ago. We've tried other "natural" kibbles but these are the BEST, hands down! Our Chihuahua's like theirs with a little warm water - it really brings out the flavor and they love the gravy!Our Chihuahua's used to have sensitive stomachs but not anymore, all of our dogs have improved skin and they have really soft, shiny fur. You also don't need to feed them as much food as the less nutritious competitor (which contains corn) and they all of them have perfectly formed stools.It's always recommended by your Vet to gradually change your dogs over to a new diet but once you do, you will never need to coax your dog to dinnertime - they'll actually let you know when it's time! We rate "Taste of the Wild Dry Dog Food" - especially "Pacific Stream Canine Formula with Smoked Salmon" because it's our dog's favorite as well as ours!

column9: Great results for allergies, company said ethoxyquin free
column10: I have a beagle with bad food allergies, I started a different limited ingredient food and she still had loose stools so I decided to give taste of the wild pacific stream a try. She has no more loose stools and its only been 2 weeks now. This is the first food I tried that helped with that. I can't say how good otherwise because its only been 2 weeks now, but so far so good and I called the company and they do guarantee that it is ethoxyquin free. It is also one of the top foods on dog food analysis. Since she is a beagle and only 25 pounds, I am pleased with the protein amount for a dog her size. The last food she was on was lower protein and some are to high for her size. I made sure this food was ethoxyquin free before I purchased it. She loves it. This is the first time in a year that her stools are formed, and not very loose. I am having her allergy tested in 2 weeks so I will know if its ok for her to stay on this food but so far eliminating grains for her has been great. I won't know the full effect until a few months as far as the itchiness and biting her feet, but so far this is helping her a lot. I will give an update once she is on it longer. I have tried quite a few other limited ingredient foods and allergy formulas and she would vomit and have a ton of itching, but this one she tolerated right away and I weaned her slowly. She is very sensitive to foods.

column9: Need to coax dog to eat it, but had no problem switching
column10: My dog, a half Yorkie half Bichon, recently decided to start being picky about her food.  I tried taking it away when she would it etc, but then she'd end up eating only half her food in a day, and after several days of that (and several months of trying other techniques to get her to eat), I gave up and finally switched foods.  She wasn't happy with anything for more than a few days (dried food, that is), so I decided to try Taste of the Wild's salmon and lamb flavors, since they had lower protein and fat content than the other flavors.  She ate both for a few days, then wouldn't eat it, so I started adding a teaspoon of one of Merrick's canned foods (a super moist one), mixing it all together, and now she loves it (thus I'm taking a star away since she wouldn't eat it plain after a few days).  What I liked about this food is that I was able to switch immediately, no transition period, without a glitch (hey, she wouldn't eat the other food, so I didn't have much choice!).  And, bonus points, her stool is, for the first time in her short year long existence, perfect with this food.  It never was before.  So on the stool count alone, I decided to stick with this. It's been a month and she's still eating it - I give her salmon in the morning and lamb at night, I didn't feel right just feeding her fish and no meat, but am switching the two flavors back and forth hoping the variety keeps her going.  So far so good.  Oh, and I'm not noticing the difference in the coat that others have mentioned, but maybe four weeks isn't a long enough time to notice.

My dogs love this stuff and can't wait for mealtime. Just the right amount of protein to give them some energy. They have shiny coats and their weight is maintained on it. They have tried all of the Taste of the Wild products but this seems to suit them best. It also seems to last longer than other brands with 30lb. bags.

column9: Taste of the Wild Pacific Stream Dry Dog Food
column10: This is an excellent product in line with others made by Taste of the Wild.  The only drawback to it is that there is, understandably, a "fishy" aroma to it.  However, all four of my large breed dogs love it.

column9: shiny coats + no more doggy odors = happy family!
column10: Our German Shepherd Dogs have really taken to Taste of the Wild (TOTW). Their coats are now gleaming, the perpetual skin issues on one has improved remarkably and our senior dogs are running faster than ever, again. Our eldest had major spine surgery for an injury this summer and has made significant improvements - his mobility returned within a few weeks, which we feel was partially due to feeding him TOTW in addition to some well-researched supplements (turmeric, carnitine, magnesium, alpha lipoic acid, boswelia complex, etc) not normally needed but due to his major injury.)TOTW has totally eliminated destructive chewing / cribbing habits.  The foul doggy stench that developed when we were feeding Purina and Pedigree has now been completely eliminated.  The dogs are happier and we are happier. Thanks!

Both our German Shepherds love Taste of the Wild. We switched over from their regular brand a couple of months ago as it was getting too expensive. They both turned their nose away at four other brands before settling on this one.
my dogs go nuts for this stuff,  and its so healthy for them, you cant compare this to any other dog food when it comes to the ingredients.  good stuff

The dog loves the food and we love it because its wheat free and really helps decrease the amount he sheds. Also a good product for the money. The only draw back is that its a bit fishy smelling so it attracts the cat too!

column9: Fine product, but way too fishy smelling!
column10: I went from the bison formula to this fish one for my 4 month old German Shepherd.  We started at a ratio of new to old being 1:4 for the first 2 days, and then half for a day, and then full out. I thought this transition should be fine since its from the same manufacturer, but boy was I wrong! This was way too fast of a transition and our dog had the runs for many days afterwards. 1.5 weeks later it stiffened up well enough for about 1-2 weeks. However, at the moment she is having the runs again, although I don't think it has anything to do with the food anymore. Out vet claims it is growing pains.Anyway, my biggest problem with this food is its strong fishy smell. Its like you had raw fish sitting out in room temp for a day or so.  Just because this smell factor, I am not going to get this formula again.I'd like to note, I sampled another brand with fish formula, and it had the same problem. So I would assume all the fish formulas do this regardless of brand.I plan to try the venison next.

column9: Golden Retriever/Lab mix won't touch it, likes other formulas
column10: I feed my dog several Taste of the Wild formulas (lamb, bison & venison, wild fowl).  He likes them all except he won't touch the Pacific Stream salmon mix.  If I put one scoop of each formula in four different bowls, the food in three of the bowls will disappear quickly, but the salmon formula just sits there.  The lamb formula appears to be the favorite, followed by bison, then fowl.  Dog is a little over 1 year old, golden retriever/lab mix.  He will gladly eat actual salmon, but not this salmon dog food.

column9: Great nutrition and a reasonable price
column10: I have been feeding my dogs Science Diet for years and finally took the time to research what exactly was in the "vet recommended" (yes, my vet did recommend Science Diet) dog food.  After doing considerable research, I narrowed it down to three dog food brands.  One of which was simply cost prohibitive, the other was Wellness dog food and then Taste of the Wild.  I ordered TOTW for our new Mini Aussie puppy and was very pleased with what I received.  I decided to try Wellness for our three year old Pug who eats just about anything.  After a single feeding of Wellness being mixed into our Pug's Science Diet, he stopped eating and refused to even go near the bowl of food and suffered horrible tummy troubles.  For over a week we could not get him to eat much of anything until I ordered TOTW.  Now he is eating like there was never a problem and loves his new food.  I did some research and apparently others have had similar problems with Wellness dog food.  The ingredients that goes into this dog food, combined with the price that it is offered at, and you have a very good choice for your furry friends.
Great way to have heavy food delivered at your doorstep, no hassle getting bag from store to car and into your house.My dog loves it, and it has helped clear up his skin allergies.

column9: Nom nom nom, helped dry skin.
column10: My mutt had trouble with dry skin for a long time. We switched to a food with fish in it and that helped considerably, but when we switched to this food it cleared up completely - and she never has any digestive problems with this food.I also like knowing that the food I feed my dog is of higher quality than what I feed myself.If you have a small dog I would be a little careful buying the big bag because I have found that after a while the food can start to smell "off" which I assume means it is going bad. (Which is a good thing! Real food goes bad after a while!)My dog has never had trouble with not liking food, so I can't really say if this is gourmet from a dog taste bud perspective.

After seeing the energy levels and overall healthiness of sled dogs in Alaska who had a salmon rich diet, I was intrigued.  Granted their calorie needs are off the charts, so something designed for typical canine (or even St Bernard) consumption would be a better route to try.  Thus at first I tried Canidae Pure Dry Dog Food, Sea Salmon, 30-Pound Bag.  It was available locally, came with some recommendations (though reading online opinions were all over the map), and I needed to change food for allergy concerns.  Anyway My dog never quite took to it, and we switched to Flint River Ranch.  My dog eats the Flint River food, but he's still loosing weight as he can't eat enough of it.  Thus I'm trying this route, with great success.  He eats whatever he has in front of him, and then he cleans up the crumbs (the smallish and light kibble stick to his jowls and fly out of the bowl).  I couldn't be happier withe behavior like that in the kitchen or the more solid treasures he leaves in the yard.  All in all it's a great food.  A couple other pluses are the nice thick plastic bag and an overall lack of fishy smell.
Ive had my 2 belgian malinois on this for about a year since they seemed to have grain allergies. They love it, shiny fur, and seem healthier all around. Good product.

Read online a lot places that this was the best food for frenchies, and they were right.He scarfs it down, is perfectly healthy and his coat is great.Definitely more expensive than department store dog food, but you get what you pay for: great food.

We adopted an adult mix last year who was in need of love and care.  His coat is now soft and shiny and the amount of waste he produces is significantly down from when he ate other food.  Well worth it to me.

column4: Donna's Reviews "I Love Shopping on Amazon!"
column10: My dogs eat this they love it and have had zero stomach problems since being on it!July 3, 2011....The BEST Dog Food ever! My yorkie-poodle mix and havanese poodle mix Still love this food we buy the Salmon Dry and add a little can of the same and they have Always gobbled it up and had ZERO stomach issues!Twice I have used other dog foods and then big companies like Proctor and Gamble by them and start adding Junk ingredients and my dogs started getting loose stools and go more frequently!PLEASE don't Sell out keep this Wonderful dog food as is!

column9: Good for my sensitive stomach dogs
column10: After learning that California Natural and their company natura had been purchased by proctor and gamble, i immediately went on the search for new food for my 4 sensitive-stomach doberman mixes. All having spent seven years collectively in rescues, they all have stomach issues and after trying 3 other foods for 2 weeks each, Taste of the Wild Pacific Stream Formula was the one they all, but one, have transitioned to. Now after 6 months on this diet, I am extremely happy with their energy level, coat sheen, and they all have a very nice solid pain free movement...and I wish I'd have found this food sooner. This formula was sold as being the best one of their line for sensitive stomach dogs and it has turned out to be true. I like the fact that it is grain free and their stools are much healthier than my one dog who is still on grain food. Good quality food and the price points are great.
Best value, and the dogs like it. Produces small, compact, easy to pick up and flush down a toilet, stools. I feed it to my German Shepard,chihuahua and Yorkshire Terrier.

I just started my 14 wk old GS pup on this recently.  I was giving her Innova Large Puppy breed and she had soft stools at best, but mostly pudding-like since she was 9 wks old.  The first day that I replaced just 25% of her meal with TOTW, it was like magic - perfect stool!  I am praying that this continues. . .I did read that anything that has fish meal has ethoxyquin - so I am not thrilled about that.  I have read horrible things about almost every supposed great food though, so I'll keep with this for a little while and then find something w/o fish meal.

Taste of the Wild has recently issued a recall. I ordered this from Amazon and got a tainted bag of food. I am currently on the phone trying to get ahold of the dog food company's customer service. I'll post with an update of what they say to do, and then may contact Amazon. (Hopefully shipping back will not have to happen - the idea of shipping 30lb of dog food does not appeal). In the mean time, hold off on ordering this food until Amazon can assure us that they will not send tainted products. Here is the article about the recall.When Diamond Pet Products recalled their Chicken Soup for the Soul food, I expected a recall of Taste of the Wild to follow. The holistic, grain-free food is made by the same company.And today comes word that, indeed, Diamond Pet Foods has issued a recall of a limited run of Taste of the Wild dry dog food over concerns about possible Salmonella contamination.According to the press release:To determine if your pet food is recalled, consumers should check the production codes on the back of bags. Any production codes that have a number "2" or a "3" in the 9th or 10th digit and an "X" in the 11th digit in the production code should be discarded. The best before dates are December 9, 2012, through April 7, 2013.The recall affects only products distributed in the following U.S. states and Canada. Further distribution to other pet food channels may have occurred.AlabamaFloridaGeorgiaIndianaKentuckyMassachusettsMarylandMichiganMississippiNew YorkNorth CarolinaOhioPennsylvaniaSouth CarolinaTennesseeVirginiaCanadaPet owners who are unsure if the product they purchased is included in the recall, or who would like replacement product or a refund, may contact Diamond Pet Foods via a toll free call at 1-866-918-8756, Monday through Sunday, 8 am - 6pm EST. Consumers may also go to diamondpetrecall.com for more information. The company is working with distributors and retailers to ensure all affected product is removed from shelves.

I have a 2 year-old Siberian Husky to whom I fed Eukanuba for her first year of life. She would eat the food but more often than not I had to coax her into it. I would have to add a little something extra to get her to eat, such as: cheese, yogurt, apple sauce, tomato sauce, etc. Even then sometimes she would just lick the extra ingredient off the food and leave the kibble. She would completely miss a meal at least weekly. I eventually learned that the commonly used grains in such foods can irritate a dog's stomach as they wouldn't naturally eat corn or wheat in the wild, so I tried this food.After reading the ingredients label on this product I swear to you I thought: "This reads like something *I* would eat!" There isn't a single ingredient in this food you will not recognize and I was excited to see my dog try it. Needless to say, she absolutely loved it! She likes it so much I occasionally worry she's actually eating TOO FAST. Since I switched she has not missed a single meal in over a year and it takes NOTHING extra to get her to eat. Further, when the bowl is empty she'll spend a good 5 seconds licking it clean.I'm happy to say my 50lbs girl is in excellent health with pearly-white teeth.Now this particular blends main ingredient is salmon but I believe they have others with fowl or bison so you might need to find which one your dog prefers. This food IS more expensive than your standard grocery-store/pet-store food BUT you will have to feed them LESS per meal given the improved nutrition profile. I highly recommend this food for active, medium to large breed dogs.(Edited for typos).
Hoping this new dog food will have amazing results with my dogs. I like the list of ingredients and they seem to like the taste.

column9: Great dog food . . . $25 cheaper at my local feed store.
column10: Great dog food . . . $25 cheaper at my local feed store. FIVE stars for the dog food . . . ZERO stars for the sellers price gauging tactics.

column9: Good food (if you hate your dog)
column10: I love ordering from Amazon, but unfortunately I have nothing good to say about Taste of the Wild dog food. I have been feeding this food to my 3 dogs for several years now, but with the most recent dog food recall affecting TOTW, I am switching to a different brand. Taste of the Wild is made by Diamond, which is famous for pet food recalls. There are plenty of other reasonably priced, high quality, grain-free pet foods on the market, that have NEVER had a pet food recall. No reason for me to continue risking my pet's health by feeding it this garbage. When I contacted TOTW regarding their latest recall, they were rude and dismissive of my concerns. Too bad. TOTW (and all other Diamond products), will no longer receive my business or recommendations. Suggestions: Fromm (never had a recall-in business since 1904), Orijen, Honest Kitchen, Halo, Dr. Harvey's. Try dogfoodadvisor.com when searching for a new food. Lots of reviews and good information.

Found many small, yellow, hard pieces in the bag, many stuck to pieces of food.  It looks like kernels of corn even though there is not supposed to be corn in the food! Quite disturbing.  The bag was ordered from Pet Solutions.

I say the food "May" have caused Hives because I cannot be sure it was related to this food but it definitely could have been... My 9 month female boxer first started with tiny bumps which got worse over a period of 3 weeks. Not long after our larger male boxer puppy started getting large Red hives on His face also.The only thing different about their diet was this food. At first we did not think this was from the food (they were on it 2 weeks before any symptoms) and tried every other avenue to locate the cause of the Hives, Bug Bits, Fleas, Recently Washed Bedding Etc...After looking to every other area for the cause and the Hives only getting worse and worse we stopped feeding them this food altogether. It has only been 2 Days since we switched them over to a Natural Balance L.I.T. Allergy Formula and so far the Hives have stopped from getting any worse. Its still too Soon to say for sure this was the cause but at least the Hives seem to be slowing!

column9: For a Healthy Dog, Avoid This Dog Food
column10: One of the ingredients on the label is "Natural Flavors" which is glutamate in hiding.  Glutamate is a neuro toxin which can destroy your dog's health.  The company is very deceptive.  They avoid giving a direct answer.  They call glutamate a vegetable extract which it indeed is, however, when one component is extracted, it creates an imbalance that can be harmful.  I will say this.  My dogs like it, but that is the purpose of glutamate, a flavor enhancer.  Added later:  Why should anything need to be extracted to enhance the flavor of quality food for pets or humans for that matter.  I now make many of my dogs meals from mostly raw ingredients and give them Organix dog food when I need a quick meal.  For those who are concerned about their pet's health, I suggest the book "Natural Health for Dogs and Cats" by Dr. Richard Pitcairn, D.V.M.

column9: This is great sauce! Glad it's on Amazon!
column10: This a great hot sauce. The sauce has some heat to it but is controlled and still has wonderful flavor. I eat it on many things and was happy to find it on Amazon. Do yourself a favor and try this sauce.
I don't usually leave reviews but i am a hot sauce collector. This is the best hot sauce on the planet. Just a heads up..

This is the best hot sauce ever!  It is not too hot and has a great flavor. I first purchased this years ago, when I was at the grocery store looking for a new hot sauce.  The lable said "Try Me" and I was hooked. I put a tablespoon  in my Cup of Soup to really jazz up the flavor.  I put it in everything from chili to soups to tacos.  Try it on french fries!

column9: Great hot sauce, big on flavor
column10: This tastes fantastic. My only complaint is the heat, it is not quite as hot as I was hoping, but I'm sure the majority of people will find it just right.

column9: omg! THE BEST on the planet!!!!
column10: yes, i bought this @ randalls discounted out...omg. the best hot sauce i have ever had. i will be stocking this in my house regularly. my father started me out on hot sauce at an early age, and yes, i married a hot sauce lover,too.  we usually try a new one abt twice a month. we do not need to look any further for the perfect hot sauce. awesome product. i cant wait to see if they sell any other stuff.
I live in the PNW and could not find this product anywhere. I ordered it here for a great price and it is already half gone. This is the best hot sauce EVER!

I found this at a local Hannafords supermarket for either $2.50 or $2.70 a bottle, it's hands down the best buy for a bottle of hot sauce.I tried a cap full first, and while it's not the hottest habanero based sauce I've had, it is up there with the most flavorful.  The first time I tried this on some chicken and spanish rice however, I did not think the taste worked out as well on the chicken and rice.  I tried it again on the same kind of chicken and spanish rice, and it was wonderful.  Whether it was something I ate right before or what, I don't know, but I don't think it was a bad bottle as it was excellent plain.I have also tried it on burritos, and that was exceptionally good as well.

I am such a fan of this sauce, I came to Amazon just give it some love.  My local IGA actually carries this sauce and it's by far one of my favorites.  Whenever we have pizza this guy is on the table.  Not too hot but the the flavor is great.  This is not a sauce I grab when I am having mexican food or chili.  I use El Yucateco Green Habanero sauce or Dave's Insanity Sauce in chili and usually El Yucateco or Cholula in Mexican food.Having said that, I am a chili head and can't get enough of the heat... this sauce will forever have a place in my fridge.Many have come and gone but this one is a keeper.

column9: One of the Best Hot Sauce in my collection
column10: For some reason the local stores I visit no longer carry this brand of hot sauce, not sure why?. I was fortunate to find it online and it was shipped very promptly. This sauce is one of the best in my collection of hot sauces.

This is the only sauce I will use in my chile or jerky.The local market stopped selling it, so I get it online.It's well worth paying shipping. A lot of heat & a great tangy flavor.Make it mild or wild, this is what you want !!1st mate.

column9: My favorite hot sauce by far!
column10: I put this stuff on everything.  It has a good heat but a great flavor!  Not boring or too much vinegar, like Tabasco.  I always have a few bottles of these around.

I have bought and use a wide-wide variety of hot sauces.  IMO Tabasco is ----.  This is my absolute favorite.  Not the hottest, but I drown my food with it.  Sometimes I find it cheaper than this at Whole foods, but this is a better price, than Safeway.  If you think you're a connoisseur, and you haven't tried this, you owe it to yourself to try it. My 12 year old loves it too.

I really like this hot sauce, enough that I keep buying the 6 pack when I run out.  This isn't very hot at all, but it has a great flavor.  I sometimes add a lot of this and then a little bit of another hot sauce for heat.  This does have vinegar in it, but not a bad vinegar taste like Tabasco does.  I would have given it 5 stars if it was hotter, but this gives a lot of people a way to add good flavor without adding too much heat.

Yucatan Sunshine is the best hot sauce there is in my humble opinion because it gives you the habanero heat yet it's not intolerable. Better yet you get the intensely rich flavor of the habanero pepper and it's sweet, but not sugary and you don't feel the need to add salt either. I grow several varieties of Habanero, chocolates, ghost, heirloom, and Scotch Bonnet Red and Jamaican Giants as well as Tabasco, Jalapeno and Thai chilis. I'm even growing the Bhut jolokia this year. They all go well with Pimiento a mild meaty sweet pepper and make great sauces for pork chicken and fish. Since I never have enough home grown to last until the next season Yucatan Sunshine provides the best alternative for me in heat, in flavor & in fresh taste. Especially on pizza during football season! PEACE.

Tabasco® stinks up your dish with aroma of vinegar, this doesn't. it has heat but a lot of flavor too. not super-hot so i tend to use a lot more of it than concentrated sauces.Bottom line: this is my favorite hot sauce.

For those that can handle Tabasco, give Sunshine a try.  It is bursting with flavor and has adequate heat.  If I want amp something up for heat I add Dave's Temporary Insanity Extract Sauce to a flavorful sauce like Sunshine.  Yucatan Sunshine is my overall favorite hot sauce, but sadly I can't buy it local anymore!

column9: The only hot sauce I use
column10: This is the best hot sauce I've ever had, it has a little heat but it's reall focus is on flavor.

This is a smooth, sweet, flavorful tea. I absolutely love it. It is an excellent replacement for after dinner coffee. The caramel flavor is amazing. I sometimes have it without dessert in place of the sweet. Try this anytime you feel the need to indulge. The Insfuser Bag is simply elegant. The stay fresh packaging is a wonderful idea.My only criticism is of the brewing instructions. Revolution uses the same instructions for black, red, green and white tea. Any research will tell you that there are differences in the brewing processes.
I have had a difficult time finding "lemon pepper" seasoning that the first ingredient is not "salt".This is no salt "0" sodium.

This came in a variety box of decaf kcups, and it's the worst of the bunch. Almost no flavor.I made a cup of decaf Breakfast Blend for my husband, and I made myself a cup of Newman's Own Organics Decaf Special Blend, K-cups for Keurig Brewers, 48-count in 2 Boxes of 24 Each. I thought he'd like the Breakfast Blend because that's often what he drinks in the morning. Apparently, my logic was flawed. My husband explained he mixes a cup of regular Breakfast Blend (for the caffeine) with a cup of dark roast (for the flavor), and then he said "Decaf breakfast blend is about as pointless as fat-free ribeye."The Newman's Own decaf and the Green Mountain Vermont Country Blend DECAF (24 K-cups) Keurig were both very good. I can't tell much difference in the taste of those decafs compared to regular coffee.

I had a lot of problems with squirrels trashing my suet feeders. They don't like this stuff but woodpeckers absolutely adore it. No more squirrel problem! Shipped quickly and was well packaged, but only four stars because I think the price is a bit on the high end for suet.

I have been taking care of a stray cat for a little over a year.  Last November ( 2010 ) the cat was attacked by either a hawk or raccoon and its face was seriously wounded and it looked like it would lose its eye.  After reading a book on herbal care I learned that Echinacea/Goldenseal work together as an antiviral/ antibacterial agent so I went on the hunt.  I found this product on Amazon and ordered it right away.  I added 10 drops to wet food twice a day along with 1000 mg l-lysine as per a vet's recommendation.  It was a long cold winter but the cat returned twice a day for its medication.  Eventually after 5 months of regular treatment the wound healed and the cat's eye cleared up.  I do not know if the cat would have survived without this treatment.  I recommend its use to anyone who is working with stray and feral cats that have been wounded or are ill and who do not have immediate access to veterinary care.

Hi ... I recently purchased Animals' Apawthecary Echinacea/Goldenseal Blend for pets.  I have used this before to boost my cats' immune system.  It is an excellent brand!  I purchased on-line from Spring Valley Herbs via Amazon.  Their price is great including shipping and I would recommend them.  The first order showed that it was delivered by the USPS but for whatever reason, it was not located.  They replaced it within a week or so without charging me and I received the replacement quickly after it was sent.  I will definitely purchase from them again!
This product was supposed to help my dog heal, but all it did was mess up his stomach and give him diarrhea.Don't try it if your pet gets sick easily.Pretty disappointing.

This is not the Snow's clam chowder I have eaten my entire life.  Apparently, Bumble Bee has taken over Snow's and has changed the clam chowder recipe to such a degree that it is completely unrecognizable from it's previous state.  It has gone from the best canned clam chowder to something that is almost unedible.  Don't waste your money on this. . . you will be very disappointed.

It started raining this morning and I was feeling the hunger.Hmm...Yes! Snow's Authentic New England Style Clam Chowder.Into my fave cast iron pot. Heated up and into a bowl.Wait. What is this? So much for my clam chowder dance I did in the kitchen as it heated up.Pretty thin. Not too thin, but not thick like an ACTUAL clam chowder.Flavor: Bland. Very.I ate the entire bowl nonetheless, (hate wasting food)I kept thinking, where are the clams!!!!I think I bit down on one. It looks NOTHING like the picture either.Blech! The worst clam chowder I have ever had in a midwest diner beats this.Very bummed.
This is NOT the clam chowder I grew up with. It's thin, the taste is off and there is very little potatoes and definitely no clams. This product does a major disservice to New England!

Snow's New England Clam Chowder, Ready to Serve, 15-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12) VERY UNHAPPY! Snows Ready to Serve WAS the best. Now that bumbule bee has taken over it is a watery disapointment. Just think of BUM and go no further. If they go back to the original let me know, otherwise FORGET IT!

column9: Snow's New England Clam Chowder, Ready to Serve
column10: Unfortunately, in the past two years, this product has changed drastically -- no flavor,much thinner base and there appeared to be bits of dehydrated chicken included.This product formerly had a creamy rich base, clams and flavor.  Why did Bumble Bee do this?I would have been happy to pay more for what it used to be.  In its day, no other competitor'sproduct could touch it.

We were so disappointed.  I haven't been able to find Snow's Clam Chowder in my local stores for about 2 years so I was so excited to find it available here.  Unfortunately, I didn't read the reviews.  This is NOT SNOW'S CLAM CHOWDER.  This is some garbage that Bumble Bee has decided to market using the Snow's name.  Now I have 10 cans left from this case that will probably be fed to my neighbor's pigs because we certainly won't be eating the rest of this.  What a waste.
This is the Best canned Clam Chowder that I have ever eaten--I so miss it--since moving away from Maine and now living in the south where u cant get stuff like this-will be so glad to get

5lbs is quite a lot of Warheads! They were delicious and exactly what I wanted. Unlike another reviewer, I did have Blue Raspberry in my bag, but there were a lot less of them than the other flavors. Pucker up!
The price for the amount of candy was great and arrived quickly, everyone enjoyed the mixture of sour candy and lasted awhile.
wicked sour don't eat too much though your toungue wil be raw for a week. I highly recommend this but I noticed there were no blue rasberry warheads???

It's almost impossible to find a powder-based blended drink mix that's organic and fair-trade. This one is both, and it works like a charm. You'll need to play a bit with the portioning - in our coffeeshop, we use a single short shot of espresso, plus 2 ounces of milk, and roughly 20 ounces of ice to make a 16 oz. blended drink. Very popular in the 100% mid-Atlantic summers ...

column9: Tastes better than any other Frappe Blend I've tried!
column10: I'm extremely picky when it comes to coffe flavor, but I loved this frappe blend. The coffee flavor isn't overwhelming or bitter. I was a little nervous buying it in such a large bulk, but it the cost isn't as bad when you break it down by serving.  I'm happy I finally found an organic frappe that tastes good.

column9: No no no no!  How could they go so badly wrong?
column10: Boy oh boy.  Walden Farms is really a hit and miss operation.I think this stuff is probably my least favorite of their products I've tasted so far.  What makes no sense is that the ingredients that might add alfredo-esque taste, if they would choose to employ them in the recipe, aren't caloric.  Spices and salt would go a long way toward making this stuff edible.I will add that though the sauce is also as thin as h-e-double-hockey-sticks, I can deal with that in a zero-cal food. That's a sacrifice I can live with.  But it's the sickly-sweet flavor and the lack of any sort of savory component that makes this stuff such a startlingly-awful flop.  I suspect there's a whole lotta Splenda goin' on in this stuff.  Give it a pass and just thin out some other bottled "lite" alfredo sauce using fat-free milk.

column9: Expected Yuck (Calorie Free) But It's GREAT!
column10: Not sure why there are so many negative reviews here, but those reviewers got it wrong.  Take it from a butter, sugar and use the real thing kinda girl...this sauce has a lot of good flavor.  Only reason I ever tried it is because it was the only brand available at my local health food store a couple of years ago and I did not want to go to another store.  Boy was I PLEASANTLY surprised. I use it as a white sauce for pizza as well as alfredo dishes.

column9: Not truly an "alfredo", but not without merit
column10: First, this is a zero calorie, diet product.  I think anyone purchasing this product must fully understand that concept before tasting it.  It WILL NOT taste like the thick, rich alfredo sauce you'd get in a restaurant or make yourself.Ok, with that out of the way, the consistency is a bit thin but not water-thin.  Tasted on its own, out of the jar, its oddly sweet and not entirely good, but not entirely bad either.  It has tremendous potential to be improved with spices and some other small additions.  I warmed up the sauce with some sauteed (in PAM) onions, garlic powder, salt, black pepper and a bit of parmesan cheese.  The cheese helped thicken the sauce and bit and the pepper and onions definitely improved the flavor.  I served the sauce over spaghetti squash and it was delicious and fulfilling.  So, 3 stars since its not that great out of the box, but has tremendous potential for a low-calorie sauce option.As a baseline for those reading my review and deciding whether to purchase this particular Walden Farms product, I've tried MANY of their products and LOVE the pancake syrup, strawberry syrup, chocolate syrup, caramel syrup, honey dijon dressing, creamy bacon dressing, thousand island dressing.  I hated the marshmallow dip, the ranch dressing.  I really like the BBQ sauce, the chocolate dip and the caramel dip.  The mayo has a scary consistency but is a good "extender" for smaller servings of regular mayo or when mixed into a tuna salad.  I've tried many other dressings and liked them just fine, but the others weren't "stand outs" in any way.Happy dieting!
I found that it was pretty tasty expecially on whole wheat pasta.  Yes, it is thin, but a little goes a long way.  Both my husband and I thought for a diet product this was okay.

I'm afraid I have to agree with all the other negative reviews here. Maybe if I added my own Parmesan and butter to this sauce it would be at least tolerable. But if I have to do that then whats the point. I appreciate that Walden Farms is out there trying to give us some healthy alternatives. This one is a miss though. I use and enjoy some of their other products.

I wanted so desperately to like this sauce. Out of the jar, it smells and tastes awful. I cut it with sour cream and it didn't help matters, and adding extra seasoning (a lot of extra seasoning) did help for as long as the sauce was kept near boiling, but as soon as it cooled down any, it went back to smelling and tasting disgusting. I was really disappointed.

column9: This made me want to throw up
column10: This made me want to throw up, I wouldn't even want to experiment with this product. Not just zero stars but negative stars.

This was terrible! Don't buy it. I would rather eat air! I can't even describe how it tasted. If I could give it zero stars, I would have. There was not much flavor. Just sort of pepper with water and flour taste. I could have done a better job with a little seasoning some powdered milk and water.

Alfredo sauce is mostly cheese and cream based anyway so the "zero carb" selling point, while true, does not justify the high price tag in my opinion. Most any Alfredo sauce should be low carb in the first place. The reason why most aren't is because the thickness in Alfredo sauce comes from flour or wheat flour to give it that heartiness we're used to.This product doesn't contain flour so it's a lot thinner than traditional Alfredo sauce would otherwise be and is pretty much cream, cheese, and a bunch of spices. The funny part is that Alfredo Sauce is typically used with pasta which is chock full of carbs so you're really not going to gain any "low carb" points by using a sauce that has 0 grams on a bowl of pasta that has 100 grams.In terms of taste? This product, like many other diet products, tastes "off." You'd probably be able to tell it was trying to mimic alfredo sauce but you'd know something wasn't quite right about it. It's not a bad taste but like other reviewers have said it's kind of a strong, tangy, and in many ways synthetic taste.It's not great, bottom line, and Walden Farms makes some other really good products so personally I would skip this one. That being said it is truly a dieters product with zero carb, calories, fat, etc... so with that in mind it's not a BAD product when you consider it doesn't contain all the stuff that usually makes food taste good :-)

Tonight I had it with tofu noodles, chicken, broccoli and red pepper. I cooked it with some garlic, an onion and some black pepper. My husband tried it and thought it was great, and he usually doesn't like the this stuff.Use it as an ingredient instead of a stand alone sauce and you will find a ton of uses. But use it as a sauce alone and you will be disappointed. I find that is true with all Walden Food products. But I have been eating this with a low calorie diet and have lost 45 pounds in three months. Give it a try, be willing to experiment. You won't be disappointed.

Arnold Diaz did an expose of these pizzas.  They contain triple the amount of calories and carbs.  My local store took it the lab to be analyzed and came back with the same results.  They taste good but you might as well get a real slice of pizza.

column9: Filler food is empty, leaves your cat always needing more
column10: This review will make me sound really stupid, but whatever. I don't really care as long as people find out what's real and can avoid my mistakes.I got my wonderful little sweet Bella Bean when she was a few days shy of three years old. She had been bounced around from house to house and eating whatever was cheap. I have had cats around me my entire life, for about twenty-five years now. My mother always just fed them whatever, the kinds of food you buy in the supermarket - Friskies, Nine Lives, Kit & Kaboodle, stuff like that. And our cats were always fine, at least in terms of their eating habits. They would eat in the morning, stop when they were done, come back, and eat some more when they got hungry.My housemate at the time was working for Hill's and assured me that this was the best food ever made, so great, so on and so forth. I now know that she is an utter buffoon, but I initially trusted her judgment, which is so unfortunate because she doesn't think. She also had plenty of coupons for free or deeply discounted bags, which made it a much more attractive choice.I first tried feeding the little Bean an unmeasured amount of Science Diet in a bowl, but that didn't work, as she would devour it in one sitting. So then I took to measuring it, and she did the same thing. Then I started parsing it out to twice a day. That didn't work either, because she would start going crazy in the middle of the day, running around, intentionally destroying things, deliberately spilling her water, crying, etc., until she got more food. So then I split it into three servings. Same thing. Then it got to be four servings. That was a little better, but it was too much maintenance and unrealistic to be around every day to feed her four times. So then it went back to three. All the while, I was trying to reduce the amount of food I was feeding her to less than 3/4 of a cup because she was a little chubby. Reducing was hell. She became even more hungry, but I figured she would get used to it. Not really.For over a year, she would wake me up every morning looking for food in a serious way, knocking things off my desk, ripping up any paper she could find, scratching at the door and committing general acts of mischief. As soon as she got food, she was back to her sweet self, but only for three or four hours.We thought she was bored, we thought she was a little nutty, and maybe even had a kitty eating disorder. She always wanted food. It was kind of funny but in the end it was just sad.A few weeks back, we took her to a new (good, non-money factory) vet for her second checkup since I've had her. I talked with him about her being always hungry. He asked what she ate, and I told him the adult indoor Science Diet. Without saying as much, he basically told me that this food is garbage and I should look for something else. He said cat food should have a protein followed by a carbohydrate as the first two ingredients. Science Diet does, in a very loose, by-product kind of way - ground up slaughterhouse leftovers and corn dust. Then they put a bunch of vitamins in it to make it "healthy," instead of just using good ingredients from the beginning. Not that I care about spending money on the Bean, but this food is way too expensive for what it is.So we began transitioning her onto Wellness indoor formula about two weeks ago. She is still eating 50 percent Science Diet with 50 percent Wellness (you really shouldn't just give a cat different food one day out of the blue) but SHE NEVER FREAKS OUT ANYMORE. It's amazing. And it's 100 percent because she is eating real food now, along with that sawdust and chicken hearts I still regrettable have to feed her. We have her down to eating twice a day, only 1/3 cup in TOTAL. She was eating three times a day, 5/8 of a cup in total. Now she eats some in the morning, walks away, eats some more a few hours later, and then looks for dinner about twelve hours after her initial feeding. No more knocking things over, no more trashing Dad's papers on the desk, no more howling, no more deliberately spilled water on the floor. It's incredible.I feel so bad that I was doing this to her for so long. We really thought she was just being dramatic or whatever. But no, she was genuinely hungry because she wasn't eating any real food.Do your cat a favor - buy her or him so food made with real ingredients, things you would eat - Wellness, Halo, Innova, Evo, whatever. Figure it out for yourself, but please don't feed your cat this. It's garbage.

I got my cat at a shelter and they feed this to the cats there. My cat Wanda loves it. Never any waste and it makes for a cleaner litter box. Cuts stool odor down 90%. No dyes that can stain either. Keeps Wanda happy and very healthy.

My cat is picky, especially when it comes to dry food.  She will happily go days refusing to eat anything if I push a kibble she doesn't like on her (damn torties!.  I switched my cat from friskies to Hills Scienc Diet when she grew to adulthood.  Then I decided to try one of those natural diets, with no fillers, and only uses real meats and blah blah blah.  One she wouldn't go near, and the other she would eat reluctantly.  Except the super active, petite 7lb 4oz tortie grew to just over ten pounds, waddled when she walked, because she was horribly obese, and slept 24 hours a day, waking up only to eat, and her coat was staritng ot lose it's shine.  That scared the hell out of me!  So I switched back to Hills.  With a week, she was starting to show interest in toys again, and was already starting to lose that swaying flabby fat belly.  Now she's back down to 7lb 7oz, and very active, healthy, and happy.  I will NEVER switch her food again!

I took in a foster cat almost one year ago and have tried almost everything to rid him of diarrhea.  The vets were unable to diagnose any parasite or physical problems, and his behavior has always appeared happy and healthy.  The vets said it could be a food allergy, so I began trying different foods.  A couple of months ago, I bought SD Sensitive Stomach.  I had been reluctant because of the ingredients - I strive to avoid foods with "meal" of any kind - as well as the price ($40 for 15.5 lbs).  After a year, five other foods and several supplements, though, I was desperate.  Sensitive Stomach did the trick.  There was a noticeable difference within a few weeks, and the stools are completely normal now.  His weight gain has been constant regardless of food, so I do not attribute that to the Science Diet brand.The drawback is that my other two cats prefer this food to their original brand, so it's quite expensive for three cats.  The other two have not gained weight with this product, and their appetite does not appear to have increased at all.

My cat was born in August 2001, so he's almost 10 years old. Three years ago he started to throw up quite frequently. The vet ran tons of VERY EXPENSIVE tests and for the most part ruled out anything that can be treated. We tried changing food but nothing worked. I tried giving him home cooked food as well and that made throwing up even worse. So one day I was in a pet store and the clerk said he had the same problem with his cat and suggested the MOST EXPENSIVE FOOD IN STORE. I was skeptical but I had nothing to lose (but money). Three years later my cat is doing fantastic. He only throw up when I feel bad for him and give him tuna as a pity treat. He's healthy, bouncy and seems to enjoy food. The big bag lasts us for ever. We bought a bag on November 5th and today again on March 19. That's 4+ months for $40 (which is how much the bag costs in pet store). I think I can afford $10/month for my buddy. I have no idea what's in there and I don't really care. All I care is that my cat looks happy and healthy. Food purists who believe in feeding cat organic chicken and brown rice might not care for it.

My eight month old kitty, Jitterbug came to us eating Science Diet and everything was fine.  I slowly switched him over to Purina indoor, which I've always fed my cats and had no problems with.  Well I started noticing Jitterbug was leaving small little balls of poo all over the house!  Instead of taking him to the vet and paying a lot of money on tests I thought I'd try this expensive food first and what do you know, no more poop balls!  It's too bad it's so pricey, but if I don't have to deal with feces outside the litter box, I'll pay top dollar.  My cat has been on this formula for a month now and I'm very pleased with the results.

Our cat was a stray that showed up at a friend's farm.  He was in very bad shape...very skinny, lethargic, and his fur was very wiry!  We got him on the mend with a visit to the vet and some antibiotics.  But it wasn't until we started feeding him Science Diet that we noticed the change in his fur.  It made such a vast difference!  He has the softest fur I have ever felt on a cat!  The Science Diet seems to help with the hairballs, too.  It is a bit expensive, but it's worth every penny to me.

I'm not thrilled about the fillers and ground meal stuff in it as a food.  I try to look for better ingredients.  However, my vet said my cats had some tartar and sore gums.  I started mixing this stuff in with their regular food, and now (2 years later) my oldest is 4 with healthy teeth and gums.  I saw improvement in just a month or so.  Now looking at several annual visits in a row with good dental health and no tooth brushing.  Kitties seem to like it.  Healthy weight cats with dry food to graze on all they want.  I order from petfooddirect though.  When you consider the shipping costs, it's usually a little cheaper there unless amazon has it for free shipping.

column9: Great product, but trust your vet not the hype
column10: I have two cats, one 6 and one 2 years old. Both are indoor cats in excellent health. I saw the negative review and talked to my vet about it. I've also asked a number of veterinary professionals what to feed my cats and they all answer the same thing: Science Diet. Sure, you'll see stories of how one person's cat had issues, but even if that's 100% true, it's 1 case out of millions. Science and fact aren't based on someone's experience.So my point is, I love my cats and I'm very concerned about their health. I trust people who actually have medical degrees and experience with a wide range of animals. My only caution is do not fall for some hype or scare tactic that recommends some unproven or untested food or some fad diet for your pet. Don't listen to me, don't listen to the negative review. ASK YOUR VET what they recommend, and follow their instructions. My guess is you'll end up buying the Science Diet anyhow.
