This stuff is insanely good. I thought it was just going to be Nuttzo with cocoa thrown in as a gimmick, but boy was I wrong.CHOC seems to have a texture, taste, and consistency all its own. You still get the classic Nuttzo seven-nut butter blend in addition to huge chunks of each nut, but now there are dark chocolate bits and a deep cocoa swirl added to the mix. Really gives the whole thing a new and magical "kick" -- a bit like what a healthy Nutella-Reese's combo might be. Somehow the stuff manages to be even crunchier than original Nuttzo, too, which I assume has something to do with the slightly rearranged order of flax and sunflower seeds. The resulting mouthfeel is close to divine. This is the kind of spread that makes you pause to parse and savor each chew.The chocolate chips boast a refreshingly short ingredient list: organic cocoa liquor, organic cane sugar, organic cocoa butter, and organic cocoa powder. The cocoa delivers a deep, rich bite while still allowing all of the nuts and seeds to shine through. CHOC is not for fans of the super sweet goop you'll find with other popular PB blends, however; the chocolate here is fairly dark with a total sugar content only 1g higher than plain Nuttzo per serving. (Compare this to an equivalent serving of Dark Chocolate Dreams, which packs about 7g of sugar. Nutella contains over 20g!) CHOC will certainly satisfy those looking for a more subtle, refined, multi-layered taste experience. And did I mention the crunch? :-)Anyway, this is by far the tastiest thing I've tried in the realm of chocolate nut butters. I love to eat it with ice cream, oatmeal, yogurt, fruits, and of course straight from the jar, as recommended by the manufacturer. CHOC isn't exactly cheap, but considering all the potent and organic ingredients blended here in such perfect harmony, I'd say it's worth the premium.P.S. Hope to see it on shelves here in Seattle someday!

I regularly buy these after trying them at a food and wine show in Madison, Wisconsin.  I think teriyaki is my favorite flavor but also like zesty hickory.  A bit expensive at $2 each, but better than throwing your money away on the crappy mass produced beef sticks (ie slim jim - gross).

I first became aware of Taj Mahal Tea in my favorite Indian Restaurant; and they were gracious enough to share with me the name and brand. It is smooth; and rich in taste. OK...I started going through an "obsessed with Greek food" phase after going to Mykonos (yum!!!)So started looking everywhere for how to make Tzatzki sauce. I would check out their site if you like hard to find seasonings and sauces, tea, etc.So in conclusion, Great product!LOVE this use it everyday so far...Think I may make be coming up on an Asian food craving! Sit down boys and girls and let me tell you a story. Once upon a time, actually it was a Wednesday; anyway, I decided to go on my lunch hour from work to the nearest Chinese buffet restaurant. column9: A chili sauce worth crowing about
column10: Sriracha's a great early morning pick-me-up on the ol omlet.  It's also great on pizza, stirfry, soups, panini sandwiches (spritz a little atop the cheese the next time you make one, and see for yourself), etc.  Great for livening up roasted red pepper hummus, tomato sauces, mayonnaise, you name it.  The uses are innumerable.I'm a self-avowed chili-head, and I've tried more chili sauces than I can easily count.  Everyone has their favorite styles and brands, and I'm no different, because this happens to be one of mine.The thing I like about Sriracha is how the flavor and texture of freshly ground sun-ripened red chilies shine through cleanly ... there are no gritty/bitter seeds, no oxidized flavors from using reconstituted dried chilies, no caramelized/overcooked flavors, no competing heavy mismatched flavors/spices, no mouth pucking wretched excesses from being pickled in cider vinegar and salt, no fatiguing smoke flavors, no fruit juices, no excessive heat, no thermonuclear oil essence extracts, etc.  Most of those things have their time, place and uses, and good examples of each abound ... but not here.No.  Sriracha is just plain, beautiful, de-seeded, unobstructed, sun-ripened fresh red chili flesh, with just barely enough garlic, salt, vinegar and sugar to round it out, plus a little gaur gum to thicken it slightly, and a little sorbate for extend it's freshness.  That's it.  It's pleasantly piquant, but not overly so.Highly recommended.p.s. A convenient fallback for me, whenever Sriracha is unavailable, is Franks RedHot Original.

column9: A Potent Hot Sauce, similar to Tabasco, just Better. Buy the 28oz which costs only a few cents more
column10: This hot sauce has become a staple in my kitchen and replaced my bottle of Tabasco. Like Tabasco - it is primarily a hot (cayenne?) pepper delivery device. A few drops add a considerable amount of heat to any dish. This is NOT a watered down hot sauce like Franks, etc.While Tabasco seems to impart mostly heat along with a heavy dose of vinegar - this sauce has far more subtle tastes going on beyond the heat, yet the heat is considerable and dominates. It also lingers, on your taste buds, longer than Tabasco. There is a subtle amount of sweetness to this sauce along with faint garlic notes. While Tabasco can taste quite harsh if you add too much to a dish ---- this sauce, no matter how much you add, tastes fresh and just a bit sweet.I wanted to say in my review that this sauce had a hint of tomato yet there are no tomatoes listed on the ingredients. I suspect what I thought was tomato was simply the "sun ripened chilies" and the added sugar listed on the ingredients. But to be clear - heat - lingering heat - is the primary tasteWhile I really like this product and certainly recommend its purchase --------- I'm not sure it rates 5 stars because the overall flavor does not seem TRULY exceptional - only VERY GOOD.  There really is just one major taste evident and that is heat - and after that only a vague hint of something else which seems to be chiles, sugar and garlic. But chiles, sugar and garlic certainly beats (by a very wide margin) --- the heavy vinegar aftertaste as evidenced in Tabasco and many other hot sauces.For the $5.99 I paid locally for a 28 Oz bottle --- I'm glad to always have it on hand and it is a true staple.Amazon prices the 17oz at $5.19 and the 27oz at $5.89. It is a true no-brainer to purchase the 28oz size.As another reviewer recommended - given the potency of this stuff - you probably ONLY want to have a single bottle on hand. Larger quantities will deteriorate over time. I'd recommend you purchase this locally and not in the 2/3/6 packs offered on Amazon. I doubt many households will go through a bottle in a year. As I said: this is potent stuff.Update (July 2010) - a formal taste testI put 4 ounces of tomato juice into two glasses and progressively added 1/8 teaspoon of Tabasco or Huy Fong Sriracha into one of the two glasses until they both became too "hot" to tasteResults: With Tabasco - with each added dose the juice became not only hotter but harsher. With the Huy Fong - it became hotter yet retained a very fresh and sweeter note

column9: *Where've You Been All My Life??!!  Say YES! to the Sriracha*
column10: Ok. I'm sort of a chili-head. Been one since a summer in Mexico about thirty years ago. There's never less than at least eight bottles of different hot sauces in my fridge door. Green, yellow, red; mild, hot, and death-wish. This has got to be one of the most versatile sauces I have. I've used it on shrimp instead of cocktail sauce, or added it to the cocktail sauce. On fries or onion-rings instead of ketchup. On sandwiches instead of mayonnaise. Spice up tomato soup. On hamburgers, hot dogs, eggs. It can be added to anything with a tomato-based sauce. Even on a tossed salad, straight or mixed with some kind of salad dressing. Etc etc etc. But not oatmeal...yet.Just for the record: SERVING SIZE = 1 tsp.(yeah right). 5-calories. 0-grams of fat. 100-mg of sodium - 4% Daily Value. 1-gram of sugar/carbohydrate. 0-grams of protein. No vitamins or minerals as such. BUT FLAVOR!!Personally, I think the heat's fairly mild. Since reaction to heat levels is so subjective and various (some find this mild, some think it's too hot) the following may serve as a comparative reference. I'm using the Scoville Heat Unit rating system. You can look it up online if you're unfamiliar with it. Briefly, it rates the "heat" level by determining how many parts of sugar-water must be added until the heat is no longer detectable, using a panel of around five "judges." So it's subjective, & not as scientific as, say, high-performance liquid chromatography.Huy Fong Sriracha Hot Chili Sauce - 2,200 SHU (Scoville Heat Units) - that is, basically, 2,200 parts of sugar-water must be added to one part of this to reach the point that the heat is no longer noticeable. It has 44% of the heat of a regular jalapeno pepper.Classic Tabasco Hot Sauce: 2,500-5,000 SHUTabasco Green Pepper Hot Sauce: 600-1,200 SHUTabasco Habanero Pepper Sauce:7,000-8.000 SHUTrappey's Hot Sauce: 1,200-1,600 SHUTexas Pete: 747 SHUCholula Hot Sauce: 3,600 SHUDave's Insanity Hot Sauce: 51,000 SHUPure Capsicin: 16 million SHUGenerally: 0-5,000 SHU is considered mild. 5,000-20,000 SHU is medium. 20,000-70,000 SHU is hot. And anything above that is extremely hot.***** Several excellent websites that have ratings for different hot peppers and sauces are: [...] for peppers[...] for heat ratings of around 150 different commercial sauces.I think the best is [...]. It has BOTH peppers and sauces, AND it has color pictures of the peppers and the sauce bottles.Most people have used Classic Tabasco, & it can serve as a baseline for heat comparison. So this Sriracha is just a little bit less hot than the Tabasco you'll generally find in a restaurant when you ask for "hot sauce.".It's not going to REPLACE other hot sauces. But it's become a staple. I'm going to start getting the 3-pack of 28-ounce bottles.CHILI-HEADS UNITE!!!

column9: Not as hot as I feared and quite tasty!
column10: For years I'd seen what I jokingly called the "screaming chicken" hot sauce out at various restaurants, but I was always too intimidated to try it, even though I love hot sauce.  The mostly non-English labeling and contents made me think it was probably wicked hot. As with so many things I was put off by, I'm kicking myself now that I've tried it, as Sriracha sauce isn't that hot and in fact has a nice touch of sweetness to it that makes it a great addition to Thai and Chinese dishes.  Truthfully it's nowhere near as hot as Tabasco sauce and on the Scoville Scale of hotness it ranks only at the 1,000-2,5000 range making it medium (Tabasco is the next level up).  As a self-confessed hot-head hot sauce lover I have to admit Sriracha has a really unique consistency that is thicker than Tabasco, yet blends well in many Asian dishes.  I typically love northern Thai food and Sriracha works well with it and with Szechwan as well.  Sriracha gives a nice pop of hot without being overpowering like some hot sauces or the truly hot Thai chilies that rate up at 50,000-100,000 on the Scoville scale.  If something is a bit too bland for my taste usually a bit of Sriracha gets my mouth watering. As I've learned, if you like to spice things up ask your server about the sauces and chilies and try a small little sample, but don't live in fear of hot sauces.  Perhaps the best thing about Sriracha is it's a known quality and consistent, unlike the bowls of sauces and chilies in some Asian restaurants (believe me...I've had some that really took my breath away and I like it HOT).  And certainly don't be intimidated by the "screaming chicken"; it might well become your new friend!

Popcorn? Done. Chicken noodle soup? Done. Pizza? Done. Noodles? Done. Burgers? Done. Spaghetti? Done. The bottle doesn't lie.As a college student there are a few worries that are constantly on my mind (besides school): food and money. I usually get my Sriracha from convenience stores (which is waaaay cheaper than it is here). I love hot sauce in general (Tabasco, Louisiana Hot Sauce, Valentina, etc.), but this is definitely my favorite because of the versatility-- I put a squirt of Sriracha on just about everything. Since the heat isn't overpowering and the flavor compliments and adds to the taste of many dishes, it's great for spicing up otherwise bland dining hall food or even cooking with. The thick consistency also allows it to be used as a dip.

I put this stuff on all kinds of food:  noodles, potstickers, rice, soup, mexican food, asian food, anything grilled etc.  The food that it probably complements best though is pizza.  Probably the only thing it wouldn't be good on is sweet foods.As others have said, its not the spiciest sauce around, but it has far more flavor than most hot sauces.  This stuff is so good that I take it to other people's houses when they have cookouts.

column9: Amazing.... I waited too long to try this.
column10: I usually add some Franks hot sauce to dishes for a little flavor and heat, but this stuff is wayyy better.  It has a lot more flavor and spicier, but it doesn't linger.  I highly recommend this to anyone as the preferred hot sauce!

As a wise blog called The Oatmeal once said... I love sriracha is a delicious blessing flavoured with the incandescent glow of a thousand burning suns. This stuff is delicious and I eat it on everything. Yes, it's hot. Yes, too much will numb your tongue. But it's not just heat. It's flavour. The chilies are yummy and garlic is ALWAYS a good idea.This isn't watery light hot sauce. It's thicker, like mustard. The consistency makes it practical to put on on pizza, burgers, and anything else you can think of. I have yet to put sriracha on something and not like it. Save yourself some time and buy a 6-pack. One bottle doesn't last very long at all because you will use it all the time.

I've been buying all brands of chili and hot sauce products at the local supermarket and thought I would try this brand. It is definitely the best tasting chili sauce available.  I use it on meat, vegetables, and anything else that I'm eating.  It's good to know that it is good for heart health.

Not much I can say about this stuff that hasn't already been said. It is amazing. I grew up and lived in Hawaii for 25 years and surrounded by asian foods This was usually a staple in many resturaunts but I had never tried it because I will admit I was not a huge hot sauce fan. When I finally tried this i was putting it on everything and now living in Maine I was so excited to find it in the local stores! It doesnt just add heat to a meal but so much flavor! And the natural color of it is so vibrant! The only thing I like better than this is the garlic chili sauce made by the same company. a good spoonful of that in something like a breakfast burrito is pure heaven!

This has become a fave in my house. I usually despise hot sauce and opt for cooking with hot chiles and spices. This is different. It has none of that strange flavor of Tabasco and it really is hot unlike Frank's Red Hot. You can truly taste the peppers. My hubby puts it on almost everything from tacos to eggs to empanadas and on and on. I just recently purchased the Sriracha cookbook and love it even more when used in cooking. Deviled eggs, spicy shrimp, and the best .wings ever made are thanks to this sauce. Delicious. And definitely cheaper in your local market. My supermarket doesn't carry it but I can find it at my fruit store and at the Asian grocery for less than half of what it is priced here for. If you cant find it elsewhere it is definitely worth the extra cost because it is that good and because one bottle will last a long time.

My husband has always liked this sauce with everything from pizza, goulash, on his toss salad etc.  I am glad that now I have a source to get it from.  Some of the sotres in our area use to carry it- Hannaford and Target- but now i cannot get it as orten.  Thank you.

column9: Just want one bottle and don't have time to head to china town
column10: Perfecto, reasonable price for one bottle (and prime!) and saved me a bundle of time: it is spicy so try it in a small amount before squirting more.  Has a direct 'hot' flavor with little weird after taste.  We add it to spice up a stir fry, in noodles, in ramen, hot dogs, dipping sauce... Anything!  It is pretty good hotness.

The first time I had this was at the local Chinese resturant.I saw it in the grocery store and now on Amazon.WOW!!!HOT, HOT, HOT.Will make you eyes water and your nose run.Delicious with a little bit of tangyness to it.Recommended for chicken, burgers or as a dipping sauce.Also great on anything Chinese like General Tso's chicken.Awesome sauce.Recommended.
This is the hottest sauce I've found anywhere.  A little goes a long way, so there is plenty of bang for the buck.

I am not a fan of food that is hot just for hot's sake: if it's spicy it also has to be delicious, to have a purpose for the heat.I found this sauce adds a nice touch that even Tabasco doesn't offer, it has a nice sweetness to it as well as a punch of heat. The heat isn't overwhelming or unbearable, it's just a pleasant spicy addition to food.

column9: I ALWAYS have a bottle of Huy Fong Sriracha Hot Chili Sauce in the pantry!
column10: This is a very versatile sauce!I love the slow burn, I love the garlic flavor... and, while I don't usually like sweet sauces/foods, I don't mind the slight sweetness.  I LOVE it mixed with catsup for dipping nice, crispy homemade french fries.This sauce makes Tabasco BORING!

column9: One of the Greatest Sauces Known to Man
column10: I won't say it's the absolute best hot sauce, but if you're serious about hot sauces, and you haven't tried Sriracha, you need to add this sauce to your collection now.  What I like most about this sauce is it tastes like my homemade sauce.  I can tell just by the way it tastes and smells that they use the same high quality ingredients that I use when making my sauce.  One whiff takes me back to picking jalapeños out of my garden.  It's delicious blend of peppers, garlic, salt, and just the right amount of vinegar.  This sauce is thick.  This is not some red, runny liquid that you add to your food for heat.  This sauce is more like a thin paste.  I add it to ramen noodles, sushi, and just about anything else you would add hot sauce to, but since it's more like a thin paste than a runny liquid, it really sticks to the food.  It's hard to explain just how good this sauce is.  You have to try it for yourself to see what all the fuss is about.

column9: A different hot sauce then you normally would expect
column10: I found the Sriracha Hot Sauce a couple years ago and haven't looked back. As other have stated this sauce is one of the most versatile sauces I have come across.I use it in Ramen Noodles, sandwiches, pizza, and all the other things which hot sauces can be added to. I absolutely love this stuff and it is a staple for me at any meal I can use it. I keep a bottle in my car, at my work and my house.I can go through a bottle 17oz of this about every two weeks if not sooner. I probably have about 31 different hot sauces or so available to me, and this is my sauce for a quick fix.If you haven't tried this yet and you like hot sauces do yourself a favor and add something new and totally different then you have had before to your hot sauce portfolio.

The sauce is a great mix of chilis and spice that you have to taste to believe. It's not like normal hot sauce...not too hot, but definitely gives a kick. Thicker than most hot sauce like Tabasco or something. Worth the 6 bucks for sure.
Sriracha is the best. THE. BEST. I put it on everything. It's especially good on rice or noodles. Soooo spicy and tasty and mmmmmm

Huy Fong Sriracha chili sauce is made almost entirely of chili peppers.  There isa bit of salt, garlic, and vinegar that adjust the taste, but only in small amounts.  Huy Fong brand sauce is often referred to as the "rooster bottle" because of its trademark white rooster.  This stuff is good but be warned--it is very hot.The consistency of the sauce is thinner than tomato catchup.  Even though Sriracha is a Thai food, Huy Fong is not a traditional Thai Sriracha.  Traditionally, the sauce is much sweeter (almost like a catchup).  The Huy Fong is designed more for American palates.  It is flavorful and spicy, but it is not sweet.If you like spicy food, this sauce can be used on just about anything.  Rice, steamed vegetables, eggs, red meats, sausages, poultry, stir fry, fajitas, and french fries are just some of the foods that I eat with the chili sauce almost daily.  My best advice when you first try it is to use it sparingly.  It is easy to pour far more on your food than you realize, and to make your food much stronger than you intended.
This is going to be a great hot sauce for recipes. A chef on the Dr. Oz show recommended this in a certain recipe. It has a pretty good kick to it.

This is the first time I have tasted this sauce and I love it. I purchased 2 bottles and will purchase more when this is gone. I recommend it to anyone who like spicy sauces. It is better than the other hot sauces.

column9: We Are Unworthy Of Such Perfection.
column10: Oh Mighty Apollo! I do protest that you have given us a gift that we are unworthy of! Certainly there is no doubt that Sriracha was made by the gods themselves. With such zest and flavor, how can one resist the temptation? Sriracha, you are the sweet fire nectar that makes my life whole and I take pity on those that have not sampled your perfection. Your heat keeps my soul warm in the coldest moments of my life. Should the sun come down upon the earth and scorch the land and oceans, I would take refuge in the knowledge that the gods are creating a fresh batch of Sriracha that will soon rest upon my plate. Sriracha has proven to be perfect in every bottle, and to never leave my side when I need it. Truly there is no pleasure greater in this world than a full bottle of Sriracha.As for storage you can keep it anyway you please for Sriracha is independent of space-time itself and thus unaffected by the physical environment.

I went to a Viatnamese restaurant for dinner one day and they had this sauce on every table. Thought of giving it a try and it was absolutely mind blowing.!! Had to get this for my home right then.If you like asian hot sauces, you have to try this. has a solid heat element to it with good taste of chillies and garlic. Definitely recommended!!

column9: Makes my head perspire; it's my reaction, but it's good!
column10: This stuff was included in a product I bought at a local merchant; read the plastic packet and found it on Amazon; it is spicy-asian hot chili so it's very warm (hot) especially for me; I have an idiosyncrasy of my physiology: beads of perspiration fall from my head when I eat this spice, so I only eat it alone.It's crazy-funny but it happens, and it's a great flavor enhancement (the spice); if you like this type of chili, you'll like this sauce.  Not for the palate that avoids spicy foods.

I ordered it and it came in perfect condition a day earlier then expected. Heres a couple things I've always noted about Sriracha Sauce- Keep it sealed until you use it, Sriacha sauce DOES have a shelf life and doesn't taste as good when its not fresh- The brighter red it is the better it tastes- I'm pretty sure even though its delicious too much can cause serious pain to your stomach- Remember the sauce going in is not as pleasurable as going out.That being said, enjoy :-)!

Yum. What doesn't go well with Sriracha? Yeah, you can buy this pretty much anywhere nowadays, but I live up in the hills and I'd rather stuff come to me. If you're in a similar situation I can earnestly recommend Huy Fong Sriracha.

The only reason for it not getting 5 stars is that, among my hot sauce collection, there's other sauces that go better with specific foods. I like Cholula and Garlic Tabasco are better on pizza. I favor Amazon(the hot sauce brand) Sriracha on chili, for a sweet/hot kick.There is no sauce more versatile than this one, though. You can safely put it on ANYTHING and it won't disappoint. The squeezable, perfectly-sized big bottle, with the green cap acting as a hose nozzle is the perfect vessel for a sauce with which you will be painting any edible thing you can find.
This is a great companion to my emergency "tuna can" lunches!  Spicy, hot, and a little sweet!very tasty.

column9: The Hot Sauce of My Life!!!
column10: No more of hot sauce making your food simply just hotter and saltier. This bad boy packs MAJOR flavor! The spice is perfect and the flavor is fantastic! Try it!!

column9: not a true Thai sriracha but SO GOOD
column10: This isn't the traditional Thai sriracha that's more runny. But as far as bottled stuff this is what I grew up with. On Pho, stir fries, dipping sauces and so much more.It's spicy but not overly spicy but I love things Thai hot. It is flavorful. My husband doesn't like vinegar and while this has vinegar it's not over powering.we always have an extra bottle in the pantry and one in the fridge we're using

Had not heard about this. Read about this in the Chicago Sun Times and had to try it.Had it on pizza last night. Yummy.My son mixed it in with his tuna salad along with a squirt of spicy mustard and it really gave a lot of flavor to his tuna salad sandwich. He said he had it before while visiting his brother.From what I understand, this has been gaining popularity for some time now and I may be late to the party, but if you haven't heard of or tried this and like things hot, give it a go.

Here's a story: About 15 years ago, I was at an upscale grocery store in Lancaster, Pa. and in their Oriental section I came face to face with about 30-40 different types of sauces. What to buy? Well the Huy Fong Sriracha just kept calling my name, so I bought it and was hooked immediately. Well being from the western side of the state, a few months later made the trip back home, stopped at a favorite restaurant ( the food is great in J-town) and wow - what did they have on the tables but Sriracha! Seems that this sauce had taken the city by storm while I was away! And of course - most people up here say 'I use that on everything'. Just great stuff.
The best hot sauce there is.  Goes great with everything, but not the easiest to locate on store shelves.

This bottle of heaven got to my door quickly as expected. It has the perfect blend of heat and flavor. It kinda has the Asian style taste to it as well as a Mexican side which makes it darn near perfect. It was so good, I poured some in a bowl and used it as salsa. I put this stuff on everything now!

This stuff is awesome.  Its greatest attribute is the flavor, followed closely by heat.  It's hot, too, but not as hot as my favorite habanero-based sauces.  Where it lacks in heat -- for me, anyway -- it makes up for in flavor ten fold.Also, if you like bloody marys, squeeze off a few globs of Sriracha into your drink.  I've used it to compliment my already-favorite Zing-Zang bloody mary mix and it really adds to the kick.It's a bit expensive on Amazon, though.  I've found that Amazon has a very hard time competing with grocery stores like Kroger, Sam's Club, and Wal-mart as I am able to get this stuff way cheaper per bottle than what's on here.

I used to think that ranch was my favorite sauce, it was a perfect companion to pizza. Siracha can go on pizza- or eggs- or quesadillas- or burritos- or pasta- or fries!!- or steak- or burgers- omg. The list just keeps on going. Love this stuff.

I love this stuff with a passion. I put this on nearly everything and it never get's old. I enjoy having a spicy hot sauce but if it doesn't have a great flavor then it is just not up to par. This hot sauce has a great kick and a great taste. If you enjoy your spicy foods then this is a MUST HAVE!!!
Hot but not too hot, very flavorful.  You may see Sriracha on the table at most of your favorite asian restaurants and it has earned a place on my kitchen table, too.

This is the Tabasco of Oriental hot sauces.  I use it in all my Chinese dishes.  Every kitchen should have this stuff in it.  I even use a little in my Ramen Noodles.  It is also good with chicken/tuna salad, just mix a little in the chicken/tuna mix to give it a little kick.

I was cruising the aisles of my local "largest retailer in the US" super store one day and spotted the rooster-adorned bottle with the green lid...I had never tasted, noticed, or even heard of this stuff before, but as a hot sauce enthusiast I decided to give it a shot.  Serendipity, baby!  Sriracha (hey Pat Sajak, can I buy another vowel?  how do you pronounce this anyway?!) is now my absolute favorite hot sauce, and I have about 20+ varieties on the shelf at this very moment.  One of the crucial elements to a good hot sauce is the right blend of heat and flavor, and it's a delicate balance.  Some get the flavor but not the heat (Frank's), while others get the heat right but lack flavor (yes I am talking to you, you plethora of generic Habanero-based hot sauces).  Sriracha, however, nails it both ways.  It packs some legitimate kick, but it isn't an endurance contest either.  When it's there, it wakes you up, kicks you in the pants, and you know your dish has been revved up a few notches.  But you wouldn't want to presume this stuff upon an unsuspecting novice lest they drink all of your beer, er I mean soda, in a desperate search for relief.  But right there with the just-right heat is the sumptuous flavor that goes so well with so many foods.  Unlike many of my other beloved hot sauces, Sriracha doesn't skew very heavily toward the vinegar end of the spectrum (vinegar is a listed ingredient but it's low on the flavor profile).  Instead, the sugar, garlic, salt, and chili pepper combination creates a sweet, salty, almost nutty flavor that enhances far more than it overwhelms.  I use it on nearly everything: pizza, soups, sandwiches, chips, eggs, baked beans, burgers, and the list goes on and on.  This is definitely the most versatile hot sauce I've found...I feel somewhat ashamed for writing such a long, rambling review for a freaking hot sauce, but give it a shot and you'll understand - Sriracha isn't just a hot sauce, it's a way of life.
I put this on everything I eat, I use a 17 oz bottle about every 2 months, it is amazing on Ramen, Pizza, Burritos, chips, it has amazing flavor and just the right amount of burn.

column9: Very good sauce...in it's proper place
column10: In it's class (asian), Sriracha is without equal.  Most people not from Minnesota or Wisconsin should be able to eat this.  But I must disagree with most reviewers and warn you...it is not a sauce for all purposes.If you're looking for a general-purpose pepper sauce, then be aware that peppers are the third child in this mix, behind eldest sibling - garlic, and middle child - sugar.Because of that, it will compete with the flavor of most foods, not compliment them.  This sauce will not be a component of what you are eating, it will be THE flavor, dominating all else.  That's OK for bland dishes, but a disaster for others that have already complex flavors.If you like the classic asian combination of initially sweet, then lingering heat, you cannot go wrong with Sriracha.If yer from Minnesota or Wisconsin, stay away from 'dis an' stick with dat super-spicy tomato ketchup, ya betcha!

column9: Too hot, no flavor and overwhelms other ingredients
column10: I bought a bottle of this at a local market, tried it on a sandwich and some boiled shrimp, then tossed it in the trash. Way too hot for me and it completely overwhelms the flavors of the other ingredients while adding only heat and a faint hint of garlic.If there is anything subtle or educated about your food preferences, don't buy this sauce.

Well, I'm now truly 'Ratch free.And all I have to say is, "Wow.  I never thought it would happen to me."  I can't believe what's all happened since I was found face-down in the grocery store aisle with a half-full bottle of Sriracha stuck up one nostril and and the other half the bottle dribbling out the other nostril.Worse, my mouth was stuffed full of sirloin tip samples that I - at least this is what I'm told - wrenched from the Sample Lady at the condiment end-cap.  Evidently, I saw how she dabbed her meat bites in a little plastic cup of house-brand barbeque sauce and the rest...is...my shame.The scene I made wasn't pretty. Suffice it to state, 22 people had Sriracha stains on their shirts and...that bottle stuck up my nose?  It was actually the third bottle I abused - the first one  used to drown the sample tray of steak tips and the second...well, I drank it like a little kid drinking Kool-aid on a hot day.My rage-filled rampage against the condiment companies and purveyors of flavorlessness saw no bounds.  I have a hazy memory of running stiff-armed, along an entire row of catsup bottles cascading them onto the linoleum.  The dull thuds of taught red plastic bouncing off the floor still haunts my dreams...Somewhere in the moments that followed, I found a frozen salmon and used it to knock out whole sections of Mexican, Italian, Chinese and fake Wasabi sauces into space - bang!  bang!  bang!  I laughed maniacally whenever the obscenely expensive jars of boutique blech cracked two, three, four aisles away.By then the local news had showed up - virtually none of my howl against the Jalepeno Junta was fit for broadcast.Anyway, I woke up at the Scandinavian Cuisine Sanitarium two days later knowing that I could never touch Sriracha Sauce again.  But the facts were much harsher - I didn't have a choice.  That day, the judge signed the orders authorizing involuntary tastebudechtomy.Suffice it to say, I won't be eating Sriracha any more.  I have a heck of a bill to work off at the Food Mart.Stick to Catsup.
Yep!  It's true!  Not one complaint from any of my picky eaters.  Tasty, easy to make, and shipped well.  Great addition to the pantry!
I love this stuff.  Seriously.  I wish I had a water fountain at my house that dispensed sweet potatoey goodness.

column10: To be honest, they tasted like any other instant mashed potatoes; neither really good nor really bad. I tend to make homemade mashed potatoes but I like to keep the instant around for those times when I only have twenty minutes to pull a meal together or I am just too tired to make the effort. column9: I think that I got a bad batch or they changed the ingredients
column10: I tried an envelope from two different boxes and both didn't taste good to me at all. I've bought this in the grocery store before and always liked it and other betty crocker potatoes but either I got a bad batch from amazon or they changed the ingredients. I bought this in bulk for a fair price but I had to give the rest of the boxes away because I couldn't stand to eat them. Maybe another flavor won't be as bad but I won't waste my money buying it in bulk to find out.

I use this oil in my Maxi-Matic EPM-450 Elite 4-Ounce Old Fashioned Table Top Popcorn Popper and love it. Its semi-solid texture makes it easy to work with, since there's no need to worry about spilling or dripping when adding it to the kettle (it melts to a liquid once heated). I combine it with Flavacol salt, Pop Weaver kernels, and Mor-Gold Plus butter substitute. The result is truly authentic tasting theater style popcorn.

I received a WhirlyPop popcorn popper for Christmas. After a little web research, quickly discovered that coconut oil, as used in the Real Theatre Popcorn Popping Oil, is a key ingredient to making great popcorn. Using regular canola or other vegetable oils just does not compare to using this popping oil. My family loves the popcorn we make with this oil. We will never eat microwave popcorn again.

The taste I am looking for is reminiscent of old, small town theaters with fantastic, melty, buttery popcorn - not that of today's mainstream digital 3D multiplexes.That said, this popping oil colors the popcorn the perfect shade of yellow, despite the oil's orange appearance, but we're eating it, not putting it on display.  Old time theater popcorn has a rich buttery taste even before adding butter.  This oil adds very little, if any, flavor.  Being coconut oil, the kernels pop well and are tender, but it's all style & no substance.  I'll be moving on to try the next brand of oil.

There is no mention in the product description of the "Artificial Butter Flavoring" in the ingredients.  Just thought I'd mention it, for those that want to avoid that additive.  If I'd known, I would have chosen a different product, or gone with pure peanut oil.  And yes, I, too, was surprised at the small size of the container, but that's not the fault of the product description.  I should have looked more carefully at the "16oz" written plainly in the product description.

column9: Yummy!!  Second time I bought this item
column10: The item description clearly states the size of the container and that it is one pound, so I knew what I was getting. Yes, it is a small container, but it really does last a long time.  The small size jar also makes it less messy than a gallon sized jug would be when you get to the bottom (would get all that gunk on your hand and arm).Very easy to manage when it's in a solid state.  In the summer it does soften up a bit.My family loves the flavor and the slight color that is added.  We also add salt.  To us, it tastes like movie theater popcorn.  I don't use a popper.  I use a heavy bottomed pot - allowing the steam to escape during popping.  Will definitely buy again and highly recommend.

column9: I don't work for Wabash Valley but I do love the product:)
column10: Yes, this product is expensive.  Buy it in the big box stores for about $8 or buy it online and pay the $7 shipping.  Your choice.  The product is my fav for making stove top popcorn and company never fails to ask for it.

column9: Good Taste but Beware only 16oz jar
column10: When ordering this item beware it's only a 16oz jar.  On the upside it does give the popcorn a good taste.

I love this popping oil.  I've tried straight vegetable oil, and the Orville Redenbacher popcorn oil and nothing really compares.  The container is small in size, although depending on how you pop your corn, you don't need much.  Just using this oil makes a difference in the popcorn, but I did find that in order to get the complete movie theater taste, you have to add Flavacol to the oil before popping.  As others have mentioned, the oil is part of the perfect popcorn recipe, but not the only thing needed.I was so impressed with this oil, that I sent a friend a container (along with Flavacol) as a gift.  She told me it was the best popcorn she'd ever had.  I will continue to buy this for my popcorn.

This is almost identical to the popcorn oil my husband and I used when we first got married almost 30 years ago, before microwave popcorn.  It has a wonderful flavor.  It is liquid at first but after it is opened and stored, it becomes a solid.  Makes the popcorn have a great taste.
I was looking for a good tasting popping oil, this is it . yum. but i was very surprised about the size, this "tub" is so tiny. this and flavrcol is perfect. I will be buying this again.

Great stuff. If you looking for health, forget it. Everything in moderation. It almost tastes as good as the movie stuff, if not better with the convenience of enjoying it at home watching a good movie.
We tried this instead of the pre-made bags.  The bags are more convenient but with this you can add more oil that what the manufactorer requires and get that taste you are seeking.

column9: Great, just realize what you're buying
column10: First off, for those that think this product has gone bad because it has become solid - You're mistaken. Coconut oil turns solid at room temp, that's just the nature of it. Second, for those that say it adds no flavor - You're also mistaken. This oil has butter flavoring added. You'll quickly realize this if you taste it by itself.  No, just using this oil won't make your popcorn really buttery flavored, as you can't expect a tablespoon of flavored oil to add that much flavor per kernel when you're making a huge bowl of popcorn. You should add Flavacol at a minimum, and other toppings/butter if you really need something thats majorly flavorful. Personally, this with Flavacol is all I use, its exactly the movie theater type taste I like. Also, please be aware of the size you're actually getting for the price. This thing is pretty small, but I think its worth it for the quality and the fact that I don't need a huge gallon container of coconut oil taking up space in my cabinets. Its enough to last most people for a while. Overall, I highly recommend this product and I'm sure I'll be buying it again.

I've been using the Wabash Valley Farms Popping Oil for a long time, and really love it!  The smell of microwave popcorn is nauseating, and the taste is almost as bad.  I really wish they'd ban it from our office.  When someone pops it, the normal smell is awful, but when they burn it, I have to leave the building!  Ugh!  Early on, my Mom taught me to cook my own popcorn in a heavy, lidded pot on the stove, and that's the way I've always done it.  This popping oil is luscious and makes the popcorn SO much more tasty than that nasty stuff from the microwave!  Try it, you'll like it!!  It'll make movie night at your house the BEST ever!
Many of the reviews I have seen here bash the product. Yes, if you don't read closely the product is not a large as you may imagine. The oil does work as advertised and helps make great popcorn.
Gives popcorn a pleasing color and lets the corn pop fully. I have been very satisfied. I will purchase more of this.

We got a new popcorn popper for my son for Christmas, and got a container of this oil to use in it.  It is really good, and provides an authentic, movie theater style taste.  The only negative for me is that the oil is a hard chunk, and you have to scrape it off in order to measure it out, but it really isn't a big deal. These rounds make a great beef stew. Just peel&slice 2-3 carrots, 1 rib celery, sliced, 2-3 potatoes,cubed small, 1 onion,chunk chopped and 2 plum tomatoes,chunked small. Cut tender rounds in half,and cook in the gravy. Add 1/2-1 cup beef broth, onion & garlic powder,1 tsp each, S&P to taste and 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce; let cook,covered,med-low, 30-45 min or until veges are fork tender. If it needs thickening add 1 tsp cornstarch dissolved in 1 tbsp cold water,add to stew,bring to a low boil and cook uncovered 5-10 min more. Of course add your own touches,veges or spices as you like. Serve over rice noodles or your favorite pasta.Enjoy!

First this is Spanish La Mancha Saffron, grown in Spain, by far the majority of the saffron we see here in the US. Although the Blue Crocus flower is native to Iran and not Spain the best saffron is considered to be this from La Mancha. Now as for the grading system the main difference between grades is how many long yellow "styles" are attached to the stigmas which is saffron. Pure stigma saffron (basically no yellow styles) is the best quality.This is deep bright red Spanish saffron indicating very high crocin. The best indication of grade is the "Superior Quality" label which is the translation of the Spanish "Coupe". There are just a few styles. Bottom line you might find a more purebred saffron for a higher price. But this is a very high quality product at an unbeatable price from the best growing region in the world. The flowers here would seem to grow under the natural conditions the best, perhaps avoiding any kind of chemical alteration.

I purchased this tin of saffron for my wife's birthday. Yes, a birthday present. She happens to be a professional chef who always knew the value of high quality ingredients.  Using top-quality -- and yes, this is the best you can buy -- saffron enhances so many spanish foods, risotto and a whole lot of other dishes. You always dissolve saffron in a liquid so that the intense aroma infuses the entire dish and mixes in subtle ways with other flavors. And since you need so little, this tin will last for years. There is simply no substitute. If this is your first purchase of top quality saffron, you will be impressed and wonder how you could ever cook without.

This saffron has too much style which is the thin Threads which attached  to the stigmas. The style has no CULINARY VALUE, that means NO AROMA, FLAVOR .  The stigmas are the values of saffron. The stigma is thicker than the style and looks like a horn.  I would say about 80% of the content is style. I won't buy this again.

column10: great price for very good saffron, best quality is 5-7x the price and typically unnecessary, used in multiple dishes already with excellent results.  fast shipping
This is very good quality saffron and at an affordable price. I am very pleased with this purchase. This is a big box so it will last a long time too.

My family has always used saffron to flavor rice dishes, stews, desserts and even drinks.I bought this product because it was a good bargain. La Mancha Spanish saffron, however, lacks the deep warm flavor and aroma of saffron. Usually, few threads of this expensive spice are enough to dramatically enhance the flavor of a big pot of rice or stew. Unfortunately this is not the case with La Mancha Spanish Saffron.Cooks who have used good quality saffron will notice that La Mancha Spanish Saffron is inferior.

I really liked the quality of this Spanish Saffron! I have used various brands and types of saffron. This Spanish Saffron is good for risottos and other dishes that call for this precious ingredient. This particular brand is very good quality and is reasonably priced.  There is about a one year supply of saffron in this package (assuming normal use). Besides, It came right on-time and in a great packaging. I'll order again and highly recommend this saffron.
The sun chips variety pack is excellent! They are healthier than regular chips, filling, and everyone loves variety. I am very happy with the service, price, and shipping time. Thanks!!
Sunchips are the best chips in the world. Buy them at stores. I suggest you get the "Harvest Cheddar" flavor.

unfortunately, this product was neither as pictured nor as described. there were no harvest cheddar sunchips bags in the box. i've ordered the multi-pack from amazon before and was disappointed to note that this time the chips were noticeably stale.

Sun Chips are a healthy alternative to potato chips.  They are made from a blend of whole grains, corn bran, and sunflower oil.  It's hard to find them in grocery stores except as an item mixed in with other chips, such as Doritos, Fritos, etc.  Some words of caution.  Amazon lists a variety of sources.  The cost of the chips plus shipping averages out to about $20 for a box of 30 one ounce bags (sources offerring lower prices have higher shipping costs).  The quality may vary, depending on the source.  Individual reviewers have not indicated the source that they used, so it is necessary to check the ratings for each source.

I have eaten Sun Chips for years. They have a nice crisp texture and great taste, and while not a health food, are definitely healthier than regular chips. Each flavor is unique, so this multigrain box is a really good way to sample everything in snack/lunch size bags.Shop for price. I buy these on sale at my local Costco for under nine dollars.

Same sunchips, four flavours, just individual packaging... still looking for a better deal... too bad amazon did not carry these when I ordered them, as it would have at least saved me a few more dollars.
This is a very clean crisp bright peppermint no grassy or chemical taste at all just staight peppermint.

This is my second order of the Coconut Bubble Tea Powder.  I am constantly searching for new recipes to use it with.  I tried Green tea base, white tea; rice milk.  All tastes good. Since it is such a large quantity, I was not prepared on where or how to store it.  Now, I store it in a large glass jar with a wide top glass canister with tight fitting lid available at Crate and Barrel or Walmart.

column9: Great Baby Food, but don't buy it here!!!!!!
column10: My son loves this oatmeal.  I tried it once and I love it too!!!  The only downside that I can say is that the oatmeal consistency actually varies from one package to another.  My guess is that they have different vendor making it? Sometimes one package contains a thicker oatmeal than another.  Either way, my son loves it and he can't get enough of it.  I tried to copy the flavor to no avail.  He's a devoted fan and will not touch any other oatmeal.While my heart is broken, at $0.98 each from Walmart, it may be easier for me to just let him have his way.  Don't buy this here.... Walmart selection of Sprout is somewhat limited, but it's worth it.  The roasted banana brown rice and rice peach pudding are winners too.The Stage 3, however, is not as good as the stage 2.  I tried to give my son Sprout oatmeal from Stage 3, and he didn't want to go further than the first spoon.  I tried it and I'm in agreement with him.  There is an after taste/smell with Stage 3 Sprout.

Stash sells cheap tea, but, I really prefer it.  The Bergamot (orange extract) they're using is fantastic with their black tea, which is also quite decent.  If you are a tea snob and you like the taste of moldy orange Bergamot of the "higher end" Earl Greys, then this tea is not for you.

My Poms are predisposed to collapsing tracheas and luxating patellas.(did I spell these correctly?)  :)  so I use these in along with several other supplements/herbs for my dogs and all are doing wonderful!!

column9: Two Middle Age Cats Loved It From the Moment It Hit Their Plate!
column10: Many times I buy assorted "healthy" cat food for my girls and they look at it, sniff and walk away. They eventually walk back and eat it over time. As soon as they heard me open the bag they rushed over sniffing the air. They quickly went to the bowl and finished it up. Finally settling down for a nice nap, they appeared more satisfied and quiet after this meal. I use to buy this brand long ago from another mail order company but they went out of business. I tried to buy it locally but few carry it and others said they would order it for me. Wysong was off the radar for awhile, but I'm glad I located a good source!

I am switching Sophie over to Wysong as it is what my dog trainer recommended years ago for my cats and my dog.  "People quality" as she called it.The cost for the cat food is $12 for a four-pound bag locally, so I thought I would shop Amazon to see if it was cheaper.  I found a 16-pound box -- four bags I guess -- for about $8.00.  That seemed too good to be true, but I ordered it.  It shipped, and I noticed on the UPS tracking that the shipping weight was just 4.8 pounds.So I emailed PetFood Direct through Amazon Marketplace to ask for return instructions once I receive it next week, as with shipping this would cost nearly double what I would pay locally.  I explained why, and wished them happy holidays.  I just got an email back.  They apologized for the SKU / description error and said that it is in the process of being corrected, credited my card in full, and told me to keep the bag of food when it arrives.I will absolutely shop this merchant again due to their level of customer service.  Thank you to Susan Ferra Kemp, Team Leader and to PetFood Direct.(oh, and the item is superb for the kitty as well!)

This coffee does not have a bite like other brands and is the best tasting coffee I have found in my travels.  I can only get it here now since all the stores I did get it have quit handling it.  Their loss of my business.  Stores complain about losing business to the net, they should carry the products we like.

These chips are awesome and semi-healthy.  However, you can buy them cheaper at Costco.  I got a 16 oz bag there for $5.29, which works out to 33 cents per ounce.  If you buy them through Amazon, you pay 52 cents per ounce.

column9: My son loves these gluten free chips!
column10: After finding these once in a Walmart, we could never find these chips again.Finding them on Amazon was a nice surprise.Having a whole case of these chips was a god-send!We're very happy with this purchase.

If you like a delicous snack and you want to maintain your health also, these chips are the way to go! Rice works, plain with salt, are great for people who are allergic to gluten products. They digest well, and are made- not from white rice- but brown rice. For extra good nutrition, they are delicious with hummus and salsa. There is no downside here. They are also dairy-free. Of all the chips and snacks I have tasted, these are the best-tasting and best-for-you snacks I know!!!riceworks Sea Salt, 5.5-Ounce Bag (Pack of 12)

I love these chips and when I could no longer find them at Costco, I went to the internet. Unfortunately when they reached me they were totally crushed.  There were no whole chips, very few partial chips and most just crumbles.

Warning these are highly addictive chips!  I love the sea salt and the salsa flavors - best gluten free taste and texture I've ever put in my mouth.  I can easily clean out most of a bag in one sitting.  Very healthy snack!  Cons:  there's an awful lot of air in that bag... And they are often broken up a lot, so you have to learn to dip your dip with a spoon, then stick a bunch of broken chips to that.  So delicious, I'm willing to do that.  Here's the other bummer.... If you're addicted, you want to buy in bulk with a goal to save money.  I was shocked at the price here on amazon, in bulk.  $46 for 12 bags (5.5 oz) plus shipping at $10+.... That's $57 total which comes out to $4.73 ish per bag (5.5 oz).  I can get them at a Publix grocery store for $2.89 a bag (5.5 oz) -- that's $1.89 cheaper.  You'd think  "in bulk" combined with amazon could do better than that.

column9: What a rip off this place $5 a bag I can get $2.5 all day long!!
column10: You can buy the 5.5 ounce bag at HEB or Waltmart for $2.5. Give me a break guys! Jim and Houston

I've purchased these at Walmart.  I'm slightly ashamed to say a bag doesn't last more than a day in our house.  I'm mostly to blamed for that. :)  They are a little higher in fat then I would like.  However, they are much better than Fritos!

column9: Excellent Gluten Free Snack - even the kids love them!
column10: I found these at BJ's for about $5.29 for a 1-pound bag.  I took them to a cookout and everyone loved them - including the kids.  They are now on my list to buy every time I go to BJ's - I hope they keep selling them!
My husband, coworkers and I absolutely loved them.  Strongly recommend you try them!!!We'll be trying other flavors.  Wish Amazon sold a variety pack!!!
riceworks Sea Salt, 5.5-Ounce Bag (Pack of 12)Although the crackers are tasty, almost all of the crackers were broken.  I didn't think i was getting 12 bags of crumbled crackers and crumbs.

column9: THESE ARE OKAY  PREFER SWEET CHILE ONES
column10: These chips remind me of regular Fritos. I like the other flavor better then this one the sweet chile but some people may not like the spicey flavor my sister for one !

My title and rating are only due to the fact that this product is not from the USA... and I didn't realize that when I ordered it.  I felt betrayed because in theory, it's a great snack... just apples, right?  My son likes the taste and I thought all was good... but, the apples are imported... so if you're concerned about the whole arsenic issue of imported apples, then you may want to find a different product.

My 3 year-old is a picky eater and at times it is hard to get him to eat fresh fruits and vegetables. Maybe it is a texture thing, because he absolutely loves the apple fruit chips. I have tried other dried fruit on him but they don't have the same melt in your mouth texture.  I would highly recommend for toddlers and kids!

I actually dislike traditional dried fruit (with the exception of craisins and raisins), so I was surprised that I liked these. I tried the apples and pears today and liked them both (although apple was better, for me).  It is similar to space-icecream, in that it melts in your mouth, but I liked that it was a crunchy consistency rather than soft and chewy (that traditional dried fruit has). It almost tricks me into thinking I am eating chips because of the crunch. It has the consistency of the cheese puffs that I usually like snacking on. Since the only ingredient is the fruit, I don't feel guilty eating multiple of these in a day. It has 39 calories and 0 fat (per packet), so it will definitely help keep me from munching on more fatty snacks.

column9: These do NOT taste good; may be good for baking
column10: I think these may be good for baking but not great for snacking. The cool thing about these are that the only ingredient is the fruit. The bad part is that they don't really taste good and they have the consistency of styrofoam. They are not the mostly-dried, soft fruit. These things are super all-the-way dried fruit so when you bite them they pretty much turn to powder. My 2 year old son would snack on them but would make a huge powdery mess all over the house. The apple powder was not that bad but the strawberries make a really tough red stain in any fabric they touch.

column9: Squeaky Clean Feel is Missing BUT...
column10: The shampoo suds nicely but doesn't rinse squeaky clean. I guess that's in preparation for it's conditioner partner. The tropical fragrance is very summery and the shampoo isn't overly bubbly, it foams lightly. My hair didn't feel stripped and rough like some shampoos make it feel. My hair was silky and ready to receive the goodness it needed from the conditioner. My only gripe is the fragrance is a bit overpowering.This is Step1: Cleanse ... in the Ultra Shea line

After trying The Long Lengths Nourishing Conditioner by Clear Scalp I was looking forward to being equally impressed with this shampoo.  The pros for me were the scent (super nice) and the easy open spout.  Otherwise I was disappointed.  It is described as a moisturizing formula yet my hair felt stripped after use.  If not for the highly effective conditioner mentioned above I'm sure my hair would have felt a little straw-like when dry.

I ordered this and the shampoo through Vine. Both seemed to leave my hair in good condition but they did not help my dandruff. Also a little bit of the shampoo got in my eye and it burned. ALSO: Amazon ships this shoddily. Half the conditioner leaked inside the envelope.

The way the shampoo was packaged was a huge disappointment. I knew something was amiss because I could smell the shampoo scent as if I had the opened bottle in my hand, when in fact it was still in the packaging. So when I removed the tape I was not shocked to find 1/4 of the bottle in the packaging. It was a cremay mess, and i kept thinking by this being a creamy shampoo it will NOT rinse well, you see I wear Sisterlocks and my girlfriend traditional locs.BUT.....once I used the shampoo I was surprised. My girlfriend locs are much thicker than mine so I was concerned about the film and residue that would be left in her hair. So we washed her hair as usual 2 times, and rinsed. We didn't get that squeeky clean feel one would get with a clarifying shampoo but the shampoo rinses very well. Her hair was left with a soft, clean feel to it. Her locs didn't feel weighted down by the shampoo at all, however we noticed if you use too much you will get a feel of "too much". Just remember a dab will do it. Her scalp looked clean and her hair smelled fresh.The bottle says "cleanese to remove product build-up and allow the scalp to breathe" I believe this product did in fact do just that. THe moisture 10 system used includes shea butter, natural oils, including vitamin E, sunflower, coconut, almond, soybean, argan, and palm.Once you finish with your wash your hair is ready for the next phase adding the "Nourishing Scalp and Hair Oil" fantastic 2 step process. You can just use the shampoo and not the hair oil if you don't need it. I believe this shampoo is great for all types of hair African American as well as European, nappy or straight.Complimentary samples of this product was provided by Amazon Vine for the purpose of this review.Missy

This shampoo does do what it says...my hair doesn't feel "dried out" a day after using it. However, your hair doesn't "squeak" when you wash it using this shampoo. I was hesitant to try this at first, because some products tend to make my scalp itch. I was pleasantly surprised to find this shampoo does not do that. HOWEVER...when rinsing, my hair still feels "slick"...which I would expect if it was a combination of shampoo AND conditioner, but it isn't. It's just straight shampoo. This is why I gave it only 4 stars instead of five. To me, it just doesn't feel like it "rinses clean". But, then again, it's a good to use a different shampoo once a week to remove build-up, so...this may take care of it if you experience the same problem.

column9: All You Need is a Little
column10: Growing up, I was cursed with very wavy, very thick hair. Finding shampoos that really work well at taming frizz and nourishing the hair itself has always been a struggle. I found the CLEAR line a few weeks ago and was highly impressed with their Damage and Color Repair line. Given that, I'm working my way through their different products to see which one is clearly the best and Ultra Shea Cleanse and Nourish is that shampoo.The scent is reminiscent of a Pina Colada. Coconut is there, but it's not overpowering. I love coconut, but my husband and daughter can't stand that smell and make it very apparent when they can smell it on me. They had no complaints.What's more impressive is that with just a dime-sized amount of shampoo, I had plenty of lather to clean my entire head of hair, and my hair is past my shoulders, so I was amazed. It lathers extremely well, so you can easily get a bottle of shampoo to last. Rinsing the suds away does take a little extra time. We have soft water, so I'm not sure if hard water would make a difference or not.After shampooing, my hair did feel softer than usual. That was a very good sign. Paired with the conditioner (I'm reviewing that separately), I was extremely happy with the results.

I'm thrilled to see and feel what Clear Scalp and Hair Therapy Ultra Shea Cleanse and Nourish Shampoo, and CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Smooth & Nourish Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounce, have done for my hair in a single application. I have been using salon shampoos and conditioners on my hair for ages now, and been really displeased with how my hair has been looking. It's grey, very thick and wiry, and was dry and brittle to the touch, and had totally lost its sheen. One wash with Clear Ultra Shea has changed all that. My hair hasn't felt this soft in years, and it's actually shining!Clear Ultra Shea shampoo is dense and creamy and feels incredibly luxurious as you lather it in. I was trying to find a comparison to what it feels like, but couldn't. It definitely doesn't feel like any shampoo I've ever used before. The aroma is very subtle and quite pleasant, and I like the packaging a lot. The cylinders are sturdy, with tops that press open easily, and the shampoo stands on its feet, and conditioner on its head, so there is no confusion as to what bottle you're reaching for, half blind with no glasses on and water running down your face. I'm going to keep using Clear Ultra Shea, and those salon products will have to go bye bye.

column9: Where have you been all my life?!
column10: I was using Dove's Moisturizing Shampoo/Conditioner. It did a good job with having soft hair, but I was having snow storms of dandruff and lots of hair breakage to a point I pick off ten plus hairs off my when I got out of the shower and throughout the day. Also, with the dandruff, after the owner of my workplace (who can be very picky on appearance, down to one flake of dandruff) walked in and seeing the amount of dandruff on my black uniform, I said "That's it!"I walked into Walmart and looked at the dry scalp/dandruff shampoos. Head and Shoulders somewhat did the job, but my hair gets dry and brittle and did an okay job on the dandruff. I then stumbled upon Clear. I figured I'd give it a shot, even though it was a little pricey for me (The only downfall of this product, but better than getting $25 salon stuff). I got the Shea Cleanse and Nourish so that not only did my scalp feel happy, so did my hair. Good news, I needed shampoo and conditioner anyway. I ran out of the Dove anyway.Went home and used it that night. The results were immediate on the spot. 75% of the flakes were gone, my scalp showed major improvements, and my hair was shiny, smooth, and soft (even though I use the Suave Keratin Serum as well, this made it go from bleh to SWEET ZOMBIE JESUS THAT'S GOOD!). The nice scent of shea was relaxing and nice, and it lasted too. I walked into work the next day (I wash my hair every other day) and a co-worker grabbed me and said "Why do you smell sooooooo good?! I want that!" So, told her it was my new shampoo/conditioner.And as for my black work uniform, I have not had to brush off flakes or pluck ten plus hairs off me!My hair has never felt better. I wash it every other day, and focus on the scalp a wee bit more so that I know it's doing its job. I only use a hair straightener (with a heat protection spray) on the lowest heat setting and my hair still feels and smells amazing. A male friend of mine also has the exact same problem as me and he will be getting some today to help him out (I told him they had a mens line he can look into).Get it! Trust me, you won't be sorry. You want a happy scalp and hair at the same time, get this. I'm not regretting it now. :)

I have dry middle-aged woman hair and have pretty much been using the same hair products for years - never thinking that any other products in this price range would do a better job but I was wrong. Though I am not a fan of the coconut/vanilla scent of this product, it is not overwhelming and is more than made up by the fact that this shampoo actually makes my hair look and feel better. (scalp too!) I would absolutely buy this again and am looking forward to trying the conditioner as well.

I'm usually a no-poo girl. I loved the Clear Scalp Shea conditioner, so I thought I'd give the shampoo a try whenever I need a deeper clean. I gotta say, I kinda love this shampoo. My hair was not dry or frizzy and it felt extremely soft and manageable. Definitely will purchase ongoing.

column9: I did find the right foundation for strong, beautiful hair
column10: I am 50 year old and still have the same thick curly hair I did when I was 13.  I have been looking for the right mix of care products. Just last month I switched to three products:CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Cleanse & Nourish ShampooCLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Smooth & Nourish Conditioner,CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Nourishing Scalp & Hair Oil,My hair is dryer now that I am older and the shampoo really does the trick of cleaning without destroying my hair, it cleanses completely to remove product build-up. The conditioner allows me to much more easily run a brush through my hair. Without flattening my hair it reduces the dryness that flat ironing can do and reduces breakage.  It really does lock in moisture and provide long lasting nourishment.  The Therapy works best on wet hair, it gives deep, non-greasy nourishment to my hair and lends a healthy looking shine.  I can wash, condition and therapy my hair Monday. Tuesday I can wet my hair put the therapy in and it looks brand new.The real test was going to my salon and my stylist of 8 years noticed the difference in softness. I love the blend of shea, vitamin E, sunflower, coconut, almond, soybean, argan, and palm. It really works for me. I did find the right foundation for strong, beautiful hair.KEEPER!

I mean I was really excited to use this. I don't actually wash my hair myself-i'm no good at it. So I took both the shampoo and the CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Smooth & Nourish Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounceto my salon and I really felt the difference. I mean it's pretty refreshing. and the end result was really nice, after drying and styling she commented on how nice and healthy my hair was. My stylist has been doing my hair since I was really young and she's never said that before. I generally owe it to her but I think I have this to thank for that as well. I'm looking forward to seeing more results from this in the future like if it helps reduce breakage like it says - I hope so. And being that I recently had a cut I'm looking forward to see how long it's going to grow.

Clear Scalp and hair Beauty Ultra Shea cleanse and nourish shampoo is an effective product. It has a subtle fragrance and is not overpowering. It gives a sensation of luxury in its smooth application. This can be truly helpful for fine and dry hair. Having clean hair with enhanced body is a true advantage. Even the shape of the container is appealing. You will find this product pleasing and not that it does the job. Try it today.

column9: Works well as a combo or alone
column10: Used in conjunction with CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Smooth & Nourish Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounce, this shampoo is good stuff. One thing I like so much about it is the shea butter smell, which makes me think I'm vacationing somewhere exotic. But the more important positive point is that it leaves my hair feeling full and clean. It also apparently nourishes and moisturizes your scalp and helps it breathe. I use hair gel on a regular basis, and apprently this shampoo cleans thoroughly enough to remove product you put in your hair, which I like.The bottle is long and slender and has a convenient pop-up cap that's easy to open and close. I like how the cap end of the bottle is the flat portion that you place down; all the shampoo in the bottle builds toward that end, so you'll never have to hit the back of the bottle to squeeze shampoo out.

The third in the series of hair care products by this company that I've reviewed.this is another woman's product and like the last one is exceptional.  Does the job and leaves the hair pretty nice.  No complaints from any member of the family.So far the general conciseness is the products for women are good to exceptional and the products for men are Ok.  This one did not get the rave review from my wife as the last one, but it hasn't gotten the complaints from my son either.I'd say it's worth the bucks.  Give it a shot

I really love this shampoo. It smells wonderful and lathers up well. A little bit goes a long way. I had my hair highlighted shortly before I began to use this product, and my highlights remained shiny and bright after using this shampoo. It also rinsed well. After washing, my hair looked bouncy, not weighed down. I would definitely recommend this product as an everyday shampoo!

column9: Just what my dry hair needs!!
column10: The Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Ultra Shea Cleanse and Nourish Shampoo Gave my hair a clean and airy lift and that's rare because I have thick, kinky, and very dry hair. The Shea butter that is in this shampoo and also in the conditioner gave my hair a much needed sheen and also moisturized my scalp without weighing it down too much. I am so excited about this product and I wish it was marketed to African-American women (It's great for all hair types) as well because this product and others in this line of products provides the necessary moisture that chemicals, braids, and weaves have been stripped from our hair and these products will put your hair right back where it needs to be. The bottle design is perfect if you have a small amount of space in your shower this will fit in any tight space nicely. I like to think of this shampoo as a miracle in a bottle that is very affordable and I love it.

This shampoo has a silky, smooth texture and a clean, fresh smell. However.After about a half dozen washes, my scalp started to itch like crazy. No shampoo has ever done that to me before. After reading the other amazon.com reviews I notice at least one other user had skin problems with this shampoo. Fair warning: it's not for everyone.

I was excited to try out a new shampoo, especially one that is chocked full of Shea and other healthy oils for your hair. I usually don't fall for the hype when a shampoo says "for relaxed and natural hair" but I'm willing to give things a go at least once. When I opened the box, the product had leaked all over the bag but I was able to salvage a good amount of the shampoo. It smells great, it isn't overpowering but nice and subtle. As I began to use the product I was happy that the consistency was nice and thick, perfect for my thick and natural (african american hair) and it foamed up nicely as I worked it throughout my scalp.When I went to wash it out is when the love affair ended, my hair was left feeling like it wasn't clean and I had this nasty residue left on my hair. It felt like I needed to rewash my hair with a different shampoo. My hair didn't feel softer or moisturized, it felt weighed down and lifeless. My curls were frizzy and dull. So I flipped over to the ingredient side and i realized this shampoo has quite a bit of ingredients, including silicones, that have no business being on my hair.  This is being shoved in the back of the cabinet for days when I run out of my regular shampoo.

This shampoo did seem to plump up my straight, thin hair more than other brands. But we found it particularly effective on the dry, corkscrew hair of my two children leaving them with fluffy, softer hair. And we all love the shea butter aroma. Bottom line: at this price you feel like you've had a salon wash in your own home.

column9: My fine hair looks thicker! And I love the subtle aroma!
column10: I'm completely satisfied with CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Cleanse & Nourish Shampoo, 12.9 Fluid Ounce because it does what the advertising says: makes my hair softer, shinier, well-nourished and better moisturized... All that and it smells good too!The one complaint I have is the same as another reviewer: When I opened the manila envelope it arrived in, shampoo dribbled out onto my hands. At first I thought the shampoo container had exploded, but it actually leaked through the lid. Since the lid wasn't secure, I had to funnel it into another shampoo bottle in order to use it. That's nothing against the product; rather it's against the packager, so this product still deserves five stars, in my opinion.Review by Betty Dravis, June 20, 2012Author of award-winning "1106 Grand Boulevard"

This is a thick shampoo that lathers well and has a good scent that is not too strong. I normally only use non-sulfate shampoos, but this shampoo was pretty moisturizing and left my hair soft. I have long, thick wavy hair that gets frizzy and dry easily. I sometimes use coconut oil to keep my hair in an up-do during the day and this shampoo washes it out with no problems. I would still alternate this shampoo with a non-sulfate one since I wash my hair daily, but overall it's a good shampoo. It comes in one of those nice flat type bottles that you can turn upside down when the amount gets low.One complaint about the packaging - It arrived in an envelope and the shampoo had exploded out. The bottle was wrapped in plastic, so it was easy to unwrap and clean with a towel, but I hope that customers ordering this product receive it with better packaging.

I really like this shampoo!  I have psoriasis on my scalp and usually use shampoos that dry out my hair quite a bit.  I do have an oily scalp and was afraid that the moisturizing aspect of the shampoo would just make me a greasy mess, I don't usually buy moisturizing shampoo or conditioner (when I buy regular shampoos for when my psoriasis is calm).The shampoo combined with the conditioner would surely make me greasy, right?  Nope!  My hair is soft, nice and shiny.  I wash my hair every other day and didn't have any problems with needing to wash between my regular washings.  I'm happy with this, it made my hair soft but not greasy and kept any flakes at bay.  Definitely good stuff for me and hopefully for you, too!

There's a lot to recommend about this product...it holds its own next to brands costing much more, while providing results that are good enough for all but the most severely damaged hair and scalp. Given the large size, it works out to be a terrific bargain on a cost per use basis.Only complaint is that the shipper packaged the product in a fairly thin envelope, and by the time it reached me, the bottle was cracked near the top. About half leaked out when I opened the envelope, and even after cleaning it off, it still seemed to be oozing from the sides of the bottle. Only got to use it a few days as a result, but I definitely liked what I saw.

I was impressed with this shampoo.  It has a nice mild scent, not overpowering at all.  It works just as well if not better than many of the top salon products that I've used since 1973 when I became a hair stylist and I've tried almost all the major salon quality brands.  I have curly, dry colored hair.  I didn't think my hair felt stripped at all like one of the reviewers said, or coated.  One person gave the shampoo a poor review because it didn't cure her dandruff and burned her eye.  Plain water will burn your eye not to mention any other shampoo or soap and it's not a dandruff shampoo.My scalp and hair feel as good if not better than any of the major salon brands that I've used over the years.  My guy friend uses it and he has fine thin hair.  It works just fine for him to.  I really like the shampoo and have just ordered the conditioner to try too.

I have oily hair and have been told to use shampoo for dry hair so as to reach a medium.  In other words, use a shampoo for the opposite hair type you have.  I found that interesting and logical sounding and I've tried it, but the bottom line is that gentle shampoos for oily hair tend to work well for me.I did not know when I got this that the gold bottles in the CLEAR SCALP line were for ethnic hair.  I discovered that this shampoo works well on ANY hair and acts as a softening agent. In fact, I think it would work well for just about anybody's hair.Enter this Godsend of a product.  I JUMPED at the chance to order this!  CLEAR SCALP is a very reasonably priced product and it was very gentle on my scalp and hair.  It made my hair feel nice and soft and it has a pleasant aroma.  I love the scent of coconut and almond and my nose loved this shampoo just as much as my scalp and hair did.  Your hair stays fresh and moist while you wash and rinse and will treat your head gently.

column4: Michelle L. Beck "Always the Devourer of Good...
column9: An inexpensive alternative to prescription shampoos!
column10: Lately I have been suffering from dry scalp and have purchased several expensive shampoos, including some prescribed by my dermatologist, to remedy it. While I would not dare compare this product to some of those, I did find that this one was an inexpensive alternative. What I liked about this product.....while I have found that some of the other "dry scalp" products leave your hair feeling a bit dry, leaving you with the need to lock in moisture, this one did leave your hair feeling soft.
