And I really have to wonder what function another ingredient, "Montmorillonite Clay" (a.k.a. Fullers Earth) serves.These are sized for a medium to large dog (following the directions, an average cat should get less than half a "cookie" per day--if they even want one), and it seems to me the ingredients are more suited for dogs as well...if you are OK with the clay.

My dauchshunds adore this.  I break it in quarters and they devour the pieces.  The cats lick it but seem to have trouble eating the shards.  The smell isn't strong so it would be easy to keep some in your pocket for walks and training.

I don't really know what to make of these treats.  I was first drawn to them because of the claim they were for both cats and dogs and since it is something of an extra special treat it's nice to have something the whole family can enjoy.  But I was not impressed on any level.  Lets be honest, we all by these over priced pet treats for ourselves and not the pets.  If you honestly wanted to make your pet ecstatic you would go to the butcher shop, get tub of chicken livers or giblets, cook them up and have very happy pets.  For me this product is outrageously expensive, has an offensive smell and a texture of sawdust.The makers are trying to draw you in with this idea of it being "Raw" but do you want to feed a pet, or better yet even handle a product where the main ingredient is chicken if it actually is raw?  Though it doesn't say so on the package I don't think this item is actually freeze dried raw meat, but instead is supposed to appeal to the human's desire to feed their pet something that's healthy, i.e. raw diet for dogs.  But I see nothing in this item to make it any healthier than many other pet treats that are much cheaper in price.  I was also a little shocked at some of the health claims made on the package too.  Apparently, "Freedom from allergies, improved skin & coat, weight loss, reduced incidents of ear infections and healthier teeth & gums are just a handful of the amazing pet transformations that Nature's Variety customers experienced."  I have to call B.S. on that claim.The only real positive thing I can say about this product is that on one cat loved it.  My dog and other cat ate it, but weren't crazy about it.2 stars.

I use a lot of onion powder for seasoning many of my meat dishes.  It adds a certain zest to their flavor that I can't get any other way. The company says it is packed fresh for each order, and I believe them.  You can tell it by the aroma of the product when you receive it. I concur with the other reviewer: this is the best brownie on the planet. Until I tasted these I was a snob for homemade brownies. I can no longer consider baking my own brownies. column10: Great ingredients although, chicken should have been 1st rather than chicken broth, the only thing I do not think belongs in it is Canola oil. I have a cavalier who is an incredibly picky eater, and who has a skin condition that puts him on a limited ingredients diet.  He goes BONKERS over this food. It looks like your stereotypical mushy, canned dog food, but if my dog's reaction stands for anything, then this might just be the best dog food ever.

We have 3 poodles who needed to change from their low residue diets to something else.  Their liver counts were high and the vet recommend trying Wellness Duck and Sweet Potato.  After making the gradual change (take at least 10 days to completely change to a new dog food.  Start with 1 teaspoon a day for 3 days...then add a bit more until about day 10 when they can have their new food permanently.  If you change to a new food too fast the animal(s) will have (sometimes very severe) vomiting and diarrhea, so be patient and start small and slow).  Our little poodles liver counts are within normal range now and they LOVE this food.  They are excited about their meals now and everyone is happy.  We give it Paws Up.

column9: A bucket of soy sauce.  What needs to be said?
column10: This is a food-service portion of soy sauce.  The bucket itself is actually rather sturdy and you can probably find uses for it after you've emptied it.  That said, it's a bucket of soy sauce.  Kikkoman is a fine enough brand, and even with my use for marinating, stir frying, sauces, and yes, as a condiment for finished dishes, this is a lot of soy sauce.  The top has a little cap where you can siphon out small quantities without breaking the seal on the lid itself, and supposedly there's a spout or something built into it but I cannot locate this.  Presumably after you've exhausted the top half of your strategic soy sauce reserves you'll switch from using a baster or wine thief to a food-grade tube to extract the precious black fluid.I wouldn't bother buying such a thing at the same time, for even my level of use would have me reaching peak soy sauce sometime in 2019, finally cleaning the dregs in 2023.  If you're looking at all the bottles of soy sauce you go through, you'll finally meet your match here.  And then you'll have a nice bucket to bequeath to your grandkids, maybe they'll be the ones to finally polish it off.

column9: Makes any meat or vegetable fantastic!
column10: When I was a kid in Alabama, my dad used Dale's on everything he grilled from fish to wild game. He would tell his friends he could make shoe leather taste good with Dale's sauce. Some 30 years later we both continue to be Dale's sauce fans. The Dale's people were kind enough to send me a case before it was available online.  I told them I simply could not stand the thought of not having it again.  This stuff is absolutely delicious !!

Excellent..use as marinade on inexpennsive cuts of meat for 4 hours and your steak will tenderize like a filet and the taste is magnificent.  I use Dale's on all different types of meat and love it.  I hate being without my Dale's.

column9: Were these reviews written by Dale's corporate ?
column10: Short and sweet:My girlfriend sent me a bottle for Christmas. She lives in Alabama. I live in Maine. I'm not a 'health nut' and I love good steak sauce. This is not it ! this is a wonderful product!  it is a basic scone mix that only needs water;but so far we have made:sun-dried tomato, basil, and feta scones,cranberry-orange scones,spinach and parmesan cheese with garlic scones, andpecan scones with maple icing.easy and delicious.  they bake up with a very tender quality.  the big box contains 4 plastic bags of mix that each make 12 scones.  will definitely keep this staple in my pantry!

This is the scone mix that I grew up with. We would buy these fresh scones every year at the Puyallup Fair.  The new packaging (one big box with individually bagged portions) is an improvement over the retail pack.

Just made my first batch and I now understand what the big deal is. They are delicious. Best scone I have ever tasted. Most scones I've had are like a brick. These are light and airy, like shortcake, but fluffier. Insanely yummy! Make sure you use good jam when eating them warm.
This is a great price for a large quantity, and it's a good quality product too. Love being able to whip up a batch of these scones and add in whatever is at hand for something different each time.

This is a GREAT mix for scones!  You only need to add water, so good to have in the pantry to make a quick dessert or morning breakfast.the scones are light and the texture is crumbly.  I made them with cinnamon and raisins, next will do blueberries.So easy, and each mix ( there are 4 mixes in the box) makes 8 to 10 scones.Why buy these at 3 to 4 bucks a pop when you can have fresh from the oven with very little effort.5 stars for me!!

Don't wait in line at the fair for scones, make them at home for a fraction of the price and much better results.  I am not a huge fan of mixes, but this one is worthwhile.  I substitute 1/2 & 1/2, buttermilk or cream for the liquid for a richer flakier scone. Add a tablespoon of sugar and it makes great shortcake too.  I often add things like dried fruit, nuts, poppy seeds or other flavor with great results.  For a quick savory scone I will add in pesto, grated cheese or crumbled bacon.  Fisher scone mix has been a staple in our house for many many years.
I hate the dry super sugary things that most places call scones. This mix makes the soft, best when hot kind - popular in England, and at my house!

My family loves fisher scones with any type of berries, but recently I have had a hard time finding it in local stores, so I decided to go online and see how much I could get it for.  This is a great deal as it was even cheaper than it was in stores.  And as always the fair scones are delicious!!!

These are great scones, added dried blueberries to my first batch and plan on doing something savory next time, maybe bacon and cheese.  Even my husband liked them and he usually feels most scones are too dry.

As a child, we looked forward to going to the fair in Washington state. The first thing we ALWAYS did, was go to the booth that sold these giant hot fluffy thick scones that were split and slathered with some butter and YUMMY raspberry jam!!!! OH, my goodness, they were SSOOO good. AND NOW I can have them at home - this mix makes them just like I remembered !!!! WOW, how cool is that, thanks!!!!!!!! My rating of the Fisher scone mix is not relevant since I did not and may not use it  The Sticky Fingers scone mix is excellent and I give it a 5 star rating.

Have been having trouble finding this Frieda's Traditional Polenta. So was very happy to be able to order it from Amazon. Very good product.
FRESH, FRESH, FRESH. Long strands. Good quality, quantity and the price is also reasonable. I love the smell and taste of saffron. I would recommend this product.

I sent this product to my son who is currently deployed in Afghanistan.  The troops drink only bottled water, so this jazzes up the water a bit.  This shipped directly to my son's APO address and he received the package about a week after I ordered.  Good deal and my son is happy so I am happy.  Five stars for Propel and for Amazon!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I use empty water bottles to pre mix the Propel and set in refrigerator to chill before I put it into the lunch box with an ice block. I will carry extra with me to a restaurant and do not have to pay 2.00 for one drink, I order water and use my own flavor, it is cheaper on the restaurant bill for me.

I've been using the powdered Gatorade mix for a while now for post workout and post wild night on the town recovery for a couple years now.  I haven't ever been able to find the Low Cal Gatorade in a powdered mix so I started looking elsewhere.The Propel Zero has been great! I usually mix up a Gallon at a time to I just put 6 packets / gal.  One packet is usually for 16.7 oz of water. Going by that there's 128oz in a gallon to get a perfect mixture you would want to use around 7.6 packets / Gallon of water.  I haven't had any problem mixing 6 packets / gallon; it's actually a little on the sweet side to me so anything more than 6 packs and it would probably be way to sweet.Using sex at a time leaves you with 6 gallons of goodness which is actually a good bit cheaper than the gatorade mix and less calories too!

This is a great no-calorie replacement for Gatorade! Very refreshing, but I think its too sweet when added to a 16-oz bottle of water. I add one pack to a quart water bottle and it still tastes great!

Propel zero packetsI really like Propel water.  I used to keep a couple of bottles in the refrigerator, continuously. When I used it the opening is not wide enough for the powder to come through.  No problem, I just cut the top off the tube with scissors about a quarter inch below the strip.  I needed a heat exhaustion remedy recently.  My brother suggested Gatorade G Series Lemon-Lime (76.5 oz/Makes 9 Gallons).  I used these instead and bought Now Foods Potassium Gluconate Pure Powder, 1-poundto supplement the Propel Zero, it's a lot cheaper.  Propel had everything I needed except for Potassium, problem solved!  I use old 2-liter bottles to mix this in.  Four tubes per two liters seem to work! One tube per 17 fluid ouncesI highly recommended Propel Zero for anybody looking for a low calorie good tasting drink!Gunner, July, 2012
The drink is awesome! It tastes great and is not too overwhelming taste for the amount of water specified to use. And easy to mix especially for bottled water.

column9: The BEST coffee for you AND the Planet!
column10: I love coffee! But I love really GOOD coffee...and I found a great coffee bean that is not only excellent tasting, but also environmentally friendly! Caffe Appassionato Organic Shade Grown Espresso Roast Whole Bean Coffee is by far my favorite coffee! I have been buying organic, fair-trade and shade-grown coffee beans for a while, but wanted to find something a little less expensive -  when I found Caffe Appassionato on Amazon, I thought I'd try it since it was only about $20 for 3 - 12oz bags. I have a basic expresso/cappuccino maker and a good bean grinder and made this coffee one morning and was very impressed! These beans produce a very rich, dark and smooth expresso with a strong but not too bitter taste. This coffee really wakes me up in the morning! I love it much more than the expensive top-chain coffee houses and I know that it is also Fair traded, certified organic by OCIA (Organic Crop Improvement Association International) and shade grown to protect migratory bird populations.Why are shade grown coffee beans better for the environment? Well, we all know how popular coffee is to drink, but the beans are mostly grown in tropical, rainforest locations with sensitive eco-habitats. Some newer varieties of coffee require direct sunlight (and chemicals) to grow to optimum production levels, thus requiring trees and other vegetation to be removed from plantations, destroying the natural habitats. But the traditional varieties of coffee plants actually require the canopy of trees to filter sunlight. Since about 1996, the destruction of natural habitats, primarily of migratory birds, has sparked the movement towards going back to shade grown coffee plantations and more sustainable practices. Thankfully, companies such as Caffe Appassionato take pride in providing high quality, sustainably produced, organic coffee and the trend is growing.To get this coffee at a better price than I have seen anywhere don't forget to sign up for subscribe and save to save an additional 15%!!

I have tried many different organic shade-grown fair trade coffees.  I think that while the beans are of very good quality with most of them, what sets this coffee apart is the perfect roast.  Dark, but not burnt, with the natural oils covering the whole bean.  The flavor is deep and earthy with a touch of sweetness and exceptionally smooth.
This coffee has a great flavor, not too bitter, not too sweet.  It is an added bonus that it is organic.  The espresso comes out with a great crema and is a real pleasure.

I am compelled to warn you coffee lovers out there.  I read the reviews of so-called coffee aficianados regarding this particular brand.  I believed that organic coffee has to be better than the others I've tried just because of how its grown.  Not so, buyer beware.  This is the absolute worse coffee I have ever had the displeasure of polluting my palate.  I now believe that the first reviewer must have some personal stake in this brand, or some of your taste buds have been dulled.  I tried to return this product [[ASIN:B000GAO9WO Caffe Appassionato Organic Shade Grown Espresso Roast, Whole Bean, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 3)to Amazon, but was told that food items are non-refundable. My spouse and I tried to drink this coffee and after having 3 bags of this sludge in our cabinets, we finally decided to throw it away.  I thought of re-gifting to friends, but I like and want to keep my friends.  The only thing this coffee can possibly compliment is the garbage.  It's just so wrong that it sucks so bad.

column9: A Tasty Expresso for Iced Coffee
column10: I enjoy this coffee for iced coffee: it is really gooooood!  Cafe Appassionato Organic Shade Grown has a nice roast on the beans.  The flavor is strong,smooth and doesn't dilute with ice.  I drink it black so taste is really important, and this product holds up!  It is also important that the beans are organic and shade grown(supporting the ecology and farmer coops).

column9: An excellent espresso bean -- no matter how you make it!
column10: We make our espresso using either a french press or our Saeco "Easy" Automatic Espresso machine. These beans are full-flavored and deep, making excellent after dinner coffee. We use a rotation of Altura Sumatran Dark roast, Altura Biodynamic French Roast and Altura PeruvianCafé Altura Organic Coffee, Sumatran Dark Roast, Whole Bean, 32-Ounce BagCafé Altura Organic Coffee, Biodynamic French Roast, Whole Bean, 32-Ounce BagCafé Altura Organic Coffee, Peruvian Dark, Whole Bean, 32-Ounce Bag to keep our taste buds alive at breakfast, saving our espresso roast for after dinner.Given that our Saeco will always make the first cup of coffee from what ever bean was last in our machine, one cup of espresso will be made with one of our breakfast coffees before the just added beans reach the grinder. So we have a daily comparison of "real" espresso with other dark roasts.  There is a difference! This bean makes excellent espresso! At breakfast we split the first cup (which will be made with the prior night's beans)combined with our breakfast coffee of the day. In summer, we make our after dinner coffee in a French Press outside to save running back and forth from the kitchen. Again, excellent coffee!We have tried Starbucks espresso, and once used Green Mountain coffees in our rotation, as well as myriad supermarket offerings before we began buying from Amazon's "Subscribe and Save". This bean makes great coffee and you can taste the difference! It's not, as one reviewer suggested, just a another dark-roast coffee!

i guess the title sums it all up. I like to consider myself a slight "coffee snob" but, i don't own a roaster (nor have the time really to roast my beans). Although i woud love to do so at some point. Anyhow, somehow i stumbled upon these beans here at Amazon and after reading the reviews, decided to give them a whirl.  I was pleasantly shocked at how fantastic they really are.Normally i would order the Vesuvio blend from Batdorf and Bronson which is a great espresso blend but, runs almost twice the price for 32 oz of beans. The Appassionato though cheaper and also the fact that for about 60% of the Batdorf price i get a little more weight in beans, is superior by far.  It is very smooth and clean, grinds wonderfully and it provides a wonderful crema.We use a gaggia carezza machina and a breville conical burr grinder (not the greatest burr grinder but, it does the job well enough).

These beans are not meant for your espresso machine!Caffe Appassionato beans are roasted very dark and are oily just like a French Roast.  I would not be surprised one bit if this is French Roast.  I think many Americans like Dark Roasted Coffee because they are used to drinking crappy burnt drip coffee that sits on the burners too long.  This coffee has absolutely no character what so ever.  My opinion is that its way too dark and taste burnt.The espresso shots brewed very unevenly.  I pulled a double shot in separate cups on my Expobar espresso maker and ended up with one cup having a significant more espresso than the other.  The beans were ground very evenly in my Gaggia burr grinder at setting 4 just like any other bean I've used for espresso.  There was barely any crema!  I will try a coarser ground the next time around just to see if I can pull a more even shot.I prepare several shots per day on my Expobar Espresso Machine, have experimented with numerous varieties of beans over the past 3 years of owning this machine and have always made excellent espresso drinks.  Unfortunately, this was not the case with Caffe Appassionato.Caffe Appassianato Espresso Roast makes a good cup of coffee in the french press but these beans are the worst for espressso.  4 stars as coffee, 1 star as espresso.If you want to buy espresso beans here on Amazon, go with Lavazza.  They have a $17 bag that is very good.  I just ordered another bag of Lavazza after tasting my first shot of Caffe Appassionato.Don't let all of the 5 star reviews fool you, this is not espresso![...]

This raw organic cacao powder came in one of those electronics static bags you'd normaly see a chipset or hard drive with a recycle symbol 7 & 11-PET, ALU, PE. I was told it was "food-safe" by the seller and that "nestlé uses the exact packaging."I don't see how ROHS (the restricted use of hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment) can be food safe. I cannot return it for a full refund as there is a restocking fee and shipping charge so I'm writing this review.  At the least, common sense should tell you that organic powderd foods should not be in contact with impregnated aluminum plastics--especially when it's stamped on the bag itself stating (ROHS compliance) "that it contains the minimum acceptable levels of hazardous substances such as cadmium, mercury, and lead." This is no joke. Industry cares not about your health and therefore uses recycled materials containing these hazardous metals. A packaging containing acceptable levels of hazardous materials for a landfill is not food safe!!

Like the other 1-star buyer, this powder was shipped to me in a ULINE static shield bag which indicates that it is "ROHS Compliant." ROHS compliancy means that certain metals are banned from being used in packaging, but not necessarily lead! There is no indication this bag was not used previously for electronics, there is no origin marking anywhere on the bag and there is no nutrition label. There also is no "organic" label on the bag aside from a shoddily printed sticker that says "Organic Herbal Essence". Because of all of this I can not be sure this product is not adulterated, let alone organic. I will not purchase this product again from this seller and suggest that other buyers beware. The product itself may be fine, but why take a chance (especially if you are looking for what is supposed to be an 'organic' product free of contaminants)?UPDATE 4/12/12:I complained about the improper packaging and submitted photo evidence of the static shield bags to both the seller and Amazon. Originally the seller claimed the product was shipped in food-grade ULINE bags, but after I sent photo evidence to the contrary I heard nothing further from the seller. Amazon granted me a full refund today. If you do order this product, I recommend you double-check that the packaging is safe before opening it!

column9: Delicious and healthier alternative to other fried chips.  Nice cheese flavor.

I enjoy them plain out of the bag, and also find that they are good with salsa or dip.I wish the price was a little lower on these and wish that the bags contained less air and more chips, but otherwise I think they are great. I highly recommend that you try them.  The pricing here on Amazon, is usually about 30 cents per 6 ounce bag cheaper than what they charge at the local grocery store, HEB.  Specialty stores like Sprouts and Whole Foods charge even more for them.

I was really disappointed in this product. First of all the net weight is 4.25 oz, not 6 oz. It's about 1/3 water. Secondly the pieces are small and crumbled, without the taste or texture of crab. It could have been good quality white tuna I was eating. The taste is watery and washed out. If you're looking for succulent large pieces of crab meat this ain't it. column9: Sent it to my aunt for her 50th...
column10: I sent this to my aunt for her 50th birthday.  I didn't tell her it was coming, so when I received a very happy message on my phone from her I was thrilled to hear how much she loved it.  She was even chewing on some candy while leaving the message, which just made me smile.  When I called her back, she told me several stories about many of the candies inside, including the few good memories she has of her dad.  She took the box to work and it was a hit.These are veritable time capsules for entire generations.  Send one for a birthday, or just because.  Fun!

Although the product is convenient and the taste is good, once I was able to review the ingredients I would not have purchased this product.  The second ingredient is High Fructose Corn syrup and the more troubling third ingredient is partially hydrogenated Oil or trans fat.  All trans fat products, even products that show zero trans fat but have partially hydrogenated oil as an ingredient are products I don't purchase.  Even trace amounts cause metabolic issues.  When will food companies understand that they need to use more natural ingredients and not chemically altered ingredients?  Buyers need to help send the right message and let these products sit on the shelves.  It's voting with your dollar.  Buyer beware.

column9: Perfect for Breakfast or a Snack on the Go!
column10: These are pretty good cookies.  They're round with a 3.5 inch (90cm) diameter. They're moist enough that you won't get many crumbs when eaten by an adult.  Kids can make crumbs out of anything!The cookies are individually wrapped.  They include instructions for heating them in the microwave (if you want warm cookies).  Don't expect 1 cookie to be breakfast.  You'll need 2 cookies OR 1 cookie and some apple sauce and milk.They're yummy enough to bribe the kids to get their chores done or be quiet in church.They're healthy enough (with the oatmeal and fiber) for moms to feel better about giving their kids cookies for breakfast.I like to keep a few in my purse.  Then when my kids are suddenly starving while we're at the doctor's office or something, I can calm them down with a couple cookies.  They aren't quite as yummy when they get smashed, so try to keep them on top.Homemade cookies (so long as you don't burn them) or fresh bakery cookies are better, but this is a close substitute.

I was in rush to grab something quick from the grocery on my way to work. I usually pack my lunch but somedays I simply don't have a time for it. When I first opened up the box, they were individually packed which was a plus. However, the taste? EHhh. It was so stale. Basically not palatable at all. And more to that, as I was reading the nutrition label, the second most thing that was added as its ingredients? "high fructose corn syrup". Another big thing was partially hydrogenated soybean oils. Those two must be regulated and possibly BANNED. Of course, manufacturers still use those because using partially hydrogenated oil is much cheaper than using other kinds of oils that are still avaiable out there today. Those of you who think it's not big of a deal, ok. It is your choice to put crap in your mouth to damage your body in long run, so I don't have any control over that. Quakers obviously needs to utilize better ingredients.

column9: Good Price But Average Taste and Bad Ingredients
column10: Price on these cookies are great.  However, the taste is average.  The cookies are individually wrapped, which is nice.  But the cookies are kinda hard and meant to be microwaved for 10 secs.  It also doesn't taste much like oatmeal, but more like ginger cookie.  The texture is also not lumpy like a homemade or high quality oatmeal cookie.  It's feels like it's made more from Oat flour and the raisins r dried and small.I do have issue withe ingredients, specifically, Partially Hydrogenated Oils, TBHQ, and host of other ingredients that are less than natural for high consumption.  ThI will not be ordering any more of these.  I expected more natural ingredients from a name like Quaker.  Partially Hydrogenated Oils are not good for heart health, and TBHQ is toxic enough that companies can only put a tiny amount as preservative.  It's also used in Chicken McNuggets that many people have problems with.  I was somewhat shocked that Quaker is using TBHQ in their food.  I haven't seen this ingredient in many foods.  Maybe other companies just aren't putting it in their ingredients list.

column9: Cookies for Breakfast - Happy Thought Indeed!
column10: "Cookies are done baking!" Master Chef Greene exclaimed to an entire building of sweaty cubicle dwellers.  Master Chef, exhausted and sweaty, could have saved the trouble of this baking excursion had she only known that Quaker Oatmeal Raisin Breakfast Cookies could be heated in the microwave in only 10 seconds.Oh the labor that could have been saved!  If only she had shredded her all-from-scratch-homemade-double-oatmeal-raisin-and-walnut-cookie-recipe from her Grandma and instead bought the overpriced oatmeal and high fructose corn syrup infused cookies from Quaker!The gently wafting oatmeal aroma briefly distracted my nostrils from the overpowering musk of my overworked cube mates.  As I took a bite out of Master Chef's gooey creation my taste buds savored the wholesome goodness, but my stomach instinctively craved instead  the hollow taste of processed food.  All I could think about were Quaker Oatmeal Raisin Breakfast Cookies!  (Which, by the way, is always pronounced in the plural despite the fact that there is only one cookie per package.)These abominable Quaker Cookies ruined me for all other cookies.  Not because they are good, oh no, but because each one tastes slightly less bad than the last, creating an ever compounding craving for junk food.  Especially junk food that claims to be healthy, such as Quaker Oatmeal Raisin Breakfast Cookies.May Master Chef Greene save us all.

column9: Smooth as a baby civet's behind!

It was everything I had hoped it would be-smooth, no bitterness at all, no acid effects on my stomach, and a wonderful pure coffee taste.  I'll be ordering more! I Googled and found varying prices, and this particular seller/distributor was reasonably priced. I tried it...I loved it!! column9: Smooth But A Little Too Expensive For Everyday Consumption
column10: After learning about kopi luwak from The Bucket List, I've been wanting to try some but never could bring myself to try it due to the cost and the fact that it's been in and out of an animal.  But when I found a friend who was willing to try it with me, I figured, how bad could this be?  Granted, this was an expensive experiment but it's a once thing so the $50 was well spent in that sense.We both like strong coffee and this was certainly strong.  A 100gm bag was more than enough for a 10-cup pot with some leftover.  It didn't smell any different nor did it taste any different, unfortunately.  (Mind you, I'm not comparing this to stuff like Folgers or Starbucks.  I'm comparing it to the Malaysian coffee I'm used to.)  It was strong but smooth - it didn't have the "rancid" taste (not sure if I'm explaining the taste correctly) that some cheaper coffee tend to have and neither did it have a charred flavor like burnt beans.  Unfortunately, it still had a hint of bitterness toward the end of the sip.  I tried it black at first to experience the taste unadulterated by anything but couldn't stand it.  (I never could drink black coffee anyway.)  A packet of sugar made it pleasant but still retain its coffee-ness.As an experiment, it was worth it, albeit a little expensive.  I don't think I'll be purchasing more of this - it's an ok coffee.  I would drink it if presented with it but I won't go out of my way to get it.  Just a little too expensive for everyday drinking.  I'll stick to my Malaysian coffee - sweet, smooth, and buttery, almost.

I couldn't be happier with the customer service from Luwak Star.I ordered a bag of Luwak Star Coffee this weekend to send as a gift for a family member, crossed my fingers, and hoped it would arrive in time despite ordering very late. Just two days later, after noticing the delivery address was different from the billing address, the owner of Luwak Star emailed to ask if the coffee was a gift. She said that if so, she would be happy to include a card in the package. I was floored. What an incredibly considerate gesture. I even told her that I had placed the order too late and was worried it wouldn't arrive in time for a birthday. She responded right away and said she would be happy to visit the post office and look into rush shipping for me.There are several options for purchasing quality coffee on Amazon, but this type of service is rare, worth supporting, and will keep me coming back. I'll make sure to follow up on this review once we have a chance to enjoy the coffee!

column9: You have to be a coffee lover....
column10: This product is something you have to be open minded about trying, and you must truly love coffee to appreciate it. No one I know can imagine why I decided to purchase or drink this.The packaging was standard USPS shipping package. Ordered May 1st and arrived May 5th, where it was estimated to arrive between the 8th and 23rd. Ships out of California, so if you live closer, it will probably be sooner.The package contains the whole, roasted beans, so you'll need to grind it to your desired texture. The included instructions were nice, but following them for a French press delivered a slightly weak cup. The coffee was smooth, slightly chocolatey in undertones. Debating doing an espresso brew with it.Overall, you can't go wrong if you purchase this. But you have to love coffee to appreciate it for what it is.
I have tried Kopi Luwak before, yet this has to be the best of the best. This coffee is worthy of being called coffee of all coffees. You will not regret paying for these beans.

Whoever Dennis is, he's absolutely right! I've always liked Arabica coffee and tried this based on the other comment, and out of all the coffees I've tried, this is really the best! Get some of your own.

OK, first a review of the flavor:I tried it without any cream or sugar, as was suggested.  It had a pretty pleasant, mellow flavor.  It wasn't nearly as acidic as most coffees but you have to have a pretty distinguishing pallet to appreciate it.  I added cream just to test it out and indeed, it ended up tasting like normal coffee.I give this one star because after I drank it, I ended up running a fever of 102 degrees that lasted for a week and a half.  I finally went to the hospital and they found ileitis on a CT scan of my abdomen and confirmed it with a colonoscopy.  They found no damage consistent with an autoimmune disease, like Crohn's, and they ruled out everything except a bacterial infection.  They gave me Flagyl and my fever finally broke.  The ileum is where the bacteria from your stomach gets concentrated as the contents are processed into your small intestine, and it was consistent with an infection from a pathogenic source, at exactly the right timeframe, so it was almost certain that I got this from drinking the coffee.I thought after the cleaning, roasting and brewing, it would be safe, but think about it: the cleaning wouldn't be done with an antiseptic, because doing that would contaminate and ruin the beans.  Pathogens could still live within the cracks of the beans.  Roasting still doesn't eliminate the risk of cross-contamination, and when you're brewing it, as in a French press as I did, the temperature may well not be high enough (they tell you not to boil coffee as that ruins it) to kill the pathogens.  Remember that these beans passed through a creature's digestive tract and you're drinking the extract.I'm sure not everyone will get sick, but it is a risk.  I never thought I'd get sick, but I did.  So use caution and if you start vomiting or running a fever after you drink this, get some appropriate antibiotic from your local PCP.  As for me, I'll never drink this again.  The experience was not fun.
I got these for xmas and now I have to have more. Very moist anad chewy,better then homemade.

The sauce was VERY sweet and might not be for everyone, but a bit of soy sauce or wine vinegar would mild it out nicely.I made it in three ways:First, I tried as recommended by microwave, then a quick fry in a oiled pan. This method produced (as you would expect) a tender wonton wrapper with the slightly fried texture on both sides, and it brought out the filling flavor the best out of the three methods. This produced a crisper crust  but was my least favorite out of the three.Thirdly, I deep fried them in peanut oil. The wonton got very crisp and flaky and that texture combined with the filling was my favorite out of the three. This method wasn't recommended on the package, but it should be!Overall these went very well with my meals and once as a snack, I plan to get them again!

column9: Great deal on best GF pretzels I've found!
column10: I fell in love with Glutino stick pretzels when I started a gluten-free diet six months ago. I actually think they taste better than the regular pretzels I used to eat! The only downside was the price -- the local store charged $8.99 per 14 ounce bag. When I checked on Amazon, I was pleased to find they carry Glutino pretzels. With the subscribe and save deal, the 8-ounce bags came out at just over $3 apiece. If you or your gluten-free child loves pretzels for a snack, and you have the space to store a dozen bags, this is an awesome deal! I have a handful of friends who also are gluten-free, so I've shared some of my order with them. These are amazingly good pretzels and Amazon's subscribe and save price is the best you're going to find anywhere!!

Of all of the gluten free pretzels I have tried, these by far are the best.  They are close to the real thing as I recall.  Sometimes they are difficult to obtain.  Stores do not stock them since they are a bit pricey but well worth it for those of us who are gluten-intolerant.  These are a must for me.

column9: Get these if need a POWERFUL LAXATIVE
column10: I purchased these at a local store, and had half a bag for lunch.  They tasted OK, but were definitely not worth the after effects.  Within about 7 hours after eating these my stomach started feeling awkward.  Shortly after I started having cramps and severe watery diarrhea several times throughout the evening and late night.  Looking at the ingredients, the thing that stands out is carboxymethylcellulose AKA cellulose gum.  The package I purchased said cellulose gum on the ingredients list, but on the web sites it is listed as carboxymethylcellulose.  You will find they are synonyms if you Google them.  All I had for breakfast that day was a bowl of dry corn flakes, and didn't have time to eat dinner before my stomach started cramping.  If you look up this ingredient, or look it up along with "side effects" you will find it is undigestible and can cause side effects such as bloating and diarrhea.  Never again.  All I can say is please post a review if this happened to you to others are forewarned!

column9: Great product but needs to be packed better

These pretzels are very yummy. But, be careful they can be addicting and before you know it the whole bag is gone!

column9: Thumbs up from a new gluten-free dieter
column10: We have decided to transition to gluten-free.  I bit into my first gluten-free pretzel with trepidation, but they are good!  Really good.  Maybe even a little better than regular pretzels.  Still not exactly health food, but the taste is awesome.  My kids love them, too.

There is nothing that compares!! These are better than regular pretzels!! You can't eat just one!!  Thanks Amazon for giving celiacs or anyone that is on a gluten free diet a break in the price that is normally paid for these pretzels...we couldn't do it without these pretzels! I am on a gluten free diet and so are my two little girls so these pretzels go fast in my house! You won't waste your money!!
These are great pretzels, better than regular ones.  Crunchy with just the right amount of salt.  Opened a bag at work and my co-workers ate them right up.
Most of the pretzels when I got them where smashed into little pieces. The packaging seemed appropriate. Maybe that's why there was a deal on these.

LOL, but be forewarned, you'll be hooked too!!!
Mmmmmmmmmm.... This is all I can say. This is a great snack. It is better tasting than wheat pretzels I hear from everybody including I myself say so, too! Crunchy, tasty, and great!

I bought these pretzels for my dad, who suffers from Celiac disease and Type 1 diabetes. He has a hard time keeping any weight on due his restricted diet, and often resorts to potato chips for his sole source of carbs between meals. He absolutely loves these pretzels, and said he enjoys them more than the regular kinds. I think they taste excellent, with that very slight "burnt" flavor that makes pretzels so good. They also seem to have a delicious buttery aftertaste IMO. Plus, they're very satisfying and healthier than potato chips.

column9: Better than the sesame gluten free pretzels
column10: The pretzels aren't bad for those of us that have to maintain a gluten free diet.  They are tastier than the pretzels with sesame seeds.

column9: Best Gluten-Free Pretzel - I love these!!!

These pretzels are so good - so much like the "real thing" for those of us who cannot eat gluten -(wheat,barley,rye and oats).  We recommend them highly!

These pretzels are extremely good tasting.  Very difficult to tell the difference compared to pretzels with gluten.
These gluten free pretzels are enjoyed by everyone.  Friends have even said they taste better than their regular pretzels.

column9: The Best Gluten Free Pretzels around!!
column10: You will not waste your money...simply the best!! You can't have just one!!

We had been eating the Glutino regular pretzels for a few years now and they were okay, but recently our health food store started carrying these.  I bought a bag and we enjoyed them so much I was back buying a few more.  Pretzels are one thing I've missed since going gf - but not any more!  Taste great with dip, too!

I'd never heard of Glutino before. I bought a snack pack of these pretzels at a health food store. They cost a fortune. I was shocked when Amazon had them by the case. What a great find for my son on the GFCF diet. They taste great. No different than other pretzels. We bought a whole case. We love them! Thanks so much Glutino.

column9: Yummy, but 6 grams of fat per serving!
column10: These pretzels have been a wonderful treat since discovering I am gluten sensitive, but at 6 grams of fat a serving you need to be careful of how many you eat!  Would rate them at five stars if they contained less fat, but then they might not be as yummy...

these are awesome. though they're gluten free, they taste wayyyy  better than regular pretzels. they're crunchier, no bad aftertaste or anything, and taste buttery. only thing is, you have to make sure you put leftovers in a sealed bag or else they get stale quickly, but overall awesome.
I absolutely love these pretzels.  I am very disappointed that I can no longer buy them on Subscribe & Save.  Don't know who's at fault with this but I wish you could get it worked out.

If you Celiac or just perfer gluton-free, these pretzels are a good substitution for both other pretzels and other types of snacks. Despite what O'Reilly used as a tip at the end of his show, gluten-free usually mean more "carbs" for a similar serving. But as a Celiac, varity is truly the spice of life. Celiacs first response to diagnosis is to see all the walls between them and what used to be their favorite foods. Celiacs in this day and age are so much luckier than previous generations. Firstly, because Doctors are running the proper blood tests to diagnosis gluten-intolerance much more frequently. It might appear as if more folks are stricken with this these days, but I am convinced that is just because of this increased knowlegde by the Doctors. As to these pretzels. They may or may not strike you as better than your previous favorite, but you now understand that the previous favorite were the cause of "palor", malnutrision and gastro issues. So you must resign yourself to exploring the every expanding gluten-free offerings. These are not your Philly soft pretzels, but they make a great salty and crunchy "chip" with which to scoop up some hummus, peanutbutter, etc. Also, this size bag and the Amazon price for a box of these every month or two is one of the most affordable ways to enjoy these healthful snacks. They also good straight from the bag, but it easy to get carried away. My wife and I found out about my Celiac 5 years ago. It makes you read everylabel on every product you bring into your house. You may even go as far a throwing out all porous (i.e. wooden) utensils, your old toaster and several other things and can't be guaranteed sanitazied. You learn to trust mostly the food you make yourself, but when you learn that you can trust Glutino, and you can, subscribe to Amazon for regularly scheduled deliveries of all types of life giving goodies like the Pamela's Pancake Mix which go great with chopped, toasted walnuts, blueberries and a couple of raisins although, most maple, agava and other syrups are still safe.Glutino Gluten Free Pretzel Twists, 14.1-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)

glutino pretzels are fresh tasty and best gluten free foods you can ever buy. i recomend this product for all who need to keep wheat away from their diet.awasome product and company.

column9: I  would purchase this product again

The 2.6 oz. bag makes it easy to control portions for those who (like me) are on a restricted diet. I don't eat Gluten so I am always looking for good Gluten Free snacks. Most are  like sawdust -- These taste better than regular pretzels.  I highly recommend them.

column10: Once my family tasted these at a party I threw, they love it when I bring them to their house to share for gatherings. Every person that has tried them, LOVE them. For those of us that are used to paying prices for GF food, these are not that far off. I also tend to savor them more, knowing they are a bit more costly than the rest.
Glutino pretzels are by far the best tasting on the market.These actually made my kids believe that being GF wasn't going to be so badif they could still have a good pretzel to snack on!
I have a gluten problem and have a great appreciation for these pretzels. I have no problem with Glutino pretzels, and think they are so much better than any other I have tried. I will order again.

These gluten free pretzels taste BETTER than regular pretzels.  They are light and crunchy, but they still taste like pretzels should.  If you are sensitive to gluten (and even if you aren't) I'd recommend trying a few...you could be pleasantly surprised.
If you are a Celiac, or are gluten intolerant, you won't find a better pretzel than the Glutino brand.  I have them on Auto-Delivery with Amazon.

This sea salt sampler is a great way to try different salts and determine which one(s) you want to buy more of. If you have never tried sea salts this, again, is a great way to start.  You'll be amazed how elements from the different regions of the world affect the subtle flavors of the salt.  Then when you cook, you'll notice those subtle flavors enhancing whatever you use them in. It's great!

column9: The excellent price and beautiful packing
column10: Very tasty salt, it is possible to compare the different. Most of all it was pleasant Hawaiian pink. It is convenient to take with itself and to use on work during a dinner. column9: Thank goodness for this cat food!
column10: The food this company makes is the closest I can find to raw until I actually get to feed mine raw more often. The value is amazing... actually because it is so dense with nutrients, my cats eat less and I spend less feeding them this brand of food than the other premium brands I was feeding them before.The canned is a dense pate style that needs to be mashed down. My cats had not been fond of pate textures of other brands of foods in the past. It took about 4 days for one of my cats to recognize it as her new food. She had to be enticed but it ends up she is loving it! (Patience pays off!) The other cat will eat anything and there was no problem getting her to eat it. The both now eat all 3 available flavors and seem to love the rabbit the best. The Canned Duck and Salmon is their second favorite. It seems to be more "decadent" than the other flavors (rich in oils) and has been amazing for their skin. So little dander and shedding...Their coats are magnificent! Their stools are small and odorless, similar to what it would look like if they were on a raw diet. My oldest cat who had mild digestive issues doesn't have them anymore. Hooray! I also noticed that while on this brand of food, the crusty sleepies in their eyes are just about non-existent. I hardly have to groom their faces anymore. And they are so active I can hardly believe they have that much energy for their ages.I honestly believe that having no synthesized vitamins makes a world of difference. I picked this up while in New Orleans 7 years ago, we now use it everyday. The flavors really bring food to life. If you want low fat chicken and fish, just sprinkle this on it will give your dish and a wonderful taste. You will think you are at a restaurant.
I first heard about Slap Ya Mama from my son who had been toTexas. I figured I could get it from amazon. I was able to order several and enjoy  the spice. it is not for wimps. Thanks

I was given a container (shaker) of Slap Ya Mama and enjoyed it very much.  Not having found it in local stores, I ordered a six-pack from Amazon at a good price.  Although this is a blend of salt & peppers, it is heavy on the salt.  I find it is so salty that you have to use it very sparingly.  Nevertheless, it has a good taste and is a good all around seasoning for everything from boiled eggs to soups.  Use it as you would more ordinary seasoned salt.

Once in a while Amazon recommendations really hit one out of the park. I took a chance and ordered this based on a recommendation and the reviews and I'm glad I did. We use this on almost everything we cook. It spices up chicken, red meats and even fish fantastically. It you like some spice in your food, it's addictive.

This is an essential spice that we use on many foods. It's not very spicy so it won't overpower the flavor of foods. It's great on seafood (on salmon it's amazing), eggs, and we even put it on popcorn. You get a 6-pack from Amazon which will probably last you well over a year.

column9: Really good, but a little heavy on the salt
column10: I was involved in a food challenge using this product.  It was not, however, a challenge set up by Slap Ya Mama, but rather a person in  a foodie group that fell in love with the seasoning.  We were provided free seasoning mixes of both regular and hot.Being involved in said challenge meant using SYM in as many ways as we could.  And let me tell you, there are lots of ways.  This stuff is pretty great and very versatile.  It works on meat, fish, stews, vegetables, sauces.  It is killer with sweet potatoes.  Chicken wings, dipped in butter then sprinkled with SYM and baked will rock your world.Personally, I like a mix of half regular, half hot.  This largely due to the saltiness of the regular blend, which is *really* salty.I guess a good indicator of my enjoyment of the product is that even after being given freebie mixes, I actually came in here and bought a six-pack when I ran out.

I love this stuff - it's just a simple blend of salt, black and red pepper, and garlic. I put it on my eggs, shrimp, chicken, pork, beans, pasta, mac-n-cheese, in chili, stews, soups, SLAP! I love just saying "Slap Ya Mama!" as I suddenly decide to add a dash to whatever I'm cooking when the urge overtakes me. You will have to experiment for yourself how much or little to add to your foods because sometimes I go too far and it's a little too salty or hot, but that's my fault - gotta develop a practiced hand to go with that judicious mind! Just slap it!

Simply stated this stuff is magic.  Five stars is an understatement.  We brought a box while attending the NOLA Jazz and Heritage Festival about two years ago.  I've been using is sparingly until I found that you could purchase the product online.  I reupped my supply and sent my brother some over in Dallas.
Slap is good on everything from macaroni and cheese to eggs to mashed potatoes to tacos. I would recommend this to anyone. It's my very favorite seasoning EVER!

I use to buy Spirulina in Mexico where it is a lot more consumed than in the US and way cheaper.... After checking various spirulina powder qualities, I decided to buy this organic one from Earth Circle and I was not disappointed. It's a truly good product, well packed to protect its freshness even though I would have prefered a jar easier to open. And it's easier to take a spoon of this very thin powder from a jar because any wrong move with the spoon when you take it from a bag makes a mess on your kichen counter !

For some reason my miniature/toy poodle loves fishy foods (especially sneaking into the cats food), so I was excited to find these fish recipe sticks. Made in USA is a huge must for my dogs treats after the Chinese treat issues, and I was happy to find this company offers that. My poodle is about 8lbs and this lasted her about 1/2-1 hour of chewing. More known brands (those you would find in every grocery store) usually get abandoned by my dog after a couple minutes when she realizes she doesn't care for the taste.An issue I've had with other products and my dogs are upset tummys if they eat too much. These sticks have caused no issues at all!I greatly recommend this product for those who care about quality.

column9: Fantastic!  I LOVE this stuff! (so does my daughter!)
column10: My just turned 4 year old daughter will NOT, I repeat NOT, eat fruit of any kind.  The last time she ate fruit was baby food.  No joke.  She has food aversions, texture issues, temperature issues, pickiness issues, and has been in feeding therapy for 1.5 years.  She won't drink water unless it's purified (she can tell the difference). I mean this is serious stuff.I bought one of these and gave it to her, explained that it was baby food consistency but wasn't baby food, and was fruit (didn't lie to her) but wasn't a cold smoothie like the kind Mommy makes (which she does NOT like).She slurped the whole thing down!  Tears came to my eyes I was so shocked and excited.  This whole feeding drama is very trying on my patience and I worry so often that she will have long-term problems.She has been devouring them ever since!  This as well as The Red One.  I cannot believe that she is "eating" fruit!!!  I am forever a loyal buyer of Ella's Kitchen products.  When my son is ready for solids, I will feed him Ella's baby food.  I cannot tell you how thankful and happy I am to finally get fruit in my daughter's belly!

column9: Great dairy and soy free snack!
column10: My kids love these!!  We have tried the red one, yellow one, and purple one and they love all 3.  My 11 month old is allergic to milk and soy, so trying to find him portable snacks has been a challenge, but he adores these.  And he has learned how to suck them down by himself, which is a big plus for me. My 4 1/2 year old loves them too, the challenge with her is keeping her from eating them all at once!  Amazon has a better price than our store, too, plus the only 2 stores that sell these in my area are 30 mins away.  Love Amazon for saving me the gas and delivering to my house!

My daughter currently does not want to eat fruit. I think it has to do with the texture or something. So in order to ensure that she does get her vitamins I give her these as a snack. I think they are all great and that it's a shame that they are not all available for subscribe and save anymore.

Where to use these:1. Kid's lunches instead of fresh fruit2. Your lunch for work3. Stash some in the car for a healthy snack4. Road trips5. Vacations6. Flights (note the size allows it on the airplane)7. The beachReal fruit. Nothing else.  Tastes good.

These organic pouches sell out FAST at the store, and with good reason! We love these fruit pouches-- they are portable, sized perfectly for kiddo hands, and offer a perfect, wholesome snack.  All organic with 100% natural ingredients, no pesticides, no chemical fertilizers, no genetic modifications, and no preservatives. The pouches themselves are are BPA and phthalate free.Compare the ingredient list on these snacks to the other fruit pouches and you will quickly see why these are so popular! Pure, real FOOD.

My son absolutely loves these, and we still buy Ella's kitchen products occasionally for some variety, but other brands such as Happy Baby provide the same quality organic products for a much lower cost. Ella's Kitchen has an excellent product, and we love everything we've every tried from them, but I just cannot justify the significant difference in cost. They are just SO much more expensive than other brands of really good organic baby food!

Ella's PurpleOne is the perfect in the taste department and provides the nutrients I need when these items aren't available.  It doesn't taste grainy or too smooth, I tastes like the food they claim is in there.  And from the fridge they taste even better.

column9: Organic baby food for on the go
column10: We absolutely love this product. It is great for on the go when you need food for your little one, but don't want to carry around a ton of stuff. Just shake and squeeze out on a spoon. I make most of my little one's food from scratch, but these are PERFECT for in his diaper bag.  They're easy to use, little to no mess, and no added ingredients.  When we're out and about and the little guy gets hungry, I just whip out a smoothie and all's good with the world.  Oh, and it tastes like heaven.  Yes I've tried them!

column9: Awesomely delicious. PORTABLE FRUIT for anyone. Organic, low sodium, nothing aritfical, gluten free. We all ages 2 to 84 love.
column10: Awesomely delicious. Portable fruit that does not have to be refrigerated. We keep on shelf in pantyr and in car for quick healthy snack.  Organic, 0 transfat, low sodium, nothing aritfical, gluten free. This is the favorite flavor of our whole family. We all ages 2 to 84 love these.

column9: Great for taking on the go!
column10: We discovered these at Target one day when I'd forgotten to pack a snack for the kiddo. Nummy! And nearly mess-free, if you keep from squeezing the pouch. Wow, my daughter LOVES these! She is about 10 months and this thing disappeared in one sitting. The pouch allows babies to feed themselves by using the opening as a straw. column9: Delicious, Healthy, Easy for Kids to Open Snack!
column10: My kids have tried all of the Ella's Kitchen "smoothies" and love them.  (By the way, they make baby food ones, too.)  This is a real blessing for any busy mom who has her hands full. Ella's Kitchen pouches are notably easier than most squeezable fruits we've tried and we've pretty much tried them all--the tops are nice and big and easy for even toddlers to unscrew and screw back on. column9: So Delicious, Safe and Easy Top, Perfect for Traveling!
column10: This is my daughter's favorite Ella's fruit flavor.  Not only do they come in smoothie fruit for toddlers and bigger kids (and grown-ups, wink-wink), but they come in baby food, too! It is difficult to find organic fruits and veggies where I live, so having these on hand is a daily lifesaver. Not to mention they use minimal packaging and are wonderfully portable. I got this for my 2 year old daughter to substitute for a quick snack on the go. However it hardly takes her a minute to finish it all up. She loved the taste, they are a little expensive though.

Well I ordered this unsure of the age range it was ok for...I couldn't find the recommended age anywhere. Well my 6 month old loved it! column9: One of the best baby foods for 6 month+
column10: I love Ella's because there are so many great mixes of fruits and vegetables for my baby to try. I love all the pouches, because I don't want to get jars with BPA in the lining of the lid and I also don't have time to make baby food either. column9: Wish I would have tried these sooner!

column9: Ella's Kitchen Organic - THE RED ONE

So glad I found these on Amazon, the price is so much better.  In the stores they average $1.50 - $1.79 each.
So good. My kids and I both loved it. It's absolutely delicious,, easy and a great way to get your fruits in.
They couldn't get enough of these, and I felt good about a snack that was filled with good stuff. The price is a bit high due to packaging but contents were good.

I love this product for my 4 year old. I pack one in her lunches and carry one in my purse at all times. I love that the packaging is BPA free, unlike several other competitor products. The lid is perfect for tiny hands to open and you can reseal the package if it's not all consumed. All organic ingredients, nothing artificial.

column9: Good, but other options  may be healthier
column10: "The Red One", organic baby food "smoothie"If you're like me, you're interested in this item because it looks convenient and like something your baby will actually eat -- that would be a pretty good description of this product, with a few caveats:-The nutrition content of this product is not really that great. You tend not to waste much product with the packaging design.Just a reminder, the container is a bit smaller than some of the other "bagged" baby foods:  3 oz is less than the plastic Gerber containers (at 3.5 oz), but more than the small glass jar foods (usually 2.5 oz).

column9: EXCELLENT flavor! (For my kid AND me!!!)
column10: We've always been fans of Ella's Kitchen products, but this is probably our favorite flavor we've tried! I'm almost 30 and I squeeze these purees almost as often as my 4-year old child does :) Delicious, ORGANIC, easy- great product!!

column9: great product, not what the little one wanted

We love all the flavors of the Organic Smoothie Fruits. Subscribe and Save is the perfect way to get both the Yellow One and Red One on a monthly basis. Our little one just eats them directly from the hard spout.
These are pricey, but they are tasty.  You can give them to baby or school kid (or yourself) and they will be liked by all.  Also, they don't really look like baby food.

my son is a very fussy eater, and wants to do everything himself at 16 months and these are good for him and allow him to do that.. love the products and peter rabbit ones

column9: Quick, Easy and Gone in 2 Days.
column10: I bought these to throw in the my sons lunch box and he really enjoys them.  I bought the yellow and the red, he likes the yellow ones best.  The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because of the price, you are clearly paying for the ease of this product.

I prefer to stick with organic versions of the "dirty dozen" in produce (which, sadly, includes most berries), but I also try to follow my pediatrician's advice to have my son "eat the rainbow" each day. That gets tough, especially when we get into fall/winter, when fresh fruits and veggies are fewer and far between. Organic berries (like the strawberries and raspberries in this product) are expensive, hard to find, and definitely out of season right now here in NY. Enter Ella's Red One Smoothie Fruits. These pouches are great to have around as an option to round out my toddler's colorful fruit intake for the day. Not to mention, they're delicious - think applesauce, with sweet berries added for extra flavor and flair! And they're ideal when we're on the go. With a few of these tossed into my diaper bag, I always have something healthy and organic on hand for him to enjoy. They're even a nice snack for me when I find myself a bit low on energy when we're out and about. The crushed fruit inside these pouches is smooth (almost baby food consistency), so it slurps up through the straw-like top easily. Once I've unscrewed the cap, my 17 month old can eat this entirely without my help, leaving my hands free to get stuff done. Sweet!

My little one eats very few purees nowadays.  He likes feeding himself.  However, these smoothies are good for both Baby and Momma.  a) The flavor is FANTASTIC with organic goodness bursting at the seams of your taste buds.  b)  I love, love, LOVE this pouch.  During a feeding, I normally start by squeezing a biteful at a time into a spoon for my little one.  No mess and resealable if he decides he only wants 1/3 of the container.  I've also found that after a while, my little one likes to hold the pouch and slowly squirt it into his mouth.  Once again, no mess for me to clean up, and Little Guy is very pleased at the food and being able to feed himself.Fabulous product indeed.

My 9 month old daughter loves these! She'll sometimes reject food if she's having tummy troubles or cutting a tooth, so I turn to these on those days. I never have problems getting her to eat them, I feel like she's getting great quality food, and they mix well with cereal. I also love the packaging because it's much easier to throw in my purse than a jar of food!

column9: A great snack on the go

column9: Delicious, Tasty and Healthy for my Little One!
column10: My 20 month old loves fruits and vegetables! When I say he loves them, I mean he would pick them over his other snacks. So I don't complain when he asks for them either. We have a cupboard filled with these healthy snack pouches just on hand when we run out of his veggies and fruits. We take them along wherever we go. I think its because Ella's is more firmer than the Plum Organics, which tastes a little water down.My son loves these and doesn't even mind having some of the Stage 1 for babies! I gave this product 5 stars because it tastes good, its packaged nice, they come in different combinations and it healthy!

I am a twenty-six year old female. I'm short, and my metabolism isn't the worse, nor the best. I was looking for a healthier alternative to most snacks I find at the store, I was told this resembles applesauce and to try it. It's has a pleasant applesauce feel, and taste good to boot. Only qualm is, that it's a small snack and will not make you content if you're starved. Good to use in-between meals when not starved though!Update: August 4 2011 - I recently ended up with GERD and a really bad bleeding ulcer, due to stress and grief. I have problems keeping food down and went on a baby food diet for the sake of thriving. This stays down but is beginning to cause some indigestion at times. I'm not saying it would cause you guys to reflux or anything of that sort, but it was really acidic and caused me to choke. My throat now burns a lot, and feels sore, Please be weary if you're having gastrointestinal problems. Babyfood is such a great idea if you're having problems keeping things in, and need to retrain your stomach and intestines. Just be careful, some are more acidic than others.P.S. I like this flavor better than "The Red One".
