Only qualm is, that it's a small snack and will not make you content if you're starved. Good to use in-between meals when not starved though!Update: August 4 2011 - I recently ended up with GERD and a really bad bleeding ulcer, due to stress and grief.  I have problems keeping food down and went on a baby food diet for the sake of thriving.  This stays down but is beginning to cause some indigestion at times.  I'm not saying it would cause you guys to reflux or anything of that sort,  but it was really acidic and caused me to choke.  My throat now burns a lot,  and feels sore,  Please be weary if you're having gastrointestinal problems.  Babyfood is such a great idea if you're having problems keeping things in,  and need to retrain your stomach and intestines.  Just be careful,  some are more acidic than others.
When I purchased this, I thought about a healthy smootie anywhere anytime, but it doesn't taste very good. Not sweet and yummy enough. Sorry for being so technical.

column9: Is that what they call "green" packaging?
column10: After you've consumed your THREE OUNCES of organic "green" juice, the package will remain in a landfill for the next 450 years before it finally decomposes.  I'm sick and tired of companies trying to act all healthy while using piggish materials like this for their packaging.  Give your kid a freakin' apple.
ordered a case of this, it said it was organic lemon lime soda and a picture of organic is there to. but i got natural lemon lime soda

column9: Red Matcha tea made from Rooibos
column10: I think there is a wrong description of this tea listed at the moment, this tea is made from the rooibos plant.I bought the tea since I do love the Japanese green matcha tea, but that is so energizing I don't want do drink it at night. Plus I wanted to try something new.I found that there are only about 3 companies who do sell red matcha. I tried this one from Red Leaf Tea since I saw that they had many different types of matcha available, even black and white matcha. So they appear to be matcha specialists! I sometimes cannot wait for my shipment of green tea to arrive from Japan, it takes so long. I was happy to find Red Tea and they are an American company, the shipping was fast!I love the red matcha, it has its own sweet flavor, I liked it without sugar or cream. It is very thirst quenching. I haven't tried it iced, but I read that it is wonderful as an iced tea or iced latte. I only bought the small size so I am conserving. I am using the rest to make just plain, I just add hot water and whisk or stir. It is absolutely delicious without anything added. It foams up pretty nicely also! I should have bought the bigger size from Red Tea. I was trying it for the first time.  Now I have another tea I like as much as green tea matcha!This red matcha is very healthy and FULL of anti-oxidants, even more so than green tea! It is a good tea to drink at bedtime since it is relaxing, but it also makes a good daytime tea.  I think this tea will be revitalizing if you need and relaxing if you want, it is unique.Try this: add some red tea matcha to warm milk or soymilk (any kind of milk) with your favorite sweetener. YUMM!I put some of the matcha in lowfat 1% milk with some vanilla agave syrup (I didn't have plain agave) and then used my espresso machine's steamer to foam the milk and create a delicious dessert.  I was a little embarrassed to try to get every little bit of foam out of my mug, so I made a second serving!  I still got every bit out of the mug at the end, that is how good it is!

column9: Second best canned sardines in the states.
column10: I have lived in Spain. I have tried almost every brand of canned sardines in New York. I still like the ones from Spain. This one is pretty good although not as good as those available in Spain. Since I am here I have to settle with this brand. My complaint is that the fish is a little on the dry side.Goya has the best canned sardines in the states.

These sardines are top notch. They are carefully packed and the hot pickled veggies are delicious. Add some lime juice before you eat them and the flavor is even more intense. I sent some to my family and they have been sardines eaters for a long time, they simply loved them.
I have been looking for these for years.  Items came in quick and taste as good as I remember.Vigo Spiced Sardines, 4 3/8-Ounce Cans (Pack of 10)

I like spicy food and I like sardines, but I don't like these. I simply cannot finish my pack of 10 cans. I like other Vigo sardines and I wouldn't say these are low quality, but something about the mixture of these strong flavors doesn't work for me. I can taste them for hours.

Sardines packed in oil (soy, olive and EVOO) are too bland for me. I've tried them with green chilies, chipotle and Louisiana hot sauce. These Vigo are hotter than the others, but not by much. I kick it up a notch with Tabasco Habanero or Jalapeno sauce. If you like 'em midly hot, these may be just right for you.
The hot spiced and lemon versions are our favorites.  These sardines are a great value for the price.
On the whole a good effort that falls a bit short--not very hot and spicy, a bit too much salt, and a rather inconsistent texture of the fish among separate cans.  Ok, but could be better.
This product is now made in Morocco and not Spain, as falsely claimed by Amazon. Being Moroccan-made, the sardines should probably be sold for $1 a can rather than $2.123.

column9: A few hypersalty mushy sardines per can
column10: On my personal scale of 0 (worst) to 5 (best) IMHO, these affordable sardines that I have bought and tasted repeatedly in 2011 are rated by me as follows: odor 2/5; presentation 3/5; taste 3/5; texture 2/5 and quantity in can 3/5.I will not buy again.
Discontinued at local stores, I found them at Amazon for the same price. Sardines are a bit spicy but fresh and delicious.

It's 10 tins in individual yellow cardboard boxes shrink wrapped in plastic. Item arrived with other items all in seemingly good condition. I opened one, ate it, and it seemed fine. Then, looking closer, I saw that a number of boxes were discolored. It seems that they were soaked with oil. I found the worst one, opened it, and the can inside seemed okay with no obvious defects. When I "oil canned" it (compressing and releasing it repeatedly), I could hear air hissing in and out. I immediately threw it away, of course! Then later I got to thinking--no shipping damage; other items fine; so it could either have "burst" from bacteria growth due to improper cooking, or the canning equipment was defective and no seal was ever achieved. Either way, this could be a one way ticket to the botulism hall of fame (the graveyard). I had already eaten one, and already thrown another away, so I haven't returned them, but beware that you should be very careful before you eat any. Make sure you hear the vacuum release when you open the can. The other eight cans seem fine, and I'm still here to write the review so the ninth one must be okay too! The pickers at Amazon might have caught this if they paid attention, but it wasn't obvious even to me.
The exact amount of bite that does not detract from the taste of the sardines.
Takes me back to my childhood.  I always stopped at the People's Drug Store and got a pack of Chuckles on my way to school.  Now I can LOAD UP.
This one quart sprouting jar is perfect for sprouting a weeks worth of sprouts for two people nicely.

In my younger days I used to grow sprouts in between paper towels. I recently wanted to get back to doing my own sprouts, but really didnt wantto go the paper towel route again. I researched a few styles and purchased this sprouter. I am quite pleased with the ease. I agree with the first reviewer that the hulls will not come out with the lid on, but it isnt difficult to add water and gently swish the sprouts. The hulls will float to the top for you to discard. I have my second batch of sprouts under way. I like it and would recomend this product. (No chance of paper towels drying up while your at work, and no need to mess with cheesecloth).

I bought the sprouting jar with lid and the seeds.  Both the jar and the seeds came with instructions on how to grow sprouts.  One set of the instructions was vague, but the other set work well.  The seeds sprout well and require little attention other than rinsing and draining a couple times a day.  The instructions say that when the sprouts are ready you can fill the jar with water and the seed hulls will float out the lid - the openings in the lid are too small for this but I just put them in a bowl of water and they float to the top.  Otherwise great product and it works well.

I like this product, it grows sprouts well. It's a bit pricey considering you can buy the strainer lid seperately for around $4 and use it with any standard qt mason jar.Some have said that when using the separately bought strainer lid with their mason jars, it leaked at the threads.  The lid fits tight and snug on this product.Also, this jar is square shaped so it won't roll when set flat, unlike some older mason jars.I'm going to buy a sandwich blend of seeds, alfalfa alone is OK but not as peppy tasting for sandwiches. I suggest buyers order both alfalfa and a sandwich blend.Pressing a finger on the strainer lid gets the last remaining water out faster. A good draining is key to a good crop, it uncoats each seed of water and allows it to "breath."To de-husk my crop, I place a handful in a bowl of water and swish the crop around. Husks that rise to the top I scoop out along the side of the bowl, the remaining husks sink to the bottom. I lift out the sprouts and shake the water out or let drain on a plate.  I store in partially open plastic sandwich bags, they last longer if they can "breathe" a little.

I've just eaten my first batch of alfalfa sprouts from this sprouter.  I never knew what REAL/FRESH sprouts were supposed to taste like! They're delicious and they only took 4 days!  This is such an easy way to make your own sprouts.  The only gripe I have is that I bought it for DOUBLE the price at Whole Foods.  Next time, I'll do my research before buying elsewhere!

column9: Don't let  water in fast enough through the lid
column10: This sprounter jar was a little expensive for just being a plastic lid and glass canning jar.  The lid will be great for not rusting but the holes are small enough that the water was slow to go in for rinsing.  I don't want to have to take off the lid to rinse twice daily. I keep 5-7 jars going all the time in different stages of sprouting so I have at least one jar of sprouts ready to eat each day so I need to be fast at rinsing. I always sprout alfalfa seeds so could easily use larger holes anyway. I did get these Jars in a very short time after ordering so that was nice. I have a few lids that have stainless steel screens that fill really quick and rinse in a flash but still keep the seeds in. I like those lids better.

Sprouted successfully. The instructions say to have it on its side with the bottom tilted up a little so the water drains out the top. This is kinda awkward to arrange with the shape of the jar. I get good results just laying it flat on its side with a towel under it, but if you're worried about seeds rotting or bacteria growing in any pools of water (presumably this is why they want it tilted) just prop up the bottom with another folded towel or two for the right angle.

column9: Gently rinse and drain slowly, prevents mangled sprouts
column10: I finally figured out how to sprout, rinse and not get the seedlings all tangled up in a big mess.  After about 3 days of rinsing as directed, I see the seedlings beginning their growth orienting the leaves upwards, while the roots mat at the bottom. Then I gently rinse, gently tilt sideways to drain, so I don't distrub the growth orientation.  I end up with sprouts that are not tangled, but with clear leaves UP roots DOWN orientation, like you would by in them in wholefoods supermarket.Love the rinsing once daily, prevents rotting. Sprinkle after each rinse with seaweed fertilizer solution. Fantastic.
Just what I was looking for.  Had one of these years ago and lost it in a move.  So easy to make your own sprouts this way. Great to have FRESH sprouts again.

Sprouts have become the ANSWER to the freshest veggies I can find.  Grow my own, the entire family is involved in "watching the MIRACLE of the SWIFT GROWING WONDERFUL SPROUTS".Being able to GROW containers of our own FRESH SPROUTS every three to four days has been FANTASTIC!Honestly, it has been almost an IMPOSSIBLE task to find FRESH, GREEN CRUNCHY, SPROUTS that are worth even buying, much less TASTE WONDERFUL !WE HAVE CHANGED OUR ENTIRE DIETS and gotten the entire family to eat "SPROUTS", we can grow, PLUS they have discovered that SPROUTS TASTE GOOD!  THANKS for the great product!PS:  The grocery bill went down too! It costs just a couple of pennies to grow sprouts!
the wide mouth jar allows for easy extraction of sproutsthe cap has very fine holes that does not allow for loss of small seeds (like alfalfa)very practical set up

This jar makes sprouting brown rice easy.  Just add rice, add water.. lightly shake.. drain water out.  Then let sit for about 8 hours.  Rinse and repeat.  After a day or two you have perfect sprouted brown rice. I never had a problem with mold.Pricing seems to have been adjusted to include S&H.  I originally paid $10.95 for the jar itself and the shipping was insane.. $6.99!!!  Now it looks like they just bundled the costs and say "free shipping" when in fact they just padded the price to include the shipping cost!)

When I first tried this product I used a tablespoon of seeds.  Much too much for the container, but I got some excellent sprouts following the directions.  Next time I used a teaspoon but forgot to drain them thoroughly and ended up with spoiled sprouts.  As long as you follow the directions and use less than a tablespoon of seeds, the results should be rewarding.

column9: Great for making your own sprouts
column10: This is an awesome kit for making your own sprouts.I've made three batches, and they are all great - excited to try more than just alfalfa!

column9: Exactly what I was looking for!!
column10: The perfect sprouting jar.  Can't get sprouts any fresher than growing them yourself at home.  Highly recommended.  Company has several great ideas for all sprouting needs.

At first my jar did not arrive and I let Amazon and the company know about it. The tracking said it was delivered but I never got it. The company not only made good on it, but threw in an extra jar which was very nice..no quesionts asked. I also got the seeds from the same company..big variety pack and have been really enjoying the sprouts. I eat lots of salads and they are a good addition. The jars are sturdy, work good and the sprouts grow pretty fast. They also throw in a big bag of alfalfa seeds. If you like to be healthy and eat well, would recommend.JanLos Angeles

For those of us who like to grow things, it's hard to wait for planting season. This makes waiting a little easier. This sprouting jar allows you to grow a portion of your own food. You don't even really need this jar, however. You can get the same results with a glass jar and a bit of cheesecloth. But this item comes with a package of organic alfalfa sprout seeds and sprouting instructions. I bought a couple of these as gifts for kids to use as learning tools, and I'm completely satisfied with the purchase.
Don't let the low price throw you off. I'm a chocolate junkie and this is one of the best (instant powder) hot chocolates that I have tasted.

This Carlos V chocolate drink mix is mostly CHOCOLATE with just a little sugar and vitamins added. It is an excellent "pick me up" and doesn't have all those corn ingredients. Two heaping teaspooons make about 1 cup of great hot chocolate; you just add boiling water to the powder and stir. You end up having about 12 carbs per cup, a little more if you add milk to cool it down. Shelf life is about 17 months. Everyone in our family, including kids, LOVE it! You can fix it hot or cold, in milk or water. The cannister is perfect.

column9: We know good chocolate when we taste it.
column10: My son and I are chocolate lovers and we do admit that this powder drink is the best.  I was looking for a chocolate powder mix that taste good, mix well with cold or hot milk, and inexpensive. I took my chances and bought it.  My son was the first to try it and he said this is not like the other powder mix that taste like it has a lot of sugar or you need to use more than three tablespoons to taste the chocolate. Most chocolate powder float at the top of the cup when mixed in cold milk. Not Nestle Carlos V Chocolate Dink mix. I pray this product continue to sell because I hate to try something new.
very chalky, does NOT dissole easily in cold beverages, and is not very chocolatey at all!

I have Not tasted It, I think Its comes from Mexico or something, when I bought It I was looking for something different more natural the closest I have found Is Ghirardelli and even Its Not very good It does Not taste as good as Nestle hot chocolate but does Not have all that unknown stuff which may be made from Animals with mad cow disease but still have to microwave It to kill the bacteria. My yellow lab that was always hungry and a scavenger just like My Cat tore open a can and died a few hours later, I do Not understand It I have had Dogs and Cats before and Never had a problem feeding Them.
The first order of Pig Ears were large (4x6" average) and thick, but my second order of Pig Ears are half the size and thin.  Definitely, a lower quality.

Currently I have a five months old bichon frise. When I first got him as a puppy, I thought I picked out the best food for him, Blue Buffalo at Petsmart. However, when I got home, I did more research and found Orijen. As owners of bichons, or malteses, or poodles know, they tend to have problems with tear staining because of their white fur. Since I already got him Blue Buffalo, I thought I'll finish it before switching. Because of the tomato pomace (it's the leftover tomato seed, pulp, and skin) in the ingredients list, he had tear staining problems. I did nightly cleanings of his eyes, but it was still noticeable.Now it's been a month since Orijen Puppy, and I just realized that it's been a few weeks since I had to clean his eyes. Even my friends who visit us constantly commented on just how clean and bright his eyes look.Besides helping with the tear staining, Orijen is an all-around great food. I've also noticed his coat has a sheen to it. His poops are solid, not too soft or hard. He loves it, gobbles it down each time. I am extremely excited about feeding him this awesome food! And I will whole-heartedly recommend this dog food to anyone. It's totally worth it.

dogfoodanalysis dot com rates all Orijen dog foods 6 out of 6. I had been feeding my puppy Natural Balance Organic Formula (no dairy, only one meat source), but after discovering that it was only rated a 4, I started looking into higher quality foods. Switching was super easy, my puppy loves Orijen. Since she's been on Orijen, I haven't noticed any smelly breath like she used to have, and her poop doesn't stink! I know it sounds crazy, I had read that in reviews about this food before, and could barely believe it but it's true. Orijen puppy has 10 total meat ingredients (it's 75% meat!), including fish, and no grains, which are not part of a wild dog's diet, instead having a good range of fruits and vegetables, as well as vitamins, minerals, and probiotics. All the ingredients Orijen uses are very high quality and their meat sources are closely monitored and sustainable. I've heard some people say that Orijen formulas are too rich for their dogs, so maybe don't try to switch from any really low end stuff. It is a high protein, low carb food, meant to mimic a wild dog's natural diet. I think this is about as close as you can get to that with a dry formula.The only cons I can think of is that it's hard to find, there's only one place I can find that carries it locally (I live in the suburbs of Detroit, lots of pet supply stores...) and it costs $40 for the 15.4 lb bag there. The lowest I've seen it online was for 34.99, but with high shipping. But, I feel that providing premium food for my dog will ultimately save on vet bills later and improve quality of life for her, so I don't mind the cost so much.Also, just FYI, Orijen does do a frequent buyer's program, after you buy 12 bags you get the 13th free. The local store I buy it from set me up, you have to keep receipts and the barcodes from the bags and it has to be the same size bag every time, but I don't think it has to be the same formula. It's kind of strict but I think it's going to be worth it by the time I need that 13th bag.

I bought a Toy Poodle last summer and found that he was getting really dry/flaky skin.  I was given some no-name food from the breeder and my vet suggested this may be the problem.  After recommendations and a search for the best dog food--I finally found it!  My boy absolutely loves it and his itchy skin was gone.  His coat is so much softer and shinier now.  I recently switched to Orijen Regional Red and he loves it even MORE!  If you can get a hold of some of that stuff I suggest you do.  It is a little pricier than the other Orijen formulas but I can almost guarantee your dog will love it.  Every time one of his puppy pals are over they're always sniffing and licking his empty bowl.  Worth every penny!

column9: AWESOME DOG FOOD FOR SALIVA/TEAR STAINS!
column10: I have a pure white, 2lb, 5 month old, Morkie(maltese/yorkie mix).  We were having problems with staining around her mouth, feet, and HORRIBLE tear stains.  She was also constipated one day and then had toothpaste texture poo the next on her old dog food.(diamond puppy).  After a lot of research I decided to try Orijen Puppy.  AMAZING!! NO MORE SALIVA OR TEAR STAINS!! I can not tell you how much better she looks! her coat is even softer! as for her bowls, they are a nice, round, and firm.  She seems much happier and is a lot more active on this food than on her old food.  I was worried about the price at first, but with these results i would pay more!  I think ANYONE who owns a white dog and is having problems with the staining should give it a try! There is no fillers or Tomato Pumace, which is believed to cause staining in Maltese dogs.  I would give 10 stars if i could!!

So far, so good. I switched to Orijen Puppy after much research.  I didn't want to do the raw food thing, so I thought Orijen would be the next best thing. Previously I was feeding my pup Blue Buffalo and wasn't having any problems.  I am now feeding 50/50 Orijen and Blue Buffalo to use up my stock of Blue Buffalo.  He loves the food but I honestly don't think he's too picky.  No issues and he seems happy.  I was a little concerned about the high protein content, particularly with the poster claiming liver damage to his dogs, but it appears he isn't a legitimate poster.  He posts that claim on every Orijen product and all over the net...no details and no follow-up.

We are currently switching our 5 month old Basenji from Wellness brand to Orijen puppy food and the little guy is actually picking out the Orijen and leaving the Wellness (we are mixing it to make the transition easier). Its nice to know that such a healthy dog food is also so palatable!

column9: Our Frenchies love Orijen Puppy Formula
column10: We transitioned over to Orijen Puppy after getting a new pup and doing much research. Our 2 yr old Bella was eating not-so-good wet food, but loved Orijen instantly. Our puppy (now 6 months) loves it too. Bella has a lot less dandruff now, they also have less waste, but boy are they gasssssy! Gas has always been a problem with our Frenchies, but it is very common with this breed too. So, we are still very happy that we are feeding them the best food possible and their coat is beautiful, and less waste to pick up.

When I first got my Shiba Inu puppy, I put him on this kibble. He liked it and had no health problems from eating it, except one which didn't bother him much, but made life hell for myself & my wife. While eating this food, the puppy would release huge, terribly smelling dog farts. He did this with alarming regularity, every 20-30 minutes my wife & I would look at each other, sniff the air, then promptly evacuate the room to escape an invisible cloud of deadly (DEADLY!) gas wafting over from the dog's direction.The puppy, being a dog, would usually follow us to wherever we ended up, only to administer another dose of the stench 30 minutes later. And so went the round robin, with all 3 of us changing the room we occupied twice an hour.We endured 3 weeks of this before switching to Wellness dry kibble which made the farting problem go away. The Wellness food is slightly worse as far as ingredient quality goes, but it's still very good so we're ok with using it.I'm still rating Orijen puppy food at 4 stars based on the ingredients, which are excellent. While on it, other than farting, the dog was happy and looked great, no problems with stool or health. So I'm not saying that this food is bad - in fact, I think it's one of the better ones out there. I am saying that every dog is different (surprise, surprise!) and that if you do decide to buy Orijen, start with the smallest bag to determine it works for you before committing to a bigger one. I now have about 13lbs of Orijen dog food left and no idea what to do with it.Actually, now that I write this, I know what to do with it. I'll ask a friend to watch my dog at their home for a few days next time we go on vacation, and provide him with Orijen puppy food. Then ask him how things went. Cruel, I know, but oh so funny!

This is good. My puppy needs the best. This is pretty good. High in protein, good ingredients. Although I have a picky eater so he stopped eating it after a month. I had this and tried large breed but large puppy breed pieces are too large for my puppy. It smells like meat. A little dry.

column9: Puppy's coat shines on this food
column10: Pros:- I feed less of this food than Taste of the Wild (15 lb bag typically lasts 1 month + 1 week)- Puppy maintains healthy weight- Puppy is more alert and active- Puppy's coat thrives on this food- Has magically rid my puppy of his doggie smell- Bag is vacuumed up so the food stays fresh- Kibble size is just right for a medium breed puppyCons:- The price is excruciatingly high for a dog food- Puppy produces exceptionally loose and smelly stools- Horrendous, paint-peeling gas

We have a 7 month old Havanese who has a very sensitive stomach.  He came to us with Royal Canin indoor puppy but he was scratching constantly.  I got him some generic puppy food thinking dog food is dog food right?  Wrong!  He ate it and liked it but about a week later had diarrhea.  We didnt know it was the food at first, but after reading the ingredients realized it was the corn in it causing his reaction.  I then began to do research and switched him to Nutro small bites with chicken meal, rice and oatmeal, also a bad idea.  He didnt even eat it, I mixed it with some chicken broth, which helped, but then the diarrhea returned.  So, I finally found Orijen!  I wish I had just gotten it in the first place.  He loves it and always begs for more although we don't give in because I dont want to over feed him.  But, there is no more itching, his poop is firm and round and since we're not feeding him as much now, the cost is not a factor.  I would definitely recommend this food to everyone.

column9: Great food, but gave my puppy terrible gas.
column10: Researched puppy chows before adopting our Bassador and loved the mix of ingredients in Orijen. Unfortunately it gave our puppy terrible TERRIBLE gas. We were able to quickly identify that the food was behind the gas issue. We switched it up to Wellness 3 days later and the lethal gas is resolving. Still believe Orijen is a great product, just not for our puppy.
My 9 month old loves this food and he is picky! Wag.com gets it to me the very next day after I purchase it. Wag.com you are WONDERFUL!

This product is very healthy for my puppy.  No worries about poision from another country like what happened in other dog foods.It contains everything my dog needs.  I hope Canada keeps up it's excellent work and does not ship any of its products overseas where standards are so low, cheap labor  and they jail people that tell the truth about their horrible products.

Found this on a consumer report website and it had the best reviews.  The ingredients are great and it's one of the best foods out there, but my dog just loves the food he was raised on, his royal canin puppy formula.  Maybe it's the smell and the shape?  Anyway, I swap back and fourth when the bags run out so he's happy and I'm happy :)

Our rescue puppy was being fed Pro Plan and we switched to raw green tripe mixed with Orijen regular puppy food.  (We have had him for 3 weeks now.)He is doing very well on this mix.Energetic, firm stools, nice coat and overall health is excellent.So far, so good.(Note, one half of his diet is raw meat and bones.  Right now, green tripe the most raw meat, followed by beef neck bones and turkey necks.)ETA:  Oh, I forgot to say he is a Border Collie/Golden Retriever/GSD mix.  He is 3 months old and weighs 15 to 20lbs.

I slowly transitioned my pup to Orijen over a period of 2 months and she is now on Orijen completely. She is presently losing her teeth (she is 5 months old to date) and she seems to be swallowing the Orijen kibbles instead of chewing them. The Orijen kibbles seem harder than her previous dry puppy food but comes out in her poop appearing digested (even at present as she swallows them) compared to the old puppy food which still appeared like round kibbles in her poop. Her coat looks great and her poop is softer yet formed. Her poop does not stink with the bad smell it had with her previous puppy food product although it does have a quite distinct smell since being on Orijen. She has also been passing gas with the same distinct smell but I do not mind this at all. I am guessing that it probably is because of protein by-products. I am very pleased with this product.

This is an excellent dog food.  When I switched my Labradoodle puppy over to Orijen she had no problem whatsoever digesting it.  It is difficult to find this dog food at pet stores in my area.  However, when ordering on line, it is sometimes a long wait for your shipment due to this product's popularity.  A lot of pet supply websites are sold out.  So when you are somewhat near running out be sure to order ASAP as it may take some time to get it.

We have two rescues; a beautiful Carolina Dog and a hound mix.  They are thriving on this wonderful dry food.  The Carolina was very picky until I found Orijen....the hound has filled out and his coat shines!  I try to buy strictly "made in USA"...but this is a big exception!  Thank you Orijen!
I have a 4 month old German Shep / Rotty / Lab / Husky mix and he wasn't eating much food... 2 cups a day. Since I purchased this he eats up to 4 cups a day! He seems to love it. Shipped very fast!!!

column9: liver damage? I don't know about that, but stinky poo, gas and breath? yes
column10: this product has turned a pleasant smelling 5 month old puppy into a dog that smells worse septic tank. A few people have been claiming liver damage, I'd doubt that. Dogs do eat protein diets naturally, and there are a lot of disreputable vets out there. That said, something in this product is just not for my dog. A 35 pound bag was only $40, and I had been paying $16.99 for a 15 pound bag of that Beneful crap. So obviously the price was great. Furthermore, it appeared to be a high quality food--no bad fillers and REAL MEAT as the primary ingredients, and the reviews were all positive. The first four ingredients in the food are all named meat products. The first two of these are meat inclusive of water content (about 80%) and once that is removed it is likely that these ingredients would be more accurately placed somewhat further down the ingredient list (ingredients are listed in order of weight). However, since it is followed by two meat meal ingredient, our confidence in the meat content of the food is increased. We do note that this is followed by five grains, potatoes and tomato pomace ahead of the fat content, and this diminishes our confidence, making the food appear to be heavy in grain/carbohydrate content.There are further meat ingredients 14th and 15th on the ingredient list, though these are too far down to make up a substantive portion of the food.The main grains in the food are barley, rice (two forms), oatmeal and miller. These are low-allergenic and a good quality source of carbohydrates and additional protein. Potatoes are a further carbohydrate and protein source. Flaxseed is a good quality source of Omega 6 and Omega 3 essential fatty acids and the food contains a nice range of fruits and vegetables. We would prefer to see the use of whole eggs rather than egg product in the food.The manufacturer is guaranteeing the use of ethoxyquin-free meat and fish sources in their foods and a statement to that effect has been placed on the front page of their website.Overall this is a great food! However, these high quality foods such as Orijen Adult Formula Dry Dog Food or Acana Provincial Prairie Harvest Grain Free Dry Dog Food or Blue Buffalo Adult Dog Dry Food, Chicken and Rice Recipe, 15-Pound Bag are better for your pet.

column9: Easy to use and okay flavor, but expen$ive
column10: I was looking for a Jello-type mix that was sugar-free and did not use aspartame, as most mixes do, because I cannot tolerate it. Since this was sweetened with Splenda, which I can tolerate fine, I bought it to try. Although it uses both natural and artificial flavors, I was pleasantly surprised to see that it uses mostly natural ingredients, including natural colors. There is no aspartame in it; the sweeteners are sucralose (Splenda) and acesulfame K. The package makes two half-cup servings at 20 calories/7 g carb each.I used the first package to make a diet drink from another cookbook. Although the package directions call for dissolving the package in a cup of boiling water and NOT adding ice or cold water, the mix dissolved easily in a half-cup of boiling water and I was able to add the other ingredients.The main drawbacks are the package size (2-serving instead of the 4-serving common package, which means you have to remember to use 2 of these packages when 1 is called for in recipes), price, and that the flavor isn't very strong. While the flavor was acceptable when made as directed, when I had to add a little more ice to the drink recipe, it noticeably diluted the strawberry flavor. At $1.50/pkg when purchased in this order of 10, two packages are about triple the price of a single comparable 4-serving aspartame-containing mix at the store. But as an occasional treat to help me achieve my weight-loss goal, I will be keeping it around.

column9: Good but not as memorable as I'd anticipated.
column10: I am not a coffee snob. I am, however, a former barista who appreciates coffee that has been properly roasted ground and brewed. When I have company I often am complimented on what a good cup of coffee I've served and delight in explaining to my guests that my secret is fresh, coarse ground beans and a french press. That said I do like Starbucks' Breakfast Blend quite a bit though I prefer medium roasts and have recently discovered an excellent fair trade store brand Columbian that is divine.Unless I am in the mood for a coffee treat (think Caramel Frappucinos) or a home brewed cappucino I only drink my coffee black. I've loved the smell and taste of coffee since I was far too young to be drinking it so when I drink it I want to taste coffee, not sugar and dairy. A badly made cup of coffee is downright depressing. I won't drink percolated coffee unless there is nothing else available because it tends to destroy the oils in coffee beans that give them a smooth flavor. Same with overly roasted beans. But I'm getting off subject here...What did I think of Melitta Cafe Collection's Blanc et Noir?The first thing I noticed when I opened the bag was that I wasn't instantly hit with its scent. Half of what I love about making coffee is what I like to think of as the foreplay... that enticing odor teasing me when I open up the bag! Okay, I guess I can live without it. As this is a very finely ground blend I chose to prepare it as espresso. I would not recommend this coffee to those who use a french press (course ground is best when using that method) as you will end up drinking a LOT of the powdery grind that passes through the mesh of your press which for some can cause digestive upsets and for others is just gross. I did not try percolating it but I'm certain others who will review this product will use that method so check out what they thought if you'd like to know.I tried Blanc et Noir both as my preferred cuppa, black, and with steamed milk, as a latte. I was expecting a much stronger flavor for such a beautiful dark brew. As a stand-alone cup of black coffee it wasn't overly memorable. Smooth without the bitterness darker roasts often have or the acidic bite of lighter roasts. It sounds good in theory but by combining the two they somehow loose what makes each special. Which is why I tried it with some steamed milk and a little foam as well. I must say that if you like milk in your coffee this is a lovely coffee to pair with it. Unlike traditional espresso which is a dark roast, the added light roast just gave it something I can't seem to find the right word for.While I don't think Blanc et Noir is one I'd choose for brewing at home given other options I would definitely request it if it were being offered at a coffee house I was patronizing.

I'm not a coffee connoisseur but I do drink a lot of it and I have a definite idea of the type of coffee I like and what tastes good. So, based on my limited palate, I can say that there are some things I like about this coffee and some things I don't. This is a medium sort of brew that is neither too strong or too mild and this makes it easy to drink. It's also easy to drink because there is no bitterness or harshness. The downside of this coffee is that there isn't much flavor. It's a sort of bland coffee without much substance "in the middle." I can see this coffee being used in an office or during the day when the caffeine effect is more important than the flavor. The only downside to this is that it's a bit pricey for an everyday drink at an office.

This is a dark, fullbodied, rich, satisfying coffee.  It isn't bitter either, which is nice since alot of plain coffees I have tried tend to be bitter.  My preference is flavored coffee, but I did enjoy this coffee.I have used Melitta coffee filters before.  Now I will be on the lookout for their coffees.  The price is also reasonable.I think this is a good, everyday coffee, suitable for family and friends.

My usual coffee is a dark French roast from New England Coffee Co; I buy it ground, make it a bit strong and use it up before it loses its freshness. Like anyone else who appreciates coffee, I don't want any bitter or burned taste in my brew.This Blanc et Noir ground coffee from Melitta is a blend of light and dark roasts, so I thought it might taste bland. I was pleasantly surprised that it has such a good flavor, though I did need to make it stronger than the package directions recommend to enjoy it fully. Thankfully, making it stronger didn't introduce any bitterness to the flavor. This is a pleasant coffee. I brewed it in a basket-style electric drip pot, which is all I have available at the moment. I don't usually mind if my coffee cools a bit in the cup--don't need it piping hot to enjoy it--but I found this Melitta coffee to be far more flavorful at a just-poured temperature.I probably won't give up my usual coffee for this product, but I'd certainly buy it above other brands when I can't get my preferred New England coffee; that's an eventuality I have to prepare for, since I don't live in New England any more!Linda Bulger, 2010

I am a Folders Classic Roast kind of girl, I can't tell you the exact notes that I am picking up when I drink Melitta's Blanc Noir coffee - all I can tell you is that it's pretty good, not great, just pretty good.  I have been fiddling with the exact measurements, thinking that you have to use slightly more then you usually would when making a pot, but be careful not to use too much since it tends to taste "burned" or over roasted when you use too much.Also, for some reason, flavored coffee creamer seems to be intensified with this coffee blend so do not use too much.  I know, it sounds weird, but that has been my experience.With the name that Melitta has given this product, I was thinking that it would have had a more dominate flavor.  It just was not that way for me.  Back to my Folgers.

So many brews, so little time.  First, like with many of the cheaper brands, the bag doesn't open easily- tends to rip. It, of course, has little flaps to close it up.Once opened, it produces a deep and rich smell- for those who simply enjoy, can I say, the bouquet of coffee.  Tastewise-what can I say?  People prefer different brands for different reasons.  For the most part, one knows immediately if this cup suits them. This one is nothing stellar at least not in our house.  At least it wasn't bitter or burnt tasting.Definitely will drink if nothing else left in cupboard.  Not bad, but simply, not our cup of coffee.

column9: It's coffee, nothing wonderful, nothing bad.
column10: I am not a coffee drinker, but my wife is so I got this for her. She likes her starbucks and she'll drink the McDonalds version coffee.Her overall impression of this was it was ok. She wasn't overly impressed with it. I will say that from my non-coffee drinking point of view, when I received this the fresh scent of coffee was very overpowering compared to most bags of coffee I have ever touched. It smelled very fresh.The overall impression however of the taste, it was decent. Not a high end, and not something that will make you want to pour it down the drain. It's just a basic coffee that you could drink every morning.

I used this coffee this  morning.  The kitchen smelled good even when I'd just opened the package and even better.....actually wonderful....while it was brewing.  Great taste. In fact, I think I'll go make another pot right now.  Highly recommended.

Not too intense,  very good coffee.We usually grind our own but I couldn't tell the difference with this.Good enough and smooth enough to drink black even if you're used to adulterations.The price is not available so I don't know whether I could afford to use this for every day coffee or not. I would if I could.

Now it's possible to have coffee shop flavor at home. Melitta Blanc et Noir is full of enticing aroma and smooth, rich flavor. We've been grinding beans at home up till now, but this ground coffee product is the first we've tried that is satisfying in every way, and doesn't turn bitter with time after the package is opened. Highly recommended.

This is a very strong, robust coffee that can be overwhelming if your taste buds prefer a more mild flavor. However, my husband adored the flavor. He loves a 'hardy' coffee and often makes it so strong I think my eyes will pop! Whether or not my enamel remains on my teeth depends on who reaches the coffee maker first in the morning. So, if you are like my hubby and love an extra robust flavor and want to fill your house with that grand, eye-popping coffee smell, this particular blend of Melitta Cafe is for you. If your tongue needs to adjust in the early morning and you tend to even out the taste of the beans with milk, I recommend a milder blend.

column9: Not as bold as expected, but very smooth.
column10: We used this in our Keurig and were delighted.  I think my husband was expecting it to be stronger and bolder, which is why it is getting 4 out of 5 stars.  For me, it was perfect, but he was hoping for something to slap him in the face!  I am a "lots of cream and sugar" coffee drinker, and I used about half as much cream as I normally do.  The coffee is amazingly smooth, so I just didn't need as much.  My husband drinks coffee with nothing in it, or just a small sprinkle of sugar and he also enjoyed it by itself.  I think this may be making a regular appearance in our cupboard!

When roasting coffee, there is always a decision on how far to go.  Too little does not develop the nuanced coffee flavor but gives a solid drink, too much yields acrid, bitter blechh so common in certain national chains.  Melitta has addressed this dilemma by including both horns, a well-roasted Noir, and substantial body from the so-called Blanc (medium roast).  What you get is a very drinkable blend without the harsh overtones which have been modulated by the lighter roast.  Of course, being a pre-ground blend, it is important to store properly after opening to maintain this flavor balance.

I don't consider myself a coffee "connoiseur", but I do know what I like and don't like.Typically, I start my day with a glass of coffee in a frapuccino-style drink, and may have another in the course of a day. I know; many of you are thinking, "Who cares what THIS guy thinks, the way he drinks coffee?"Well, even though I'm not a "purist", the coffee still makes or breaks that drink. Many of the dark roasts give me a very strong, bitter drink that I don't enjoy whatsoever. Other coffees are so bland that I end up with a slightly-colored milk drink of no particular character.I made the coffee as espresso in my Krup machine, then used it as the base for the drink. It came out of the espresso machine with the proper visual, a nice frothy top. Adding the other ingredients -- milk and sweetener -- I found the taste to be rich without bitterness, slightly complex, not at all over-roasted. I then added some Torani vanilla syrup, and thought it was quite delectable.I'd put this coffee on a par with Starbucks.One thing I'd like to point out. The product page discusses this being a "Pack of 3". I only received one bag of coffee. Now, I don't know whether this was due to the fact that I received the product through the Vine Program, and quantities were reduced because I got it for free for the purposes of reviewing it, or if there's actually some other issue like a shipping or printing error. I'm simply reporting my experience.Obviously, this has a big effect on the "value" of what you're buying for that price.

I'm pretty picky about my coffee. It has to be bold. Has to be smooth. Bitter is bad. Burned beans are bad. And hotel conference room coffee from the 100-cup percolator pot is generally the most vile thing on Earth. Little styrofoam cups filled with overheated pool chemicals and mop-bucket waste.In fact, if you've ever taken a sip of the latter and remarked "hmmm, not a bad cup of coffee!" then perhaps you shouldn't even consider the purchase of a premium blend, as you would simply be wasting your money. You've destroyed your taste buds and they probably wouldn't be able to appreciate the difference anyway.So I opened the little bag of Melitta with a healthy dose of skepticism. As it was available only ground (given a choice, I grind my own beans), I wondered if it could really be any good.Following the directions on the bag, we put eight teaspoons of coffee in our French press with 24 oz of water, added almost-boiling water, waited about 5 minutes and pushed the plunger. And?????It was quite a bit better than I expected it to be. No hint of bitterness, and low in acidity, it was a very smooth cup of coffee that was lacking in only one area. It wasn't as bold as I would have liked. Having said that, I must say that if a restaurant were to serve this, I'd be thrilled, as I find most restaurant coffee to be less-than-stellar.The Melitta is certainly not going to replace the coffee my wife and I have been purchasing exclusively for the last several years (Raven's Brew, which in my opinion, blows away Starbucks, and even Gevalia), but we'll definitely enjoy the next several pots. Although I may go a little bit 'heavier' on the coffee-to-water ratio next time.- Jonathan Sabin

My sack of Melitta coffee is labeled, "Extra fine grind, Blanc et Noir, Light & Dark Roast."  The sack, which is airtight until cut, and which contains a firm fastener, contains 312 grams of finely ground coffee.  This product, therefore, will be convenient for adults to brew their coffee early in the morning, without waking up the little ones with the loud grinding sound of grinding coffee beans.I prefer to brew strong coffee, and for this task, I used a brewing machine from Cuisinart.  This machine contains a fine metal filter, not a paper filter. The coffee had a convincing, rich flavor, with a slightly acidic taste.  At any rate, I found this product to provide a brew that was superior to that from Star*****.  I have discovered, with repeated samplings over several years, that Star***** coffee powder has the flavor of ashes from burned wood, or perhaps worse.  I do not think that the Melitta product can match Peet's coffee powder.  Once the Melitta bag is opened, the powder in the bag does not generate much  of an aroma.  In contrast, when a bag of Peet's ground coffee is first opened, it provides a dynamic symphony of aromas.This is about the history of the Melitta company. In 1908, Melitta Bentz, a housewife from Dresden, Germany invented the first coffee filter. On July 8, 1908, Melitta Bentz received a patent for her "Filter Top Device lined with Filter Paper" from the Patent Office in Berlin. The 35-year-old housewife was transformed into a businesswoman and, during the same year of her invention, the company bearing her name was established.  Melitta USA, headquartered in Clearwater, Florida is part of the privately held Melitta Group of Minden, Germany. Melitta USA is responsible for the sales and marketing of Melitta coffee filters, coffee, and non electric coffee systems in the USA.

column9: Well balanced, not bitter, substantial flavor
column10: Gotta start the day with a cup o' joe, so I put the Melitta Cafe Collection Blanc et Noir Ground Coffee through its paces. For those who care about such things, I brewed the coffee in an electric drip coffeemaker, using a non-bleached paper filter. I used 18 ounces of water (or three cups according to the coffee package) and approximately 2 teaspoons of coffee per cup as instructed on the package (plus my signature "one to grow on" teaspoon that always goes in for a little boost).When I poured the cup, I was pleased to see that the coffee was very dark. I drink my coffee black and I like it strong, so my ratio of water to coffee seemed right for me. I did notice that there wasn't as much aroma as I would have liked. What I did smell had that freshly brewed scent but it was subtle. The flavor was very balanced - not bitter like an overly roasted coffee (Sorry Starbucks) but not wishy washy like most grocery store blends. It was the kind of morning coffee that I enjoy, flavor without being too bold and in my face first thing. Not too much acid, but a bit of a zing. I guess that's why it is a blend of light and dark coffees, which seems to work well.My normal coffee is Gevalia Stockholm and this compared favorably. I thought it was tastier than my runner-up coffee (when I run out of Gevalia), Dunkin' Donuts. I would definitely purchase this blend and I'll recommend it to the coffee fiends in my family.

I really enjoy Melita's canned coffee, so I figured this collection would be a real treat. I absolutely hated this blend. This is entirely a matter of taste. I believe the actual quality of the coffee is acceptable, not great, and not bad. The description does not specify the blend to region or location. However this is most assuredly a Arabican blend.As I stated, this is a matter of individual taste. Personally I detest Arabica blends. They leave a strange earthy aftertaste that stays with you for hours. Had I known this was Arabica derived, I would not have purchased it. That information is entirely missing from the product description.From the quality and freshness of this blend (taste aside) I will not be purchasing any further Melitta coffees from this bagged collection. The coffee was nowhere near fresh, the grinds were excessively dry and somewhat stale.
This was a gift for my husband who drinks coffee every morning. (I do not drink coffee.) He says it is an excellent full bodied coffee that is strong but not bitter.

I enjoy coffee and drink 2-4 cups of the stuff a day. Im not a Cafe snob so im not going to pretend i know a lot about the Cafe subject. I bought a Melitta Coffee maker(a rebadged Hamilton Beach) and i figured hey why not try Melitta Coffee. I'm use to buying the Spanish Coffee (Bustello and Pilon). They both are Cuban Espresso blend. That stuff is fine however it is slightly bitter. This Blanc et Noir with light and dark blends is wonderful. There is almost no bitter taste in it all. The one thing with the Melitta coffee some of the "character" of the coffee seems to be subdued. Maybe a little to much, robbing the blend of much character or boldness. Seems like in a effort to make a smooth non-bitter coffee some of the characteristics of the coffee was subdued in the process. This isnt to say it has no flavor or character in it. It does, and i can detect the two different levels of the blends. I still enjoy the blend however i dont know where to purchase this locally. I live in a major city so im sure some store must carry it. The price of a individual bag itself isnt bad. A bag of Gevalia here retails for $9-$10, the Melitta is about $7-8 online. However once you factor in the shipping everything equals out. As it stands im not sure if willing to spend twice the amount of what i usually spend on a bag of Coffee. Maybe as a occasional treat i may order it.

Like a good bottle of scotch - a very rich and distinct flavor, yet as smooth as the day is long. There's no bitter or burnt aftertaste.  This is my favorite "everyday" coffee, and it is reasonably priced. What more could you ask for?

Like most people (I suspect) we tend to stick to the coffee we know and love.  Neither of us are what you might consider "coffee snobs" but we both have pretty strong feelings on what is good and bad coffee.  We lean toward stronger brews, but not too acidic.  Hidden flavors are a plus, but not required.  We seem to rotate between Starbucks (Yukon, Pike Place or Pike Place Reserve), Seattle's Best (Henry's Blend), Frederick's, Caffe Vita and El Diablo (on Queen Anne in Seattle!).  So when I was presented with this through the Vine program I was skeptical and was a little concerned and assumed I might be writing a not-so-favorable review, however that turned out to not be the case.  Here are my basic pros and cons:Pros:Bold and Flavorful, but not offensively so!  Other reviewers have called this "really strong" or "too bold" but I guess it all depends on what you drink.  Personally, we didn't find it so.  Starbucks has a penchant for burning their beans at times giving the coffee and almost acrid, acidic taste - even in the beans you purchase from the store.  This coffee was smooth, rich and good to the last drop.The bag itself was easy to open and reseal.  All too often I end up fighting open a new bag of coffee only to have it all over the counter.  Resealing the bag then requires magician's handy work.  Not so here.  Seems silly to critique the bag itself perhaps, but it's true!!Cons:No adventures here.  Don't expect hints of this or that, or nutty edge.  Not even sure this is a con!All in all, I'd buy this again and I'm glad I gave it a shot!

I do not know whether our product was out-dated, but my wife and I were both very disappointed in this brand of coffee. It had a bitter taste and simply wasn't what we had hoped. In comparison to other dark roast brands, I simply cannot recommend this one. We did not care for the flavor.

I am certainly not a coffee expert, though I have been drinking the stuff for 50 years or so.  Nor do I have any of this awesome coffee-making apparatus I see advertized.  I just have my trusty old Melitta drip coffee maker--put the coffee in a filter on the top and pour in your hot water. So, I am certainly no cafe gourmet.  I found this coffee to be quite good in brewing it up.  The coffee is very rich and dark and has a pleasant aroma, especially after you pour hot water on it. It can be too strong if you overdo it, but used in moderate amounts it generates quite a satisfying cup.  Otherwise, it is very easy to utilize even in my primitive equipment. It stores well also--I had my test batch in the fridge for several months and it was just as captivating when I pulled it out as when it first arrived. So, I guess the best term for this coffee is "moderately hearty" and quite pleasant.

column9: A Little Earthy but Still Pretty Good
column10: To be honest, I wasn't as taken with this blend as the others, but I think that has to do with my own taste buds. It's a bit too earthy for me. Still it's pretty good overall.

This ground coffee was pleasant - not over-roasted, not too weak. However, it's nothing remarkable - we're not talking particularly high-quality beans or a particularly fresh grind. Still, wouldn't make a bad pantry stocker for emergencies (if you're a coffee snob), or a gift for those who aren't really into coffee to begin with. Nothing against Melitta, they're a great brand, I just felt this wasn't quite up to snuff with their reputation.

Melitta Cafe COllection Blanc et Noir coffee has a very smooth, refined armoma you notice as soon as you open up the package. That same aroma translates well throughout the brewing process and remains once poured into your cup. Once you taste it, you will find that the flavor is bold yet smooth, it has a slightly dark, powerful flavor without any of the coarseness or bitterness. I went directly from one of those high-pressure coffee pod brewing systems to using the Melitta in a percolator, and it seems Melitta has helped me find my way back to a better cup of coffee.

Melitta is definitely a good blend of coffee, but it might be a bit too strong for those who prefer a milder flavor. The aroma is strong, which only serves to accentuate the excellence of it. You can't go wrong with Melitta if you prefer a strong coffee in the morning.

column9: A really nice, smooth coffee worth trying...
column10: We're not huge coffee drinkers so I'm by no means a connoisseur but I AM very picky and don't like a real harsh, bitter coffee.  I was really pleasantly surprised to find that this coffee had a really nice aroma to it and brewed up quite nicely.  Very smooth...no bite at all but quite mellow with a nice flavor.  I'd definitely buy this and think it's worth it for others to try it.

I like preground coffee just for the convenience, but I realize grinding your own beans just before brewing is going to be a lot better than the usual "coffee from a can".  These are vacuum sealed bags of preground coffee.  It's a great compromise as the coffee is pretty good on the taste front.  The  three bags are small enough that with regular use, you can go through a bag fairly quickly and then open the next vacuum sealed bag without fear of letting your coffee sit around too long exposed to air.  I use sugar and fair amount of cream in mine, so the flavor really has to stand out.

I've tried to capture the taste of really fine coffee I've experienced in some excellent restaurants without much success--including grinding my own beans, buying expensive ones at specialty shops, etc.  This product, while not quite doing justice to my memories of great coffee, comes closest.  It is somewhat expensive at about $9/lb.  Supermarket coffees are, of course, much cheaper--and you can get larger packages at discount places for much, much less.  I even tried mixing this coffee with Folgers--and it was pretty good too.  Naturally, this coffee is much richer so one needs to experiment a bit to figure out how much to use in your coffee maker.  I drink coffee straight up--no sweetener, no milk products, but I like it pretty strong--but not burnt or over-roasted.  This coffee is not over-roasted or bitter (unless you use too much of it).  I found it superior to the other Melitta products I've tried as well as to other much-vaunted brands such as Starbucks, Seattle's Best, and Gevalia.  But taste is on the tongue of the beholder...

column9: Not Bad, Just Not Anything Special
column10: Pretty good.  Nothing earth shattering though.  Maybe I don't have as keen a taste for coffee as I think I do, but this tastes like a lot of other "gourmet" brands to me.  Which is to say it's yummy, just not anything special.

column9: BETTER THAN I EXPECTED -- NICE AROMA
column10: Surprisingly mellow coffee with a lingering, embracing aroma that impressed my snobby visitors from England.  I recommend this for your snooty friends.
Rich, somewhat strong flavor.  Great aroma.I am a coffee drinker and I totally enjoyed it.Thank you.MEF

As I opened this package of coffee a wonderful aroma burst forth, strong and robust.  The coffee itself is finely ground, and a deep rich color.  I brewed the coffee in my usual drip style coffee maker.  The resulting coffee was rich, and full flavored but only slightly more so than my usual grocery store brand.

column9: A strong coffee with a wonderful aroma
column10: This coffee is a great way to start the day, though some may prefer a more mild blend. I truly enjoyed this coffee, however, because I love strong coffee, particularly strong coffee that fills the room with strong aroma. If you prefer a more mild coffee, this may not be for you. But if you are like me and want your coffee strong, then I highly recommend Melitta Cafe Noir Ground Coffee.

column9: Now my working day Thermos Coffee
column10: Generally I drink only home pressed espresso - and way too much of it - so for the past few months have been going with drip brewed coffee (except on weekends!) in an effort to cut down on the amount of caffeine I drink.This works, as I can make drip coffee weaker than espresso without it being too watery, whereas weak espresso is simply dreadful. Recall that "Caffè Americano" is espresso with hot water added to it to make it weak enough for our usual national preference, and is not the sort of coffee that I enjoy.Perhaps because it is so finely ground, I find myself using under half as much of this Melitta "Blanc et Noir" coffee as I had been using with my previous home ground mix for my drip brewer and still ending up with OK coffee.The "Blanc et Noir" also seems to be quite "smooth," though I do find myself adding about a third of a teaspoon of sugar per pint else it is slightly bitter - which seems characteristic of all pre-ground coffees.Though I did get a complementary bag of this coffee from Amazon for review (which is how I found out about it), I liked it well enough that I now have it as a regular order on my Amazon "Subscribe and Save" program.It is not great coffee, but it is good coffee. It is what I now take to work everyday for it is much better than that which I can get at the hospital, and, as am using less coffee to make it, it not only has further decreased my caffeine intake, but is cheaper as well.Disclaimer: This item was initially provided by Amazon to me for review.

When I first received the coffee I wondered how a mix of light and dark would be anything different than just a regular medium brew coffee.  After tasting it I was hooked.  It has the rich dark taste with any bitterness and a smooth finish.  Very comfortable to drink yet bold.

We spent some time living overseas and grew accustomed to the fine coffees and espresso so readily available. After moving back to the States, we've searched for comparable coffee, but nothing quite measures up.I've tried some of the other Melitta blends, and they've been...ok...but not spectacular. This Blanc et Noir blend, however, blew me away! It's strong without being the least bit bitter or acidic, rich with a full body. I don't know if/how the flavor may change while sitting on the shelf or in the fridge, because we drank this up so quickly. This is robust coffee for being a blend, and sipping it for breakfast gave me a little taste of Europe.

I'm not a coffee drinker, but my husband drinks a ton of coffee ... Starbucks, McDonald's, Dunkin' Donuts ... you name it, he's probably had a cup of it to drink.  Anyway, he usually buys the Dunkin' Donuts brand at the grocery store (because it tastes good and doesn't cost that much) and LOVES he Starbucks (which is a very expensive habit).  I had him try this one and he said that it tastes good (actually he said that it "taste expensive, but that it was good").  He finished the entire bag off in no time! :)

column9: Something to look forward to in the morning.
column10: I was surprised just how pleasing this coffee was beyond my regular brands. It's strong, but not too edgy, full of aroma and good taste and definitely something I'll be getting again.
I enjoyed this coffee. It was smooth and rich. A bit chalky if brewed too strong. 3.5

I openly admit to not being a coffee snob, with the amount of sugar and cream I add it would be hard to claim that I was very picky however I do have a few coffee's that I normally buy and like and tend to stick with medium blends. Prior to my last pregnancy I only used my french press but lately I'm back to the drip maker since its just faster and easier so I thought I'd give this pre-ground coffee a try.It's not bad. Granted it's not amazing either, it does have a bit stronger flavor then I'm used to but I expected that... thankfully it's just richer and not bitter which sometimes can happen with stronger coffees IMO. My mother was visiting and she prefers a very dark coffee but said that this one was acceptable (as someone who drinks her coffee black I figure she's a better judge then I am). So while I won't go out of my way to purchase this for myself it is a coffee I'd probably keep on hand for guests who like a stronger coffee.

Some coffees try to impress by including a particular strong added flavor or mixing in a variety of tastes so as to distract from the often bitter taste of the coffee itself.This Melitta Cafe doesn't do that.  Rather it has a very pure, direct and yes smooth taste that is surprisingly not bitter.  It is a coffee for those who enjoy sitting down with a hot beverage and enjoying the moment.  It does not grab your attention, but that's not what I'm looking for in a cup of coffee.The mix of dark and light roasts are very finely blended, and give the coffee a robust flavor, and a great, welcomed dose of caffeine.I'd definitely get this again.

column9: A little too weak for my taste
column10: Melitta European Roast Extra Dark is my daily coffee, so I should have known that this blend (Blanc et Noir) would be weaker than I'm used too.  If you don't like strong, dark, flavorful coffee, then Blanc et Noir may be a good fit for you, but if you like a little more "strength," you might like the European Roast Extra Dark.

WE MADE THIS IN THE DRIP COFFEE MAKER -- SO GOOD!WE MADE THIS IN THE FRENCH PRESS -- TASTEY AS EVER!WE MADE THIS IN OUR STOVE TOP ESPRESSO MAKER -- LICKED THE CUP!WE MADE THIS IN MY FATHER-IN-LAW'S $2,000 ESPRESSO MAKER -- WHOA MOMMA!IT WAS ALL SO VERY DELICIOUS AND NOW I AM SO CAFFEINATED I THINK MY HEART IS GOING TO EXPLODE.

I love coffee, and yet I'm not the type of person who distinguishes flavors and aromas generally coffee falls into one of two categories for me - good coffee and garbage coffee.  Good coffee is generally coffee you have to pay for, you get it at a resturant or at a coffee shop, or make it at home.  Garbage coffee is generally found free from your employer.This stuff falls under good coffee.  I like the scent, I love the taste, and since I love my coffee extra strong, I don't need as much of it as I generally do with store bought coffees.  I took the bag to a friends house and everyone there agreed that this was an exceptionally flavorful and enjoyable coffee.Now the packaging on the other hand... you're not getting that bag open without scissors.  If buying for people with arthitis go ahead and buy them some scissors too otherwise they will just sit and stare longingly at the bag.Final opinion - yes I would pay for this coffee, and yes I enjoyed the entire bag of it - 4 stars

This is really delicious coffee that I would recommend and buy again.  The rich aroma as it brews lets you know you're in for an excellent cup of java.  The flavor is deep and robust, a great way to start the morning.

column9: Nice mix of coffees for the days you want something "different".
column10: I love dark roast coffee. There is nothing better than the smell, feel, and flavor of a good dark roast. Unfortunately, a lot of places thing "dark" means "burnt". After I've had some bad "dark" roast coffee, it is nice to have something a little mellower. Melitta Cafe Collection Blanc et Noir fills in nicely for those times.The flavor is not light roast, or dark roast. I wouldn't even really say it is somewhere in between. It is definitely not a "Medium Roast" like the Maxwell house some reviewers have likened it to.While this will not be replacing my dark roast anytime soon, Melitta Cafe Collection Blanc et Noir has earned its place in my pantry for those times when I just want something different. Not light, not dark, but somehow both.

column9: Just a good coffee - nothing spectacular
column10: We typically buy our coffee from Trader Joe's - it's economical, tasty and you can grind it fresh at the store. But we thought we'd check out this coffee from the German Melitta Group. It's got a good, strong flavor but there's really nothing especially memorable about it. If you're looking for a good coffee, there's really nothing to object to here - but there's also nothing to boast about. It's straight-up coffee. It's also surprisingly fresh for being pre-ground which is nice.As a side note, it's certified Kosher. I would think that most coffee would be Kosher, but after a little research it appears that's not something you can assume. So, if you're looking for a Kosher coffee - check this one out.

My wife and I really enjoy a strong cup of coffee. This Melitta Cafe Blanc et Noir ground coffee fits our requirement perfectly. I will admit that very few exotic coffees have the ability to satisfy our taste buds. But this one does. It's rich smooth flavor and deep roasted taste is on the stronger side. I don't ever want to be able to see the bottom of my filled coffee mug. I love the taste and it has no bitter after taste. Great coffee!!
Didn't think this coffee was good or bad- just blah.  So, if it's on sale, grab it if you need cheap coffee for days when you don't demand good taste while getting your caffeine dose.

This coffee was very good at breakfast, it is low acid and brewed up in our Hamilton Beach drip machine nicely. I gave it a 4 star instead of 5 because it is a very fine grind, probably closer to an espresso grind than a drip but the description doesn't say that. It did work in the drip machine. I found that the best way to get a not to strong cup of coffee was to measure one teaspoon of coffee grounds less per cup then I normally would. Once I did that it made a very fine pot of coffee.

column9: Nice, smooth, medium-bodied cup of coffee
column10: My husband and I enjoy trying various flavors/types of coffee, although we tend to prefer lighter roasts--"breakfast blend" varieties are some of our favorites.  However, Melitta's Blanc et Noir professed to be a combination of both light and dark roasts, so I decided to take a chance on the idea that it in the balance, it would not be too dark for us.Turns out that I was right--the mix of light and dark roasts does produce a more medium-bodied coffee.  We found the end result (made in our drip coffee maker) to rich and smooth without being bitter.  However, I can't say that the flavor was particularly remarkable or notable; it was simply a good, decent cup of coffee.  Furthermore, although I realize that the extra fine grind is supposed to be an advantage, it means that we cannot use this coffee in our French press, which we use occasionally as an alternate to our drip coffee maker.In the end, this makes a nice cup of coffee, but I'm not sure that I'd choose to buy it on my own, mainly because there are other products that I prefer.

This is one of the best coffees I've had. It's smooth, rich, and full-bodied. You can brew it up very strong without bitterness or any unpleasant aftertaste. It takes cream and sugar well, but those of us who like our coffee black will enjoy the flavor.It's very finely ground, and quite delicious.

I am not sure what the rationale is for combining dark and light roast coffees, as the result you get is neither fish, flesh, fowl nor good red herring, but something akin to . . . well, Maxwell House.I have nothing against Maxwell House, I made and drank a lot of it in my younger days as a soda jerk, but we've moved on. Distinctive coffees are the thing now.My terms of reference are high, since I live on Maui, where I have easy access to Kona coffee, still the very best, and a selection of estate-grown Maui and Molokai coffees that are good but not quite as good. (You may never have tasted Kona, even if you paid for it; one of the big chains for years sold more coffee as Kona than Kona ever produced.)I was also not a fan of the very fine grind of this coffee, which the producer claims helps bring out the full flavor. Not necessary, and I ended up having to use two Melitta filters to keep sediment out of my cup.

I thought this coffee was very good, but I drink lattes and tea more than regular coffee, so I don't necessarily trust my judgment.  As a result, I shared it with a coffee-loving colleague at work.  He brewed a pot and came back with these comments:  "The coffee is just as yum as I remember it. I made it espresso-style today.  Melitta coffee reminds me of a morning kitchen in Germany: making coffee, slicing bread and cheese, and preparing all the jams. As it's brewing, Melitta smells like coffee should smell - none of the burning scent you often get with other coffees. As for the flavor, it is dark, rich and bold yet smooth with only a slight bitter after-taste, which I actually like. I highly recommend it, especially if you're used to Folgers or other more commercial brands."

Disclaimer: I am reviewing a bag that I received for free through the Vine program.It's OK, decent, not remarkable. I usually prefer dark roast, and this one is a mixed blend of dark and lighter roasts, so it's not as dark as I like it. And I usually prefer to grind my own beans, at least at home. But for a bag of pre-ground coffee that you can mail order, it's not bad. I don't know if that makes it competitive, price-wise.

My first try at a mixed blend.  The aroma is good and taste is fine.  But what is not here is much character.  It does not make for a memorable cup.  So as others have said it's good but not great.  Melitta's Columbian may be a much better place if you are new to this brand.

In the interest of being objective I must first state that I am fond of at least two other Melitta products: The European Roast and Melitta's unbleached #2 filter cones. I'm not one usually taken by fru-fru coffees, so I wasn't expecting much before trying Blanc et Noir. But I was most surprised at the taste - midway between my usual Melitta dark roast and most-favored chocolate Vietnamese #1. This is an interesting blend that will satisfy. I just wish that manufacturers would still with an honest pound, instead of manipulating ounce measurements to extract profitability - this coffee comes in slightly over 11-ounce bags.
This coffee is good, it's just a little strong for the strength I usually drink!

I am a coffee snob of sorts. When I received this "Blanc et Noir" coffee from Melitta, I was ready to be underwhelmed. I was totally positively surprised! The very tightly sealed package kept the pre-ground coffee fresh until opening. The fine grind is suitable for cone and similar drip coffee makers. My normal brew is Peet's dark roast (French, Italian Espresso, etc.) and so I added a bit more coffee to test out the B&E blend. It came out full, rich and smooth. It is definitely a medium by my taste, but it is not a wimpy tasting coffee. it has a full and rich coffee flavor without being bitter or burnt tasting.Now if you really, really like the off the charts dark roast coffee, this is not the one for you. I am still likely to buy a lot more Peet's in my life. However, I will probably also get some more Melitta as a result of this test because it is a very satisfying coffee to have with breakfast or other food. It is strong enough that I still feel like I've had coffee, but not so strong that I am finishing the whole pot myself due to elimination of all other takers. In other words, you can serve it for a mixed taste crew of coffee drinkers and everyone is likely to be satisfied to one extent or another. In fact, the majority (I think I am fringe) are going to be actually impressed.One note: You have to cut the top of the package to open it. It will not just pull apart like many vacuum packed coffee bags. If you cut the package just between the wire re-sealing closure and the seal at the top of the bag, you should be fine with it.

If you're a fan of darker roasts, there's not much to dislike about "Blanc et Noir" from Melitta -- not much that I could detect, anyway. On the other hand, there wasn't a lot to set it apart from other similarly-priced dark roasts on the market. It is a perfectly serviceable coffee I was happy to have in my rotation for a week or two. But it won't displace, say, the coffee I brought back from a recent Hawaii vacation as my weekends-and-special-occasions choice, nor did it evoke all the memories of European cafes the marketing promised. But as I said, it's not a bad choice by any means if darker beans are your thing.
A good, smooth coffee. While better than many brands, it still isn't as good as regular Chock Full o Nuts and certainly not worth the price. In my opinion, anyway.

column9: Smooth taste, no bitterness or 'burnt' aftertaste.  Very finely ground.
column10: I was wary of this coffee before I first brewed some, because I usually find that anything described as a 'dark roast' has a bitter taste to it.  But I really liked this blend -- it makes a fairly dark coffee, but I couldn't taste a trace of bitterness or a "burnt" flavor.  Maybe that is because it is blended with a mild roast?  Who knows.  Anyway, I would definitely buy this again...makes a great morning cup of coffee: strong but not bitter.Note: It is very finely ground, so you may actually want to use a bit less of it than with regular ground coffee.  Also, it would NOT work in a French Press coffee maker (which needs a course grind).

Rating a coffee product is difficult because it's so highly personal.  This produces a pleasant cup, something I would not hesitate to serve to anyone.  Why four stars? I have a rather acute reaction to anything approaching a bitter taste -- and I found that this has the slightly bitter aftertaste one finds in many French roasts.
