I found that I could only fit around half a potato (diced) at a time. This wasn't a big issue for me because it only takes around 5-6 minutes for the steam to be done. But there were times that I used the traditional steamer basket/pot to steam 2-3 whole potatoes at once (for the freezer) and used the beaba blender to puree.* STAINS - the plastic material is a bit porous so you will see stains (especially from carrots and beets). The plastic steam basket will DEFINITELY stain. Mine is an orangey-color, from the carrots and sweet potatos.* EXPENSIVE - it is quite costly and it's really hard to find these on sale. If you plan on using it for one kid, I would reconsider. If you plan on using it for more than one kid, might be worth the investment.Overall, I'm very glad I made the purchase. Not only is it functional, it looks super cute on your kitchen counter. And makes the baby food making process that much more "fun".

column9: Great for full-time baby food makers!
column10: So some of the reviews will scare you to death, but let me tell you, this is a GOOD device! As with everything, you have to clean it. It's easy, pour white vinegar in and let it rest overnight.This cooker does everything but EAT the food that you have made. (and it might do that, I just haven't learned how - LOL) It is very easy to use and the results are perfect. I highly recommend this item to those who are on the fence as to what to buy. It's a great little invention and makes your life easier!!

First of all - to those who are having problems with mold/sludge - you need to take the lid off of the steam chamber after you steam EVERY time when it's still hot.  The water just evaporates out and you will have absolutely no issues.  This is a completely safe machine if you use common sense.Secondly, this machine has given me exactly what I need to create a healthy diet full of variety for my little guy.  It wouldn't be simpler to use.  You can do EVERYTHING with this one machine, and do it well.  I have had no problems with the processor, and it's created incredibly consistent, smooth purees each time.  If you're having problems, try adding a bit more liquid to your mix.The beaba silicone freezer thingy is really nice, but expensive.  We have one, but I also took my 50% off coupon to Michael's and got a Wilton silicone mini brownie pan which works great too.Put this on your registry, and when your babe is ready to eat solids you'll be glad you did!

Pros:-Easy, all in one clean up.-BPA free-Doesn't take up a lot of spaceCons:-Makes small batches. Can only fit half a sweet potato and barely two apples-Takes longer to make bulk baby food because you can't blend while it's steaming-Steaming times are way too long, and you have to let the unit cool off for 5 mins before you can touch it or else you get burned

I received this product as a gift.  I was so excited to use it.  However, I'm sadly disappointed with this product.  The puree is very weak!  It takes far too long to blend the products, having to stop many times to stir the contents because it doesn't blend evenly.  The only nice feature is the clean-up--only one bowl to wash.  This is totally overpriced.  I wouldn't even buy it if it were under $20.  Save the money and use a blender.

I was unsure about purchasing this product because I am a full time working mom in grad school and wondered if I would ever have the time to make home made baby food....so I let a friend in a similar situation try it first :) She told me it was awesome, fast, and easy to make food for a whole week in just an hour. So I gave it a try and I am so glad I did. I can make everything for my little guy in just a few short minutes. The longest time is spent while the food is cooking and you don't have to be hanging around watching that happen, so I can fold laundry, cook dinner, or study while it is happening. This was a wonderful purchase, and I would highly recommend it!

I am not a chef or even much of a cook. I bought this hoping it would make preparing food for my 7 month old easy and convenient and it is. I spend large parts of my weekends making all kinds of baby food because it is so fun and so very easy. Before I got the Babycook I used my magic bullet which was easy as well but it wasn't nearly as convenient as I had to boil  the apples (I don't have a steamer) and then I could only do a little amount at a time as the magic bullet can only handle so much due to space and power issues. The Babycook is small but it is better than pulling out the wedding gift blender that hides in the back of the pantry.I just read a review about getting mold in the steaming chamber so I rushed over to check to see if I had any especially since I tend to leave the water in there between uses but no, it was clean. I will empty out the water after use in the future and keep an eye out but so far all is well.I also read a review where they said that your baby would grow to not need this but what I have found is that is works great for adults too. My husband does not like vegetables and I have to admit I am not good about eating them myself so how do I handle that now? I use tricks from Jessica Seinfeld's "Deceptively Delicious" and add the pureed veggies to our adult dishes. I don't feel as bad eating a large slice of macaroni and cheese pie if it has cauliflower and butternut squash puree in it. So not only am I saving $$ by not buying packaged babyfood but I am also adding good nutrients to our food as well. Will I recoup the cost of the unit when all is said and done? Who knows and frankly this penny pinching mommy doesn't really care.

I love that I can steam, puree and reheat all in the same machine.  I also love that I don't have to keep my eye on the food that I am steaming.  I just add the water and get back to playing with my baby girl.  I couldn't be happier with this product and I think it was well worth the money!

Got this babycook as a family gift and am very disappointed. The steamer works well, although the reports about the steaming well developing odor are scary. The blender works for about a half second until it spins freely, all the food stuck below it, not processed to where I can feed it to the baby. Maybe I'm not getting this right? I am following the instructions from the cookbook (small portions). So the rest has to be mashed with a fork and then there is still cleaning to do. I don't see how this is easier/faster than a proper blender...

We've been using this product for about a month now and are very pleased not only with its performance, but the resulting foods.  We have a small apartment, and no dishwasher so even the thought of breaking out pots and pans for steaming, then the blender or food processor for blending seemed dreadful.  Especially because if we wanted to make batches of a couple of different types of food, we'd have to clean all of those big things in between each type of food!  The Babycook is nice because you steam and blend in one machine that has a very small counter footprint, and is very easy to clean.  If you want to make multiple foods in one evening, you simply rinse the basket, blending bucket and spatula b/w each food.  I should also note that my husband works full-time and I work out of the home 3-4 days a week and we still find this very convenient.  It doesn't take long at all.  Also, we definitely have not seen any of the "mold" other reviewers mention.  We've descaled with vinegar once in 4 weeks.  It isn't always possible, but I find it's best to get to the machine as soon as you can after it's finished steaming.  Then you unscrew the water reservoir's top (CAUTION: this can be very hot.  I use a dishtowel or pot holder) and let it dry out completely while it is still hot.  VERY LITTLE moisture will remain in the reservoir.  As for cost...locally our organic baby food costs about .85 a jar.  We would need to be able to make roughly 142 jars of food for this machine to pay for itself.  Each time I make food (every 2 or 3 days)I make about 8 jars.  So in about 17.5 evenings, we will cover cost.  As I mentioned earlier, we've had it for a month, so this great machine has almost already paid for itself.  Suffice it to say that if you have limited space and time, but really want to know exactly what is in your baby's food (and be able to feed them what you're having as a family, just as a puree) this machine is worth it.  Lastly, I have given this product 4 stars (instead of 5) because I have not found it super convenient for reheating - a feature that is advertised for it.  If you want to defrost or reheat something, it cannot be in a plastic container (makes sense...) it must be in glass or some polycarbonate container.  Well, everything I use for storing my son's food is plastic...and once it's frozen there's no getting it out of the plastic and into glass just to defrost it.

I love using this thing, yes it makes small batches, but 1 batch makes 12-14 ice cubes which is 12-14 ounces of baby food. Typically when babies start eating they eat 1-2 ounces a day of baby food, so 1 tray lasts 1 week or more.You don't need to make huge batches when they are little and when they are big you just put when you are eating in there and dice it up!People have mentioned issues with cleaning, but I follow the rules for cleaning and make the food with boiled water or nursery water.....and I clean it with baking soda....no mold problems what so EVER

OK, so the machine itself when we first got it was good. Then i washed it and saved it for baby number two and all went downhill. It was not even over a year before I used it again. The steam didn't steam properly and the blade got dull fast. I called customer service and got condescending answers and telling me i needed to re purchase all of the items. Then they said it should be better. I told if it doesn't will you give me my money back or may i return the items and she said no. I needed to redo it many more times and I am not doing it right. I don't get how many ways you can push a friggin switch but regardless I am going not recommending this or will I buy another one ever again.

column9: Makes making your own baby food easy!!!
column10: I never write reviews, which is interesting, because I live by them when searching for quality products.  That being said, if I do write a review it is because I have extremely strong feelings about a product.  I have been making my own baby food since 2008 when my first child was born.  It really isn't that hard once you have your system.  But than a friend gave me the Beaba Babycook and it changed everything.  It takes all of the guess work out of the process, and is much easier to clean up than my previous system of using large pots and pans, a strainer and a food processor.  If you are thinking about making your own baby food for more than one child this is an investment for you, totally worth it's price.  Enjoy!

Whenever I read recipes for baby food, the amount of work that goes into them--chopping, cooking, blending, pureeing, etc.--seems really daunting. So I was really happy to find the Babycook, which does everything: you just steam your fruits or veggies, dump them out of the basket into the bowl and puree them. Ridiculously easy to use. It's also very easy to clean, as the blade is detachable. I've experienced the lime buildup that other reviewers have complained about, but descaling it the night before I plan to use it keeps it perfectly clean.

Love this machine-its all in one steamer and blender. Watch the mechanism for snapping bowl onto stand as the first one I purchased came cracked and probably from someone not watching as the parts line up to snap into a locked position. Worth the money as I can set it to steam and walk away-and I have twins so anything that cuts down on time is a huge plus!

I have read through the entire instructions for the Beaba. It is very basic and lends to common sense.I was under the impression that the Beaba did the steaming and blending in a complete cycle. You have to steam, then pour the chopped food into the blending bowl. So, two separate steps for the operator.  FYII would like to mention an important note, it says to NEVER place anything other than water or distilled white vinegar in the water steamer.  CLR is a chemical, please DO NOT put this in the water steamer to clean the machine. I think we are all using the Beaba to keep a very clean,  "chemical-free" diet for our babies. Why would you use a chemical in the water steamer?  To properly maintain the Beaba I would recommend leaving the lid off of the water steamer AFTER you have completed your cooking. This should ensure that no mildew or mold grows in the water steamer by completely drying out or at least by not promoting a ideal environment for growth.Also, the baby cook book that come with it only has 12 recipes, 3 for each stage of food for the baby. Not all that great. FYII will update after frequent use (=

I love this machine! Just reading the directions at first I was slightly intimidated, but once I actually used it, it was very straightforward. It's so easy to just throw in whatever I want to cook for the baby (usually whatever we're cooking for ourselves) into the little machine and turn it to "steam." While it's cooking, I can do whatever else I need to. After 15 minutes, when it's done, I can either just give the steamed food to the baby if it's mushy enough, or tip it over into the blender part and puree. Mold has not been an issue. Carrots did stain the cooking tray slightly. Some people have said it will be useless after the baby gets to solids, but I think it will be convenient for me to steam single-portion vegetables for myself. One flaw I'm not a fan of--it would be nice if when it was done cooking/steaming, it made some sort of "ding" or alarm sound. As it's designed now, the light just turns off.

Hey,I'm a first time dad.  This product is GREAT!!  We could either be spending 50 cents or more for each premade baby food container from Gerber, or you can use this!  So, to list off its pros and cons:1.  Really easy to use.  Put some water into the steam side, put whatever you want cooked in the basket, turn it on, come back ~10-15 minutes later, chop it up in the blender side (we add more water and oatmeal at that point too), and then serve!  Start to finish is about 20 minutes tops, and only about 5 of those minutes are you actually there doing anything (the rest it's steaming so you're free to do whatever while it works).  Cleanup is very easy, just wash it out, which also just takes minutes, tops.2.  Cheap to use.  Fruits and veggies are cheap to buy at the store, certainly cheaper than buying pre-made baby food.  You'd be amazed how many meals one sweet potato will provide for a baby, I know I was!  Plus, you can theoretically cook anything in it for your baby, although we have yet to expand past fruits and veggies.3.  Expensive to buy.  On the other hand, we got this as a gift, so that wasn't a factor for us.  The little bit more effort this is over buying premade food seems like a tolerable cost to us (we both work and this seems well worth it to get her quality food we make ourselves...plus it's kind of fun, haha.)Ok, so that's pretty much it.  My wife and I are really happy with this product, and would totally give it to other people in the future (if we liked them enough to spend $135 on them, at least, haha!)

column9: The best purchase I got so far for my baby!
column10: I can't say enough how awesome this cooker/steamer/blender is!  It literrally takes minutes to make (not counting the time it needs to steam the veggies of course). I make fresh purees for my baby every morning before going to work..It's so easy!  I cut up the veggies, put it in the steamer basket to steam cook, by the time I get out of the shower and change, the food is ready and I just puree it for 20 seconds and my daughter has fresh yummy veggies for the day!  It  is super  healthy  for her and she LOVES it!

this product is o.k. but i think you can get away w/out it and be fine ...not really worth the money. CONS: it only makes a very small amount of food at once. if I am going through the trouble, i'd rather make a bigger batch and freeze it. Also, the lid on the resevoir gets so hot and is shaped oddly so that it is difficult to get a grip of it to take off. a serious caution, the booklet i got w/ mine (purchased in 2008) has recipes that include foods that you are not supposed to give to babies under a year old!!!!!finally, the blend mode does not have an optional 'stay on' so that if you want to puree something, you need to stand there and hold the button. you can't do something else while it's blending b/c you need to be right there to keep it running. PROS: technically, it does what it says it does, and it is easy to clean. I find that even though i own this, i tend to use my good old pan w/ a steamer basket and then puree in my food processor. works just as well, saves time, and makes more at once.

This product is simply amazing. Steams fruits and veggies perfectly and the food processor is phenomenal. Very easy to use and even easier to clean. I truly enjoy making my baby's food. One tip I have found is to remove the water left after steaming into a glass cup and slowly add it back to the bowl while processing. The lid must be on to blend the food, so it will take you a few times to remove the lid to add the water; however, you can control the consistency of the food this way. Mommy and baby are really happy with this purchase. :)

column9: Great for fresh cooking not for freezer user
column10: If you are like me and you don't like to freeze food, the babycook is just great.I cook every night for my daughter (she is 10 Mo) some vegetables (swiss chard, leaks, brocollis, sweet peas, squash, carrots, spinach,....), meat (mostly chicken with lemon and thym and then I mix it with yoghourt).The cleaning is easy.Though when I cook apple sauce I usually use a larger pan, as I cook a very large protion of it. Still she doesn't eat the vegetables if it is not freshly cooked.If you want to cook large portion and freeze them this is certainly not what you are looking for.
Do NOT get this. Your child will be eating mold. The company needs to address this issue but won't. This company is dangerous.

I purchased this product for much cheaper from diapers.com. It is wonderful. Unlike another reviewer, I like that fact that it doesn't prepare a large portion. I don't have a lot of freezer space and I like to offer my daughter a variety of foods, so, making a pound of sweet potatos at one time would do me no good. I rather prepare a few carrots, a few apples and oranges, and other small recipes, than have a whole lot of one thing. It's easy to clean and saves you time on having to clean out a steamer, and processor. I LOVE IT! ALSO, IT IS BPA-FREE!!

This babycook is AMAZING!  It's easy to use and clean.  It steams and blends food too.  It's perfect for people who want to make their own food and know whats going in the ingredients. It's not just for babies either!  I like to make smoothies with it.  It's easy to clean too.  I just use distilled vinegar and the mineral deposits come right out!  I recommend this to all of my friends!

I purchased this to make my son's baby food. I love how you can steam and puree in the same container! I'm all for less clean up! It's great that you can just turn in it and let it cook, you don't have to keep watching it. The only things I would change is maybe it beeping when the timer goes off instead of just the light going off, and I wish it was a little bigger. I like making big batches of baby food and freezing it. This you can only do a little at a time. But other than that, it's great!!

I made my 1st child's food using a pot of boiling water and steam basket, then transferring it to a bowl and using a kitchen aid hand blender. It was such a chore and so much clean up. I always felt I had to do 10 pounds of carrots to make it worth my time thus making it an even bigger chore and there'd be a few chunks I just couldn't get. Then of course freezing in ice cube trays and all that hassle. Plus when boiling water on the stove, I occasionally would forget about it and burn my pot. Now that I have a toddler and 6 month old and working full-time, I was tempted by the baby bullet commercials, did some research and decided to try the Beaba instead.I LOVE IT!!! It's no longer stressful and a huge chore. I can easily throw in a couple carrots while I'm cooking dinner for everyone else and now there's dinner for all. The food comes out so smooth. I don't have to pay attention to water boiling on the stove. I can just let it steam and it turns itself off when ready and then I can puree when I'm ready. Clean up is as easy as top rack dishwasher. I leave the lid off the water container when I'm done as I read the reviews on mold, so I've had no problems there. If you question whether to spend the money, I would say it is totally worth it. It pays for itself in a couple weeks/vs buying baby food especially if you have a big eater like I do. Highly recommend this thing.
I love my Beaba! I love that I can steam and blend in one appliance and clean up is very simple. It feels good to make fresh wholesome food for my son and not feel like its a big project .

I bought this for my son who is now 10 months. I love the idea of it. Love making fresh food, my baby loves it too. I use the BabyCook almost every day. However, it could be better. I've had to replace the blade, nut and the main bowl because each part has broken in the 6 months I have been using it. Given the price, the product parts could be made better. I've spent bout $60 getting new parts. If I find myself with another little one in the future I'm going to try a new brand and hope it's made of better quality parts.

column9: Want to love it more but there are issues
column10: Intended to make baby's food, thought I would just use my steamer basket and food processor but got this for Xmas and use it daily. I've steamed and pureed fruit, veg, meat, fish, grain and used it to reheat. I like that you just set it to steam and walk away (you have a baby after all). It's generally easy to use and clean. Complaints about big batches are funny because I can't do SMALL enough batches! I like to make just one or two servings to eat that day. I don't want to serve frozen food all the time or the same food day after day. Babycook does not blend small batches, I have to mash by hand! This is exactly what such a tiny appliance should do!There are also design issues, not how it looks (it is cute) but how it works (it is finicky). The spatula and mixing lid are awkward extra pieces to keep track of and clean. The mixing lid is useless. When removing the lid to stir there are two messy lids to remove, set down on the counter and clean, etc. It works just fine without it. The spatula is not great at scraping the bowl and if it is only intended to lift a hot basket, this could be solved more intelligently. Teardrop lid handles are slippery and difficult to grasp. Blades are not easily removable.

I have made 2 vegetables for my baby so far. I think that this machine is a huge time saver and is so easy to use. I first felt that this might be an unecessary luxury but bought it with a gift card after a few of my friends had raving reviews about it. I have to say, if I can have a gadget that saves me time allowing for more time with my little guy then it is so worth it! It is nice to know that I can make his food and not worry about additives or preservatives. I have no complaints yet!

I bought a Beaba Babycook about three months ago. My husband and I love this product. It's so easy to use. It does an amazing job of doing all the hard work for you. You prep your food and add the water and it steams, and purees it for you. I decided to prep and freeze some baby food, I made apples, carrots, sweet potatoes and zucchini in about an hour and a half. VERY EASY!

column9: So easy to use and clean up!
column10: I could not believe how easy this product was to use and so fast!  A whole squash steamed soft as could be in just 15 minutes.  Then blending it to baby food consistency in less than a minute.  I love my Beaba Babycook and highly recommend it to new moms!

column9: Great Appliance for Homemade Baby Food
column10: I got the Beaba Babycook last week for my 5 month old baby.  It worked GREAT!!  I read many mixed reviews here in Amazon but was willing to take the chance so I can make homemade food for my baby.  I used apple as the first start and it turned out to be so tasty.  Since I just started introducing her solid food so I ended up finishing the rest of the batch myself.  It took a little time to figure out how to use it first as the instruction is not very clear.  Anyway, after you have figured how this product works, it does a great job!  I used a medium size apple and it could make about 3 servings.  It is so compact that it takes so little of counter space.  I love it and I am so glad I brought it.

I was very excited about this product when I bought it - the idea of steaming and blending the food in one gadget seemed like a big time saver. However, it's not nearly as much of a time saver as it seems. The bowl is tiny, so to make enough food for just 2 days or so, I had to fill the bowl at least twice to steam the veggies(and that's about 10-15 min of steaming each time). An average-sized cauliflower took me 3 steaming session to get through, so that's almost an hour of steaming. Then the blending... unfortunately, this product is not nearly powerful enough to blend veggies quickly. Even with adding a lot of water, the food seems to get stuck and the blades are just blending what's on the bottom of the bowl and not moving the food around at all. You also can't move the food around without taking apart the whole contraption - likely because of it's baby-proof design. Several times already I ended up pulling out a regular blended and transferring the veggies to finish blending them. I've now given up on this disappointing product and will have to return it. I'm hoping that a regular-sized food processor and a steamer will do the trick in a lot less time and with much less effort.

This device makes steaming and pureeing so easy and fun, and the cleanup is so much easier than washing a pot and colander and the blender.  All the cleanup with steaming and blending the normal way made me reluctant to make my own baby food.  Having this device makes me have no excuse.  It seriously is fun to steam the food and blend it for my little one.  I also use it for myself, as steamed fruits and vegetables are tasty!

I've had this product for about 6 months, and in the beginning it worked great.  I was using it every week to make a surplus of baby food to feed my daughter throughout the week.  I properly descale it with vinegar regularly, and follow instructions for water amounts.  Then, about a month ago I noticed that when I steamed the food there would be a puddle of water that formed underneath the mixer on the counter.  This worried me a bit because I'm not a huge fan of electrical appliances sitting in puddles of water!  I tried to tighten the blade so that it wouldn't leak, but no use.  I contacted the company, and they told me I needed a new rubber gasket which forms the seal around the blade hole.  I ordered one, and after I replaced the old gasket it worked fine for one steam, but then the very next time I used it the thing leaked again!  I ordered a five pack of the rubber gaskets, thinking that if I'm going to continue to use this thing I'll have to replace the gasket every time (absurd, but I really liked the product).  Well, I put in a new gasket, and it STILL leaked!  So now I'm left with a package of gaskets and a leaky baby food maker.  I'm going to attempt to contact the company, but I don't have high hopes for a refund or replacement.

I cannot personally attest to the performance of the food maker.  I can only attest to the enthusiasm of my daughter and daughter-in-law when both received them as a gift from me.  They report big buck savings on feeding their three daughters (a twin and a single born within 5 days...yes, to different families).  They find the Beaba easy to use and most importantly, their daughters seem to be thriving on their food.  Happily, I have been left out of the prep of food, but take great pleasure in playing with and even feeding the girls.

This was a gift for the birth of my second child and I love this. It is so versatile, I've even used it to make applesauce for my four year old from fresh, local, farmers market apples. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who is looking to make food for their baby. Well worth the investment for any child.
Maine Lobster!! Is there anything that tastes better? I can't imagine anyone being disappointed in this product or this company. Definately would reccomend.
this is it, no shell anymore, just lobster and flavor mixed just right...will get a re order again and again...

column9: Very good but higher here than at Duncan Hines' 3rd party seller
column10: This was a very good cake - made 4 of them - wouldn't know it was a box cake.  Little disappointed to find it for $1 less at Duncan Hines' web sitebut the 3rd party seller was in New York & we're in Southern Calif. and needed it in a hurry.  The seller was extremely helpful and communicativeand assured me it would meet my deadline date, which they did.Don't know why you can't find these products in the store - but thank goodness for amazon.com - they always come up with just what I'm lookingfor.
Years ago, I made Red Velvet Cake from scratch, but now, with this mix, it is just as good as from scratch! I highly recommend this cake mix!
I bought these recently and was really impressed.  They're basically low calorie cheetos that come in different flavors.  I loved them and would definitely buy again.
bought these as an add-on --  they are much better than expected. will be reordering if available.adding 3 more words - geez
If you want fresh crunchy peanuts get these! This is our fourth order from Feridies. We give as gifts and eat a lot of em' . Just keep them in the fridge after opening and they stay fresh longer.

For some reason we don't see a lot of Virginia peanuts in California. Ralph's supermarkets carried their own brand for about 2-3 years but it has since been pulled from the shelves, which is a shame because there's nothing like Virginia peanuts. They are large and crunchy in a way that puts Planters to shame. But as is the case when supermarkets no longer carry our favorite products, consumers must take to the web to satisfy their palettes.I found Feridies Peanut Company on the web and, judging by all of the positive reviews, decided to take a chance. Well, I'm happy to say the gamble paid off. These nuts are exceptional. They have the perfect amount of salt and are crunchy in a way you'll have to taste to believe. Give them a try.Update - Just found out that the grocery chain Bristol Farms carries these nuts. Not cheap, but definitely worth it.

column9: Not the original Knorr Pesto Sauce mix-this is loaded with artificial ingredients.
column10: I bought a huge case of these knorr pesto sauces because my fiancee and I used to eat them a year ago all the time and back then they were delicious.  But then we moved and my local grocery store did not carry the knorr pasta sauces.  However when they arrived and I opened the package I was in for a big disappointment.  One thing I used to love about knorr was they used real ingredients-real parmesan and romano cheeses. Apparently not any more.  Now this sauce mix is completely artificial-corn starch and preservatives and artificial flavors-blech!  It doesn't taste anywhere near as good as the original.However I give it three stars because it's still tastes better than a lot of the sauces in the store and at least you can use olive oil in your sauce instead of the vegetable oil based sauces in the store.  Knorr should be ashamed for ruining a great product.  If they had stuck to the original recipe, I'd have given it five stars.  I know they are saving money by using artificial ingredients but the cost is too high as this affects the taste and our health.  I wouldn't have bought 24 packs if I had known the recipe had changed.  I hope they will reconsider the change and put real ingredients back in this product.  Here are the ingredients since Amazon doesn't list them:Maltodextrin, corn starch, wheat flower, salt, whey (milk), monosodium glutamate,spinach, garlic powder, basil, sugar, natural flavor (soy), onion powder, spice
Mmmmm.....this sauce is so yummy. I can't get it in my local grocery stores, so I was so excited to find them on amazon. Throw in some chicken, sundried tomatoes, or veggies to make it even better.

column9: Always my kids favorite and fresh too
column10: I have a hard time finding these in my local grocery store.  Creamy Pesto is my 4 and 6 yr olds' preferred/only sauce for pasta so it has been frustrating driving store to store to find it and not having it when the 4 yr old only wants "green" noodles for dinner.  I was very happy that Amazon carried it.  It comes in 12 and 24 pack boxes.  We went with the 24 pack box because my kids will eat it once a week.  I was worried that it might expire before we got to use all 24 but the expiration date is 1.5 yrs out from when we recieved the box so I am just thrilled!

I've tried nearly all the fancy brands at Wholefoods and Trader Joe's and even boutique bag-your-own varieties and this is the best organic granola. And when they say low fat they mean it! One gram of fat per serving and all the flavor and crunch you could want. As far as the chew, I like more than I've found in any granola so I'm used to adding my own dried fruit. That said, the cranberries here are plump and chewy unlike the dehydrated berries I come across everywhere else. Obviously, I can't say enough...
Bombay Basmati Rice Brown, 32-Ounce (Pack of 6) Ordering this product was very good process and what has been used was good. No complaints!
This extract has a very strong alcohol aroma, so much so that it is difficult to discern any pistachio flavor. You might as well use a liquer instead- you'd probably get a better flavor.

These brazil nuts were fresh & crunchy with a creamy, mild taste .... delicious!  I've ordered other bagged nuts over the internet, but they weren't fresh.  You don't always know how fresh they are (even in the stores, the nuts can sometimes be rancid).  Rancid nuts are NOT healthy and contain toxins, so if you taste one, be sure to spit it out.  These were so good I've ordered two more; hopefully they'll be just as fresh as the first batch.
Sometimes they are fresh, sometimes stale.... you never know till you open the package.Bought them a few times and this last time are inedible
these nuts are tasty. i purchased them because brazil nuts are a super food with a lot of selenium and magnesium.  they also have the 'good' fats that are so important!
For a canned soup, this is a winner!  Not quite like grandma used to make, but perhaps healthier, and the best Jewish penicillin you can keep on your shelves!

I love to make my own soup particularly in the wintertime but Campbell's Select has a winning recipe in its Chicken with Egg Noodles.  The chicken, veggies and noodles are good size and plentiful.  When you have neither the time or inclination to make your own soup, this is a satisfying alternative.  It is delicious.

I usually like Betty Crocker meals. This is the first and last time I will get this one! I followed every step of the directions and had to throw the whole meal out! There was almost no chicken or veggies in the mix. The rice came out like hard little pellets that cut into the roof of the mouth or stuck between the teeth.I am reluctant to even give the remaining 5 packs to the local food bank but hate the idea of throwing any food out. I will avoid any rice dishes from BC after this!.

column9: Great, fast and easy to cook
column10: Betty Crocker Helper Complete Meals, Fried Rice with Chicken, 25.3-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6 ) These meals are easy to fix and great. I haven't tried them all..YET. But tend to. I have tried several thou. The taste is good and like I said are easy to fix...on stove..oven or even micro-wave..a good and easy quick meal or a side. Try them, all...I plan on doin'it.

This fried rice is alright and I've had worse from restaurants. I found the taste a little strong and overwhelming. I would recommend making this and adding some white rice to it maybe to tone down the taste a little. I also found it to be a little chicken light. If you're looking for a quick easy meal or side though this will do the trick, just don't expect much.

WE MADE CHRISTMAS FUDGE THIS YEAR. THESE CHIPS WERE AWESOME. THEY TASTED WONDERFUL. THEY MELTED QUICKLY. AND THE FUDGE TURNED OUT WONDERFUL. I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS PRODUCT TO EVERYONE. SURE MADE THE COOKING EASIER. NOT SO MUCH STIRRING. THIS COMES IN A TWO POUNDS BAG SO YOU HAVE TO KNOW YOUR MEASURMENTS. WORKS WELL WITH CHILDREN IS ONE WAY TO PUT IT. EASY TO USE AND EASIER TO EAT.

Our Saint Bernard, Pearl is a very picky eater.  She'll go days without eating if she doesn't like the food offered.  Training treats were the hardest!  She liked freeze dried liver for a few days, then wouldn't touch the stuff again.  We've probably bought every one on the market with bad results on all.  We received a bag of Wellness Pure Rewards Venison Jerkey Bits in a gift bag and she'll do ANYTHING we ask of her for these treats!  It's the only thing she truly LOVES to eat!  We've shared with friends and their dogs feel the same way.  They are difficult to find in stores, but I found them easily and at a better price on Amazon.
Healthy treat,and I enjoy seeing my dogs so excited when I grab the bag!They absolutely love them :)
Our little Yorkshire terrier loves it and we love it too, because it is all natural.

Don't misunderstand my low rating, this is an excellent curry and really is as good as you would get in a quality Indian restaurant; quite unbelievable for a frozen meal in a box. The problem is the portion size is miserable since they started marketing it with the bismati rice included in the box. I am not a big eater and am normally quite happy with smaller sized entrees but you literally would need two of these if you are having it as an entree; and that is if you have the Nan bread with it!!! It used to come without the rice and you got twice the amount of curry, which was perfect (easy to cook up some rice or buy heat and serve to accompany it). Then the makers cut the size in half and included rice, making the actual curry portion half what it was. The reason the manufacturer gave for the change (reduced portion) was that customers like the convenience of having the rice included. Fair enough - add the rice, but don't cut the curry portion in half to where it is utterly misleading to pass this off as an entree. Please go back to a reasonable portion size and either add the rice and charge a couple of dollars extra, or better still, sell the rice as a seperate side dish and give at least a semblance of an entree sized curry.
They have added a cheap rice and cut the portion size of the curry in half very disappointing this meal is now a side dish rather than an entree way overpriced

I've tried every Curry frozen dinner I can find and most of them are just terrible.  This one is just incredible! My local Cub foods stopped carrying it and I was so bummed, but I suddenly found it on Amazon.  It was shipped in dry ice and was perfect to put in the freezer.  Just make some instant rice and you've got a great meal!

I buy a lot of frozen dinners, including meals featuring Indian curries.Out of them all- I prefer anything by Tandoor Chef because of the portion size and the amazingly authentic Indian taste. I found them at my local grocery store and have been hooked since. I saw the amazing deal on Amazon and decided to order these. They arrived within a day, however, they held only one ice pack. For a 12 pk order- I expected one more ice pack.These frozen dinners are great for people like me watching portion size and caloric intake. Indian curries are notoriously high in calories, but this specific one is 315 kcal. It's a great way to enjoy Indian food on a diet.I recommend Tandoor Chef Chicken Tikka Masala as well- although that one is 400 kcal. The curry is always more than the rice- you can always cook extra rice to go with the meal.Lastly, the best thing about them is the taste!

As a single, middle-aged man who never really learned to cook, I'm always keeping my eye out for good frozen entrees.  This chicken curry, which I happened across in the local Ingles grocery store, was surprisingly tasty.  And I'm very picky.  Mind you, nowhere near as good as the Indian cuisine at two or three very good local restaurants, but for a frozen meal -- incredibly delicious.  The curry sauce is really quite good, the breast meat chicken is tender and the basmati rice was decent also.

I agree with the previous review these were awesome till they added the rice. You get less product for you money. It makes them less economical. Where it was cheaper for me to make my own rice and share the entree with my daughter.

I rarely give anything 5 stars, but I love this product so much I gave it 5 stars. The flavor is fantastic for something out of the freezer section. The company recently changed the product. It was just all chicken curry, but now they've added rice to the dish. So you get less chicken curry. I liked it better when it was all chicken curry as I would cook my own basmati rice on the stove.

This is very tasty. Good deal to save a few bucks here on Amazon as well. I find this dish very similar to the Chicken Tikka Masala. Both are great, obviously this curry dish has more curry flavor than the Chicken Tikka Masala. The chicken in this dish is wonderful as well.

I have a 3 1/2 year old American Bulldog that has gone through thousands of dollars in vet bills and worthless speculations. She has been on Grandma Lucy's Rabbit Pureformance for several days now and I have already noticed the vast improvement in her demeanor and energy level. My dog used to violently scratch at herself till she made herself bleed. We discovered that she was allergic to beef, lamb, pork, chicken, and duck. Due to the simple yet nutritional ingredients of Grandma Lucy's she is doing excellent. It's been several days and NO MORE SCRATCHING...I am so excited that I had to write a review. My dog was so allergic to the many different other foods that we have tried with her that we almost lost all hope and we were going to just highly medicate her for the rest of her life. I didn't want to do that and after looking at the excellent ingredients contained in this brand of food I was hoping for the best. I couldn't be more happy and delighted! She's been on various raw, dry, wet, home cooked, and everything else with no luck. Please Grandma Lucy's never change your ingredients on the Rabbit Pureformance line of food because you have just made our lives a whole lot more stress free, thank you! Anyone with a dog that has bad allergies should really give this food a try...it might be the best decision you've ever made for your dog. I'd also like to add that the preparation for making her food is very simple. Just add warm water to the freeze dried food until you get the desired consistency that you prefer. Let it stand for a few minutes and then it is ready to serve. The food honestly smells amazing and at times I have thought about trying it myself. It's made with all human grade ingredients which is good to know. My dog Sadie is 75lbs and a 10lb bag of this fantastic product lasts us approximately 20 days. It's a good deal and so easy to prepare...give it a try and you'll see what I'm talking about.

Each 3 lb bag ends up making around 15 lbs of fresh moist food, once you add water. The rabbit has a slightly stickier texture than the chicken Grandma Lucy's Pureformance, Freeze-Dried Chicken Dog Food, 3lb, but my dog loves both of them (and he is picky!). It is grain-free and low-fat. I use the Purformance as a large part of his diet rotation. He is healthy and itch-free and has optimum digestion. You add equal amounts mix and warm water, wait 5 minutes, and done! I even tried a little bit and it tasted like human food. You can also easily stir in some kibble if you want to do that, the texture matches well with kibble.P.S. They also have a cheaper Artisan line, which I don't feed anymore because it contains white potato. If your dog isn't as sensitive, it is worth a try. Grandma Lucys Grain-Free Chicken Dry Dog Food 3lb
There is nothing fancy about these nuts.  Many broken pieces and less than 50% whole pieces. The company is not up to par.  Will not buy again.

column9: Superior Nut Fancy Salted Whole Cashews
column10: Before I started purchasing the Superior Cashews, I was buying them at Costco. Your Cashews are every bit as good and are easier to purchase.I will continue purchase yours Cashews, as long the Price and Quality remain the same.

When it comes to soup, I'm somewhat finicky. I normally don't care for packaged soups, but Imagine's Garden Tomato soup has won me over. The light sodium is just the right amount. The soup is creamy and tastes fresh and refreshing. What more can you ask for from soup? It's really good.

Saw a deal at my local grocery store for this. I grabbed two and waited a few weeks before I actually tried it. It is so delicious. I am normally very picky about tomato soup, I LOVE IT HOMEMADE! But, this is better! Organic, low in sodium, and soooo tasty! I sprinkled black pepper, garlic powder, and a little chili powder just because it is what I always do. This will be a new staple in my pantry. So happy I found it on Amazon so I can buy it at my deal price everytime!

column9: Finally, a tomato soup that isn't SWEET
column10: I prefer my tomato soups to be savory and often, they have a sweet edge.  We found this in our local grocery store and loved it but they stopped carrying it.  I am SO HAPPY to find it on Amazon.  I highly recommend it--our 6/8 year olds even love it and ask for seconds!
Open and pour into saucepan, heat and serve, virtually no cleanup...just a delicious meal, low in salt, fragrant and tasty. Great price as well. Delivered to my door.  What's left to complain about?
So delicious I can't wait to buy more of them next month. Fresh and delicious.
I can get these puppies for $4.99 each at Staples; 6 would come out to exactly $32.85 without coughing up $15 dollars more or having to wait for them to arrive at your house.

I've ordered most of the cheaper Tea's Etc add on teas and all have been great both in terms of flavor AND value. I cold brew using disposable tea filters closed with toothpicks in Takeya Airtight Drink Maker Pitcher / Jug, Set of Two and it works wonderfully. (Those jugs are great, even better if you can still find them half price at Costco.)I'm glad I ordered this when I did, the price has more than doubled! I'd still say it's a GREAT value. This is my go to tea when I want something with a little more flavor than "regular" black tea. I don't sweeten my tea, but I think this would be a perfect sweet tea for a hot day. The orange flavor is very palatable unlike some others. It's noticeable without being pungent or artificial. It also isn't spiced like many other orange teas.
Arrived nicely packaged and sealed. An aromatic, lovely tea that I love to blend with others to make custom iced tea blends. I love this Oolong orange with fruity black teas. Recommended!

That is right, open the bag and just get your nose close and smell it. You know this is a quality product instantly. Some of the tastiest tea I have had and the Oolong and orange are a great mix. Even if you aren't a tea drinker at all, once you smell this tea you will want to try it. I am very glad I bought this product it is a favorite of mine.

Ok, I admit it. I love sugary breakfast cereals. I always have.  As an adult, I know that they are not always the best choice and try to eat healthier ones. I also want to get my fiber, too. But sometimes you just don't want "twigs and leaves" for breakfast. Kellogg's Frosted Mini-Wheats Little Bites in Cinnamon Roll Flavor are the whole package. They are smaller than regular mini- wheats, which I really like, but packed with yummy sweet cinnamon flavor-and of course they have the delicious frosted side. They are a great way to get your fiber and are made with whole grain, so you can feel good about feeding them to your family. Kids will love them, but so will adults. I even eat them straight from the box as a little sweet snack.

column9: Very sweet with an unappealing aftertaste
column10: I was anxious to try Kellogg's Frosted Mini-Wheats Little Bites Flavored Cinnamon Roll Cereal as our family loves cinnamon rolls and we enjoy the Mini-Wheats line of cereals. We all sat down with a bowl and were more than a bit disappointed. My husband didn't like them and my son thought they were "disgusting". My daughter said they were OK but terribly sweet and I had close to the same opinion. I normally don't eat cereal as a breakfast food with milk, but prefer to eat mine dry as a snack. This cereal doesn't work at all for snacking. The milk seems to cut the aftertaste and makes them tolerable, but dry - they were awful. Not a cereal I'd recommend.

Son likes it because it is sweet but not too sweet and he would definitely like to get it again.  He gave it a four star rating instead of five because it doesn't seem very healthy with the coating of frosted sugar on top of each bite.  He did like the cinnamon flavoring.

column9: No Sodium! No High Fructose Corn Syrup! Healthy AND Delicious!
column10: I love shredded wheat, especially Kellogg's Shredded Wheat. I don't have a preference when it comes to what size- the large ones, bite size or these mini little bites all make for a delicious breakfast or snack. The best thing about these new cinnamon roll flavored ones is I noticed they eliminated high fructose corn syrup, and instead added brown rice syrup. Corn syrup is much too sweet in comparison to brown rice syrup, and I definitely prefer my cereals without high fructose corn syrup. I also love the fact that there is no cholesterol and no sodium. Almost all cereals have some sodium, which I don't like. Sodium makes the heart work harder, so I look for foods that have no or low sodium. In comparing the sodium to my other favorite cereals, plain Rice Chex has 240 grams of sodium and Frosted Flakes has 140 grams of sodium. Another thing I like is these cinnamon roll little bites give me 90% of my daily iron needs, in comparison to Rice Chex 50% or Frosted Flakes 25%.As for calories, these cinnamon roll mini bites have 190 calories for a 55g serving. Rice Chex is 100 calories for a 27g serving and Frosted Flakes 110 calories for a 30g serving. They all are pretty much even on the calories when you do the math. They are all the same on the fiber content as well- 25g of fiber for all 3 different cereals. The huge difference on these Kellogg's Frosted Mini-Wheats Little Bites Flavored Cinnamon Roll cereal is NO sodium, NO high fructose corn syrup, and 90% of your daily iron, besides 25% of many other B and other vitamins for the day. Of course, the wheat fiber is a big benefit. The tiny bit of cinnamon added makes them sweet enough to eliminate the too sweet and fatty high fructose corn syrup, and that's a great thing for everyone's health. As for the taste, they are just as delicious as all the other shredded wheat, with the addition of the cinnamon of course.  This cereal is actually much healthier than my other favorite Rice Chex and Frosted Flakes and deserves 4 1/2 stars.

Honestly, I usually like this type of cereal anyway, so maybe I'm a little biased. Regardless, I think this is delicious. It didn't quite fill me up, I was able to eat two bowls of the cereal alone or one if I added fruit or yogurt. Highly recommend eating this with vanilla yogurt- SO good!!The cinnamon roll flavor is amazing- though I felt like it tasted a little bit more like maple syrup than cinnamon roll. Which I also love, so no complaints. Will kep buying this one!

column9: Enjoyable and Tasty--But Lots of Carbs
column10: Kellog's has brought out a new Frosted Mini-Wheats Little Bites cereal--this time it's Cinnamon Roll. I liked the size which makes it almost perfect for those of us who love to snack on breakfast cereal at all hours of the day and the cinnamon flavor is not too strong. The carbs seem a little high but, on the plus side, these are very good on iron, thiamin and solid on fiber. While there are better products on the market, this was not a bad cereal by any means.

column9: Have you had your 47 biscuits today?
column10: I must admit that I've never seen portion control described in just this way.  I suppose Kellogg's decided that trying to get square Little Bites into a round measuring cup would be confusing so they just counted them out for you.  So, of course, I counted them out for myself too.  At least I did for the first serving so I could see how much space 47 biscuits took up in the size bowl I normally pour cereal into.  Then I added 1/2 cup of milk (but not skim milk) and ate that for breakfast.  I was starving in about two hours.  The next morning I measured out the 47 biscuits again, but this time I added a banana and a healthy dollop of plain yogurt plus the milk.  Now that combination stayed with me for almost four hours.  Quite respectable from my standpoint.Now let's get down to the numbers.  This cereal is made of 100% whole grain fiber in a size that is nearly half the size of a Mini-Wheats Bite Size (according to the information on the box).  If you are familiar with that size then you understand that these pieces are pretty small.  One serving of 47 biscuits contains 190 calories, or 230 if you add 1/2 cup of skim milk.  This gives you 24% of your dietary fiber for the day which is actually quite good.  The label also states that one serving provides 90% of the daily requirement of iron.  All other vitamins and minerals fall into the 0% or 2% to 25% range.  The first ingredient listed is whole grain wheat, but the second is sugar and there is no indication that I could find of what specific type of sugar that is, just in case that is really important to you.There are games on the back of the box for kids to play while they are eating their cereal with the answers printed inside the box and a segment on the side of the box called Mom's Homeroom which contains a pop quiz of questions pertaining to your child's school work.Now for the taste.  Try as I might I just can't come up with the taste of cinnamon roll.  What I do seem to get is the taste of maple, albeit a slightly artificial maple.  I even tried eating a few of the biscuits dry to see if I was confusing my taste buds with the added ingredients I was putting on and still tasted absolutely nothing but maple.  I usually read when I'm eating my cereal so I had nothing but little spoonfuls of fiber strands - but soft fiber strands - by the time I got about half way finished.  If you want this crisp when you bite into it, don't dawdle over your cereal bowl.  Also, the portion measurement will go to heck in a hand basket when you begin to pour out all the little crumblies that have rubbed off the biscuits and fallen to the bottom of the bag.  That final portion will be all crumbs all the way.  So what did I think about this product which was new to me?  Well, it isn't bad, but it certainly isn't good enough to tempt me into buying it again.  I don't get the cinnamon roll taste at all, it doesn't stave off the hunger unless I really augment it with other items, and the crumbs in the bottom of the bag will have me eating mush for the final portion.  Not very tempting.

column9: Nice addition to the Mini-Wheats line-up ...
column10: I really liked these. They had a nice cinnamon-y taste with just a hint of vanilla. Not *too* sweet, they hold up well in milk.But my FAVORITE way to eat these is dry, right out of the box, as a snack. They're the smaller version of the standard Mini-Wheats, so it's easy to measure out 100 calories-worth, and tuck them in my bag in a snack-size zip-loc Baggie. Great on-the-go treat.Definitely will be keeping these on hand.

column9: I love the "Little Bites" but not so much the flavor
column10: I am a big fan of Mini-Wheats. I eat them often for breakfast. I have tried the frosted and plain, but never anything with a flavor. I was curious to try this one.First, I love the "little bites" size. I find they are easier to eat, they don't get as soggy as fast and they fit on my spoon! I also like the fact that it appears to fill up a bowl more, even if that's just my perception.I liked the sweetness that the cinnamon roll flavor added. I could certainly tell it just wasn't a cinnamon flavor, but a vanilla one, too. Sadly, there was also something very manufactured about the taste. Maybe it was an aftertaste or just some flavor that I wasn't expecting, but I didn't love it.I am going to stick with my normal frosted version. I like that much better.

When you first open the box you get a blast of cinnamon that's stronger than anything I've experienced, even working for a baking company.  But add milk and the taste is subtle and enjoyable.  A terrific entry to the shredded wheat family.

I'm a snacker of cereal products.  There it is; I've confessed that I'll eat cereal right out of the box as a snack in the middle of the day.  And the Frosted Mini-Wheats on one of my favorites;  sometimes I'll mash up the cereal and mix it in with some yoghurt and eat it that way.  It's very tasty to do this, and I think maybe a bit healthier than just eating sweetened cereal right out of the box.And the cinnamon is a nice touch.  Cinnamon, it turns out, it a spice that is good for you; helping to control blood sugar levels (although this isn't the best way to get cinnamon, for this purpose, obviously).  It adds a nice touch of flavor to the product, and if you enjoy the taste of cinnamon, it is an added bonus.Just be aware that this is a higher-calorie cereal, and there is a fair amount of sugar in it.  It's not going to be a health food for you, unless you restrict the intake (as I don't) to breakfast, and don't go overboard (as I sometimes do).

Another sugar filled version of mini wheats.  What's not to love?  Other than the whole sugar filled thing.  As an occasional treat, they're delicious.  Tastes a lot like the original mini-wheats with lots of cinnamon.

I have been a long time fan of Frosted Mini Wheats and have tried all of the newer flavors that have recently added to their lineup (Strawberry, Mixed Fruit, etc.) so I was very excited to try this one when it came out, and it did not disappoint.  At first I was a little skeptical about it being the littler size, as I thought it was going to get soggy quickly in milk, but I ended up eating it so fast because it tasted so good I did not even notice!  The cinnamon roll flavor is fantastic, now to overpowering and not too little that you can barely taste it like with some other cereals.  This is a win for me, will definitely be buying this one again and again!

column9: Front mini wheats with a brand new kick!
column10: As someone who already enjoys mini wheats, I was eager to try the cinnamon rolls flavor and while I have no problem with the regular flavor, this is a good change-of-pace of flavor.  While I would not say it tasted like cinnamon rolls, it did remind me of Cinnamon Toast Crunch a bit.  As with regular mini wheats it was still sweet, but not too sweet, so this is by no means an old-fashioned sugary kids cereal.

I like Frosted Mini-Wheats and I like cinnamon rolls, but this did not turn out to be a very good pairing.  It tastes exactly like cinnamon rolls but ends up tasting too sugary.  It maybe be because I doubled up the serving size (the box claims to hold eight severing but I finished it off in four bowls) because one recommended serving juts did not fill me up.  Whenever I have a craving for Mini-Wheats I do not see me picking up this flavor and will just stick to the original.  And I stick to the actual roll kind whenever I have a hankering for cinnamon rolls.

If you like sweet cereal but want to avoid the super-sugary cereals peddled to young children than Kellogg's Frosted Mini-Wheats are for you. I liked these little ones because they fit on my spoon better and the Cinnamon Roll flavour was satisfyingly cinnamon-y enough without being overpowering. I will say that due to their smaller size they do absorb milk a bit faster than the regular sized Mini-Wheats but I'm of the weird ilk that enjoys their cereal slightly soggy so it didn't bother me a bit but if you prefer your cereal crunchy 'til the last bite then this cereal isn't for you. But if you like your cereal sweet and a little soft and delicious then you really have to try this new Mini-Wheat flavour.

In my family, cereal is never consumed normally (ie: in a bowl with milk and a spoon) as, in a family of gamers, we usually stick to the tried and true method of munching out of the box while engaging in some tedious task involving an electronic device of some kind.  Call us primitive, but the hand-in-box method helps us stay full all day without gorging on junk food via drive-thru or conveniently placed over-priced vending machines.Kellogg's new cinnamon-flavored Mini-Wheats certainly was consumed in the aforementioned method by myself and my house-sitting brother and we came up with the following results; cool.Truth be told, they tasted like Cinnamon Toast Crunch but in Mini-Wheat form.  Makes sense, really, as all they had to do was swap around the flavor dispensers and called it good.  This isn't a bad thing, it just isn't a new and revolutionary idea like Krave was (something I could definitely get addicted to).  I enjoyed munching on them, but it just isn't munch food given how easily the Mini-Wheats fall apart in my hands.  Maybe I should try a spoon?  Either way, it just wasn't for me, but they tasted good all the same.

So maybe it doesn't taste exactly like a cinnamon roll (there's no delicious cream cheese frosting), but I still loved the taste of these new Mini-Wheats.  One thing about the Little Bites version that I've noticed is they get soggy fairly fast.  I prefer this cereal when the milk has just saturated the bites.  The only solution I see is to only fill the bowl halfway.  Nutritionally this is pretty good too.  Mini-Wheats offers 24% of your daily fiber and comes in just under 200 calories before the milk is added.

The ambition behind this cereal seems to be to have miniature, little bites of a cinnamon-roll type taste. Certainly that taste is there, but it is a little light. I'd prefer a stronger taste, since mini-wheats like this otherwise taste about as good as cardboard. The frosting adds little flavor, mostly sweetness.All in all, this cereal is tasty enough, but it's not good enough to take a favored spot on my breakfast table.

column9: Nutrition and taste will appease both children and parents
column10: If you've ever had frosted mini-wheats then this "Little Bites" version will already be quite familiar - it's essentially the same thing but smaller. I'm not quite sure what the point is of making mini-wheats even smaller, but it does seem to be a bit easier to scarf down a couple of bowls.I definitely like the taste. It has a cinnemon flavor, which is easily noticable as soon as you open the box, with (what tastes to me like) a hint of vanilla. I suppose this is supposed to mimic a "cinamon roll" flavor, but I don't think that's a very accurate description. It's sweet but not too sugary, and it has a very fiberous texture. Overall very pleaseant, except that the mini-wheats tend to quickly soak up the milk which makes it heavy and soggy.The nutrition facts are pretty typical of a cereal like this: 190 calories (w/o the milk), 1 gram of fat, 46 grams of carbs, an assortment of vatamins, etc. It's not bad for you, but it isn't a cereal for the health-nut either. A nice middle-of-the-road cereal which, I assume, will appeal to both children and parents.

I didn't know what to expect when I recieved the packgae.  But the moment I opened the cereal box, I was in heaven!To start with, the aroma smelled like the chain store in the mall and my mouth started watering.  I couldn't wait to get some ice cold milk and dig in.  Each tiny bite expolded in my mouth like fourth of July fireworks and the cinnamon urged me on to another bite.  Really the only problem I had with it is the bowl just disappeared.Seriously, I wouldn't let a little one (two and under) eat these without an adult nearby because they can cause choking.  But other than that, they are a very good way to trick kids into getting their daily fiber.

This product was just okay for me.  It's another sugar-packed cereal product with no uniqueness other than the fact that they are littler versions of Nabisco's Shredded Wheat Minis. I don't like cereals that get soggy quickly and this one does.  In general I believe that almost all commercial boxed cereal products are WAY,WAY,WAY over priced, and their sugar-packed content negates any nutritional benefit for an increasingly obese nation. Oh, did I mention that they are WAY over priced? I don't recommend this product.

I'm a fan of regular Frosted Mini Wheats so I pretty much figured I'd like these. They don't seem to have as much "frosting" as the original ones, but these are delicious! The cinnamon isn't overwhelming and they're very sweet but it isn't overboard. The "minis" are also easier to eat. Keep in mind that this isn't the most "diet friendly" cereal, but still quite delicious. I'd buy these again for sure.----------Update: The box is nearly empty at this state and I totally intend to buy more of these. I realized that these actually really do taste similar to cinnamon rolls in flavor, and a bowl of these can curb my sweet tooth very well. Delicious! Will buy again.

column9: The small size make a huge difference
column10: The problem with standard "mini wheats" is the size.  One mini wheat is too small to be satisfying face-stuffing spoonful, but 2 or 3 was kind of awkward.  With the "little" version, which is about half the size, it is easy to scoop up a spoonful of just the right amount.I like the taste of this cereal as well.  But I knocked off one star because I don't see why it should be called "cinnamon roll".  There is no roll essence to it.  Actual cinnamon rolls do have a bit of their own flavor among bread products, in addition to the sugar and cinnamon.  This cereal is really just frosted mini wheats with a little cinnamon added.  That's a fine and tasty cereal, but the name is gratuitous.

When you open the box on these Cinnamon Roll Mini-Wheats Bites you will go crazy!  The smell of these is fabulous.  I would give the smell alone 5 stars.  The taste is not near as strong as the smell, unfortunately.  The taste is not bad, don't get me wrong.  When you smell these and then you take a bite you are a tad disappointed because you want them to taste exactly like cinnamon rolls, which is how they smell.  Overall, it is a good cereal.  The size is just adorable and much more appealing to little kids.  My son won't go near a full size or even a mini sized wheat cereal but he loved these.  My husband also loved these, but thought the smell far outdid the taste.  I would buy these again for sure (if on a good sale or with a coupon) but they will not replace our usual round O's cereal.  Try them and see, they may be your new favorite!

The flavor does do a good job of capturing the character of a cinnamon roll, but these are more sugary-sweet than regular frosted Mini-Wheats.  It really captures the cinnamon flavor, and some of the smoothness, but the sugar overwhelmed these traits.  I did like the smaller size bits too.Overall, this a little to sweet for even an occasional treat, much less a regular breakfast.

My daughter assisted in this review; her comments were that they were "good!" and that she liked the cinnamon flavor and that they were not too sweet, but sweeter than the Quaker mini-wheats. In other words, kid-approved!

This cereal has a great cinnamon flavor, and isn't as sweet as I suspected it might be considering it is 'cinnamon roll' flavor and not just cinnamon. In fact I would even say that it isn't as sweet as Cinnamon Toast Crunch, and not as over-powering either. I love the texture of the mini-wheats and so this makes for a great combination. With it being part of the 'little bites' brand the pieces are very small, great for kids, but still a good cereal for adults too! An adult could definitely eat this cereal without feeling as though they're eating a blatant kid's cereal (no outrageously bright colors or noxious fruit smells). A great cereal for all the family.

I like this cereal but I'm weird I like it dry-no milk for me. I eat them as a snack. They were pretty good but tasted like they're made with brown sugar, must be the brown rice syrup. Tastes fine just I had to find out if there was brown sugar--nope!I'd recommend this if you were a frosted mini-wheat cereal fan. I like the Little Bites especially for a dry snack LOL

This cereal is great!  My usual cereal is Frosted Mini Wheats Bite Size and I'll pull out the most heavily frosted bites for myself and leave the less-frosted bites for my hubby who doesn't quite share my love of sugar.  These cinnamon roll flavored Little Bites are similar, but smaller and easier to eat (especially for kids, I'd imagine), and just as sweet with a nice smack of cinnamon.  I love cinnamon sugar, so this cereal is right up my alley.This cereal also has the usual amount of fiber for Mini-Wheats - 6 grams fiber per 47 Little Bites, which is plenty of fiber for me.

Well, simple to review...it is delicious, even straight out of the box without milk. Why not? Basically, it is candy...sure, some fiber and vitamins, but lots of sugar. That said, treats are fun, and anyone can do with a little fun. For a breakfast, just combining it with some seriously nutritious stuff like orange juice, fruit, etc can round out a healthy breakfast. So, overall, pretty good.

My family has eaten Frosted Mini-Wheats for years and have always liked them.  These are as we say in our family when something is really good, the bomb-diggity!  We loved the cinnamon roll flavor.  It wasn't exactly like a cinnamon roll, but close enough for us.  It is sugary but also high in fiber which is a plus for me.  I also like the little bites size better than the regular Mini-Wheats.  A bowl of these mini-bites with a banana and milk make a healthy enough breakfast for me!

Finally!  Something new that all of us like!Kellogg's Frosted Mini-Wheats Little Bites Cinnamon Roll Flavor are absolutely delicious!  AND they fit with our dietary restrictions (G6PD deficiency...but check with your docs/nutrition folks to make sure it fits with your restrictions as ours may be different)The best part?  My son, who is 8 and has autism and likes things that are of uniform consistency (i.e. cheerios...plain cheerios specifically) gave these the ol' stink eye at first as it wasn't all "perfectly equal" and some pieces were bigger, some broken, some conjoined, etc but I asked him to take two bites, with milk.And he loved it.  Hallelujah!  This is a kiddo who could eat the same thing every single day for the rest of his life and be totally happy and most new foods that we try result in him spitting it out or vomiting immediately.  So this is a pretty big deal to us.The flavor is fantastic- it's sweet and cinnamon-y- sort of like if you took the flavor of Cinnamon Life and put them on frosted mini-wheats.  It's not overpowering Cinnamon (kiddo hates anything that has so much cinnamon that it smells "like Christmas" or feels even slightly warm- he's definitely a "just a little dash" sort of a Cinnamon person where I tend to like a little more spice)...As an adult, the serving size is done by the piece or weight.  I counted out the number of minis into a bowl and it was a substantial amount, though the carb count is fairly high compared to my usual plain cheerios.  I am a type 1 diabetic and count my carbs to calculate my insulin dose.  For anyone watching their carbs, they might want to weigh out a serving size first, as a visual.  As far as volume goes, I could eat half of the suggested serving and probably be satisfied, as the mini-wheats are pretty filling.  Again, your mileage may vary. As someone who watches her carb intake closely, I'd probably turn to this cereal instead of some other sweet, when the craving strikes.  For my kiddo, who is very active and doesn't have to watch his carbs, I'm just happy he's eating something.There was quite a bit of "settling", and I've had similar settling with boxes from our local supermarket, so it is to be expected and I think it happens with most cereals- even Cheerios get that dust but this was a few good handfuls of "sticks" that nobody in my family wanted to eat.  I'll probably just chuck them in muffin batter the next time I bake, otherwise they will get chucked.

column9: Does taste like a cinnamon roll, but not as sugary
column10: The cereal tastes like a cinnamon roll, without being too sugary.  It stands up to milk and doesn't break down.  The box is pretty skinny, so when it was mailed it was crushed somewhat, which made it hard to stand it up on the shelf, so that's a note to people who will buy this product to be shipped in the mail.  Other than that, I enjoyed it and might buy it in the store if I got a hankering for a frosted cereal.

I have yet to find a frosted mini-wheats that I didn't like and this one is no different. It is the first time I have had the "little" mini-wheats and I like them just as much as the regular size. These little mini-wheats pack a powerful punch of cinnamon roll taste. I think they are a good compromise if you a craving a cinnamon roll but still want something that is good for you. While this cereal does have a lot of sugar it is also full of fiber and iron. Sounds (and tastes) like a good compromise to me!

column9: Flavor is definitely reminiscent of cinnamon rolls. Sugar seems bordering on excessive...
column10: I'm something of a shredded wheat fan. Generally my favorites have tended toward post honey nut shredded wheat or possibly the Kashi cinnamon shredded wheat. Though of late I've rather preferred it plain, as I'm trying to cut back on sugar consumption.All said, the falvor of this is what I says it is. It definitely tastes like cinnamon rolls. But, on the other hand it seems rather excessive on sugar at 12g/cup, so probably on the order of 12-20+g/bowl, depending how big a bowl you prefer. To me that seems pretty unbearably sweet after having been off sugar for some time.I don't know whether the "little bites" (that is squares about half the usual size) add or detracts from the overall appeal. Not sure why the bites need to be mini-er than the usual bite-sized shredded wheat already available...? Maybe for kids? To compete with other small cereals like Cheerios or Golden Grahams? Hard to say. Didn't do much for m one way or the other.If you like sweet cereals, and or really crave the taste of cinnamon rolls, this might be for you. If not, well, I suppose you could take it or leave it depending on your tastes. I'll probably stick to plain shredded wheat of health reasons. But, overall, it wasn't bad. If I was still into sweet cereals I might like it more than some others I've had. Though, again, I tend toward more lightly sweetened things than heavy-handed sweetening, generally.

column9: Not bad, but definitely not a favorite
column10: My kids and I all enjoy Frosted Mini-Wheats. Given the chance to sample a new to me flavor I had to jump on it. Had I not known this was a new flavor I would have assumed these were the Maple & Brown Sugar Mini-Wheats because the flavor is very similar. Straight out of the box these are yummy little things, but in a bowl with milk not so much. The first two bites were great, but the flavor just doesn't hold up. By the time I finished my bowl of cereal all the flavor had vanished, and I felt like I was feasting on plain 'ol shredded wheat. Not a bad thing, but when you're hoping for something a little sweet it can be disappointing. I'd buy them again, but probably to use as a dry cereal snack.

My nine-year-old Daughter is nuts about this cereal. She's been my main sounding board for this review, since I personally don't care for the cereal as a breakfast food. I'm not nuts about the way it tastes in Milk. Oddly enough, I love it straight out of the box, as a dry snack, washed down by a glass of Milk. My Daughter ran through the box pretty quickly, and we've added it to our grocery list, so consider this a recommendation from two generations.

column9: Great cinnamon flavor; perfect for a snack!
column10: I love cinnamon-flavored cereals, and when I'm going to eat a bowl of cereal for breakfast (or, let's be honest, dinner), I usually gravitate toward the shredded wheat. Lately, I've been buying Kashi Cinnamon Harvest--basically because Kashi has done a good job of advertising and convinced me their cereal was healthier. So when I received the Kellogg's Frosted Mini-Wheats, I pulled both boxes out to compare. Here's how they stack up:Serving Size: 55 g--Kashi, 55 g--Kellogg'sCalories: 180--Kashi, 190--Kellogg'sFat: 1 g--Kashi, 1 g--Kellogg'sCarbs: 43 g--Kashi, 46 g--Kellogg'sFiber: 5 g--Kashi, 6 g--Kellogg'sSugars: 9 g--Kashi, 12 g--Kellogg'sProtein: 6 g--Kashi, 5 g--Kellogg'sBoth are certified "Whole Grain," and Kashi is certified organic.Basically, the two cereals are quite similar, especially if you don't care if your cereal is certified organic. So for me, it comes down to taste, and Kellogg's wins that battle hands down! When I want cinnamon, I want to really be able to taste it, and these Mini-Wheats Little Bites are PACKED with cinnamon flavor!The one drawback is their size. Sure, they're cute, but when you add milk, they get soggy very quickly. I recommend just snacking on them right out of the box--forget the milk!

column9: Very tasty, just not as satisfying as I prefer
column10: If I can't have chocolate for breakfast, I'll take cinnamon as the second runner up!  The Cinnamon Roll variety of Frosted Mini-Wheats intrigued me.  Cinnamon can often be either too heavy or cheap-tasting in cereal.  However, I found the cinnamon flavor very pleasing in these Mini-Wheats!The serving size felt rather small.  I eat about 300 calories for breakfast, and by the time I eat a serving of these Mini-Wheats plus 1/2 cup of milk, I have just enough leftover for an egg and that's it.  I realize that doesn't sound like a big deal, but when I ate it, I just didn't feel like it was quite enough.  The extra sugar content drives up the calories, so there is simply less there to eat.  For example, I could eat two pieces of whole wheat toast with Smart Balance plus a small banana with the egg for a similar calorie count.For an occasional treat for breakfast, I keep Frosted Mini-Wheats around, because nutritionally it is still better for me that a donut.  I just don't eat them on a regular basis.And I don't really eat chocolate for breakfast, in case you were wondering.  Usually.

column9: Not as Good as Frosted Mini Wheats
