The inside is a gooey, liquid and delicious honey. They are really tasty and I found that they did give me a decent amount of energy and did not make me jittery. I tested these drops out on a day when I only had two hours of sleep. I had one drop in the morning and one a few hours later. The only caffeine I had was in the form of some diet tea. They definitely helped me to stay awake.One package contains 9 "drops". While the serving size is 1 piece, three drops equal 100% of your daily value of Vitamins B6, B12 and C. While this may be a great way to get your vitamins and energy, they do have a down side. Each piece contains 5gm of Carbs and 5gm of Sugar. I really hope that they make a sugar free version of these in the future because they are great other than this. The drops are also caffeine free.Ingredients: Sugar, Corn Syrup, Milk, Honey, Butter, Natural Flavors, Vitamin B6, Vitamin B12, Vitamin C. **PLEASE NOTE THESE DROPS CONTAIN MILK. IF YOU ARE LACTOSE INTOLERANT, YOU WILL NOT BE ABLE TO TAKE THEM**I love that I can toss these into my purse and have something with me that will really give me energy. As long as the carbs and sugar are not an issue for you, I highly recommend them. One pack will last you 3-9 days depending on how often you take them, at the current Amazon price (10/25/11), they are a little over $1.15 for a pack of 9. So, they are also a cheap way to get energy.PROS:*great price for an energy product*great tasting*they give you a decent amount of energy*you get 100% of your daily value of Vitamins B6, B12 and Vitamin C with 3 drops*highly portable/small*No caffeine or harmful additives*May take care of your sugar fix and give you motivation to get off your booty at the same time :CONS:*5gm of sugar each drop*5gm of carbs each drop*Hard on your teeth since they are hard candy & sugary

column9: Tasty, yes, but energy boost, doubtful.
column10: Ambrosoli-Honees Energy Plus Vitamin Caramels: These are sleeves of individuallywrapped candies that claim to provide an energy boost in a natural way. They are mildly sweet, containing a honey based filling. After eating FOUR of them, still no noticeable energy boost, but I was picking the filling out of my teeth. It is VERY sticky. The taste is really mild, like a bargain brand of Werther's, which now that I think of it, would probably give you more of a boost than these! Pass on this purchase.

I received a 1.45 oz package of these drops to evaluate. Not exactly enough to cause a sugar high.  That's nine drops, three for your "daily requirement". All I can attest to is the taste which is alright if you like cheap candy. The first ingredient is sugar, the second is corn syrup. I don't know if it's true but I've read that B12 is most effective by injection or sub-lingual.(dissolving the little pills under your tongue).In my opinion you'd be better advised to buy a trusted brand of mufti-vitamins and a bag of caramels if that's what you crave. If you don't like taking pills you could try the "gummy " candy type vitamins.

column4: Wandrwoman "Wise as Aphrodite, Beautiful as A...
column10: These Energy Plus candies are billed as "honey filled caramel drops". Each foil wrapped package contains nine small (1" x 1/2") rectangular candies that resemble European-style cough drops. The caramel outside is hard and when bitten into the soft honey filling oozes out. The caramel honey flavor is not bad, not scrumptious, just OK.The reason they are named "Energy Plus" is that in addition to sugar, corn syrup, milk, honey, butter, and natural flavors, the ingredients also include a middling amount of vitamins B6, B12, and C. Each 20 calorie candy contains about 35% of the daily recommended values (based on a 2000 calorie daily diet) of B6, B12, and C. Now let's understand that is is not a food. Other than 5g of carbohydrates and 5g of sugar there is no protein, no fiber, no fat, no cholesterol and no salt. This is a candy that has been fortified with three vitamins.One probably derives more of a sense of energy from the carbs and the sugar content rather than the B vitamins. It seems a better choice to have a really satisfying, tasty caramel candy Werther's Original Creamy Caramel Filled Hard Candies, 5.5-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12) and take a daily multivitamin Centrum Performance Multivitamin, 60-Count than consume these.On a positive note, these candies are manufactured by Ambrosoli in Como, Italy. If you've never visited beautiful Lake Como I highly recommend doing so. Lake Como & Its Surroundings (Travel Adventures).

Okay so these don't taste bad at all.  And given that they have B vitamins that's saying a lot.  They are caramel flavored hard candy with a soft honey center.  20 calories per piece, 33% of B6, B12, and C.  The C can be had easily anywhere so I don't consider that much of a plus.  But B vitamins (imo) taste *nasty* and are the vitamin that make me nauseated anytime I take a multi vitamin.Since B vitamins do help me feel better if I'm dragging (as well as vitamin D) I will take it every so often and have to choke down the horsepills.If you have trouble taking vitamins but you need more B vitamin supplementation these may be the best way to get there.  I'm a big fan of the sugary/chewy method of taking vitamins when I have to take vitamins so take my advice in that context.  I don't take them often but I prefer the non-pill forms when I have to take them and this is the best non-pill form of vitamin B I have tried to date.For what you pay for this you get about two and a half months of 100% dv of B6 and B12.  Since most vitamins cost around ten bucks for a month's worth of any of the non-pill-forms these are priced about the same as any of the other solutions.  If you have trouble swallowing pills these kinds of solutions are worth it.

column9: Like the Added Vitamins, but Where is the Energy?
column10: Ambrosoli Honees Energy Plus Vitamin- Caramel are simple little candies with added vitamins. They are drops that need to be dissolved in the mouth, releasing sweet caramel flavor and vitamins as they slowly dissipate.Honees Energy Plus Vitamin- Caramel have a pleasant flavor that is very much like a piece of caramel flavored hard candy. In essence, that is exactly what they are: Candy, but with added vitamins. They are sweet and pleasant to eat, with a sugary sweetness that most will find pleasant enough to recommend. And they have added B6, B12, and C vitamins for good health and other benefits.I have nothing against placing additional vitamins in my body and Honees Energy Plus Vitamin- Caramel are certainly better than the average candy for that reason alone. Supposedly, they offer an energy benefit as well, but I cannot see how one of these small drops should be expected to add energy. Looking at the ingredients, sugar is about the only significant energy- enhancing ingredient, but even the sugar content isn't that much and it isn't nearly enough to boost one's overall energy level. I felt no different after taking one of these than I did before.Honees Energy Plus Vitamin- Caramel are relatively inexpensive and they do offer more than standard candy, so I suppose they have their usefulness. I wish there was some actual energy enhancement because it would come in very handy during the mid afternoon when I often find myself feeling a little sluggish at work. But the product does have added vitamins and a pleasant caramel taste, and this is enough to convince me to award these with an average rating overall.

It's difficult to remember, eating these, that they're supposed to be vitamin supplements.  As other reviews have already said, they're small hard candies.  Sweet, but not too sweet, tasting more like honey than caramel.I can't say I really notice any difference in energy, however.  I know there's a great push for energy supplements these days, but I think these would be better marketed as vitamins (or candy) than energy supplements.The taste was pretty good, but I won't be getting these again, mostly because I can't imagine that regular intake of hard candies would be too easy on teeth, although they're nice once in a while.

column9: Not a "health food"... not particularly good candy either.
column10: I was curious when I saw these "Honey Filled Caramel Drops".  The largest printing on the wrapper reads "Energy Plus". The "plus", I guess, is that each lozenge comes with 1/3 the daily requirement of vitamins B6, B12 and C.Nine lozenges come in each wrapper, and this listing is for a box of 24 of these - so 216 lozenges total.Here are the ingredients, in the order listed on the label:SugarCorn SyrupMilkHoneyButterNatural Flavors (I always love that one...)Vitamin B6Vitamin B12Vitamin CAnd I guess some lawyer made them write again (in case you missed it in the previous sentence): Contains: MilkSo... are they good "vitamins"?  They taste better than my multi-vitamin... but they aren't exactly multi-vitamins, are they?  You have to eat 3 to get your minimum daily requirement of B6, B12 and C, then you're still short of vitamins A, D, etc.Are they good "caramels" - Not by any American expectation of "caramel", but they're imported from Italy and if you broaden your American definition of caramel to "sugar-filled treat", it fits the bill.  They're not particularly nutritional poison - despite 2 ingredients being "milk" and "butter" it lists the fat and cholesterol as 0, and they're only 20 calories per piece.To cut to the chase: I won't be getting these again.  They're not suitable as a vitamin substitute, and they're not tasty enough to find their way into my "treat" rotation.

column9: Mostly sugar and corn syrup, but good flavor.
column10: As with some of the other reviewers, I am a bit uncertain why they labelled these as "honey filled caramel drops." No caramel here that I can taste, but there is a nice honey flavor. I wasn't surprised by the list of ingredients. Primarily Sugar, Corn Syrup, milk, honey, flavorings and vitamins. I had something similar to these when I was growing up, so there is a nice association with these chewy little confections. Yes, they have a bit of vitamins in them, but really, are you eating them for any reason except the flavor? A nice occasional sweet treat.

I was disappointed that these are not caramels- the description should read " caramel-flavored hard candies" as that is what  these are.However, I was not disappointed in the taste- these are made of largely natural ingredients, and they taste like it.The " liquid honey" center is more chewy than liquidy. Texturally these are not really as described- but again they taste good.A for "energy", energy is in this context a synonym for calories, and the small number of calories per piece is not going to do much.The vitamin content is okay  -about 1/3 of the RDA for 3 main vitamins-but using these to get your requirements could be pricey.So,  I like the  taste, I like the natural ingredients, and these are a healthier substitute for candy, but they aren't a great source of energy or vitamins.I'd buy these , but mostly for the taste rather than the nutritional claims.

A nice honey taste.  If you don't mind the 5 grams of sugar.  If you have a problem swallowing pills this is a convenient form of getting your vitamins,These particular vitamins are very important to vegan and vegetarians,IMHO.I recommend them for non-diabetics.Gunner  September, 2011

column9: Small boost, but that's about it.
column10: Been trying these for about a week, and I enjoyed a noticeable boost at first, but it was short-lived and I was back to being sluggish.I work at a law firm as an admin, so I need to be at my computer all day. I get tired, so I drink plenty of coffee, tea, and the occasional Coke. I ordered these to help with the energy levels, and since caramel-honey seems like a good winter flavor, I thought the masked taste would be nice.But it's just another caramel-honey drop. Nice honey inside, and a brittle caramel shell on the outside. Like I said, the first few drops were good for a quick boost, but my energy depleted, and I'm tired as ever.Blah.

column9: sweet honey caramels + vitamins = thinking energy
column10: These Energy Plus candies are really tasty.  They taste like a hard caramel which eventually gives way to a soft honey center.  They have a modest amount of vitamins in each drop: 33% of your daily recommended value of two of your B vitamins and also C.  I don't notice any vitamin flavor, which is nice.The sugar content is pretty moderate (5 gm), mostly because you are spending a long time sucking on a small portion.I enjoy having these around during my work day.  I find that small hard candies are a nice little treat and energy boost throughout the day (for long days doing computer work, in my case).Likes:- Very tasty.- Moderate sugar and calories (10 minutes of enjoyment for 5 gm sugar and 20 calories).- B vitamins give me an energy boost.- Natural ingredients:  Sugar, corn syrup, milk, honey, butter, natural flavors, B + C vitamins.Dislikes:- The gooey center is a personal preference.. Sometimes I wish these were solid so they would last longer and not be quite so sweet at the end.

column9: Good-tasting, non-pill means of getting some vitamin B
column10: I was attracted to the idea of something that would help me get some B vitamins without gagging on gigantic pills.  Some Vitamin C is a bonus, but Vitamin C is pretty easy to find in non-pill formats.The caramel taste isn't as good as something like Werther's Original Hard Candies, 34-oz., but it does taste good.  And I like the honey-filling too.I like having a good-tasting, non-pill means of getting some vitamin B, though this is something I would have to hide from the kids so they don't just eat up the entire package.

If you think of this as good for you candy, it is ok.  They contain doses of several B vitamins and vitamin C.  As far as making you feel energized, they aren't an energy drink, but they do contain energy type vitamins. The taste is pretty good and I'm sure they are better for you than most candy.  They come in a convenient packaging that can be carried in your purse easily so you can grab when you like as a good alternative to hard candy.  Overall, they have some benefit and if you are in the market for a good way to get some extra vitamins, give these a try.

There is no question that people are finding different and new ways of finding the best in their vitamins. Now, they can be found in different places that can be sweet. That also is here in these Ambrosoli-Honees Energy Plus Vitamin Caramels. They do taste pretty good. It tastes like your sucking on a caramel piece with a drop of honey. They are a delight to taste, and they do have B and C vitamins. While you'd have to 3 of them to get a full serving of your Vitamins B6, B12 and C, they are a clever way of getting kids of taking their vitamins. Still, while they do cost a lot, they are worth the money. I think they are worth it, because they taste good, with the honey that makes them shimmer.Price: B-Taste: B+Overall: B
The flavor of this energy bar is good,but I was surprised to see such one candy bar when I open the package.I thought I can get a whole box.

These individually wrapped "candies" remind me of a candy called Milkfulls we used to buy in Canada. Not sure that they provide any medicinal value but they are very tasty and worked well as a cough drop or lozenge.  They have a sweet and slightly creamy taste but not a true caramel flavor.  My kids liked them too.

column9: Tasted Decent Enough but Seems Too Tiny to give Energy Boost
column10: I ate a pack of these last week and since I like the taste of honey they did taste pretty good to me - well actually I have to confess that I ate the whole pack in one sitting...see I had the munchies and these were the only thing I had in reach.  Actually, after I ate the whole pack I was still hungry.  Each piece is really about the size of a Starburst candy so my personal vibe was that eating a few tiny squares wouldn't be giving me any extra energy on top of all the other coffees, (diet) red bulls, and cliff bars I frequently consume.  They did taste pretty natural and I could taste the honey.  I might eat them again for a sweet tooth fix but at $1+ per pack and non-filling I'll probably stick to cliff bars and just secretly raid my office neighbor's starburst jar for a sweet tooth fix here and there.  Overall I give 3 stars out of 5 in consideration of price/value and other alternatives out there.

This candy tasted good. A real honey flavor. The ingredients don't state much honey though, mainly sugar. I liked knowing I was getting 33% of a few vitamins while eating it. I cannot feel any extra energy, but then who feels something when they take a vitamin? I'll tell you who, someone who should be seeing a doctor not eating candy. I take this candy after a meal so I can absorb the vitamins better. Vitamin C and B6, B12 can be taken at higher doses without side effects, so If I take a multivitamin at diner time on top of this, It won't be overkill. While the product stated pack of 24. I only got 1 pack. This is not a reflection on the product, but it may be a reflection of the ordering process of this product.

I liked the taste of the caramel flavored energy chews, but I did not notice any significant energy improvement. I'm a candy eater and I found myself wanting to eat them all at one time (greedy, I know), but I didn't.  Maybe if I had, I would have gotten that jolt I was looking for.  Overall, the taste is good, but there was no noticeable change in energy.

For the most part.  These candies are tasty, although one of the selling points (honey in the center) seems largely pointless to me.  It's what I enjoyed least, actually.  However, they are tasty, and since they're packed with B vitamins, you could certainly do a lot worse.  20 calories each and a third of your B's with each one.  No weird aftertaste, either.  Worth your money, definitely.  If they could just do something about the honey...

column9: Good but only a hint of caramel
column10: Tasty candy but there is just barely any taste of caramel and I really didn't get any kind of energy boost (maybe for someone who doesn't use much sugar or caffeine these would provide a real boost). But they are good and the honey center is very soothing and tasty.

column9: Is my "jump start" of the B vitamins in this candy or possible placebo effect?
column10: I don't know.All I know is that these energy drops taste really good, no weird aftertastes, and I feel a "pep in my step" after only having just one.I am going to start getting these as a much welcomed alternative to energy drinks and shots.  All my body needs is some B vitamins in the form of something tasty.This will be a main staple in my book bag.

column9: Not a huge boost in energy
column10: First - when I received these, I got a single package of 10 pieces of the product - not a "Pack of 24" - not sure what happened.  These taste really good, but I didn't notice any significant difference in my energy level.

I like the caramel better than the honey flavor, but both are tasty.  I guess there are vitamins in there, but it seems to me that this is candy.  I love the flavor and the chewy little honey nub inside.  However, I am not sure I get an energy boost anymore than I would with a regular piece of candy.

column9: Lots of vitamins, little energy, OK flavor.
column10: These are hard caramel flavored candies with a soft honey interior.  Laced with vitamins, I cannot see much energy benefit.  More energy in a tablespoon of honey.  Not a bad taste, but not great either.  Still, a sweet treat with vitamins?  I guess that's better than some alternatives.

I can't really say that these candies are giving me any more energy than I would get from having a Starburst, however, they do contain some vitamins and are caffeine free.  I have been taking one every afternoon as a pick-me-up instead of buying some garbage, and eating just one piece seems to do the trick. So if you're looking for something handy and better for you than just plain sugar, this is a very good option.  They're also very tasty which is definitely a bonus. I will be purchasing more of them in the future to keep in my purse whenever I need a little extra something.

column9: Good flavor with vitamin content - worthwhile
column10: First impression upon unwrapping, each piece is a bit on the small side.  Upon eating, it is as a hard candy which gradually melts in mouth with a good flavor while melting.  Finally, once the outside melts, the inside is soft and chewy and also has a good flavor. In that this product has some vitamin content in addition to an enjoyable flavor, I think it's a worthwhile buy, providing the price is not too high.

The product is a "granola bar" looking silver foil packet containing nine individually wrapped candy lozenges.  Each lozenge contains 20 calories of "sugar, corn syrup, milk, honey, and butter" (actually labelled that way, in that order, on the wrapper).  The product is actually manufactured in Italy by the G. B. Ambrosoli Ronago company, and imported by Andre Prost, Inc. of Old Saybrook, Connecticut.  The label goes on to say that "Honees" is a registered trademark of Andre Prost, Inc.At a time when people all across America are spending $ billions on little tiny bottles of caffeine marked "one hour energy," it appears that the Prost company is trying to cash in on the "energy" fad with a more honest approach that simply provides a blast of sugar. They have added vitamins B6, B12, and C to the product, so that three lozenges contains 100% of the daily requirement of these vitamins.Its very pleasant tasting.  Its got a nice caramel flavor, and the liquid honey center is a very nice reward at the end.  And I'm a person who enjoys the taste of honey and its benefits for a sore throat who is also aware of its high caloric density.  I was surprised that its only listed as the fourth most common ingredient; perhaps because honey is so much more expensive than sugar.For someone who normally enjoys hard candy (I'm not - my dentist advises against it.), "Honees Energy Plus" might be a nice addition to the product choices.  When I ordered the product, I was expecting a granola bar type experience, not a hard candy.  I suppose they are hoping people will overlook the calories to focus on the vitamins and energy.  Its a worthy idea.  Yet the candy, energy, and throat lozenge categories are all busting with product entries and are very competitive.

When you read the ingredient listing on the package you quickly learn that sugar, corn syrup and honey are listed as part of the ingredients of this "healthy" hard candy with a chewy center. At 5 grams of carbohydrate per piece they are not bad as candies go. Healthy? well if three of them gives you your recommended daily requirement of Vitamins B6,B12,and C then they are healthy enough for that. Plusthey could be seen as a good replacement for cough drops and throat lozenges. Thetaste is okay, something between honey and caramel not enough of either to make an impact though.

I liked these. Unlike some of the reviewers, I immediately tasted the caramel. The addition of vitamins is a plus, but alas, they contain lots of sugar, so there is a trade off. The honey center is a nice touch. According to the product description, three of the drops provide 100% of vitamins B12, B6 and C. But many of the other needed vitamins are missing, so you'd still need an additional supplement if your goal is to get all of your daily vitamins. But if you're a caramel and/or honey fan, you may want to give these a try.

column9: A sweet honey drop of energy.
column10: Ambrosoli-Honees Energy Plus Vitamin Caramels are a sweet way to get your daily dose of natural energy (a non-caffeinated treat) along with Vitamins B-12,B-6 & C.  9 doses are included in each pack (3 drops equate 100% of your daily B-12,B-6 & C recommended intake of your daily Vitamins.  Each caramel (not carmel) drop has a honey center and it tastes good (only 20 calories).  I enjoyed the way it tasted and it gave me a nice shot of energy to give me that extra boost that I need to get me through the day.  So, if you're looking for a daily pick me up that wont make you crash or a tasty and convenient way to get your daily vitamins then you will want to get some Ambrosoli-Honees today!Made in Italy.

This is nothing but candy "fortified" with a nearly insignificant amount of vitamins. A little honey. Some sugar. Some corn syrup. And a few grains of vitamins mixed in. Candy. You'd get the same energy from just about any caramel candy, and the vitamins are so scant that it's not going to impact you one way or the other.But put a couple of grains of vitamins in candy, call it "energy plus", and it apparently makes it easier for some folks to justify having a piece of hard candy. And since it doesn't taste as good as a good quality caramel candy, some folks can convince themselves that the poor taste is the trade-off for candy that's "good for you."If you want some candy, get some good candy. At least you'll enjoy your vice more. If you're looking for something healthy, this isn't it.

Am not quite sure  to whom we should direct the 3 rating.  It clearly says "pack of 24" - we received 9!  Also, am still waiting for that burst of energy.  If this had been advertised as a candy it would have received a higher rating as it is tasty - thin hard carmel coating over honey.  Lovely to melt in your mouth.  Will add to these comments if the energy  burst comes later. However,it did  not note that it was delayed. ;-)
This is a good grocery for us.If you want to cook Chahun,your choice is so good!But it's a little expencive.

I was so disappointed when I received my package.  I ordered these for my husband for Christmas as he loves them but I was expecting the 'LARGE' fireballs.  I wish the distributors would specify in their description whether the fireballs are 'small' or 'large'.  I was under the assumption that since it was a 3lb bag, it would be the large fireballs.  I still have the container from the last time I ordered Atomic Fireballs and it had the weight listed as 3lbs so I thought I would be receiving 3 lbs of large fireballs.  I am still debating on whether to return them or not.  I am going to wrap them and let my husband open them for Christmas.  I will leave it up to him whether or not I will return them and search yet again for the 'LARGE' fireballs.  What a bummer because I love them too..the big ones!
I always have a pocketful of these with me at work.  I'm hooked!  I used to be a smoker and being able to pop a fireball in my mouth drastically cuts down on cravings at work.

It's expensive, and it can be had for less elsewhere, but it's really, really, really good. If you have to refrigerate it, it turns very hard but softens up easily in the microwave.We sent some to my son-in-law who is stationed in Afghanistan. His unit went completely ape over it! If you have a soldier serving somewhere that relies on "drops" for grocery, this is a super treat for them!

I ordered a case of 24 and every single can was severely dented on the seams.  This drastically reduces the shelf life.Update:  I got a response from vendor and they said they would take care of the problem
This is really good stuff! had some last year and got myself a case for the long haulI would recommend this to anyone

I keep some at work. Another reviewer mentioned it being hard to chew when it's stale, never happens in our household, but try adding to soup or a pot of beans.  Do think outside of the bag. You can even just moisten it and zap for a moment in the microwave.

Ok, to preface this, I AM A VEGETARIAN. With that being said, I haven't had REAL beef or turkey jerky in quite some time and I have been missing it dearly. Having tried many vegetarian jerkies I can honestly say that this is by far the best! Most soy based jerkies are strangely on the oily side and the flavors are usually off. Being a "dry style" jerky fan I am pleased with the chewiness of Stonewall's and the WILD flavor. I have tried most of the other varieties of Stonewall's but none seemed to please me as much as the WILD. I'm also on Weight Watchers and have found that they are fairly low on points (4pts per bag) and are a great source of protein for vegetarians (14g). Be warned, the WILD is quite WILD, spicy spicy but in a good way!

The Hot Pastrami flavor is divine!  I like spicy things and just ordered another shipment of these because I went through them faster than I had anticipated.  They are moist and chewy, but not so chewy that you're still chewing to make it swallowable after all the flavor's gone.  I think they struck a nice balance.A caveat: If you're used to Tofurky Jurky or Primal Spirit, these will strike you as a little bit airy.  Also, these are a bit higher in fat than the other brands: 8 or 9 grams per 160-calorie package.  These ones don't really feel too oily in your mouth, though.

This is a great jerkey substitute if you're vegetarian. The problem is, when it is stale, it's very hard to chew* (but still tastes good). When it is fresh, it is absolutely awesome.Stonewall's is my favorite brand of vegetarian jerkey. If you don't like your jerkey hot, I suggest you try mild or teriyaki. Otherwise, this is the stuff for you!*Edit: Someone suggested heating in microwave for about 10 seconds to soften it, and that works beautifully!

It is not easy to find healthy protein-laden foods, particularly snacks, that are vegetarian and tasty.  Stonewall's Jerquee fits the bill.  It is exceptionally convenient to pack in my carry-on bag when I travel.  This is more than a review.  This is a heartfelt "thank you" to the maker!  Well done.

I usually love these little treats, but the ones i got must have been sitting around at amazon for a year or so, because they were really hard and  unedible. had to give most of them to the dog :(  However, the expiration date had not expired (SELLBY NOV07), so i would say Stonewall's needs to move their expiration date up a few months.

column9: Pretty good if you don't like meat :)
column10: I thought this was pretty good if you don't like meat and still want something that is "chewy".I don't know what the other poster is talking about when he/she said it was "airy" as I have not noticed that at all.It is not as tough as real meat would be, and the Teriyaki flavour is really good too.I did find the Jerquee to be a bit greassy as they do use some oil in it.But I have had people that do eat meat try this and they really did like it. I would buy this product again!
The absolute best vegan jerky around and believe me I've tried them all. The heat is perfect.

column9: I could eat the whole case in a day!
column10: My local health food store started selling these 10 years ago and then stopped to focus more on vitamins instead of food!So now I order these directly from Lumen and usually get the case of "over and unders" which contains packages that they can't sell to stores due to the weight being off. This is your best bet since I read reviews on here of receiving them stale off amazon.The best flavors are the original mild, bbq beef and the teriyaki beef. I HATE the Cajun varieties, they are so dry and tough to chew.They are high in fat so I usually have to make my husband hide them from me since these are a rare treat for us in the house, I could eat 4-5 bags in a row!Caution if you eat too many bags over a period of a few days, you may experience gas!Try ordering direct and you'll be enjoying the BEST veggie jerquee there is in the US!!!!PS These are made in Louisiana, could you ask for anything more authentic besides the real thing (meaning meat)

I loved the small size of the bags to bring along when I hike, paddle or any time I am going to be needing a snack!  Especially ideal if you are a vegetarian but even my non vegetarian friends enjoy them, once they try them.

If you're looing for a nice inexpensive jerky treat, you'd be hard pressed to find better. Stonewall's original and stonewall's original mild are some of the best tasting jerkey you'll find. What's best, is that this product is meat free. So for all you vegans out there this is especially a great treat idea. The package here is a store display container.  I keep them in the closet and when we remember we have them, it makes a perfect snack.  I think we'll be working on the box for about 2 month and that's with two jerkey freaks eating them.

The texture on these things is all off.  For one, they're incredibly airy.  I am a huge fan of Primal Spirit and Tofurky Jurky, and had been used to denser vegan jerky when I first tried these.  It felt like I was chewing air.  Also, because these are higher in fat (8-9 grams per 160 calorie package), they are a bit oilier.  Coupled with the airiness, when you bite down on these, you can feel the oil oozing out of the little nuggets into your mouth, which isn't too pleasant.I don't think the flavor is anything special, either.  To be fair, I'm not sure what chicken tastes like or is supposed to taste like, but there are plenty of wonderfully flavorful vegan and vegetarian products out there.  This is not one of them.
I love this stuff! The texture of this reminds me of real meat.  So if you are a new vegetarian you might want to try it!  I like mild and teriyaki the best!  Makes a great snack!

column9: It does the job as chew-toy for vegans
column10: An ethical workout for the jaw.  It tastes a little sweet, but teriyaki is supposed to.  Of course even considering a "vegan jerky" is to knowingly enter a state of sin.  This is a long-shelf-life processed snack food, not carrots and celery pulled fresh from the organic garden, but hey, no refrigeration required.
I didn't like these at all.  They're too hard and chewy with a weird texture.  I wouldn't recommend this product.

I've tried two flavors - Pepperoni and Original Wild - and have enjoyed them both.  The texture's pretty good - nice and chewy.  The moisture level is okay, but it could be improved by being just a tiny bit more moist. There's also a little bit of an aftertaste (which I didn't find to be unpleasant, but some might).  The spice level on the Pepperoni and Original Wild flavors were perfect. The Original Wild was medium hot, so it might be a little too much for some.  I loved it though.  I recommend that people try to buy this locally before spending a lot of money on it.  I bought mine from a local vegan store online, then discovered that a large grocery chain carries it in their health food section.

The "Original Wild" is a bit spicy for me, but "Original Mild" is spectacular, and Teriyaki Beef even better. Also like the spicy chicken one. I've tried all the veg jerky products and bewildered that none of the others come even close to this one for quality of flavor and texture. The others are loaded with sugar and taste more like candy than jerky; a couple of them are outright slimy; one was hard as a rock and flavorless. But the only time Stonewall's Jerquee ever displeased me was when the Poulsbo Market used a paper-punch to create holes along the top edge and hung them on a peg to dry out -- which I didn't realize until I got them home and they'd all been turned into hard lumps (which I ate any way). So now I have to buy them on amazon. I'll still get the fresh sushi at Poulsbo Market, that stuff's a dream, but what possessed them to poke holes in packaged foods???

I have always liked these but I haven't had them in years.  Today, I was hungry and saw them at the natural market checkout counter.  I got the flavor "spicy 'chicken'" and LOVED it.  It is clear that this is a love or hate product.  I buy Primal Strips when in need of a snack I can eat in the car and they are just ok...oily and get stuck in my teeth.  Flavor is just OK.  Stonewall's are drier and puffier and chewier but somehow, don't get stuck in my teeth.I am on a low-carb diet and these are only 7 g of carbs for 13 g of protein.  I am getting a case of the original mild since it is Prime.  Would like to see more flavors available on Prime.Definitely suggest buying a small pack first given the love/hate aspect.

I've been eating this stuff here and there for many years.  I purchased a packet at the grocery store and the product was speckled with mold.  Unfortunately I didn't realize this until I popped a piece into my mouth whereupon I instantly realized something was very wrong.  It was not expired.  I traded it in or another which was also moldy. ick.

I love other brands of vegetarian jerky. This one, I hate. It is spongy instead of chewy and smells and tastes like concentrated, stale, off-brand dog food. I could not get this funky crap out of my mouth fast enough. I should also mention that I'll eat just about anything, including bugs and grass. If it came down to it, I'd turn to them before ingesting another piece of this food-like substance.

I just purchased this jerky from a local store because they recently quit carrying the kind I like in my town. I ate a piece and thought it was disgusting. I wanted to give it a chance, so I ate a couple more pieces. It has a grainy, nasty texture and a terrible burned BBQ sauce flavor. For some bizarre reason it's made out of soy flour instead of strips of soy.The best soy jerky I've ever had is Tasty Eats jerky, since it's chewy and had a wonderful flavor. Flavor is of course subjective, but personally I thought the taste of Stonewall's is terrible, and the consistency is nasty. It tries too hard to look like meat, which I feel is pretty irrelevant to the demographic of people that will be eating it in the first place. Luckily it's Gluten-Free, so hopefully I can pawn the leftovers on my boyfriend...

I think its interesting how spread out the reviews are on this product.  I guess its one of those love it or hate it type things.  Personally, I LOVE this jerky and cannot get enough!!  My favorite flavors are the hot pastrami and teriyaki. You do have to chew quite a bit but its not the same weird chewy texture some other veg jerkys have, like primal strips.  I hate primal strips but I had them about 10 years ago and never ate once since, so if the formula has changes on those then disregard...  So maybe try a small bag of this before ordering in bulk.

I picked these up at Natural Grocers because I used to really love jerky, but am now vegetarian for four years, and I didn't like the Primal strips enough to re-purchase. I purchased the Original Mild and the Teriyaki flavors.The texture of these is spot on if you like toughier jerky (I do), although the outside has a weird sort of clumpy coating. Unfortunately, the taste is TERRIBLE. Both varieties honestly tasted like dog food. I also had two friends (one recently vegetarian, the other not) try them, and they said exactly the same thing. My friend's toddler-aged son loved them, though.I liked these even less than the Primal strips, and would not recommend them.
I bought all different flavors of jerky from this brand and it is sooo gross. I had to spit it out. Never again.

The overall flavor is pretty good (esp. for being vegetarian) and the texture was fine but, the one I tried, "original wild" was just TOO (spicy) hot! I don't mind a little heat but this was rediculous.  My mouth was burning for an hour afterwards.  This may be "fun" for some but not for me!  And I will give the "mild" a try - just to be fair).

column9: Stonewall's has had mold on it lately
column10: I use to buy a lot of this jerquee from Amazon, but for the past two months or more every shipment has been bad.The stuff has been covered in toxic mold, and I had to throw it away and get my money back.I will be ordering it direct from the factory from now on.I have read here others have had the same problem buying it via Amazon.Other than that, is is the best tasting jerquee out there.

The product I bought from amazon was old and moldy.  When I called the company (Luman Soy Foods)they replaced the old product and took care of me.  The product is great, just get it from the company directly!

column9: product was moldy, but company willing to fix problem
column10: I think the jerky would have been good, but...The packages I received contained jerky that had fuzzy white stuff growing on it. None of the packages had a read-able expiration date. The clearest packaging shows Aug 2011 (which means the product still had 6 months left in its life). When I contacted Lumen, however, I did get an email and phone call from them expressing their concern about my complaint. The man I spoke with was genuinely interested in investigating the problem. The company directly sent me three free packages to replace some of the moldy ones.

The seasoning is good, but the texture is not to my liking; it's almost spongy, and microwaving did not improve the texture for me. It is a little too dry and chewy, and has a weird aftertaste. I have not tried the other versions of this jerky. If you prefer a dry and chewy veggie jerky, I would go with the Vegan Dream brand. They have a sampler pack, with 6 different flavors. Also, as I follow weight watchers online, the 1.5 oz package has 4 points, with 8 grams of fat, 152 calories, 3 grams of fiber. There are lower calorie veggie jerkies available, if that is a concern for you.

I used to order bulk bags directly from the company years & years ago, but the shipping was a killer.  And I tended to eat about 5 servings at a sitting.  Through Amazon, I get 16 nice one-serving packets & free shipping.  I use it in rice or noodle dishes (shred it & add near the end of cooking). This is terrific stuff!!  I prefer the Hot Pastrami, but try a few of the others to see which you like best.

column9: Addictive and Actually Gluten Free (despite label)...
column10: This stuff is like crack.  There's no other way of describing just how delicious it is.  If it gets old, it gets a little hard, but they never sit around long enough to get old at my house.  I order this constantly and sometimes they run out, which leaves me craving it and miserable-- or begging my local health food store to dig in their back room for stray bags.  It's THAT good!!!  The only catch on Amazon is it's ingredients list wheat (in the soy sauce) as an ingredient, but the kind I've been getting are also labeled gluten free on the front.  I'm fairly confident it's a typographical error, because I've been eating it for a year now and no gluten reaction!  Enjoy!!!

i had high hopes for this stuff. i have tried several types of veggie jerky, in search of the tough, fibrous, highly seasoned jerky of my old meat eating days. granted, my memory is likely hazy as i haven't eaten meat for about 20 years. however, this stuff is NOT like beef jerky. true, they are a bit hard and chewy. and they are very flavourful, but....in my opinion, not in a good way.if you have ever had those dehydrated soy slices made by "so soya" (and others) then you know what these are. take those slices, marinade and fry or bake, and you've probably got something like this jerky. they have a distinct flavour - i really can't pinpoint exactly what flavour it is, but it is consistent in all of the varieties and it is not too pleasant. i found the tofurky jerky to have a better flavour and nicer dense texture, but i think my search for the ideal jerky shall continue.
I like to take Jerquee on trips since it doesn't need refieration.  This is one of the more spicy flavors which I really like.  I bought an entire case for my last camping trip
This isn't my favorite veggie jerky, but it's OK. I like the size of the packages. It's great for international travel when you don't know what the food options will be.
Try it--You'll like it. I buy a case of this stuff 3 or 4 times a year. Great snack on the trail or when I travel abroad.

column9: It's good but I ordered MILD and they sent WILD
column10: I love the mild and ordered it but received WILD. I ate it anyway but it's not as good.
I was looking for a meat free alternative to jerky that had a little kick to it. This item fits the bill!

I like all the Stonewall Jerquee products. Very tasty and satisfying to chew. Easy to pack, toss in a purse, travel bag, etc. Helpful for vegan's/vegetarians on the go, looking for protein away from home.
My title for this review says it all.  I like the Stonewall's Jerquee products, but this flavor is just too hot for my mouth.

column9: Not as good as other flavors. . .
column10: . . But, it could just be my taste buds (or lack there of).  I like the Stonewall's Jerquee items very much, just not this particulare kind.

column9: There isn't to much I can say . . .
column10: So far STonewall's Jerquee is the best of this sort of item I've found.  I always have it on hand.

As with all foods, your mileage may vary with this product depending on freshness and all that. I didn't much care for it at first, but I found it to be an acquired taste and I actually do like the product now.It can be a bit greasy, but word has it that if you let greasy 'jerky' products sit out overnight in the open air that it helps with that. I've never had an issue with it, so I don't know for sure, but I suppose it'd be worth a try if you like the taste but find it a bit oily.All in all, compared with some of the gross real-meat jerky products I've tried, this stuff is pretty good. But don't take my word for it, try it out for yourself.
I bought this for my son and he loves it!!!  A great snack, or a little something to have a long with lunch.

column9: Not as good as the "Wild" flavor
column10: These are tasty but not nearly as good as the "Original Wild" flavor. They were also quite stale when they got to me.

The first split second after popping one of these in to my mouth wasn't so bad. Then reality set in. The taste that overcame my mouth was honestly the worst I think I've ever experienced. I can't even describe it. I immediately spit it out and promptly tossed the two packages I bought. Yuk!

I COULD rate this item but "Mild" wasn't what I received.  The sealed box that said "Mild" on the outside actually contained "Wild" packets.  What a disappointment.  I was able to sell the item to a friend who liked it.  Order with caution.

when i first tried this, i like it right away!  great option for vegetarians and vegans especially if you used to eat meat and enjoy foods with tough textures.  the peppy pepperoni is my favorite flavor out of all of them but the rest are good too.

column9: What the hell is wrong with these reviewers?
column10: I've had plenty of fake meats, and i like primal strips, these, like others said, as well as all of their flavors, looked and tasted like a dog treat, they smell awful too, it was extremely disgusting i almost puked.
Awful taste it was soft and airy I fed it to my dogs.

I have no idea how someone can give this anything over 1 star.  This vegetarian jerkey is HORRIBLE!  As other reviewers mentioned...it tastes and smells like pet food...specifically, dog food.  I bought this for my g/f and she spit out the first bite.  We threw away the entire package.  What a waste of hard earned money.  I think the people that work for this company are reviewing this item, b/c it is disgusting.  Don't take my word for it...go buy some, but use it as a gag gift
The coffee bean direct dark house blend is excellent and no bitter aftertaste.  Love the convenient 5 lb bags which is a great buy for a big coffee drinker.  Love it!

With my favorite brand no longer available, I decided to try the Coffee Bean Direct.  The dark house brew had a pleasing flavor, a hint of sweetness and no bitterness.  All in all, a little better that my usual brand, and at a respectable price. The 80 oz. bad is large and should last at least a month, but being bagged, refrigeration is a must.  A finely ground, dark roast, it even looked appealing when I opened the bag.  So unless you are into grinding your own, this is a solid choice, for a strong, bold cup of coffee.

column9: A mellow way to start your morning
column10: Coffee Bean Direct Dark House Blend, Ground Coffee, 80-Ounce BagI've got to say it is really nice to occasionally be able to by my coffee from Coffee Bean Direct already ground. Sometimes you don't wantto hear a grinder running early in the morning. That said besides the convience of ground coffee, I really enjoy the mellow flavor and taste of House Blend. And to me it is a good value. The coffee always shows up when expected and it really makes a good gift to all on my list.
I love coffee, and have tried many high end coffee's and this stacks up with the best.  The price is great and the service is impecable.  Thanks for a great product.

column9: My favorite of all potato chips
column10: First, I wouldn't trust anybody's opinion on a food item because everyone has different tastes. Secondly, these chips are awesome and you should buy them because I say so.  Okay, well, actually, I suggest you go buy one bag somewhere prior to buying a dozen bags and finding out you don't like them.  I do love these chips though.  Most Vinegar/Salt chips are too wangy or tart for me.  These chips have a mildly tart, slightly sweet vinegar flavor.  Also I am a salt-aholic and these chips satisfy my salt cravings perfectly. Texture is similar to other kettle type chips - plenty crunchy.  Totally yummy!  I'm salivating just thinking of them.

I am usually indifferent to potato chips, but these are the exception.  I first tried them when visiting a friend in Colorado and thought they were delicious.Don't order them if you've never tried them, because they are not like other salt & vinegar chips, and if that's what you're expecting you'll be disappointed.  The malt vinegar gives the chips a slight sweet taste which goes quite nicely with the salt - for those of us who like these chips, anyway.Incidentally, this is is a good price for these chips.  Assuming you can get free shipping, it works out to about $1.60 per bag, which is cheaper than you'd ever find them in the store.

These just arrived today so we immediately broke into them. They are awesome. The vinegar is pretty subtle compared to some other vinegar & salt chips, which is actually nice. You don't get that sort of acidic burning feeling on your tongue when you eat them, which allows you to eat more. Uh-oh! If you are after a real hefty vinegar flavour, this may not suit you. Still worth a try because they are yummy!

These are the worst potato chips I have ever had. They are way, way too salty. And, to make matters worse, the manufacturer adds fructose sugar to the recipe, which adds an inappropriate sweet note. I would definitely not recommend these chips. Luckily, I did not buy a case. I picked up a single bag from my local grocer. I do not understand all the favorable reviews for this product! I think these chips are just awful!

These are very unique and oh SO GOOD! I only buy them on amazon, I try to resist because once they arrive I can't stop eating them! They have a great crunch, a typical kettle cooked chip, very thick with a great amount of salt and yes a slightly sweet vinegar taste. These are def malt vinegar, not white vinegar flavor. Absolutely the best, I can resist most chips but not these!

column9: how could you not love these?
column10: best chips EVER. if you don't love these delicious, crunchy, delectable items, you may not have a soul. Malt vinegar delights!!!
These be real good.  These be real, real good.  But I repeat myself.  I now have the required number of words.

Great tasting salt n vinegar chips. Not available in New Jersey stores so we buy them by the case. Packaged well; unique flavor, we have bought several cases over the last 6 months +++++. They need to get their distribution network in gear and this product will take off.

These are the best chips ever. Beware: you open a bag and before you know it you've eaten the whole thing. Trust me, it happens no matter how hard you try.  These chips are just the right level of saltiness, and the malt gives it a sweetness with the vinegar that is incredible.  If you've ever been to the Carolinas or other states down south and had malt vinegar on your french fries, this is sort of reminiscent of that. Love these chips.

column9: A true GOURMET chip... slightly sweet, but vinegary.
column10: My favorite by far of any "salt and vinegar" chip.  The fact that they use malt vinegar, just moves it up 10 levels. Very addictive.

Ordered these last week. If you are use to Lays Salt and Vinegar or most other brands these will not have a very good taste for you. My son ate one bag and so did I and we both said we thought they tasted funny. Will probable throw the rest out that's how bad they taste to us. The salt part is ok but the vinegar taste very sweet, almost sickening sweet.

I bought a bunch of this food to try out for my dog. The first day i noticed he has the worst gas i had ever smelled from him. And my dog isn't normally gassy. I alternated this food with the Rachel Ray food as well as normal dry dog food. Every day i fed him the chef michaels brand (i bought a few different flavors, and they all had a similar result) he gets gas, but is fine when fed other food. It was so bad i ended up giving away the remaining food i had bought.

I have two "dog nieces" that go absolutely crazy for Chef Michael, especially the beef versions - tenderloin, porterhouse, etc. The two get some mixed in with their dry food as a treat and, with a touch of hot water, it makes a nice gravy for their food.  I found it is easier to order this from Amazon, as not all pet food stores carry it.  Shipping was fast, and definitely convenient!

I love the Pecan Pumpkin Butter, and the Apple Butter.  It's not too sweet and has the perfect consistency.  I used the Pecan Pumpkin Butter to make a pie for Thanksgiving and it was delicious.  I used a Williams Sonima recipe, but their pumpkin butter was a lot more expensive.  I had a problem with a broken jar, but they quickly sent me a replacement.
Not quite enough salt for me but the best pistachios ive had from amazon I've tried so far. If anyone knows of better pistachios I'd like to know about. Please leave feedback with the brand.

Hello, my name is Tom, and I'm a pistachio addict.  I can't help myself and these are excellent pistachios.  Do me a favor and don't buy from here so there will be more for me... If I could grow pistachio trees in Illinois, I'd never leave my backyard. I can't control myself...

Got them just a day or two after buying them.they were gone in days! Everyone loved them!I will be buying more and in different flavors <3
These honey sticks are not only very good, but they are convenient to take anywhere.  I use them all the time in my tea.

column9: 2nd order not as good as first
column10: This was my second time ordering this product. I absolutely loved the first order. The second order however was a let down. The sticks were very difficult to open on both ends making for some pretty messy situations. While I will most likely order again I hope the seller has corrected this problem.

column9: Can't Get Enough of Dave's Burning Nuts
column10: Dave's Burning Nuts are so hot I could barely keep them in my mouth.  As an avid fan of spicy nuts, I've searched far and wide for some hot nuts that could properly satisfy my taste buds.  I have finally found my nut match in Dave's Burning Nuts.  Seasoned with salt, habanero chili, spices, onion, garlic and paprika, these nuts will explode in your mouth and blow you away.  Be careful when devouring these nuts, however, they're addictive.  One is just never enough.  But if you're not careful you'll find yourself with a burning mouth and an uncontrollable craving for more of Dave's Burning Nuts.  And no one likes to run out of nuts.  Especially when they're this tasty.  These nuts are a perfect snack for those enjoying them on the go or a relaxing afternoon in bed.  A great and delicious low calorie snack, these nuts will sneak up on you and find their way down your gullet.  The spicy/salty combination will leave your taste buds wanting more.  In this world, there are only two kinds of people.  Those who crave burning nuts and those who fear them.  Don't fear the nuts.  Embrace the nuts.  Pop them in your mouth and enjoy every delicious moment.  At $10.40 a can, you can't afford not to taste these burning nuts.

These aren't simply peanuts with a lot of heat.  They have a good flavor from the seasoning that makes them very savory, and then the heat becomes assertive after a few moments.  I enjoy them alone or will mix them into my favorite Chex Mix to make things interesting.  Probably my favorite spicy nut, and clearly better than the so-called Kick-A** nuts that have the donkey on the label.

These suckers sneak up on you in a serious way. Haven't met anyone yet who doesn't love the taste. After that, the camp divides into those who regret the burn and those who crave it. I set 4 cans of these outside my office, and they were devoured by our teams at work within days.P.S. Please get rid of that other idiot review here.

Excellent with warm sourdough whole wheat bread and very convenient.  One box easily serves three people.  Fast free shipping. The entire case arrived intact and well packaged.  Will order this again.

column9: Tasty as is, or use as a base
column10: The flavor of the soup struck me a bit sweet at first...sort of like pumpkin pie. But as I got used to the taste it really grew on me. This soup is lovely just as is, with lots of potential for interesting garnishes - a swirl of cream, toasted spicy pumpkin seeds, grated asiago cheese, coconut milk, panchetta....use your imagination, and serve it to admiring dinner guests!It also makes a welcome addition to chicken stock to thicken up homemade chicken vegetable soup. The flavor profile lends itself well to putting an Asian spin on my old classic recipe.Oh, and it also tastes awesome mixed half & half with Amy's chunky tomato soup.

This is a perfect lunch-sized tin of pasta salad.  The tins are vacuum packed with no need for refrigeration.  Better still, the lid is cardboard!  No messing with sharp metal edges or hard-to-pull tabs.The tins each come with a small spork and salt and pepper packets.  I enjoyed this product as a side for my lunch, although my wife might eat this by itself.  She thinks the product is perfect the way it is; I think it could use just a touch of seasoning.  The salt and pepper help, but I like to try different flavors - lemon pepper; poultry seasoning; Caesar salad dressing; and Italian dressing are some that I've tried.I can highly recommend this product.  Check out their salmon and vegetable version, too!

column9: Wonderful Meal for Those Who Appreciate Good Flavor!
column10: I was searching for something simple to give to my mother, I am a caretaker of a very fussy eater.  After reading the reviews on this, I thought I would give it a try....well, what a pleasant surprise! She loves them, particularly this one, I have tried one other one with her so far but she didn't like it like this one.  I originally was heating it up, but lately she's been eating them cold,,,,,,,,,likes them both ways.  Am so glad Amazon carries this, has made my life easier. Thanks!

column9: I like it, but it's a product of Taiwan...
column10: While I love the product, if you read the label carefully, you realize that this is product of Taiwan, not France. For those who try to avoid groceries from China/Taiwan/Hong Kong, thought I should let them know....

i love these! they are so good and i am even a VERY picky eater. they are very healthy too and make you feel very full. and as the package says, they are ideal for vegetarians like me! buy them all them time. love!

I would label this as emergency food, as in no food in the house and I'm hungry. Reminds me of chunky soups without the liquid.. but what do you expect from food that doesn't require heating and lasts forever? At least its healthy!
Flavor is pretty good.  But it is chocked full of mushrooms.  I don't like them.  I didn't like the sauce packet at all.  I wont order this one again, I will sick w/ the 3 bean one.
I have always enjoyed this fast on the go dish! The sauce adds the flavor that makes this seem home-made! Will buy again!
Great taste. A good item to keep in your refrigerator for a quick snack or with soup for a lunch. A bit expensive but a great time to keep in the frig.

I'm a college student and being in a field that requires a lot of my time, I usually can't make my lunch. The on the go tins are fantastic because I can just stick them in my backpack for an emergency lunch and they'll last forever. I think the pasta is really good, I eat it at room temperature with a little salt and the sauce. The sauces are always weird for the Gourmet on the Go containers (honey for salmon??) but most of the time they really add a lot of flavor. This one not so much, but it may just be me. The meal is a little tiny, and you don't feel "full" afterwards. But you don't feel hungry! So if you're set on that full feeling, eat an apple or small snack with it. I only gave it four stars because it's not delicious enough that I'll go out of my way to eat it.

column9: I like the brand, but I did not like this one
column10: I purchased the Salmon and veggies and the sweet corn, which are both pretty good, so I though I would give this a try.  Too bad I did not try one, instead I gambled and got the 6 pack.  Unfortunately I really don't like these.  I was thinking pasta salad, but what I got tastes more like pasta and canned beans or something.  I could not get more than a few bites in before I just chucked it.  I tried it cold, and then hot thinking it may be better - how wrong I was.  Later I found that they sell these at Whole Foods, which is a much better way to sample them.  Hey there's an idea, a sample pack, too bad they don't sell anything like that here.

I received the package in the mail today, tried one, and instantly loved it. These are amazing! They're very tasty, low in calories, and filling. I highly recommend it and it's one of the best precooked, instant food I've ever had. Not too salty which is definitely healthier. Great for weight loss. I will definitely be buying more in the future.

column9: Not as good as Salmon and three beans
column10: I love St. Dalfour brand ready-to-serve, but not this one. Almost want to throw up when I eat it. The salmon pasta and three beans are highly recommended on the hand.

I've tried this as well as many of the other choices, and they've all been good. The veggies are healthy and if you get one with beans & rice, the tuna or the salmon (which I haven't tried yet), you'll get a balanced meal. The best part? They all come with a plastic-covered small fork, salt & pepper and a gourmet sauce that's different for almost each variety.I rarely have time to make myself food to take with me, and being busy AND a diabetic, it's important that I have something to eat when I need it. This way, I'm not stuck eating junk or not getting enough to keep me going for awhile.The ONLY negative comment I have is that the cardboard box which covers the meal is rather flimsy, and also is open on the sides. So in a bag that's moving around, it sometimes can come apart, and then you have to search for the fork and condiments in your bag. Put it in a plastic bag so that you can easily find the items if it comes apart.
I have had the pasta and vegetables for lunch and it was very filling along with being very tasty. It is very easy to prepare and is also very good eaten right from the container.
Perfect size, taste, and price.  Great for Lunch, Snack, or even a Light Supper.  I will buy these again!
This is one of my favorite "ready to eat" meals. I love to add a few olives and maybe some marinated artichoke hearts. Very tasty and light.The veggies are delightful and so easy to prepare..

This is one of the best canned products I've eaten. Its quick and easy.It's low calorie (200 calories per can) and low sodium, yet satisfying and tasty.  I'll have it for lunch or a snack. I'll bring a couple of cans with me on trips, where it might be difficult to find healty things to eat.

Having had gastric surgery it's been difficult finding things that actually provide the nutrition required when I go to work in a fast paced health care setting. I've tried 6 different types of St.Dalfour and all have been great, gives me over two servings so I share healthy options. This is one of the best products I've found in a long time.

I fell in love with Krusteaz Almond Poppyseed muffins years ago when my mother made up a batch for the family. Much to my dismay, this particular Krusteaz flavor is difficult to find in my local supermarkets, with most stores opting to stock the Lemon Poppyseed variety but not the Almond Poppyseed.These muffins are fluffy and delicious, and they are very easy to make. There's nothing like enjoying a muffin hot out of the oven, which is a pleasure even the local bakery cannot provide!
These muffins bake up deliciously and are like bakery muffins, tender and moist. I prefer these to any other I have tried, and I'm pretty picky.

column9: Poppyseed Muffins With Great Crunchy Texture
column10: This mix produces a poppyseed muffin with great crunchy texture.  All you need is the mix, a cup of water, and an egg (although you can make an "extra rich & moist" version by adding 1/3 cup vegetable oil to the mix).  The box contains a large packet of poppy seeds, which you fold into the batter.  The finished muffins look exactly like the photo on the box:  lots of poppy seeds!The muffins have a strong almond flavor, which must come from almond extract, because it has a slight "chemical" or "medicinal" edge. This is fine with me, but some might not like it.  Each muffin has 240mg of sodium per muffin, so the mix is okay for persons on a low-to-moderate-salt diet, as long as they don't eat too many!The box also has instructions for using the mix to make almond poppyseed quick bread or pound cake. I've tried several of the Krusteaz muffin mixes, and they're all good, but this one is probably my favorite.
These are our favorite muffins.  I would encourage everyone to try these and they will thank me later.  We hope everyone finds this out.

I absolutely love this flavor best.  I don't add the poppyseeds to the mix.  Instead I add chocolate chips.  The muffins are rich, yummy, and so flavorful.  My family can't get enough.  Unfortunately I have to order this flavor online as it is not sold near me :( However, it is worth it to see my family smile :)
These are SOOOO good!  And I can't seem to find them in the grocery store any more, so I buy them a case at a time now.  They are just delicious almond muffins!
This is my favorite muffin mix.  Not only does my family love them, but I get compliments every time I make them.

column9: Not bad, but rather bland -- I added berries
column10: I am a big fan of Krusteaz muffin mixes -- I usually bake several dozen once a month or so (oat bran and fat-free banana are my favorites), then freeze them and have a couple for breakfast every morning (I nuke them on high for about 10 seconds each and they are ready).  I had never tried this kind before as it's not one my local grocery stores carry, so I bought a case from amazon.  The first time I baked them, they smelled AMAZING in the oven and I was looking forward to trying them.  Unfortunately, I was disappointed by the taste -- they were just very, very, very bland.  They tasted to me somewhat like vanilla muffins (I can't taste anything like almonds in them), but actually they didn't have much of a taste at all.With my second box, I added frozen mixed berries (blueberries, strawberries, blackberries, raspberries) to the mix -- I think about a cup or cup and a half of the berries (no need to defrost them first).  This improved the taste quite a bit, so I think this muffin mix just needs SOMETHING added.I will continue to add fruit (maybe nuts too at some point) to the 10 boxes I have left, but I doubt that I will order any more.  I really wanted to like these and am surprised no one else mentioned how bland they are.  (Maybe it's just me.)

Be careful what supplier you select because returns aren't allowed. I had ordered this chocolate several times via Amazon. From Amazon directly, the G&B bars (made in Canada) arrived promptly. Then in late 2009 my first (and last) order, fulfilled Nutricity, arrived a month after the order had been placed, and then only after an inquiry to the seller. The bars were dry, stale and hard, the color of cocoa powder rather than chocolate bars. Although the bars still had 10 months to go before expiration of the sell-by date on the wrappers, they were a disgrace to the good name of G&B. It may be that they had been stored improperly, or that the single paper wrapper used in the Italian plant (the Canadian maker uses an inner foil wrap) allowed too much air to get to the bars. Green & Black's is my new favorite dark chocolate--by a mile. I highly recommend it for anyone who wants to eat dark chocolate either for the health benefits it provides or for its delicately bittersweet flavor. This particular brand of dark chocolate tastes amazing.The company G&B is from Canada and is famous for organic, fair-trade, 70% dark chocolate. This particular bar has had the same recipe since 1998. It was previously labeled "vegan," but per the G&B website, the label for this bar no longer says vegan and indicates that milk is an ingredient because both their "milk chocolate and dark chocolate bars are made using the same production line...and a recent audit revealed that traces of milk residues can still be found on manufacturing equipment despite intensive cleaning." The ingredients listed on the package are: organic bittersweet chocolate (organic chocolate), organic raw cane sugar; organic cocoa butter; soy lecithin (emulsifier), organic vanilla extract; organic whole milk powder. There is a warning that because this is manufactured in a facility that uses nuts and peanuts, those with allergies to them should not eat this product.The question some may ask who love sweet, milk chocolate is, why pay more money (often quite a bit more) for dark chocolate such as this that doesn't taste sweet? The main reason for most people in the over-50 crowd is the health benefits to be gained from consuming dark chocolate. The more chocolate contained in a chocolate bar, the more of the good stuff--cacao--that you are getting. In short, the more "bang" for your "buck."Over the last four years there have been dozens of scientific studies analyzing and confirming substantial health benefits from a small amount of dark chocolate consumed daily. The latest findings from a Harvard study released in early 2011 indicate that as little as 6 gm. of dark chocolate (about 30 calories) is a sufficient daily "dose." (That is equivalent to about 1.5 of the tiny squares of this chocolate.) The original German studies in 2007 used Ritter Sport chocolate, but I haven't so far been able to discover which kind of Ritter's dark chocolate was used by the researchers. However, since Ritter's only makes two types, 50% cacao and 71% cacao, this product, at 70% cocoa, fits well within the parameters of that study.The health benefits of dark chocolate are due to the flavonoids contained in cocoa. Flavonoids act as antioxidants in the body, which both prevent and reduce inflammation. Over many years of medical research, inflammation has been found to contribute to or directly cause a host of diseases, including high blood pressure, heart disease, and cancer, as well as autoimmune diseases like arthritis.Flavonoids are found in the pigments of fruits and vegetables which give them their color. The darker and deeper the color of a fruit or vegetable, the greater the amount of flavonoids it contains. Cocoa is derived from the dark-brown cacao bean, which is the fruit of the tropical tree, theobroma cacao. In any chocolate product, such as this one, the higher the percentage of cocoa/cacao, the more flavonoids the chocolate contains.Dark chocolate such as this product is better for your health than milk chocolate because it contains more antioxidants, which are good for you, and less sugar, which is not good for you--especially if you have diabetes or are struggling with your weight.The FDA defines categories of chocolate based on how much cocoa/cacao is in a given product:1. Unsweetened chocolate with no additives is 100% cocoa. Most all brands of unsweetened baker's chocolate fall into this category. Their ingredient list will state simply, "chocolate."2. Bittersweet chocolate contains 35-99% cocoa (35% is the minimum), and it must contain less than 12% milk solids. There is a large range of products in this category, and the product names reflect the amount of chocolate they contain. Unsweetened chocolate is very bitter, and the more cocoa in a product, the less room for sugar, and the more bitter it will be. In order to avoid frightening off customers who are used to sweet chocolate, marketers often substitute the words "dark," "extra dark" or "intense" for "bitter" if that word is not paired with "sweet," for example as "bittersweet" or "extra bittersweet." This product lies at the top of this range.3. Sweet chocolate contains 15-34% cocoa (15% is the minimum), and it must contain less than 12% milk solids. It is sometimes also marketed as "dark chocolate," even though it has a much lower percentage of cocoa solids than bittersweet, which can cause consumers, in such cases, to purchase a product with less cocoa in it than they realized they were getting. Everything else besides the cocoa and milk solids is essentially sugar.4. Milk chocolate is only required to have a minimum of 10% cocoa, a minimum of 12% milk solids and 3.39% milk fat. The rest is sugar and milk.

column9: Amazon, Please Keep Selling This Chocolate Bar!
column10: I really love this chocolate bar.  I was delighted to find it sold once again thisChristmas season by Amazon and eligible for free shipping.  I would definitelykeep buying these bars by the box all year if it was sold by Amazon with free shipping.It is a good deal that way.  Thanks!

I've been eating dark chocolate since Hershey came out with Special Dark in the 70's. I discovered Dove, Ghirardelli, and more recently Scharffen-Berger, etc. A few years ago I tried this stuff and, honestly, I haven't looked back. column9: best dark chocolate, and low caffeine
column10: This is by far my favorite dark chocolate, and has become a regular item for me to get through my workday.  I also enjoy their 85% dark bar sometimes, but the 70% is the best all-around bar.  I don't find it bitter at all, unlike other common non-organic name-brand chocolates, which are often bitter even though they have far less cocoa content.  They also have a lot more sugar, and yet this low sugar bar is still less bitter.The other thing to note is that the caffeine content of Green & Black's dark chocolate is significantly less than the name brand non-organic ones -- 6mg per 40g serving, as opposed to 30+mg.  This is due to the other chocolates grinding up the whole bean including the shell instead of removing the nibs from the casing first, presumably to cut costs.  I'm guessing the shell is also what is adding to the bitterness of other chocolates.Now I just need to find a way to stock up on cases of these at a discount price.

I have been sampling a number of 70% dark chocolate bars recently and this is as good as any I have tasted, plus it is organic.  However I would urge anyone who wants to try this product to check your local grocer first.  I bought mine at my local Publix supermarket and it was much cheaper than any price on Amazon.  The same is true for Lindt and Ghirardelli chocolate.  Plus no shipping charges.

If you're looking for a tasty, silky dark chocolate, this one is a treat.  Nutritionists recommend having an ounce of 70% or above dark cocoa per day.  This has a rich, silky taste and texture.  Not too bitter and not too sweet.  I'm happy with 3 squares of it which is about 60 calories.  I picked mine up locally at the health food store in town and a single bar was over $4.00 to give you a price comparison.  My son was able to find them at Walmart but I don't like driving that far and would order in bulk to keep in the house. These are tasty.

column9: Save Green and Black's from Hersheys!
column10: Green and Black's chocolate has always been great - when I moved from the UK to the US I was very relieved to find it in my local Whole Foods - saved me carrying in pounds of it every time I flew back from the UK! Green and Blacks chocolate is smooth and full of flavor; luckily, Cadbury's, who bought them a couple of years ago, did not mess with the G&B formula, and let them produce their chocolate as they always had.Now if Hersheys buy Cadbury's, it may be a different story - Hershey's have ruined any small artisanal chocolate they acquired - it always becomes like Hershey's so-called 'chocolate' - a sickly-sweet, fatty, gross confection that does not deserve the name of chocolate. column9: Loved it til I found GM ingredients in it

Green & Black's bars are broken up into small, thick rectangles, which I'm not a big fan of because I like to nibble at flatter squares of chocolate, as opposed to those who like to break off the chunk and put in the mouth whole.  That being said, I really enjoy this 70% bar!  This bar is a great break from the extremely high fat content of the 85% bar (15g as opposed to 25g!), but still rich and has a beautiful chocolate taste with a wine-y undertone.  I usually don't go below 80% cacao content of chocolate bars because I believe the lower percentages are too sweet, but I do like to have this bar on occasion, and it's one of my favorite plain chocolate bars in the 70% range.
