I've given this unique dog treat "4 stars" instead of five as an average based on the varied reactions from my two small dogs. The smaller Malti-poo loved the treat and from his reaction would give it "5 stars". He immediately licked the roller, received the treat, and wanted more. Our Cavalier King Charles Spaniel is a pickier eater in general and wouldn't even try it at first. He finally did, but didn't seem to like it. We have the chicken flavor and it may be he just didn't like the flavor.Since our Malti-poo likes it so much, I have just ordered the three-pack that has chicken, liver, and bacon flavors. The three-pack is a better value than the individual packs and I'm hoping our Cavalier will like one of the other flavors better than the chicken. This is a unique idea to reward dogs with a treat without filling them up like traditional dog treats.** Update:  I ordered the three-pack and my Cavalier definitely likes the bacon flavor much better than chicken!

I came across this PetSafe Lickety Stik and decided to give it a try.  We just got an 8 week old Bassett Hound puppy and decided to try out this Lickety Stik as a training reward due to its low calorie content.  Bassets are know to get fat quick so a low calorie reward is needed as Bassetts basically only respond to food.Basically, this thing has the same construction as a stick of roll-on deodorant.  You turn it upside down, the liquid inside saturates the ball in a second or so and your dog takes a lick or two of the ball.  It works fantastically for training a puppy or dog.  We got the bacon flavor and she absolutely loves it.The puppy loves it and will do anything to get a lick of this thing.  It smells terrible to us(a really disguisting rancid bacon odor)but she absolutely adores it.  The price of $8 may seem a little high, but we've have been using the same Stik for over a month now, numerous times each day and we still have a third of it left.  We will definitely be buying more of these.Lickety Stik is a fantastic product that is great for training or just a treat.  Highly recommended!

column9: Good idea for certain dogs/needs, but...
column10: As other reviewers have mentioned, this looks like a bottle of roll-on deodorant. It's not quite what I was expecting. You have to squeeze it a little to get the liquid to flow, and then the dog can lick at the roller ball, similarly to how a hamster would drink from its water bottle. It works well enough, and my dog likes the taste okay. It seems to bother her that she can't chew on it, and it bothers me that I can't just hand it to her and let her go to town on it. Yes, it's convenient and non-messy to carry around. For my dog, the low-calorie aspect isn't necessarily a good thing. For example, when I take her on a hike, she runs around like crazy, so I actually want her to get some calories from her treats. The other times I give her treats, I'm usually giving her something chewy that will help remove dental plaque. So overall, this isn't a great option for my particular dog. If your dog has a weight problem and you like to give it treats, this is probably a good alternative for you. This isn't something that I'll purchase again myself.

column9: Just don't set it next to your roll-on deodorant... :)
column10: Imagine doggie treat flavored underarm deodorant.... have to squeeze just a bit to get the roller wet, then turn upside down and let the dog lick it. Unique idea.  Would probably be useful as a training tool. Our dog definitely likes it.  I imagine this works best as a daily treat. I shudder to think what would happen if you let the roller dry out, dog ends up with a tounge rash trying to push the roller past the dried out spot... or worse, squeeze to hard and drip doggie treat juice all over!! I'm just saying...  :)All in all, worth a try for the dog that has everything or just needs a change of taste...All the best,Jay

column4: Sarah Vigil Swiger "Author of The Divine Plan"
column9: One out of two dogs love this stinky treat!
column10: I have two dogs, one Black Labrador and one Chihuahua.  The Lab can't get enough of this stinky treat and even tries to grab it from me with her teeth.  She will lick on it all day if I let her. The Chihuahua sniffs it and snubs it. She couldn't be less interested. So, one out of two dogs loves this stinky treat.  Humans, on the otherhand, hate the strong smell.  I think it's fun and can imagine it is a great treat substitute for obese dogs who need to watch their calorie intake. If you aren't adverse to strong odors you'll love the handiness of this Lickety Stik!

Like other reviewers have said, this may take a short time for your dog to get used to. The dog learns to lick the roller ball and get to the juices. This may not be as satisfying a treat as doggy biscuits, but I can see this product being useful for training. For instance, if your dog pulls on the leash when you go for walks, stop and call the dog to you. If he listens, let him have a few licks before continuing. I can also see it being useful for dogs who are overweight and whose owners want to cut back on calories yet can still give the dog a little treat for good behavior.

I am only reviewing the Bacon flavor, but my dogs picked up on how this works pretty quickly and love the taste of it.  At first they wanted to bite the bottle and chew it like a treat but I worked with them for about a minute or so and they got down that you only lick it.  I have 3 dogs and all three of them liked the taste of it.  I like it because it seems like a more personal treat than just a dog biscuit.  I recommend this!

column9: My Yorkies think it is yummy, but I think it is inconvenient
column10: Both of my finicky yorkies love this treat, but I don't!  It smells awful and I have to hold it for them to enjoy it, unlike other treats that I toss to them and let them enjoy while I enjoy a little peace and quiet.  Also, the liquid gets in their "beard" so the odor of the treat lingers even after I tuck the bottle back in the treat cupboard.  It is rare for both of my dogs to agree on a treat and it is fun to watch them enjoy it, but it is inconvenient.  I will not likely repurchase this.

I am of the curious sort when it comes to dog treats and new ways to reward dogs so I jumped at getting this product.Lickety Stick arrived and three dogs were eagerly sitting in front of me; a cocker spaniel, a norwegian elkhound, and an australian shepherd.I unwrapped the stick and squeezed a little juice out of the tube onto the roller. I presented it to all three dogs. The cocker spaniel and the aussie eagerly licked away. The aussie licked away so much the cocker needed a wet cloth over the top of her head due to dropping juice on her head. The elkhound however, wanted no part in it.After a couple days of using it and trying it out I am left with the premise that it's an interesting take on a a dog reward - but in the end, the execution and possibility of making a mess leave this treat stuck in the treat drawer. I don't see myself buying these in the future.

column9: A Little Weird, but my Yorkie LOVED it.
column10: I guess I didn't really read the description of this product very well, but this was not what I expected! It is like a little roller ball of deodorant only it is filled with liquid log treats. (this one is bacon) It was easy to open, but I did have to squeeze the bottle a little and then roll the ball around to get the initial liquid to come out. Once my dog realized what she was supposed to do, she was ALL OVER IT. In fact, she got so excited that she made her self sick. I'm saving this one for an "every now and then" treat.

column9: Not sure it's worth the trouble
column10: My little dog (a Shih Tzu) seemed to have trouble licking the rollerball consistently enough to fully enjoy the treat.  Her inclination was to try to bite the top - and I'm wondering if that's what most dogs would try to do.  Of course, a dog can't tell you in words if they like something - you have to go by behavior.  And when we took this away from our dog, she really didn't protest like she does when it is a favorite treat.The premise behind this product is interesting - and I can understand why the idea of a rollerball made sense.  I'm just not sure it all works together well enough.  I can't envision seeking this out and purchasing it for my pet.

column9: OK, maybe not so great for large dogs
column10: I tried this on my mom's dog while he went through his resume of tricks, but since his mouth is bigger than the Lickety Stik he kept trying to bite it.  He got annoyed after a few tricks when he realized I wasn't going to give it to him and wandered off to find my mom who was holding actual treats.

What a great idea for a treat.  Lickety Stik is constructed like a roll-on deodorant with a flavored dog treat inside.  Hold the Stik upside down and my dog licked away at it.  It is low calorie (great for my dog who is on a diet). It is also very easy to carry.  I keep it in my pocket.Since it has a cap and has plastic construction, it doesnt get crushed in my pocket. It makes a great little reward during training sessions.I find it especially helpful to reward my dog when Im teaching him a new trick. With the lickey stik he was very eager to see the stik come out.A few notes on the Lickety Stik's use.  The first time you use the Lickety stik, you may have to move the roller-ball with your fingers to get the treat to flow a little.  Once the dog understands that licking the ball makes the treat flow, it is not an issue. Also when he is done licking, there is no dripping.The Lickety Stik also has a clear window at the base of of the bottle so you know when it is time to reorder.The Lickety Stik is not large which makes it easy to trasport. However it does mean that if it is your primary treat for you dog, you may run out quickly.Overall, I can say that the dog was enthusiastic about the stick. It was easy to use. It was fun to give. I am happy with this product.

When I picked up the padded envelope from our mail basket, my cocker spaniel snapped to attention.  By the time I had the bottle out of the envelope, the Rottweiler had joined us.  Their anxiety grew as I struggled to break the plastic wrap around the top.  Finally I had the bottle ready for action, after a very long 30 seconds.I had to rub the roller ball to get the liquid inside to lubricate the ball.  Squeezing the bottle forces the liquid to ooze around the ball.  Both dogs wanted to eat the bottle rather than lick the ball.  They give it a five-star review and suggest that the Vine program send more to our house.The rottie still wants to eat the bottle. The cocker has learned the licking technique.  The cocker is quite responsive to the sound of the bottle being shaken. (Cockers are the original foodies.)The major problem I have is that the ball does not move freely.  I get some liquid on the ball and hold it out for the cocker.  She licks it very clean.  Then I have to squeeze more liquid out and roll the ball around with my thumb.The ingredients seem to be healthy, or as healthy as something with bacon fat in it can be.This product can be a great training reward, but you will have a sticky thumb. The first time I offered my thumb to be licked clean, the cocker started to eat it. If you are training your dog, you probably will want a rag to keep your thumb clean.My vine review philosophy is to first test the product without regard to price.  Now that I have checked the price, currently around $8, it seems a good value for a training tool.  $8 does not buy a decent size bag of training treats.  And the dogs are much more responsive to the bacon than to freeze-dried lumps.  However as just a treat for being a good dog in general, it is not as satisfying as a regular-sized biscuit.  Pity my poor dogs who are only getting this one bottle of bacon treat.

column9: Finally a treat both you and your dog can enjoy!
column10: First off, i would have to say that I did not find the Bacon flavor to be appealing at all.OK I'm kidding.  I didn't actually lick it.But my dog did, and she loves it.The basics:The container is like a roll-on antiperspirant.  If you use roll-on deodorant, and buy this product, you may accidentally sport a new aroma if you are particularly groggy in the morning.Its a no-calorie treat if your dog is ... uh... "easy to see" as they say.  My dog is a bit thick (like a barrel on stilts), so I had some high hopes for this product.The pros:My dog loves it.Its low calorie.No crumbs!The cons:You can't throw it in the laundry room as an easy way to get them to be put up.I had to hold it upside down, and it would drip.When my dog is aggressive she threatens to take it away from me.Overall, I would say that this is one of the few products that delivers exactly what it promises.  I recommend it.

For those that follow my reviews you know I have many dogs so I just had to try out this product.  It was so funny the day I received it. I was surrounded with furry friends. Incase you don't know dogs can smell just about anything and they knew something was in my hands that they were going to like.  The container reminds me of roll-on deodorant.  I know that sounds gross but nevertheless it did. It is made where the dogs lick the top of it to receive their treat.  Okay, now all I had to do was let the dogs lick it and believe me they were ready.  They piled around me and all took their turns, it was so cute.  Now, did they come back for more?  You bet they did, each seeing who could get their tongue on it first.  I could tell to them it was a tasty treat and for me it was a time to interact with my animals and show them love. You can't just let them play piggly wiggly and lick it all in one day, because they would, believe me. You have to allow only so many licks.  I liked this product and so did my dogs and plan to purchase it for them. Dog biscuits are of course a lot easier, you just throw them and they catch, but this is a special treat that allows you time with your animal. Nice product.

column9: Perfect for use while training your dog
column10: The Lickety Stik is fabulous!  My dog immediately took to it and gets so excited when he sees the bottle.  I have been trying to train him to fetch a ball and then give it back to me, but I have had to wrestle the ball away from him.  I was worried about giving him too many treats because of calories, not to mention the expense.  I started letting him lick the Stik once or twice each time I got the ball away from him.  It didn't take long before he would drop the ball when he saw the Stik, and now he puts it directly into my hand, just so he can lick the Stik. I plan on using it to train him to do other things, as well.Considering how many times I have used it, it is a good value for the money.  It's kind of awkward to give him as a regular dog treat, so I save it for training and give him dog biscuits or other treat.

First of all, let me say that my dog likes the taste of this treat - a lot. However, I have a large dog...and evidently an impatient dog. Rather than lick this "roll-on" treat, she would rather just bite it and chew it. That's really the only down side. Found out my daughters kitten liked it too. It's weird, like a 1980's deodorant company trying to do something profitable with their out of date product line. I wouldn't buy it, but my pets liked it.

It's a good idea, but my dog did not get it at all.  It's design is like a roll on deoderant - the ball inside moves while licked putting more of the liquid flavor onto the ball and into the dogs mouth.  You can ration how much the dog licks and put the lid back on.The smell wasn't strong unless you put your nose on it for a big whiff.  It must have smelled good to my dog because she went nuts over it.  The problem was it was too small and she kept bitting it and trying to yank it from my hand.  Then later when I was gone - she got it off the counter and chewed through it.  Yes, I know - she wasn't well behaved with it.  BUT she couldn't resist the temptation and after I had let her lick it I guess she figured it was fair game.Overall - I believe it's made for a little dogs but I didn't know that when I got it.

column9: The Dog loved it, I didn't
column10: Well, when I ordered this I wasn't quite sure what to expect, but it sure wasn't a roll on deodorant container filled with stinky liver flavored liquid.  For me personally, I've always stood by the belief that while the dogs are the one enjoying the dog toys and treats, the are more made for the humans than anything else and there is something totally repugnant about a dog eating from a deodorant container.Jilly, my puppy, loved it.  She kept on trying to take it out of my hand and bite at the container until she realized she had to lick but she did love the flavor.  The only real negative is that Jilly got "liver breath."  Also the ball in the container didn't spin and I had to squeeze and I got a drip or two on the floor.  I have wood floors so no harm no foul, but if you have carpeting you might get a stain, but Jilly helped with the clean up.But I couldn't quite get over the container and even though Jilly loved it the doggy breath and the fact I didn't like her licking a deodorant container was a big turn off.  Plus, if I used roll on deodorant I won't want my dog to associate it with treats, in case she got in the bathroom and ate the real deodorant which I'm sure could make her very sick.3 Stars.UPDATE:  The cat found this on the table and started pawing at it, so I opened it for her so she could have a lick and she loves it more than the dog!

I was excited to get the Lickety Stik for my dogs. It sounds like a good idea BUT the roller part DOES NOT roll and in order for the dog to get something to taste you must squeeze the container which can be a mess. I have four dogs, as I dog train in obedience and in tracking. In the beginning all four were interested, but then they all became frustrated with it. I ended up with $25.00 of this garbage. SAVE YOR MONEY.it's not worth it!

I have three beagles and a lab.  To be honest, when I read about this product, I was dubious as to its ability to make them happy.  A lick?  That's it?Well--I was right, and wrong.When I first broke it out, the lab tried to eat it--he wasn't happy with the one lick.  The beagles saw him try to eat it, and then they were all about eating it, too.  But once they realized what it was all about, they LOVED it.  They were like crack addicts.  I put it on the dining room table, out of reach, and we kept catching them walking on their hind legs, noses over the table ledge, trying to get it.  They got so sneaky!  Climbing onto the chair?  Really?  When it was time for bed, when they usually get a cookie, they all ran to the table and gave me the distinct message--"WE want THAT!"Last night I put the Lickety Stik on a tall shelf in the hallway of the house--and this morning, they "knew" exactly where it was, and wouldn't leave the hallway until I grabbed the thing and walked them outside.So, we're calling it either crack for dogs or catnip for dogs haha..It's sort of like a roll-on deodorant style container.  The beef-gravy-like substance covers the ball and they simply lick it off.  Of course, as I said above, they will try to eat it at first, until they get the idea.  Although I'm convinced that should it get left within reach, they will eat the entire container.)It's a small container--about 5 inches long.  The picture made me think it would be much larger.

My two dogs apparently loved the scent and taste based on the way they were all over the Stik as soon as I uncapped it. The problem was the roller ball. It didn't roll very well. This became the pattern -- place thumb on ball, roll, let dogs lick off residue, place thumb on ball, roll again ... It became tedious very quickly. My main dog grew impatient and latched onto the bottle with his back teeth, easily piercing the neck allowing the flavored goo to ooze out. I tossed the Lickety Stik lickety split.

I bought this product because we originally thought our new puppy had a condition called megaesophagus which requires them to eat and stay in a vertical position for 30-45 minutes after eating and other people had recommended this product to keep the dog occupied during that time.We later found that our dog doesn't have this condition (thank goodness) so I was going to return it but I decided to try it out when my puppy got a tick on her head, thinking it would keep her focused while I got the tick off (which it very much did)The only one I have used is the chicken flavor and when I took off the lid, I gagged and threw up in my mouth. It stinks that bad. But my puppy did seem to like the taste of it.

This product is a bit odd, to say the least. It is designed in a roll-on deodorant type of bottle and your dog must lick the rolling ball to enjoy his treat.When first trying to get my dog to try it, he really looked at me, looked at the bottle, looked at me, looked at the bottle etc. You could literally see in his eyes that he was wondering what the heck he was supposed to do, or what I wanted him to do. Finally he took a swipe at it with his tongue. I assume he was unimpressed because he made no effort to go for another lick, despite my encouragement.The whole idea is just weird. I give my dog treats as well..treats, or to reward good behavior, or just to be nice, or to get him to lay/settle down for a little - in other words to keep him busy for a few minutes or so. This type of treat obviously goes against the idea of keeping him occupied for awhile while keeping my time free since you have to sit/stand there and hold the bottle for him. Now, don't get me wrong, we always have a variety of snacks on hand and I would not mind standing there holding this bottle for him if he actually liked the treat. It's just one of those little extra things we do to show our love. However, he just seemed to not like the taste once he did figure out to lick it, otherwise I assume he would have continued to lick.The texture of the liquid inside just looks gross to me. It is a clearish, somewhat dark brown color. Kind of like pancake syrup although not as sticky/tacky.If your dog will lick the roller ball and likes the taste, then I guess it is a good buy, but if not it is obviously a waste.I also cannot help but wonder who sat around and thought "Hmmmm, let's create a liquid dog treat and put it in a roll-on deodorant dispenser!!"
My dogs would not lick it or even pay attention to it. I thought it would be great for training as I am a consumate treat "dropper", but they were not the least interested. Too bad
The roller ball was sort of hard to get going. My dogs kept biting the bottle and wouldn't lick it very much. It also had a very strong smell.

column9: Interesting, but what's the practical use?
column10: Lickety Stik is an interesting idea. It's a small bottle filled with a thick brown liquid - a liquified dog treat, essentially - which you can squeeze out and smear over the top (sort of like gel deodorant). Your dog, I guess, is then supposed to lick this as a treat, but unfortunately my dog was just confused. I was still able to dab the liquid on his paw, and he seemed to like that quite a bit. So it still works for me to some extent.The big issue, I think, is that I'm not sure what the practical use of this product is. Maybe it's convenient for training; instead of carrying a bag of treats, you can just pop this thing in your pocket. Or I suppose if you have an elderly dog who has trouble with solids, it might come in handy. Otherwise it seems more convenient for me (and probably for many others) to stick with the dry treats.

I bought this at a store in San Diego and I was looking at Amazon to see if they had any in stock. I am happy to see that they carry it! This is my favorite salsa. It has an amazing flavor and it is excellent poured over chicken. It is also good with chips and every other way you eat salsa, but my favorite way to eat it is over chicken or beef. Too bad they don't have bulk sizes of this salsa here!

This product says "Jolly Rancher FRUIT CHEWS".......I received the HARD CANDY. I called the Customer Service as soon as I received the wrong thing and asked for her to send me the CORRECT type of candy. She said they didn't have anything but HARD CANDY.....SOOOOOO It's definitely false advertisement because it CLEARLY states "FRUIT CHEWS" when you are ordering. I was buying this for my mom for Christmas because it's her favorite candy and I couldn't find them in any store and apparently I can't even trust to buy them on the internet anymore either. SO RIDICULOUS!!!! Needless to say, mom didn't get her candy for Christmas~ I DO NOT RECOMMEND TO ANYONE TO BUY THIS PROIDUCT if you're wanting fruit chews.....because you won't get it.

I have a sweet tooth and I come back it naturally. My father and maternal grandmother were both sweet lover's. There are very few types of candy I don't like. The Jolly Fruit Chews are delicious. Each flavor is true and defineable.

I am not sure what the 1-star post reviewer was talking about, but these are exactly as described.  I was hesitant to order these after seeing that review, but I was very pleased to find these fruit chews waiting for me in the box I received.I will definitely order from here again if I need to quench my sweet tooth craving.

column9: Wish I Could Get It In The Store
column10: For some reason this item has been dropped from all my local grocery stores. Luckily I can get it on Amazon, and on a subscription basis. Very convenient.

Power of Facebook! I love Metromint water, my husband is a physician in Seattle and we are addicted. His concern initially was if sugar was in the water, there is none! The Cherry Mint water we absolutely love. Facebook had the ad on my wall and thought great maybe they have a deal. Metromint directly doesn't however, Amazon does! Subscribe for monthly shipments and you pay no shipping if your a Prime Customer and we are, it's worth the money! And Metromint is FABULOUS!
Love Metromint Cherry Perserves it is cool going down and has an awesome cherry flavor. Can't wait for my friends to try it as well! I want to win on facebook for a case of Metromint today!
Excellent taste, and great for a pre workout meal or small lunch. I love that larabar does NOT use GMO ingredients too.
This tea is delicious and a great price.  No bitterness, very smooth flavor.  I am very pleased as are my co-workers who also enjoy tea.  I will definatly be back for more.

column4: B. Smith "The giant on whoms shoulders your c...
column10: This isn't the best mate Ive ever had, but for the price, you can't beat it. Buy this product.
Came promptly and tasted oh so good!  The tray is already a fourth gone and it's only the first day.  I would highly recommend this product.

column9: The best pomegranate tea out there.
column10: When I first got a sample of this tea I wasn't expecting to much do to my previous experiences with other pomegranate tea on the market, but boy was I surprised. This tea is a good black tea with a light hint of pomegranate, it is great stuff compared to all the flowery/herbal junk from their competitors.If you like your flavored tea to actually taste like tea then this is the one for you.Ingredients: black tea, natural pomegranate flavour with other natural flavours.

I bought this for my 20 year old son who had traveled to Europe--Ireland, Iceland, Denmark and Morocco among the few places he went. He just learned to love the Pomegranate tea and asked for it for Christmas after all his travels. The rest of the  my kids said they liked it too so it was a big thing here. It had fruity flavor he liked.

I got samples of this flavor recently in my subscribe-and-save Earl Grey.I thought it would make good iced tea, so I bit the bullet and bought the 6-pack from Amazon.  Glad I did.  I sweeten it only very lightly (about 3 tsp. sugar for half a gallon of tea) and it's terrific.Glad I bought it!

column9: A superior tea, in my limited experience
column10: I am not exactly a tea connoisseur, but I always buy my tea loose leaf and brew it in a French press because I still have one from the days I WAS a bit of a coffee connoisseur.  This tea tasted better than the Twinings brand equivalent I tried, and was much more resistant to bitterness when I lost track of the steeping time.  I mostly attribute this property to the tea leaves being whole rather than ground up like the Twinings, but I have no real evidence that that's the case.
Very good tea.  Much superior to Twinings which I also bought and regretted.  Tin seals well with an interior seal like an old time Hershey's chocolate tin and an exterior lid that screws on.

I have no idea why people rate this tea so high. It has no right orange color, rather brownish, taste is dull. Tea has no Darjeeling-specific tingling aftertaste. And it is not even cheap enough to be good for the price. I would say bagged Twinning tastes better. Not to mention Tazo or Mighty Leaf. Internet is full of better lose leaf teas.

column9: OK if You Like Mild Tea
column10: I expected a little more from this tea, i.e., more robust flavor and strength.  It's a good tea, but not great.  Even after letting it steep for longer periods than I normally steep tea, it still wasn't strong enough.  It also tended to have a moldy flavor even though the dry tea itself had no moldy odor.
This tea has a great flavor.  I'm happy with my choice and the price.  I will likely buy it again.

column9: good for black, very nice tins
column10: This tea was decent and the price was pretty good.  However, don't expect the smoothness of a good quality silver needle.  It can be on the bitter side coming from higher quality teas (and types) but it is a black tea and that is to be expected to an extent.  As far as black tea goes I liked it.The tins are really nice with two lids (as tins should be).  One lid pops in and the other fits on top and semi-locks with a twist.  Definitely worth saving to use with tea that comes without tins (in bags).
I am happy I gave this a try - it is quite good and reasonably priced. It is not a strong tea but not blah either.

Maybe not the very best darjeeling but a very good price for a decent tea. I've had more much expensive brands that weren't as good. The canister is also impressive, with an inner seal in addition to the lid. Highly recommended for those who like a nice tea-flavored cuppa!

This is a great smooth darjeeling tea, with a slight fruity taste making each cup very satisfying! I found it better when allowed to brew at least 5 minutes, however; otherwise it seemed weak to me. But then again, I am pretty hooked on strong breakfast type black teas, so it may just be a characteristic of darjeeling. Best without milk and with raw sugar. It is now a staple of my morning prelude to breakfast. Great price for great quality!
This tea tastes great, is good for the world (fair trade) and environment and you (organic/biodynamic).

I am gluten intolerant and always looking for things to eat that resemble the foods that I used to eat.  This granola is delicious and doesn't make me feel deprived.  It is crunchy and the cranberries are not too hard.

I have Udi's gluten free granola sent to me every month.  It is perfect plain for a snack, with milk, or on top of yogurt.  I keep some at work for a quick easy pick me up during the day.  It is one of those gluten free products that is so good you really can't believe it is gluten free!

Very good texture and taste, not too sweet.  Great for travel as you can eat it plain, but I like it warmed in the microwave with soy milk.  Only gave it four stars, as with all gluten free products the package looks small for the money.  Definitely re ordering it.

I ordered this product based on the appealing picture, and the fact that it came up as "organic." It is not organic, and it's not "Granola," it's just baked oats with 6 pieces of dried cranberry. I counted them, 6. Nothing else. You can't return this because it's a grocery item. Terrible purchase, dont bother.
This is clean and healthy granola for those looking for something with less sugar that's also gluten free. I like it
When they indicate dry cranberries they mean very dry. Even after soaking in milk they remain hard as little stones. I removed them before eating the granola which was OK.
A delightfully crunchy granola with the perfect amount of craisins. We love it in our vanilla yogurt. Yummy and gluten free!
This is a tasty, crunchy granola which is well made. The 12 ounce packages are too small for someone who eats granola regularly. The company should offer bigger bags at discounts.
very flavorful granola mix, excellent dried cranberries, even gluten eating folks will enjoy this healthy mix of grains and dried fruit

Looking for a delicious and gluten free selection to snack on while hiking, camping, or any other time you're on the go? Udi's Gluten Free Cranberry Granola is an excellent choice! Great in yogurt, cereals, and many other favorite recipes, this granola is also wonderful when eaten by itself. With tasty dried cranberries and walnut pieces, this granola has a nice fruity kick to it.Ingredients: Certified Gluten Free Oats, Wildflower Honey, Dried Cranberries (Cranberries, Sugar, Sunflower Oil), Canola Oil, Walnuts.Disclosure of Material Connection: I received this product free from Udi's Gluten Free Foods. I was not required to write a positive review. The opinions I have expressed are my own. I am disclosing this in accordance with the Federal Trade Commission's 16 CFR, Part 255vf: "Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising."
I love udi's granola with kiefur in the mornings, it holds up well , also great for a dry handfull snack, crunchy and chewy
I was a little sceptical when I bought this. I was pleasantly surprised. Tastes great and it's gluten free. Makes a really good breakfast or yummy snack. Udi's is great company!

I bought these because I'm lazy. I want good espresso as I'm trying to hurry out the door to work and get the kid to school on time. These deliver. Lots of different styles to keep things fresh and different. I don't think I've had one I didn't like.They're a little pricy, but that's likely because they all look like they're imported. If they were a little cheaper, I'd probably buy more and end up buzzing around the office... so maybe it's good they're not cheaper.I use them in a real pressurized espresso maker. I'm not sure they'd work well in a steam-powered one like some of the home coffee/espresso combo units I've seen/used. They're pretty dense pucks.
This was a great way to try out different types of coffee for our new espresso maker. Most of them were tasty.
This sampler had a LOT of espresso pods to test.  I really enjoyed the experience, and it helped me to decide which pod to order by the box.  Frankly, none were bad.

I bought this as a gift for a friend. The espresso pods smell wonderful but I was disappointed with the way they were packaged. All the pods came in a ziploc bag. It is fine and I don't like giving only 3 stars but I can't give it 4 stars. It would have been really nice if they were packaged in a box for gift giving. But if you are looking to try different types of espresso this is definitely the way to go.
Love these pods.  much easier then pressing your own,if they are compatible with your machine.  Great variety

I love smoked turkey wings and it is hard to find good ones.  These are not too salty, nice and richly smoked and not at all dried out.  Over all the best smoked turkey wings I have tried.  It is even worth the extra shipping, with the dry ice and all.
I like sugar free Red Bull. It's the best tasting "energy drink" I know of. I like it better than the regular Red Bull. However, if you have access to a Costco, you can get a case for ~$10 less.

It consistently delivers. This is a product I simply cannot live without. I work full-time and go to school-full time. Also? I have cats, so every little bit of energy helps.Some people say this energy drink has a slight aftertaste, but I think it tastes light and citrusy, not harsh.This product has 10 calories, versus the "sugar-full" version, which, I believe has 150.
I love sugar-free red bull. I hate being sugared up, but really need the caffeine.

column9: Total Zero Tastes Different Than Sugar Free - Don't Like
column10: I highly recommend you buy a single can of the new "Total Zero" version of Red Bull before you buy a case of Total Zero.  That way, if you don't like it, you've only bought one can, not 24.I'm a long time user of both the regular ("Original") version and the sugar free version.For my tastes, there isn't a huge difference between the Original version and the sugar free version, but there is a noticeable difference between the sugar free and "Total Zero" versions.Everything tastes different to different people, but I don't like the new Total Zero version.  It leaves, for me, a mediciney after-taste.  If you are drinking this late at the bar with your favorite adult beverage, you might not care, but I drink my Red Bulls by themselves as a pick me up during the day.Now, what do I do with the 23 other cans....?
My mom always buys the 4 pack, but the 24 pack was a better deal. Thanks Amazon!

column9: I love S-F Red Bull, but this is a crazy price
column10: The most I've ever paid for singles at Royal Farms Etc is $1.99 per can. This is way more than that. Only place cheaper than the grocery store (12 can) I've found is Sam's Club or Costco. This is no deal at all.
It came in the mail promptly. Very secure packaging. And it was a great bargain. Red Bull is expensive anywhere you buy it.  But Amazon, by far has the best Deal!! Thanks.

I really LIKE RED BULL, but at 150 calories a can - there was no way that I could have it very often.  I had looked at Costco and other places for the Sugarfree RED BULL to buy in bulk and they didn't carry it.  I was really pleased to discover it at AMAZON at a great price with free shipping.I love this stuff. At only 10 calories it is a great energy boost and definitely keeps you from eating because it really provides a tangy, sweet alternative.  Highly recommended for dieters!
I drink it before the gym.I drink it on a whim.I turn it into shots.I drink this stuff a lot.I think this stuff's the bomb.Drink on, drink on, drink on.

I had not tried Red Bull Total Zero prior to purchasing the case on sale at Amazon.  I've had the regular and the sugar-free flavors and to me, I prefer the taste of Total Zero.  In some ways the flavor doesn't seem to be as strong and overbearing as the normal Sugar-Free can.  I don't really notice any strange after-taste in comparison to the other Red Bull flavors, they all have a similar "mediciney" taste. column9: The Second New Flavor of the Quintessential Condiment!
column10: This was the second modern variation on an essentially unchanged, bestselling product for more than 140 years.  Other flavors are:Orginal Pepper Sauce (hot) (2500-5000 Scoville Heat Units),Green Pepper Sauce (milder yet) (600-1200 Scoville Heat Units),Garlic Pepper Sauce (milder) (1200-2400 Scoville Heat Units),Chipotle Pepper Sauce (mild) (1500-2500 Scoville Heat Units),Sweet & Spicy Pepper Sauce (mildest) (100-600 Scoville Heat Units),but this is Habanero Sauce (hottest) (>7000 Scoville Heat Units).Dueling histories of the McIlhenny Company are available: (authorized) Tabasco: An Illustrated History and (unauthorized) McIlhenny's Gold: How a Louisiana Family Built the Tabasco Empire, for those curious about how this most remarkable product and business empire came to be.Note: "A pharmacist named Wilbur Scoville invented the Scoville Scale in 1912 to measure the heat of peppers. A 'Scoville Unit' is actually a measure of capsaicin (the chemical in hot peppers that is responsible for their heat).Scoville's test was a comparative taste test that is considered subjective by today's standards. A more sophisticated method is in use today, but in honor of Wilbur Scoville, the unit of measure is still called the Scoville.The capsaicin level in peppers can vary from plant to plant due to local environmental conditions. This means that a pepper's rating is an average measure.The hottest pepper on record is the Bhut Jolokia with a pungency of over 1 million Scoville Heat Units (1,001,304, to be exact). By contrast, the Bell Pepper comes in at less than 100 Scoville Heat Units."

Having to re-order due to dented cans sucks, but the quality is lovely. I like it cold on top of warm buttered waffles + a bit of honey or mixed into oatmeal with fruit + coconut oil.

column9: Chicken of the sea whole baby clams
column10: These clams are really excellent and extremely tasty.  Much better than most I've had previously from grocery stores, etc.  Read  all the reviews before ordering and agree that these are the tastiest.  Some brands are very bland.

For many years now I have been making clam chowder for Christmas at my In-laws. Several have commented that mine is the best clam chowder they've ever had. I give my recipe out, but most people who have made it say "it just isn't the same." It takes about 2-1/2 hrs. to make, and you can't walk away from it. The difference, I suppose, is the love. You gotta put the love in it. CJFry

Chicken of the Sea Whole Baby Clams are tender, mild in taste,and grossly overpriced.Clams provide excellent nutrition and protein, however the current price is prohibitive.Clams are versatile and can be used in many recipes.However, I purchased this product prior to April 23, 2012 for$28.86 with free shipping.The price increase of $16.13 since writing my review 2 daysago is outrageous and unwarranted! And the shipping cost adds"insult to injury."There is no shortage of clams available and I will look for anotherproduct.Drained and rinsed, I love clams marinated in a bit of olive oilwith garlic and a generous dash of Cajun seasoning.Clams are rich in Iron for those of us suffering from an Iron deficiency.Clams are a good source of Omega-3 fatty acids and are very low in Saturated Fat. Clams provide Magnesium, Manganese, Vitamin B12, Riboflavin, Niacin, Phosphorus, Potassium, Copper, Zinc, and Selenium.Clams are a very good source of Protein.Please be aware that data suggests that the calcium in milk, cream, etc. can inhibit iron absorption.

NO TEA!  They took the tea OUT of the bags!  This was my absolute favorite tea: I drank it every day and kept it on auto-order.  Then suddenly one month I couldn't believe it: instead of lovely tea bags that justified their high price, they sent these pitiful bags with only a little hint of tea -- not enough to make even a single decent cup.  You can tell the old bags from the new by the wrappers: the good old ones were printed to match the box design, the bad new ones are just anonymous solid green.  I would never order it again.  They should charge a reduced price that's proportionate to the radical reduction in tea.  A complete rip-off.  Do not waste your money.
This is a very subtle and slightly sweet tea that makes for a good late evening drink.  Nicely packaged and brews up quickly.  Not a hint of acidic flavor in it -- very smooth and mild.

Great taste, and also great value ordering here on Amazon. I usually brew with loose tea, but these teabags are a very close 2nd place to brewing loose tea, especially when out of the house. I usually bring these teabags with me when eating out and get a cup of hot water to make my own tea instead of the restaurant variety tea bag.
just adore this tea. to bad that amazon doesn't usually ship teas to Europe so i have to find other ways...
HII tried to send you Private Message But I can not!My question is I have 3 orders Can you Please send them all in one shipment?Thank you

Boursin - Garlic and Fine Herbs - great taste our favorite spread with fine crackers. We have been served this in high end hotels several times and wanted to have some at home too. The only "watch out" is our order was almost out-of-date when we received it. We still enjoyed it, BUT...had to eat it fast. IF the out-of-date was reasonable this item would have received 5 stars!

This crumbly, white cheese is a delicious combo of feta-like texture, slight cream cheese tone. It is a sensory delighting garlic and herb experience that shouldn't be missed.It comes in a pleasant, white box that looks slightly more like a garlic supplement than a package for cheese. As shown in the picture, it does come wrapped in a silver foil packet with ridges. Like a foil wrapped, crumbly cheese cupcake.My "best before" date was Feb 19, 2010 but was literally gone in within less than a day. I had originally purchased it on a whim but both my 66 year-old mother and 7 year-old son fully support my decision to add Boursin's Garlic & Fine Herbs Gournay [not misspelled; it's their word] Cheese to our "must have" list.The Boursin website has a feature that allows you to search for local vendors but, for some areas, it is no where near accurate. Unless you know where to buy it already, I would recommend purchasing this very palatable cheese online.

I received the product very promptly and packed in a little cooler but the expiration date was 9/30/08 and I had just ordered it 9/22/08.  They need to watch that my husband wont eat anything out of date or even close to being out of date.  That was the only complaint.  Love the cheese!!!

Down in Cuba, we had Jugo de Ciruela made by a company called Watt's. We haven't been able to find that up here in Canada or the USA yet so I tracked this down online to see how it compared and it's just right. I use it in a mixed drink (that I may market so no reveal on that recipe just yet) and it's divine.Thanks to TheLatinProducts.com for shipping it promptly!

I would say that these are just as good, if not better, than Teddy Grahams. Even better, they are trans-fat free (Teddy Grahams are not). I'd highly recommend these delicious snack cookies!!FYI: my local Target carries them for 1.99 a box (on sale) or ~2.39 regular priced...that's cheaper than what Amazon has here (currently 19 something dollars for 6 boxes). Check your local stores to see what their prices are first!

I have tried dozens of these packets of snacks over the past 3 years.  Various flavors from various lots.  Some of them a while back tasted fine.  Lately, all I get are ones with a bitter, rancid taste.  Especially on the Friends variety.  Does "all natural" mean "High in THC"?What is up with that sharp nasty taste?  These things aren't expired.  I've communicated with Annie's on numerous occasions and have always recieved coupons for more, but I've given up on ever finding another lot of this product that doesn't taste gross.  My kids won't even eat them anymore.  Its like they are all rancid or something.
They taste great and I like that they have good ingredients and no trans-fat and no corn syrup.  We will continue purchasing this item and other Annie's Homegrown snacks.

I wanted to try these as a slightly healthier alternative to Teddy Grahams.  These are organic and have a few less ingredients.FLAVOR:With three flavors of "bunnies" you get a medley that is kind of nice.  However, only the chocolate ones have enough flavor to even compare to a Teddy Graham.  The chocolate chip has a very, very mild chocolate flavor, but isn't too bad.  The honey flavor is pretty bland.  Honey Teddy Grahams have more flavor, so I'd choose them over plain honey bunnies.TEXTURE:These bunnies get stale very fast.  Seal them up well, or you'll have bad tasting bunnies.  Fresh, they're crispy and crunchy and a great size for on-the-go snacking or sitting at your computer with a cup of coffee and these little cookies.OVERALL OPINIONI do like the organic factor.  However, they're generally a little more money than their competing Teddies, and I like Teddy flavor better.  It's up to you and your taste buds, but I would at least recommend trying the bunnies.  I buy them when they're on sale for cheaper than Teddies.

column9: Not just for kids......these are tasty!
column10: Ok, I have to say, the packaging did draw me in... I mean, how could the little hippy bunny flashing you a peace sign steer you wrong?  So I picked up the box...organic, I like that, 8 grams of sugar, I can live with that, no trans or saturated fats, 20% calcium, 2 grams of fiber, and I can have 28 little cookies (a combo of chocolate, honey & chocolate chip) for 130 calories.  So, the bunnies and I went home together....These are my favorite little cookies when I want something sweet but don't want to obliterate all the good eating that I did all day.  Yeah, they are a cookie, but I felt good that I could eat organic and that there were no additives or preservatives.  I like to keep mine in the fridge where they stay nice and cold and crunchy and just wait for me to pair it with a glass of milk.Great snack for the little ones as well as those of us who are young at heart!
I bought these for a friend of mind for her birthday because she loves these and cannot find them everywhere.  Everyone should try these they are wonderful and healthier then others

These are FABULOUS.  I was introduced to them by a friend and I can't wait to try all the different varieties.  These go for $2.99 at Earth Fare, so they're not that expensive, especially for how much is in the box!  I know 7.5 ounces doesn't sound like that much, but I emptied the entire box into a ziploc bag, and I've been snacking on them for the past 3 days and I still haven't made a dent!  Although, I don't have kids and I won't share with my husband, so that could be why :-)  Seriously, give these a try - you will NOT be disappointed.

First of all, they taste great.  That's what matters most to kids.  I like them too!  Bunny Grahams are also made with all sorts of organic ingredients and no hydrogenated oils, no high fructose corn syrup, and no artificial colors.  Compare the label to the Bear shaped grahams treats and you'll see quite a difference.  Another great product from Annie's.

My children love these.  It's a shame that organic foods (well, all foods really) keep rising in price.  I can't afford to keep buying organic foods as I'd like to.  If you can afford them, these are a nice treat.

In my ongoing effort to provide healthy snacks to the children in my son's class (he goes to a public elementary school), I try various organic finger foods. One of the things that has boggled my mind is the amount of graham crackers that contain trans fat- and they are marketed as healthy! When I saw these, I was pleasantly surprised- I didn't imagine I'd see an organic AND trans fat free graham cracker product.Not only are these free of trans fats AND high fructose corn syrup (which is typical of organic products, thankfully) but they are absolutely delicious. I love snacking on them and the kids in my son's class loved them! I went ahead and used the subscribe-and-save feature for this product and now his class has a steady supply of healthy and yummy snacks. :)
These are a better deal than in the grocery stores.  They're great little graham cracker type cookies.
We like the fact that there is no real junk in these.  the kids love them for a snack.  We are glad that we can get them from Amazon at a reasonable price.

I am a fan of this brand, but was extremely disappointed when I tried the Bunny Graham Friends. I noticed immediately upon opening the brand new box that there was a strange odor. I proceeded to open the metallic bag, and almost instantly correlated the smell with that of a mylar balloon (those metallic helium balloons). Sadly, the graham snacks were impregnated with the smell and taste as well. I'm all for "green" packaging and such, and realize the hidden dangers of plastic packaging, but surely there is another way to package these without ruining the flavor or earth. I will, however, continue to buy the macaroni and other products from this line, but I will never waste my money on this item again.

These bunny shaped graham snacks are really good. They are made from whole grain, are all natural, and are a good source of calcium - 20% RDA per serving. All three flavors in this pack, the honey, chocolate and chocolate chip, are delicious.

I've tried these before and liked them  buty the boxes I received smelled and tasted rotten or sort of like how paint smells. I think this batch has gone bad or something. And I'm disappointed that I wasted my money. These are going in the garbage it's not safe to eat. So gross.

All my children are vegetarian, and have been there entire life. I thought these snacks would be a good choice. It is hard to find varieties of foods for kids that don't have junk in them. I gave mymiddle daughter these as a snack for school. When she got home I asked why she had not eaten them. She said "I don't like them mommy. " I then tried them and was like yuck. I felt bad that my kids tried them. I then made it a joke letting others try them and seeing their reactions. So far NO ONE has liked them.

These little tasty bunnies are guilt free! They are the best low calorie healthy snack. They are mostly organic, and melt in your mouth! However, make sure the dates are not expired! No preservatives to keep them fresh. They are very difficult to find in stores, but AMAZON always has them!
Im not much for typing but i will say Bunny Grahams are delicious and good for you too! I reccomend them to anyone thinking about trying them or looking for a great snack!

My two toddler boys LOVE all the Annie's Bunnies (Friends, individuals, cheddar, and gummies).  They are super yummy and are a smart snack choice as they are all-natural.  I LOVE Amazon, but can buy Annies' cheaper in the large box at Target, and in individual bags at Costco.

column9: easy portion control and great taste
column10: both my son and daughter love Annie's Bunny Grahams Honey flavor cookies.  it tastes great not like other organic foods.  this pack had it in small separate packs that makes it easy for packing for snacks at school or to the park.  honey flavor is one of my kids' favorite flavors.

These Bunny Grahams taste terrible. I really hoped my kids would love them because they are organic, but I couldn't even eat them. We threw them all away. They taste like cardboard and also smell like cardboard. I don't know what everyone else is trying and why their reviews are so positive but these are TERRIBLE.

Taylor ham was part of my childhood growing up in New Jersey. Every diner on Route 9, 35 and 36 served it. I thought it was a national product. But NOOOOO. You can only get it on the east coast. For years I have had it sent to me in California from NJ family members.  For those who dont know, Taylor Ham is seasoned to perfection and is slightly salty. Fried with eggs it is remarkable. A three pound roll will last a long time as you only need a 1/2" disk to satisfy. Happy eating! g

Unique.  Without comparison.  Nothing like it out here on the Left Coast.  When friends come from The Islands, they want to take this stuff back to Oahu.  But WTF?  $200 for 4 rolls?  How can you not choke when you're paying $50 a roll for Taylor Ham?  That's like me bringing Spam from Hawaii, and charging $25 a can in Philly.  Now take a look at how much it cost to buy Scrapple on Amazon.  Are you kidding me with this?

column9: Taylor Pork Roll is the Best!
column10: Like others here, I grew up in NJ and Taylor Pork Roll was a breakfast staple for the family, especially when down at the beach in south Jersey during the summer.  Now that I live in SC, I miss it terribly.Occasionally work will take me to NJ and I'll buy however many I can fit in my suitcase.  Before leaving town, I'll put them in the office freezer overnight so they're good for transport the next day when I head to the airport.  I've made friends with many of the TSA guys in various airports just by saying "I've got Taylor Pork Roll in my suitcase."  They "get it" and laugh.  One even remarked that "[you'd] be surprised how many of those things come through here!"If you're looking for a better price on mail order TPR, just go here ...[...]Enjoy!

Great product. If your from the north east and moved south like me you will love being able to have access to your favorite pork roll.  Doesn't matter how much it cost if you love and miss a little bit of home.  Surely brought me back to my hometown with every bite.

My father a Holland native loves his Leyden cheese!! Every year we struggle to find a place to get it and ship for a reasonable rate. For the first time this year we went through amazon.com/ an excellent choice.  The vendor whom the cheese came from shipped promptly and the experience was more than satisfactory.  Especially pleasing since I ordered days before CHristmas and expected delivery after Christmas, but somehow it arrived on Christmas Eve.... fantastic service and great quality!!!

I've finished my first box of Ganocafe Mocha. It was delicious. Initially, since I had expected a different taste, I found it to be surprising. The blend of milk powders and sugars are just right. It's a smooth taste with the extra melding of the Reishi that enhances the flavor. I can't describe it. It was different enough to notice and pleasant enough to make me wish I had ordered another box before the first ran out. I've also purchased and experienced the taste of the Ganocafe Coffee, without the milk and sugar additives. You can make what you want of it. It has that specific flavor that makes it a special cup of coffee. About the benefits, Reishi is a known adaptogen herb that helps to bring balance to body functions. Reishi's balancing qualities offer support for both the body's immune and nervous systems. Herbalists use Reishi to support allergies, bronchitis, viral infections and hypertension, Its adaptogenic effect also extends to detoxification, mood and appetite, vigor, and mental alertness. There are no side effects-- it's all beneficial. I highly recommend the Ganocafe experience. Its one I think you'll enjoy and make a habit. BTW, there is no caffiene- something I thought I'd miss. I didn't. I guess the taste and results of the Reishi made up for it. Again, it's absolutely DELICIOUS, and given the costs of special coffees, it's one you can enjoy at home at an affordable price.

column9: Great tasting mocha coffee & really healthy for you!
column10: I have been drinking this coffee for 2 years now and out of all the healthy coffee's I have tried so far this one taste so good. It really makes you feel energized and ready to take on the day. Wonderful. I would recommend this coffee to anyone who loves mocha's!

I was introduced to Gano Excel Gano-cafe mocha by a friend who carried it at her health-food store,and became an instant fan! It is advertised as a healthy coffee, and I've read so much literature on it,so that was my first reason for buying it. But, now that I've been using it for 6 years, my primary reason for drinking it is the taste! I've tried other brands of mocha with the ganoderma (Reishi) mushroom, but Gano-cafe (by Gano Excel) has absolutely the best taste, and mixes the smoothest. The other brands had a tendency to be grainy and/or not mix well and settle at the bottom of the cup too much. The best "healthy" things I like about Gano-cafe Mocha is, of course, the benefits of the mushroom, but also the low caffiene level,which protects me from the acidity of normal coffees. It is less expensive than coffee-house drinks, and healthier, with less sugar and no chemical additives/preservatives. I, personally, use about half a package to 6 oz. of water, to tailor to my personal taste preference. Gano-cafe Mocha is my indulgence! Especially in cool/cold weather it is a tasty and comforting drink! I usually have at least 2 cups a day!

I was looking into ReishiMushroom and came across this brand of coffee that already has it mixed in!First of all I'm not much of a Coffee drinker... which is why I bought both the Ganocafe Classic and the Ganocafe Mocha to see if either one was right for me... tried the Classic and didn't like that one too much but the Mocha that on the other hand tasted Great! The drink gave me a natural high feeling which was very pleasant, I guess that's the effect from the Reishi =)The price does seem a bit high for only 15packets... but in a way it is cheaper than going to Starbucks.

I eat a lot of rice, so I am always buying different kinds to try out. Most frequently, I eat sushi rice seasoned with only salt and sesame seeds.  This rice is my favorite so far!  Just the fragrance of this rice cooking in the rice cooker will get people to ask where the wonderful smell is coming from. The taste is just as nice, clean, and with flavorful toasty notes.  This rice is also almost as nutritious as brown rice, just without as much fiber. the germ is intact, so you need to wash it gently in order to keep the germ intact on the grain. This is what gives this rice the beautiful aroma, taste and nutrition.This rice cooks best if you follow the washing and soaking directions on the package. Just 30 minutes of soaking and this rice will yield the same texture as polished white sushi rice. I have found that all sushi rice works best when cooked in a rice cooker, so I can't say how this rice would fare if cooked in a pot with a tight fitting lid. The texture maybe slightly more firm if done in a pot, so you may want to increase soaking time OR add a few extra tablespoons of water at the start of cooking.This rice would make an excellent breakfast rice with an egg and kurobata sausage, or any grilled fish. Nice and sticky enough for any kind of sushi as well.

I was looking for a rice that was nutritious without being a brown rice. This rice which contains the germ is more nutritious than white rice and the taste is great. It is a sticky rice with a wonderful nutty flavor.

My friend introduced me to this rice over a year ago and ever since then I cannot eat any other rice.  I tried other rice to find something comparable but didn't find anything that even came close. I finally broke down and ordered online (payed the shipping costs - but ordered three bags to lower cost per bag) and it is worth every penny!  I only wish that I could order larger bags!
This rice is sweet, soft, chewy, and tastes exactly same as white rice.(Even better than at least my previous write rice.) I was very impressed. Thanks a lot!

This bag of brown rice is delicious and cooks up quicker and tastier than the 100% brown rice. I thought it was a bit pricy but good quality for sure. 100% brown rice takes longer to cook up tender but these only has half the brown coating with most  of the whole grain outer layer removed so it doesn't take as long to cook and has a milder flavor without the bitterness of 100% whole brown rice. I still believe these has better nutritional value then 100% white rice. I get mine from an Asian store now which is much cheaper.
Bought this as a gift for my husband and he really likes the taste-he is a big coffee lover and it's nice to find new flavors for him to try.

THESE ARE AMAZING!!! Be cautioned because they are hard to stop eating!! I found them in store recently, for 3.99 by the way, and my mother and i both cannot stop buying or eating them.  I had to buy a separate bag for my boyfriend so i wouldn't have to share.  Nothing bad I can say about this product, except that it seems maybe amazon made a mistake with the price...

My cat herd (5) love Wellness canned food, especially the turkey mix.  Cat ages range from 3 to l0 and all have thrived on this food.  I supplement their diets with Wellness dry food, but the canned is by far their favorite.

Wellness is the only canned food I buy for my cats. I has no by products, preservatives or any artificial junk. No grain, and it's first four ingredients are good meats. My cats love it (even the finicky one) and I'm happy there is at least one cat food company out there that provides nutritious pet food. Thank you Wellness! Buying this is chaper than buying in the store as well, I think if you buy the same amount in the store you pay about 13 dollars more. Just be aware of the fact that you  need a can opener to open these cans.

I did some research before getting a kitten.  This was the best rated kitten food.  My little guy loves it.  It is, however, on the dry side so I find that adding a bit of water helps.  Since he gets just 1/2 a can 2x a day, I microwave the 2nd half of the portion in his dish for 10 seconds, along with a bit of water.
Cats love it! And Wellness is a brand I trust. Cats only get canned food once a week as a treat, and this does not adversely affect kitty tummies or the litter box between premium dry food meals.

column9: The Best Money can Buy for your Cat, Next to Homemade - Revised for Turkey
column10: I like to provide variety for the cats, however, I like to stick with single protein sources.  So in addition to Wellness Canned Cat Food for Adult Cats, Chicken Formula (Pack of 12 12.5 Ounce Cans), I also get this one to add on with a higher protein diet.I have 3 cats, one is now 17 years old.  I started using this shortly after the pet food recalls in 2007.  The lack of Grains, and real meat (not the processed kind you find in the grocery store), is what promotes the health of your pet carnivore.While there are some veggies, the smell will tell you the amount of meat in this product.  I supplement with one serving from Holistic Select Feline Radiant Adult and Kitten Health Chicken Meal Recipe Dry Cat Food, 3-Pound Bag.The cats ages range currently from 7 to 17.  The below feeding schedule is modified slightly (sometimes only two feedings a day, maybe half the amount of dry, etc.)  If your cat has a sensitive tummy, it is best to feed more frequent, smaller meals each day.The 7 and 13 yo boys get about 1/4 cup dry per day.The 17 yo girl gets about 1/8 cup dry per day.I then split one can between all three twice a day.  When the can is first opened, I add little hot water to the wet food.  This guarantees a consistent texture between different batches,  The remainder of the can is covered with a plastic lid, and placed in the refrigerator.  I then later pull out (don't leave in fridge for more than 2 days), separate into three servings, and mix at least 1/8 cup hot water.  Then, nuke for 5 to 7 seconds (to warm up), and walla, a gravy mix meal for kitties.I can verify 100% that their health improved greatly after switching from the cheap, grocery store dry.  Its the only reason Baby Girl is still alive.  If you can't afford heavy vet bills, put your pets on this and some money into savings, in lieu of the overpriced pet insurance.With the free shipping, it is still a deal.

Unlike one of the previous reviewers, this is one of my cat's absolute favorite variety. He usually will just lick the can clean while my other cat eats the food, but this is one he truly enjoys eating.

column9: My three male cats love this!!
column10: So far, my three male kitties have loved all the Wellness wet foods I've bought for them.  However, they really went wild over this, and it's become a real favorite.

column9: Smells fishy, so the cats love it
column10: I only buy Wellness for my cats and I try to give them a variety, so I've tried most of the flavors. The sardine seafood blend is by far the worst smelling flavor the cats have tried. And of course it's their favorite. They lick the bowl on this one. It's definitely a good pick for older cats that need softer food (mushy) or finicky eaters.

column9: Very high quality food, and cat likes it
column10: I recently did a bunch of research on Cat nutrition, and my conclusion was that the Wellness cat foods offered the best combination of excellent nutrition, good variety, and affordability.  So I bought some for my crotchety, picky, 16+ year old cat who had been eating Nutro.  To my great relief, she accepted the switch without complaint!Although I haven't had a long history with this cat food yet, I've been pleased with the results so far, and based on my research I'm convinced I'm doing right by my furry friend.  I certainly recommend it.

column9: difficult to review for a cat but...
column10: The product seemed great from the human viewpoint: high protein, no grain, quality ingredients and relatively reasonably priced on Amazon. However, my cats would not touch the food. I have one, older female, slightly fussy part Maine coon and a second, very large young male, an outdoor stray who has adopted us. Neither of them would eat it, both preferred the dry food  (Wellness Salmon). I usually give them both wet and dry food. The wet food, a different brand, is always eaten first but this time, both bowls of Wellness Canned cat food were left pretty much untouched after the first taste and remained so until I tossed the food the next day! I know cats are very particular ...they often dislike something for no reason I can understand and it doesn't necessarily imply a faulty product ...  but if a young, hungry stray decides against it, in this case, I reckon something is off with the product.

column9: She must be a picky eater.
column10: My cat barely touches this stuff, especially after the can's been open for about a day or two. This is probably because she was most likely raise on cheap food (we adopted her as an adult) but I can't be sure. Apparently healthy food is less appealing to cats...

column9: Cat loves this and it's a high quality food
column10: I have a 1 1/2 year old cat and started feeding him canned food after reading about how cats don't naturally have a strong thirst drive and need most of their water to come from their food like in nature. Also as another reviewer said, this food doesn't have any of the crappy by-products that "Science Diet" and other highly marketed brands have. These brands even have by-products in their canned food.Cats are carnivores so the majority of their diet needs to be meat (aside from the small amount of veggies you might find in a mouse's or rabbit's stomach in the wild).Aside from that, my cat LOVES this food and it is very good for him. He eats a variety of flavors so he doesn't get sick of one.

I've been feeding my cats wellness since I weaned the stray kitten and got the shelter kitten, and they seem to like all the flavours plenty but I've been alternating this and the straight chicken stuff for the past few weeks and they've basically stopped eating the chicken stuff, I guess saving space for this stuff instead.
