When I opened the package, the entire bottle was spilled and dried all over the inside.  I can't review this item however, I can say i have tried all the other MIO flavors and love them.  I would assume this would be the same.sorry !

After reading some of the first reviews I almost did not try this. A week later and some better reviews I decided too try it myself. What I found was MiO is delicious when drank; but for me this left an almost numb like sensation on my tongue which went away as soon as I ate something. Maybe I had some reaction but I found it minor but noticeable. That aside it is convenient in that you decide how much flavoring you will have in your drink by the amount  that you dispense into your water.  The flavor is as good as any instant drink mix. And is the easiest additive for a flavored drink I have used. I will not get this again but it is worth a try.

Sufficient to say that MIO Sweet Tea has a great taste in a convenient form. There are lots of drink mixes out there that are designed with portability in mind. However, this one has the added bonus of allowing you to truly measure out as much as you want -- light tea or screamin' sweet. The little envelopes of powdered drinks could, in theory, be portioned out in lesser amounts, but those packets are impossible to re-close.I just think that MIO is such a great idea, that I most definitely plan on trying out various other flavors. If they are as good as the Sweet Tea flavor, I am a fan for life!

column9: portable sweet tea  is nice to have on hand
column10: Mio  sweet tea is a concentrated liquid you squeeze into water  to make a drink. It is nice tasting,if not gourmet, disperses quickly in water even without stirring and is very portable. I really enjoy having this on hand when I'm not in the mood for plain  water. I must like  my Mio less concentrated than average or maybe I use smaller glasses but I usually get more than 24 drinks from a bottle. The bottle is a plastic, somewhat tear shaped grey squeeze container with an attached snap on lid. The bottle is about palm sized and can easily fit into a pocket  or purse/bag. I have not had any problems with leakage or breaking.  I like the other Mio flavors better than than the slightly lemony taste of Mio sweet tea though I will get this again I have also used it when i needed a shot of tea flavor in a cooked poultry dish and as an ingredient in cocktails and punches.

column4: ChibiNeko "Sooo many books, so little time!"
column9: Better than what I expected it to be
column10: I'd tried another flavor from Mio and hated it. It had too much of a chemical-y taste to it and just didn't seem to live up to all of the hype that had been going on about it. I decided to give the mix another try via Vine, so I tried this flavor. The flavor is about what I expected as well as a little better.The good about this flavor is that it's drinkable. If you're any type of Southern person then you're going to be disappointed in some regards to this flavor because it doesn't come close to matching real sweet tea, so don't even begin to have any hopes for that. However, apart from that this actually isn't that bad flavor-wise. Yes, you can instantly tell that this is a mix of chemical tastes rather than a tall glass of proper sweet tea, but for a chemical drink it isn't bad. I actually didn't mind finishing off the glass I'd made.The bad is that the mix looks completely unappetizing going into the water and that somehow I still felt thirsty after drinking this up. It looks pretty much like a bunch of chemicals mixing in with water, but most importantly the chemicals seemed to irritate my throat a little and make me feel like I was still thirsty. However, I'm more than willing to accept that maybe it's just my mind playing tricks on me.Overall this isn't bad, but it isn't great either. If it's on sale I might pick this flavor up to throw in a picnic basket and as far as non-real sweet tea goes, it's not bad. It's just that this isn't exactly something I want to run out and buy either.

I love sweet Tea and I am not even a southerner.  There is something special about sweet tea that when it is mixed right, it tastes wonderful.  Unfortunately, this sweet tea concentrate missed the mark.First of all, the package was leaking upon arrival.  Not too much to return the product.  When I opened it, the mixture had an artificial candy-like scent.  Okay, it is suppose to be sweet.  The big problem was the instructions.  "Just a few drops."  Huh?  Not to be overly anal but do you mean short drops or long drops.  Is a few 3, 4, 5, or more?  Without a clear measurement, it is hard to find that "sweet spot".  McDonalds use a syrup concentration such as this one (I assume) and the flavor is always consistent.  That is important to me.  If they want to improve on the product, add something like ¼ teaspoon per 8 oz water or something similar.  Otherwise, if you want to experiment with getting just the right ratio of mix to water, have at it.  I don't have time and if I did, chances are I would never get it perfect again.

column4: Todd I. Stark "Cellular Wetware plus Books"
column10: Tasty concentrate that you can carry anywhere so you can hydrate more enjoyably on the go.  No calories, plenty of taste, ultra convenient.  The only downside is the cost, which is a little higher than powders, the cost of convenience.  The sweet tea is my favorite.  Two or three squirts in a 20 oz. water bottle.

I can't get the hang of this MIO liquid coloring/flavoring stuff. I feel like there is an optimal amount per ounce to add and that I have gone over or under that amount in every attempt. If I could find the sweet spot, perhaps I'd like the product more. I think I prefer to have a standard dose of a flavor additive.I was interested to try it for a long time and excited when it became available through the Vine program because I had not seen it in stores. When it arrived, I was in a new place with a sink that produced nasty tap water. Adding MIO made it nasty tap water with a funky fake tea taste.Fast forward to after I tried it in filtered water--still a funky fake flavoring taste.I might try it again in another flavor--I haven't had tea-flavored water products before. Maybe a flavor that was just fruity as opposed to imitating a favorite beverage of mine (sweet tea) would be more flavorful.In general, I'd prefer plain water to this stuff.

column9: Its ok for a real "Sweet Tea" substitute.
column10: I am a fan of Sweet Tea but I don't love the sugar. So typically I'll settle for Peach flavored Iced Tea powders like Crystal Light or Snapple to add to my water bottles at home. It is easy to transport and the flavor is pretty decent. When Mio was introduced, I was curious. The fact that it was droplets of flavoring creeped me out a bit, I won't lie. When I was offered a chance to try this one, I jumped at the chance.It arrived with a stain on the plastic as if a few drops had leaked on the outer package. Not too big of a deal because it was obviously still sealed. The coloring did throw me off, although it seems to be the thing I noticed most in all of MIO's advertising.Both my husband and I gave it a whirl at dinner. We grabbed two glasses of cold ice water and added a few drops. I think I added 4, watching the coloring dissolve into the water was strange. Then I mixed with a straw and tested it, added a few more, tested again. It was about 16oz of water. Sadly, I was unable to calculate the amount I used because even with the slightest touch, it squirted quite a bit out. After that first few drops, it was just a stream.Once it was to my preferred flavor strength, it was too bad. Often, when I have a pre-made sweet teas, there is quite a bit of lemon or citrus flavor added to keep it fresh. Since I do not enjoy lemon in my tea, I was pleased that this MIO flavor didn't have a hint of lemon. In fact, it tasted a lot like normal sweet tea (without the crunchy sugar bits that fall to the bottom).I will fully admit that I am still a bit ooked out by the adding colored liquid drops into my water for flavor. My husband disagrees, pointing out that it makes more sense, distributes better and doesn't get clumpy powered bits that stick to plastic drink containers.

column9: FLAVOR DOES NOT EQUAL THE CLEVER IDEA
column10: I really do like  being able to customize how strongly favored a drink is, and I like the handiness of the packaging- the concentration keeps the package size small and portable. However,  as a frequent drinker of diet tea beverages I am disappointed in the taste. I don't expect it to taste real- either the tea  or the sweetener-but this beverage just tastes, well, TOO artificial. I tried various amounts in the same amount of water and never got it to taste good. It's not so bad that I won'tfinish the package, but not so good that I'm likely to buy it.

I got this for my husband because he is a huge fan of sweet tea but He drinks it like its water so I thought I would try a sugar free version for him to try. He really loved it. I would recommended this to my friends.

column9: Love the idea, like the flavor.
column10: Easy to use, decent flavor.  Definitely tastes like sweet tea.  Just took a few tries to get my personal preference on how much to put in, but overall pretty happy with it.  Liked it enough that I want to try some other flavors, and you can't beat the convenience.  Keep it on my desk and shoot into my water bottle whenever I want.

column9: It does taste like sweet tea
column10: I'm still a bit on the fence about this product. I can say that yes, it does actually taste like sweet tea. But it seems to me that the recommended serving of one squeeze for each 8 fluid ounces of water is a little weak. I've ended up going with two per glass, but everyone will likely prefer a different amount. Once you get the strength where you want it, the flavor is actually pretty good. Tastes a little better to me than the Crystal Light teas. It has a nice sweetness with minimal aftertaste.Admittedly, it feels a little odd to be squeezing in all of these chemicals to my water. But then again...I also drink diet sodas and eat foods with all sorts of artificial flavoring and coloring. So I'm probably the last person who has a right to argue against the notion of better living through chemistry.In any case, I think the bottom line is that it's hard to satisfy every palate with any one product. The folks at MIO have made a good sweet tea water flavoring that is worth a try, in my opinion.
I love the highly portable nature of MIO and some flavors are good enough, but this one disappoints.  I love sweet tea, and I've had diet versions before, yet this somehow misses out.

I wonder if anyone else now will admit to hating water as much as I do? I loved the MIO tea. It is easy to keep in a purse or pocket, contains no calories, and is a welcome 'companion' in places where water bottles are all that is likely to be on offer. Naturally, it is far more economical than purchasing pre-packaged tea.

I've seen the commericals and wondered about MIO just like the marketing people have hoped when paying for the advertisement.  I picked one up and was pleasantly surprised that this is a wonderful way to simply add flavor to water with no calories.It's not a sticky sweet flavor, but I don't really like heavy sweet tea.  The biggest benefit of this product is that you can add more if its not to taste.Brilliant and I'm interested in trying more flavors.

column4: K. Hernandez "DailyReadz - One Great Book Eve...
column10: I went a little heavy-handed on the first batch but no problems, just add a little more water. This stuff is great!

column9: Sweet Tea Without All of the Sugar
column10: I grew up in a Southern family where my Mother would use 1 cup of sugar per pitcher of iced tea. I have always loved iced tea and have missed it since I had to give up sugar a year ago (let's face it, unsweetened tea with sweetener is NOT the same). So, I was excited to try the Sweet Tea MIO.I love that you can add as little or as much of the MIO as you want to your water. There is no predetermined size and you do not have to shake the water to get it to mix in. You just squirt, swirl, taste and add more if needed.I personally love the taste of MIO Sweet Tea. It is definitely the closest I have came to my Mother's sweet tea without all the sugar. It may be too sweet for some people though. My Husband who's Mother was more health conscience, thinks it is too sweet. The nice thing is that he can just add a tiny bit to a larger glass of water and be able to drink it.I definitely think that MIO is worth the price. It seem like a small bottle at first glance, but it lasts a long time. Southern Sweet Tea drinkers should love it.

column9: Better than plain water, but not great
column10: I tried the Sweet Tea flavor of this product, which is really more "sweet" than "tea." It's not bad, but it took a lot of it to get a real flavor of tea so it won't last very long. In the commercials they show people carrying this in their pockets, but I don't think I'd try to carry this with me. I might keep it in a desk drawer at work, though, to get myself to drink more water. I'll definitely try some of the other flavors because I like the idea of it, and I like that it's all you need - it's sweetened, mixes instantly (which puts it miles ahead of powdered drink mixes that remain gritty when added to cold water) and it has no calories.  It's worth a try if you're not a fan of plain water.

It seems like I am brewing sweet iced tea every other day.  Being from the South I grew up on iced tea and was hopeful that this MIO Sweet Tea would allow me a quick alternative for a glass of tea if I didn't have time to brew some.  However, it fell short for a few reasons.  First, make sure you are aiming down into your glass because a little squeeze makes a strong stream and the first time I used it I ended up spraying it 4 feet away onto my newly redone white kitchen cabinets and it wasn't that easy to clean off.  It didn't stain, it just spread.  So aim carefully.  Secondly, I felt like it didn't taste anything like brewed tea.  I kept adding more hoping to get some tea-like flavor but never acheived it.  Lastly, all I could taste was sweetness to the point I thing I could have gotten the same flavor just adding a sweetener to plain old water.  So overall, I don't see the point of this particular flavor.  I did once try the strawberry-watermelon flavor and found it lite and refreshing, so there are good flavors out there but this Sweet Tea flavor just couldn't reproduce the tea flavor for an avid tea drinker like myself.

We really like the MIO Sweet Tea at my house.  Being a liquid, this is so much better than the crystal products.  I enjoy lots of ice in my beverage and the crystals would never dissolve all the way.  The MIO is already dissolved.  Also, I can make the flavor as strong as I want, whenever I want.  The bottle fits easily in my pocket or lunch tote so I have it with me all the time.Unfortunately, we cant always find it in the local stores.  When I found it on Amazon with "Subscribe and Save", I thought I had it made!  Every month my supply of MIO would arrive.  Yesterday, I received an email that it has been discontinued from that service  :(  I can only check every once in a while to see if it is put back into the auto ship services.

column9: The packaging is ingenious, the concept is great... but this flavor was not a hit in this house
column10: I got the MIO Sweet Tea for my husband, who is a constant tea drinker.  This sounded like something that would be awesome for him to have at work.  He was certainly game to try it out.The report I got back from him was mixed.  He experimented with different concentrations to find one that worked for him, but he still thought it had just a funny aftertaste.  He loved the package, and the ability to have it pretty much anywhere he has access to water and a glass or bottle.  And while he did ask me not to purchase this again, he also asked me what other flavors are available and expressed a strong interest in trying some of those.So, overall, the packaging is ingenious, the concept is great... but this flavor was not a hit in this house.

column9: Not quite Sweet Tea, but good!
column10: I like the MIO idea, that you can flavor water a little or a lot, but basically stay hydrated w/o adding calories or a lot of other stuff to your drink.As far as the success of this particular flavor, I can't say it really delivers the sweet tea experience.  Its just a tad on the bland side, and that's after putting quite a few splashes in.But I might be spoiled in that regard, my wife is from South Carolina and makes the real deal here and there.The idea is great, and its a decent price when compared to the bottles of vitamin water, etc. but this flavor wasn't my favorite.p.s.  I gave some MIO to a friend as a gift, since his wife is on him all the time to drink more water.  He's had kidney stones in the past, but just can't stand drinking plain water.  He likes this stuff, though, so its a good idea for those who need more water but don't exactly like drinking it plain.

I tried this as I have found other flavors of the product to be wonderful.  Boy, was I disappointed!  It was so grossly sweet that I can't even bear the thought of trying to finish it.  I like sweet drinks, such as Mickey D's sweet tea, but at least that kind has the bitterness of the tea to balance the cloying sugar.  Perhaps if they had added a slightly bitter undertone to it, it would have tasted better.

I had been seeing ads for Mio for months. And I had always wanted to give it a try but the price seemed to high. So when I had the opportunity to give it a try I jumped at the chance. I am also a fan of sweet tea so I looked forward to giving this a shot. Well it was not what I was expecting. I know it is a zero calorie product but the artificial sweetner used has a weird aftertaste that I found very off putting. I just could not see myself paying the high price for this product. If you are on a diet I suggest using Crystal Light. It tastes great for low calories.

column9: Strongly sweet and too one dimensional
column10: My first impression is that this product is just another way to sell artificial sweetener. I tried 2 flavors and the overwhelming characteristic is sweetness. Some may like this, but I do not. The main drawback, though, is the flavoring is not very complex. What I mean is that there is a narrow range of flavor receptors working on your tongue when you drink it. Cast in this mixture of sweetness is a single flavor, it seems. It is not complex; you clearly taste just 2 things: sweetness and a specific flavor.If you enjoy drinking something that is refreshing and/or interesting, this isn't it. For example, if you add a freshly squeezed lemon and some sugar to your water, your whole mouth seems to pick up a range of flavors and sensations that leaves a slight, but satisfying aftertaste. The MiO, on the other hand, hits your tongue with a strong blast of sweetness and flavor, disappears, then leaves an aftertaste lingering on the back of your tongue of that vague, yet strangely familiar taste all artificial sweeteners seem to have.There are better ways to flavor water, I'm afraid, than this.

This MiO Sweet Tea vaguely resembles "real" sweet tea, but there is no confusing the two. I'd say that it tastes more like the fake taste of a diet ice tea with some sugar added.I've tried it several times but never managed to finish a whole glass. My daughter had the same experience. They always end up going down the drain after we lose interest. I'd much rather have Crystal Light Iced Tea.UPDATE: For some reason, I didn't throw this out. I kept experimenting, and I've come to like it a lot. I find that two hard squirts works perfectly with a pint of water. It is a nice change to just drinking water and it avoids the calories and caffeine in soda. I'm bumping up my review of MiO Sweet Tea from 3 stars to 4 stars.Still, it doesn't taste much like real sweet tea.

column9: A good flavor in a nice compact package
column10: I really like this product.  A long time user of powder products like Crystal Light I really like the ease of getting this mix dispense and mix up in water.  I also liked that you can add it to the intensity of your liking.  The sweet tea is a rich tea flavor with a sweet, but not too sweet, taste.  I loved that the package is a size that I can toss in a plastic baggie for travel, as it meets the 3 oz or less rule.  As a frequent traveller this was quite a bonus for me. Can't wait to try additional flavors.

column9: A nice no calorie, portable drink option
column10: This product is a nice no calorie, portable drink option. The choice for a non-carbonated beverage is enhanced by this product. It is an asset that it can be taken to any place that has water and be able to make a glass of tea.

column9: Handy, No Mess, No Calorie Flavoring
column10: The bottle states this product is a "Liquid Water Enhancer," which is exactly what it does, flavors water or other liquids with a hint of flavor and artificial sweetener.  I tested two flavors, Mango Peach and Sweet Tea.Pros:*Handy bottle; one squeeze delivers enough flavoring for a cup of tea or cold beverage.*No caffeine.*No calories.*No fat.Cons:*No nutritive value.*Contains 3 dyes:  Yellows 5 and 6, and Red 40.I find this a useful product, especially in the evening when I want something with a bit of flavor but don't want caffeine.  I've added it to hot water and hot tea.  I like the handy delivery system.  I could stand a bit less sweetener and a bit more of the flavoring but I will probably keep a bottle on hand as it's quick and easy.

column9: Not great but not terrible (and easy to use)
column10: I can't say that I'm crazy about this stuff - it's not the best sweet tea flavor I've ever tasted (and I'm a fan of sweet tea) - but it's also not terrible. The container is cool - very easy to store and even easier to use (pop the top and squirt it into your water). It does take a good amount of the liquid to make your drink taste like sweet tea; the first time I tried it I used what I thought was quite a bit and still had a drink that tasted like watered down tea. After getting the balance right (too much vs. too little) I've worked out how to balance the amount of MIO with the amount of water, but I'm not particularly thrilled with the sweet tea flavor. Easy to use but I like water enough that I can't see using this that often.

column9: A little bit too sweet for my taste but tastes exactly like it says
column10: I love the idea of being able to enhance my water with this simple solution. Sure, I can brew my own tea and put some sugar in it, but this seems like the easier solution. You just squirt it into your water and drink it.If you are just using this for one glass of water, only one squirt is all you really need to make it taste like sweet tea. It also dissolves very easily and did not require too much stirring on my part before it was blended in. The color does actually look like tea.Upon tasting it, while I enjoyed it as it does taste like sweet tea, it was just overloaded with sugar. I am actually quite a sugar junkie so this may be a bit too much on your taste bud if you're not into too much sugar. In fact, the sugary taste of it overpowers the tea flavor so I was a bit disappointed with that because I love tea.This is definitely easy to use. Just be sure you are OK with a lot of sugar.

column9: It's ok but not a great substitute for the real thing
column10: We make our sweet tea in our house from tea bags.  I was curious to give this water enhancer a try to see if it would be a good substitute for days when I just didn't feel like making a whole gallon of tea.  While I found it to be ok, it really didn't satisfy me as a good substitute for our tea.  The bottle was also a little difficult to use--sometimes it would put out a drop or two and then other times it would squirt out a bunch.  I'm sure there's a trick to evening the flow but I couldn't do it.As a side note, this is much pricier than buying other drinks (e.g. soft drinks), particularly when you calculate the added cost of bottled water if you use that.  I probably wouldn't buy this again.

column9: Don't be scared by the price, lots of bang for the buck
column10: The MiO packs are about the size of a large egg, and you only get four of them for $25. Normally, this would be an instant turn-off. However, each little bottle is about 25 servings, so you're paying only a quarter per serving, which actually makes this a really good deal, especially if you're like me and fill up your water bottle at drinking fountains (where I go to school we have the nice ones that use sensors to fill bottles).All that value would be pointless, however, if it didn't taste good. The sweet tea flavor tastes good, but since there's no caffeine, calories or sugar you shouldn't expect the diabetes-inducing goodness of Southern sweet tea. Since it's a squeeze bottle, you can tailor the taste to your particular palette. Obviously, if you like your teas lighter (like me), you'll get even more servings and thus even more value.If you find drinking water bland, but don't want to give in to the temptation of soda and other less-healthy alternatives, this is a very good option.

column9: Not as good at the Peach Tea
column10: Having tried the peach tea version of Mio, and being a fan of sweet tea, I was happy to try this flavor out. It's pretty good, definitely reminiscent of sweet tea, but it's not quite the same. I also had to use about twice as much liquid to flavor the same amount of water than when I used the peach tea flavor. Again, my only complaint is the price; you're paying more for the bottle and the wow-factor than the actual flavoring itself.

This is a great treat for those of us who are not disciplined at drinking as much water as we should.  With just a short squirt, you can change plain water to a refreshing, clean, dulcet drink.  A little bit is all you need so even a small bottle goes a long way.

column9: Make the plain old water better
column10: I finally gave this item a try. We drink alot of water in the house but we are not really into flavored water, so this one actually taste really good. With a smaller amount, it makes the water taste like unsweetened ice tea, when more is added, it adds a bit more sweetness. Flavoring so subtle that I didn't feel like I'm drinking soda.I also like the dispenser, it shoots a stream of liquid into the glass perfectly.

column9: A little goes a long way
column10: This product is definitely as advertised. You can use a little or you can use a lot depending on how flavorful you want your water. A word of caution, though: if you use too much, you're water will have a weird after taste. MiO is great for people who love water and people who don't particularly care for water. When added to the water (just a couple of squirts) it tastes just like sweet tea. I actually prefer to drink the MiO over juice now because I am missing the added calories of juice and getting the benefits of water. I would recommend this product especially for children. It's hard to get a child to drink water, but with MiO, they don't even have to know that they are drinking it. One last good thing about MiO is that this little bottle goes a long way. Depending on how much you use, you can get 24 servings from one bottle.

I absolutely hate the lack of taste water provides, so I was eager to try a selection from the MIO family.I liked the ease of using a liquid enhancer rather than a powdery one.  It was easy to add more flavoring to the water, and the liquid texture provided a more even taste than the mix-ins of its powdery competitors; however, MIO Sweet Tea could use some improvements in the taste department.  I had a difficult time mixing in an amount that was just right.  When using the recommended amount, the tea was weak and had very little taste.  After experimenting and adding to meet my satisfaction, I noticed that the tea leaves a nasty aftertaste.  I typically drink diet sodas and other sugar-free drinks, so I was unpleasantly surprised by the blah taste of MIO.MIO Sweet Tea is OK at best.  I may try some of the MIO fruit flavors in the future, but for now, I prefer to stick with the powdered water enhancers.*An added note:The dye in the MIO Sweet Tea stains.  It was all over the outside of the bottle when it arrived.  While trying to clean the bottle before using it, I ended up with dye all over my hands and had to wash them several times to get it off.  I believe the messiness was a result of the package being sent through the mail in a bubble wrap envelope rather than a box.  That said, I did not factor this into my overall rating.  I am simply providing this as a warning to other consumers, so that they do not risk staining clothes, hands, etc.

I was a bit skeptical.  My wife likes Mojito's in the summer and I'm pretty good at making them.  However, they can be a bit heavy on the sugar/sweet side.This mix was pretty good and easy to make (there was no bad aftertaste, either).  Put it in a tall glass with some ice.  If you're a fan of CL lemonade or other instant drinks, this is a decent substitution or if you just want or have the non-alcoholic versions.  I would purchase this product and use it.

column9: Pretty good with FDA-approved artificial sweeteners.
column10: This stuff is very convenient.  A tiny bottle can travel with you almost anywhere(about 3 inches x 3 inches x 1 inch in dimensions and weighing at about 2 ounces.)  All you need is a container and tap water and you got sweet tea anytime you want.  It doesn't even require mixing as the mixture dissolves instantly and dare I say magically as soon as it gets poured in.  The drip spout is drip-free and is similar to some of those new smart drip spouts that you see in the market.  It will only eject when you squeeze the bottle.As far as taste goes:  I found it very acceptable.  It is ZERO calories as it uses artificial sweeteners.  Those of you who have sophisticated taste buds might not like it, but if you don't care as long as it tastes good, then this is the one for you.  It uses sucralose and acesulfame potassium, which at the time of this review are FDA-approved and considered safe as artificial sweeteners.

Add a few drops of Mio's Sweet Tea water enhancer to a glass of water and it transforms ordinary water into something like the flavored waters you can purchase at the grocery store. The Sweet Tea liquid did give the water a tea-like taste, but don't expect it to taste just like sweet tea. It's more like essence of sweet tea. I found that I needed to add a bit more than suggested to give it enough flavor to my liking. As I'm not a diet-beverage fan, I didn't care for the slight diet-taste that the beverage had.Diet drink fans looking for something different should give this a try. It's a nice alternative to carbonated beverages.

This is relatively tasty!  The color was nice, and it's zero calories.  You can definitely tell it's a "diet" beverage, and there is no guide for how to mix it - it only says 1 squirt per 8 ounces.  But it's about the fastest drink you can make, and there's no grit at the bottom like with some powdered drinks.  I would definitely try other flavors!

column9: A convenient alternative to Crystal Light
column10: I've seen the catchy commercials for MIO, so was happy to try it out, and sweet tea seemed like a worthy flavor. The marketing idea of a "water enhancer" is pretty slick.Pros: It's easier to make a drink with something like this vs. those little tubs of powder that Crystal Light offers. While CL has more flavors, MIO is more easily portable and is easier to adjust, in terms of how much you actually add to the drink. It's convenient,Cons: Sure, it's not as healthy as just plain water. (Including vitamins or other healthy options in MIO might be a great way for them to get around this in the future.)All in all, fun to try - if you want to drink more fluids, but don't love drinking 8 glasses of water a day, this would be an easy and tasty alternative.

Got this stuff because the wife was interested in it.  BLUF, don't bother with it.  The directions say to use a few drops per xx ounces and I couldn't even taste it when I did that.  The second time I tried squeezing some into my glass it shot out at about a 45 degree angle all over my counter, narrowly missing my shirt sleeve.  FAIL!  After suiting up into a rubber protective suit and goggles, I managed to direct some of the liquid fun into my cup finally and it was a mediocre letdown.  I don't know what the people have been drinking that gave this stuff good reviews, but I rate it one step above pond water.

I've heard lots of good things about MIO and so I was glad to try it out.  I don't taste a "tea" flavor at all..?  Maybe I didn't put enough in, I guess.  It has a sweetness to it, just not a "sweet tea" flavor.

I am so glad that I decided to try the MIO liquid. This stuff tastes great and very handy for travel. I have been hesitant to try the MIO because it is a little more expensive than other types of water enhancers but this is definetly worth it. I love that I can control how strong I want my "tea" to taste and I get a lot of use out of one bottle. This product is very quick and easy to use especially if you are on the go. It's great how MIO is liquid so I don't have to worry about powder residue in my drink. I always hate the gritty residue that the powder leaves in my drink and in my mouth after the fact. The bottle is small but remember it has enough water enhancer in it to make 24 servings.I am very happy with this product and I will be trying other flavors of MIO as well.**This product does have added dye in the ingredients so please be aware of that if you are allergic to dyes.**

Mio Liquid is a water enhancer.  I've tried many water enhancers and some I like and some I don't.  Mio Liquid I like.  With no powder, it's more consistent when you blend your water.  No more powder residue at the bottom of the bottle or glass.  Also, if you flavor isn't quite to your taste after a few drops, you can drop in more to suit you.  The sweet tea is really good.  It's sweetened just right to my taste and doesn't leave any aftertaste. A really good product!

The entire family enjoys these.  They give good flavor for those times you want something besides water.  I would rather not have artificial sweeteners & additives but sometimes water just doesn't satisfy.  I do like that you can add as little or as much as you want.  I tend to waste the powdered additives or add it to a LOT more water while hubby prefers his drinks sweeter.  It's tasty and has a good tea flavor, slightly artificial tasting but to be expected.  Would definitely buy again.

Overall this is a great idea that is well executed.From a convenience factor, it doesn't get any better than this (ok, another beer reference, can't help it).  To have a little squeeze bottle that can turn a glass of water (or bottle of water) of any size into an instant drink is amazing.  It reminds me of being a kid an adding food color to liquid, except this liquid includes the flavor!The tea flavor is great considering it is sugar free.  It is exactly what I expected and hoped for; a nice sweet tea flavor that does NOT try to get fancy with any extra junk (no ginseng / etc ... this isn't some baloney "energy drink" - it is just good plain old sweet tea).I'm a big fan of the little crystal packets, but this product exceeds those in that you don't have to open up a packet every time, you can adjust the amount of flavoring depending on the size of the drink and your preferences, and it mixes even easier than crystals.The ONLY negative to me is that the advertised quantity of "24 servings" that a bottle makes seems to be more like "10 servings" based on my flavor preference and using 16 oz bottles.  Still not a bad value, but 24 servings would taste like sweet tea that was full of ice that has melted ... not strong enough.But overall this is a great product - highly recommended!  Now if they could only have something that can make instant beer ....

column9: Artificial sweetener aftertaste aside, a good sugar-free sweet tea alternative
column10: "MIO Sweet Tea, 1.62-Ounce (Pack of 4)" is a good sugar-free sweet tea alternative. In fact, IMO its far better tasting than the other MIO flavors I have tried. My biggest gripe with MIO is not the flavors themselves, which are actually pretty good, but the unmistakable artificial sweetener aftertaste that lingers after every swig. Even the sweet tea flavor does not avoid this, but it is somewhat more tolerable than the other flavors I have tried.Gripes aside, it's pretty good for what it is. At $13, the price is certainly good, as you get nearly 100 servings between all four bottles. In all, recommended.

column4: Fernando H. Ramirez "The Common Man's Final Word"
column10: I am a BIG fan of MiO... I buy these and mix them with 16.9 bottles of water INSTEAD of drinking sodas.  The taste is awesome, and I actually look forward to drinking it.  I put two squeezes into a bottle, and I'm ready to go.  The cool thing about MiO is that one small 'bottle' usually lasts me a week.  So I'm saving money by not buying sodas (which are $1.50 each), and saving calories at the same time.  The package is nice and small.... fits comfortably into my small soda bag.  I also take it into restaurants and order water instead of a soda.I usually buy Grape and Berry, but Amazon gave me a chance to try Sweet Tea... and this one is also a winner.  The SWEET TEA flavor is exactly what it's supposed to be:  a Sweet Tea-tasting flavor.  I enjoyed it so much, I'm going to start buying it.  Now... it doesn't taste EXACTLY like Tea, but there's enough of a flavor there to bring you the sensation and feeling of drinking a Sweet Tea without the calories.  And that's the whole idea. If you like it sweeter... just add more MiO!As a previous user of PROPEL... I like MiO much better.  And to use up the horrible tasting PROPEL ZEROs I had left... I just put a squeeze of MiO into it, and make them taste good.  I was really enjoying the two flavors I've tried so far, but I'm going to have to add Sweet Tea flavor now.  Sweet Tea hits it out of the park for me, so I highly recommend it.

column9: One of the better MIOs I've tried
column10: I absolutely love Mio Berry Pomegranate and Fruit Punch, but hate Peach Mango. I was a little iffy on trying the Sweet Tea, but I really liked it. My only problem with it is that I like my iced tea stronger, so I end up using more Mio than I usually do and go through it more quickly. Besides that, I really enjoy the taste and will buy it again.

column4: Jaime Vendera "Producer of Kindle books for 7...
column9: MIO got me off sweet tea!
column10: I actually discovered MIO months ago when it was on display at a store. Reluctantly I tried it, knowing my caffeinated/sugar induced addiction to McDonald's Sweet Tea was slowly swallowing me like a black hole, haha. I've tried other imitation tea liquids and powders over the years but nothing came close. MIO was definitely different. It gives you a solid tea flavor, but without that slight afterbite that drinkers of really strong tea may experience. I began drinking it daily in place of regular tea. Though I did have caffeine withdrawals at first, the change was actually an easy one to make because the MIO flavor was so similar to real sweet tea. And the great thing was that I could change the strength of the flavor to my liking with as few or as many squirts as I liked. Now I am caffeine/sugar free and I've even lost about ten pounds.One final word-I've tried the berry MIO. Did't care for it at all. But, that may just be my own tastes. I'm not trying to negatively affect this review, but I felt it important to note that not every MIO flavor may be as great as the tea.

PACKAGINGWhen I got this in the mail, some sort of seal had broken and it had leaked in the box. So if you're planning on keeping it loose in your pocket or purse, maybe keep it in a plastic baggie to make sure it doesn't leak all over the place. I do like that this one package makes approx 24 glasses - seems much easier than carrying around several packets to get you through a day if you like to add the little flavor thingies to your water. But if the package leaks...not good.TASTEThis stuff doesn't taste BAD, but it doesn't really taste GOOD, either. And definitely not like sweet tea. If I had to force it, it maaaaybe taste like a crappy version of canned Nestea-type tea. I put 2 squirts in a glass of ice water and had to add a third to make it string enough. If you get other, fruity flavors, you could probably use as much as you want (to get a hint of fruit flavor in your water) - but for tea, you really need it to be fairly strong or it just tastes like gross, watery tea. Also, I think fruit flavors would probably still taste OK at room temperature but the tea flavor didn't.

If you want a substitute for the powdered stuff and prefer a liquid then this is for you. It is certainly convenient to just make one glass and add more of it to get the taste you want. I must have a crazy sweet tooth because I had to squirt quite a bit this stuff to get the right amount of sweetness.  It tastes great and similar to McDonalds sweet tea or Arizona Southern Style sweet tea which is my absolute favorite.

column9: Absolutely artificial. But it tastes good.
column10: I have a hard time understanding who this product is for. My best guess is that it's somebody who wants to appear healthy and "drinks water" but doesn't actually like the flavorless quality of water. Like bottled flavored water beverages, this product adds flavor with no calories.But in the process, it adds chemical ingredients to your water. Propylene glycol, sucralose (artificial sweetener) and acesulfame potassium (also noted as a sweetener). I'm not saying any of these, in the quantities ingested using this product, are bad...but it seems odd to me to take water and add something to it that contains chemicals.The benefit is that you get flavoring without any calories. Does this product taste like "sweet tea"? Yes, it does. I've been using it for over a week about once a day, and I would say it tastes like sweet tea. However, I've noticed a mild "alcohol" scent from it (probably the popylene glycol). The scent is very similar to that of any "extract" you probably have in your baking cabinet, like vanilla extract.The flavor is sweet without being incredibly artificial, due to no real sugar being in the product. The color is dead-on "tea" -- it's the right shade of brown, and just like tea, if you want more flavor and squeeze more of this into your water, it will get darker. It's an interesting concept.So what you end up with is a sweet-tea-flavored water...which lacks all of the benefits of actually drinking tea. Tea, after all, is healthy for you. There's no caffeine in this product and no sugar, so it doesn't offer any type of energy boost.It's artificial in every sense of the word.Personally, this isn't something I would use long-term. It has a good flavor and is convenient (small enough to keep in my desk drawer at work), but it doesn't quite fit into my overall nutrition goals. I would rather reach for a bottle of diet iced-tea before using this as a substitute.

So easy to use! You just get a glass of water, or a bottle of water if you're on the go, squirt in your desired amount of MIO and your water is transformed into sweet tea! That easy! You can adjust the amount of flavor you want by adding more MIO to your water for a stronger flavor, I have found that I need one squirt and about ½ of another squirt for my tall Coke glasses that I have at home. If you're like me water can be a very boring drink to drink but you really don't want to drink high fructose corn syrup so for me MIO is a great way to make water more enjoyable.This is the second type of MIO that I have tried, Peach Mango was the first type, and if I adjust the taste to what I enjoy I find it to be just as great as any sweet tea I could have made from scratch at home. For example Lipton sweet tea is one of my favorites, but prices are a little high for me and it takes time to make a batch. Plus who has time to wait for your tea to get super cold without diluting it down with a ton of ice cubes? I don't! MIO comes in handy just when I need, on the go, when I'm in hurry, and when I just want something that is not water. I don't find the taste to overpowering in lemon flavor or too sweet since I can adjust to what I like.The amount of times I can use 1 container (about 25-28 depends on how many squirts you use) makes MIO an affordable substitution to some other brands. I am very thrilled with MIO and would recommend giving it a try. Plus now that I have tried two flavors , that I have both enjoyed, it just makes we want to try more so that  every time I drink water I can have a different type of MIO.

Tap water is a funny thing and it's not a generic taste that we might otherwise expect. Cross into a neighboring city and you can imagine a dead carp sucked hard against the grate on the city's water intake and flavoring every glass of water. Eat in a restaurant down the road and you might imagine the water originating from someone's swimming pool.  In another place, the water well might be too deep and has struck some brimstone ring of Dante's inferno. Water is not a generic taste.Airport water by the bottle is perhaps a higher profit per margin/gram then cocaine. I buy one bottle of airport water just past TSA (if I forget taking and empty from home) and refill the bottle from drinking fountains for the entire round trip. In a blind taste test, I believe I can identify the airport by the taste of the water.Some have taken to adding a slice of lemon in the tap water to `normalize' the taste. This MIO concentrate is far more effective. A drop or two will titrate the water into a common, generic and appealing taste experience.It works. It's an expensive water treatment but not nearly as expensive in the long run as paying the enormous sums for the truly generic taste of refined, distilled Dasani and the like temptation.MIO is a far better value for your travel $ then the airport water vendor looters.

column9: My daughter loves it......and I don't.
column10: I have never tried Mio but my daughter had tried the Pomegranate flavored one which she liked but thought it was quite strong.  We received the Sweet Tea flavor and my daughter tried it in her bottled water.  My daughter absolutely LOVED it!  She thought it was much better than the previous flavor she tried.  It supposed to last 24 servings (a serving size is 1/2 tsp).  I suppose depending on how strong you like your tea how long those 24 servings would last.  It says that you use one squeeze for 8oz of water.  It has -0- calories, it does NOT need refrigeration but says that for best quality use within 1 month of opening.The Mio is sweetened by sucralose and acesulfame potassium (as per label).UPDATE:I tried the Mio...and I've tasted sweet tea but this tastes terrible.  Perhaps I like lemon tea because this doesn't taste like sweet tea I've had.  My daughter still loves it though....

Well, since some other user decided they'd paste their review on to each flavor allow me to give my short but sweet review:MiO is delicious. I like that I can just put in the tiniest of splashes in my drink and just have a hint of flavor... or splash a lot in and get a real flavorful experience. It's a quick and easy thing to use. It's also fun to watch it splash into the water. I've also found it's good to flavor different types of alcohol.In regards to the criticism by other reviewers for it containing propylene glycol - don't be in a panic like them. propylene glycol is harmless unless ingest massive quantities of it. Using a canard like "it's considered harmful to pets so humans shouldn't ingest it!" is just alarmist behavior. Chocolate is harmful to dogs. Better not eat that then!Lastly, in regards to it having so many "food colorings" - well, if you don't like anything that flavors your water to have anything artificial in it, squeeze a lemon into it. Put a dash of sugar. Or just drink the water plain. You know what you're getting into when you buy this stuff.Bottom line: This is my new favorite drink flavoring. I will be buying from them again and again.

I get dehydrated easily and struggle to get water in my system every now and then. I decided to try MIO out, hoping it would get me to drink as much water as i could. Well, it does work for me so far. All i need in my water is just a hint of flavor. Nothing too overpowering. A tiny squirt gets the job done. A little taste goes a long way for me. Would have been better without the added coloring though. Will be getting another MIO in mango peach when this current supply runs out. No nasty aftertaste for me.The only bummer that i encountered with this shipment was the bottles of MIO were leaking despite them being sealed in their individual plastic wrapper. I had to wash them off before stashing them away in my locker. No way will i want to carry them around in my pocket or bag. In the condition that i found them in when i opened the package, i don't want them anywhere close to my bag or clothes since they leaked so easily during shipment.

I am a avid crystal light drinker and i bought Mio the sweet tea version today.  I like the idea of adjusting the taste as i go and sweet tea taste pretty good.  I've always found that crystal light was way too strong so i always had to dilute it with more water.  And with regards to additives it's your choice as a consumer as to whether you are going to consume it or not.  Personally I'll take my chances because I'm an adult and I can make my own decisions.  I personally like this as a alternative to crystal light bottom line.

column9: Well worth the money; better tasting than Crystal Light & similar powders.
column10: I tried MIO because it was on sale locally. I chose the sweet tea flavor because I knew that flavor would be easy to compare to other no-calorie powdered drinks. I am a big fan of the Walmart version of Crystal Light (Walmart's is less expensive and better tasting than CL).The delivery method is a great idea. You can adjust the amount depending on the glass size or your mood, it can go into a water bottle just as easy, it's convenient to carry, great for camping, at the office or whenever you don't want to make a whole pitcher of drink mix or don't like the taste of your tap water.The flavor is FANTASTIC. Better than any sugared or non-sugared powder mix! The cost for such a small bottle seems expensive, but it is super concentrated, excellent flavor, you'll drink more water than ever before, well worth the price when you compare it to bottled water or other drinks.

column9: Oh Mio Myo You. Whatever Shall We Do?
column10: "Liquid water enhancer." I suppose that is a better advertising term than "artificially sweetened, flavored soft drink mix." The latter is more informative, though. Mio uses natural flavorings and Sucralose for sweetening. (Sucralose is sold under the brand name Splenda.) Actually, in minute quantities, Sucralose is not bad as an artificial sweetener. Ever since cyclamates were banned as sweeteners in the U.S. in 1970, I have been searching for a sugar substitute that does not have a long-lingering, unpleasant aftertaste. Sucralose is the best I've found so far.Mio rates the calorie count as zero. Mathematically, based on the rules of rounding, they can get away with that statement. Since there is under one tenth of a calorie per serving, it is close to zero, but not actually zero. You would probably become sick if you consumed enough of the product to reach one calorie.To achieve the maximum rating of 24 servings per container, you would need to use only 1/2 teaspoon of Mio per glass. I have found 1/2 teaspoon to 8 ounces of water is sufficient to appreciate Mio's flavoring, but I find this concentration to be too sweet. Adding 4 - 5 ice cubes seems to curb the sweetness. Using more water dilutes the flavor. You will need to experiment to find the right ratio for your own personal taste; I provide this insight as a starting point.Although these little "bottles" of Mio are convenient to carry around with you, they are rather expensive. I find some of the powdered, instant teas available on the market to be just as good and a lot more affordable.

This is the 2nd Mio product I've tried and I must say that it is a little dissapointing.  There are no guidelines as to what quantity would provide the optimal taste; I suppose that the concept it is "season to taste" product.  If you want your beverage to taste more like a weak flavored water, use less--if you want a more pronounced taste use more.  I found in my trials that a few drops are too little, and a squirt can be too much.  I like my drinks to taste like someting, so I've used more.  The sweetness is a bit overpowering; but using less results in a weak drink that I found unpalatable.  I suppose this product is best for those who want tepid tasting flavored water, in that case a few drops would suffice and a bottle would last quite a while.  I found it to be very artificial tasting and not as good as those drink pouches you put in a bottle of water.  The only really good thing about it is that since it is a liquid, it dissolves readily in your bottled water whether the water is room temperature or cold.  So I'd say this product is not for me; but those wanting someting less sweet than your average diet drink mix might find it appealing.

I was shopping today and I am normally a water drinker and put nothing it in, but with summer and drinking a lot more I wanted something different.I have never been a fan of the powdered drink mixes, such as crystal lite and all them, I hate that taste that it leaves in you're mouth and for some reason I often end up with clumps of powder in my bottle!  I hate that!Mi0 is very good, you can add a bit or a lot, but just a little bit really sweetens up your drink and has a lot of flavor.  It mixes up nicely since its already a liquid.I know some commented on the concern of certain ingredients in Mi0.  Frankly I dont think its a bit issue.  People drink soda by the gallons, this is a lot better then soda.This is like anything and drink it in moderation.  I have several bottles of water a day of water, but I just use 1 with my favorite Mi0 mix.Wonderful drink.Its a bit pricy, I am not to sure why.  Even in stores (in my area) ranges from the mid $3.00.

Very happy with this purchase. Everytime I try to buy it in the store, it's always sold otu, Especially the Sweet Tea flavor. Price is good, not anymore expensive than when I purchase it in the store. Love to use this when I go to restarants, just order a glass of water and add this. Save $ and calories. This is a great product for people who have diabetes or are trying to cut back on calories. Would definitely recommend this.

I have tried several different Mio products, I also live in the south where sweet tea is a staple. I wouldn't say this is like tradional sweet tea but it does have a pleasant taste and is easy to carry with you. the package seems small but it does go along way. A great addition to any water bottle.

I really, really wanted to like this product as I think it's a great idea, but I just didn't like the taste. I love sweet tea and was really looking forward to loving this product, so was very disappointed. I tried it in a bottle of water, then twice in a glass with more, then less water. Tried adding more of the liquid to the water, but could never get it to taste like sweet tea. It tasted like chemicals and was undrinkable. Couldn't add it by the drop, as it was hard to squeeze the bottle, then it squirted out and you couldn't really control the amount. Had someone else try it as well, and they had the same problem. They also didn't like the taste. Sorry that this doesn't work, as it's a great idea.

MiO is an interesting new twist on drink mixes--in fact, it doesn't even call itself a "drink mix" (a phrase that probably evokes images of chalky powder and overly sweetened fruit-flavored drinks); technically, it's a "liquid water enhancer." You use MiO by squeezing the desired amount into your water (according to the directions, "one squeeze for each 8 fl. oz. serving). The dispenser design is practically flawless--MiO won't start dispensing until you forcefully squeeze the bottle, so there's no danger of accidentally pouring too much into your water. There is, however, the danger that you won't be able to accurately measure one "squeeze"--exactly how long does one "squeeze" last? How much MiO should I add for the flavor I want? You've just got to figure this one out by trial and error. It didn't take me too long to judge how much MiO I should add to my 20 oz. bottle of water (2.5 "squeezes"), and the resulting beverage was quite tasty indeed (although it *was* artificially flavored). I find MiO a lot more convenient than those individual powder drink sticks, but it takes a few tries to get the hang of it.

column9: It's even better than I expected
column10: My wife first brought home a... umm... bottle?  Container?  Squirt dropper thingy?.. of MIO a few months ago; a strawberry-watermelon flavor, if memory serves me, and I enjoyed it tremendously.  Always looking for something to drink that's not just water but rarely having a container of something in the fridge -- at least not for very long -- I was personally growing tired of powdery drink mixes and the mess they would make.  The measuring dirtied spoons and measuring cups, and frequently there was powder still at the bottom of the glass when I'd finished, making the last gulp seem as though I'd just swallowed syrup.These MIO packages change all that.  When you gently squeeze the container, a concentrated squirt of drink mix neatly goes into your glass, and after a sip or two, you'll know exactly how many squirts will make the perfect strength drink for you.  I find that I don't even need to stir any more than a brisk oscellation of my glass.  The squirt nozzle is very accurate, and nothing gets dirty.I'm more of a fan of the Lipton lemon iced tea flavor than the "sweet tea" flavor that's now so popular at fast food chains (my wife loves sweet tea like that, and like this MIO flavor), but I find that in the right squirt count, the flavor of this product is extremely similar to those products.And like the commercial on TV, this packaging is very portable, and I've had no issues with drippage from the bottle.  Lastly, and I think this is truee with all flavors, MIO liquids are caffeine-free, carbohydrate and suger-free, and calorie-free based on an 8-ounce glass.I would recommend that you try a MIO, but BEFORE YOU BUY ONE at the store or on Amazon, you might want to do a Google-search or check out the MIO Facebook page because I understand you can order a FREE SAMPLE from them to try it out first.  My apologies for the caps... just wanted to make sure you saw that before you place anything in your shopping cart.  :^)

This is the second MiO product I've used. I haven't considered either with the highest regards but they do make a convenient emergency beverage enhancer. MiO comes in hadny 1.62 ounce packs, easy to carry and simple to use. If you're thirsty but don't feel like drinking plain old boring water then just give MiO a squirt. A quick shot for a little splash of flavor or a long squeeze for a stronger flavor. The problem is that a small dose of MiO Sweet Tea tastes like murky water. And a strong dose tastes like cough syrup. There are much better MiO products than Sweet Tea. If you can get past the taste though MiO is a really great product. Easy and convenient, you can get plenty out of each container. It's better than carrying around a bunch of those Crystal Light singles packets for sure.

column9: A portable sweet tea that tastes pretty good
column10: If you've never lived or visited the South, there is a common drink available in all restaurants here- sweet tea.  It consists of iced tea that is brewed with copious amounts of sugar.  If you're from another region of the country and visit, you'll typically order iced tea and gag when you drink it, because you will not expect the amount of sweetness you taste.  Even sweetened Nestea or other name brand products availble bottled don't have the same amount of sugar.  Once you get used to it however, it's actually a pretty good summertime drink.  And to me, real sugar is better than the chemicals found in most soft drinks, diet or regular.  They just feel much heavier in my stomach.All that out of the way, I was surprised at how close this approximates sweet tea while using artificial sweetener.  It tastes like sweet tea, but manages to find the middle ground between real sweet tea's flavor without the sometimes (to me) strong chemical tastes found in diet drinks.  The color used actually helps determine how much is needed to make it taste like the real thing.  Too light and there is hardly any taste at all.  Overall, a smart little product idea and a good way to vary up your water intake.

column9: You ought to try this - it's good.
column10: I bought a few of these Mio "water enhancers" to try. They are small bottles of artificially sweetened concentrate that you squirt into a water bottle or add to a glass of water. It only takes about a half teaspoon to flavor a glass of water so each bottle will make about 20 - 24 servings. I got a couple of the fruity ones as well as the Sweet Tea flavor. The fruity ones taste too artificial and chemical-y to me but I found the Sweet Tea flavor to be really good. To each his/her own - I like it, my wife doesn't. These are perfect to keep in your desk drawer at the office or to take traveling. Give the Sweet Tea flavor a try, skip the fruity ones. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

I was making my own sweet tea for a while but this is so much easier. It's very sweet, easy to use, doesn't spill, and lasts a long time. Doesn't quite taste like homemade but after a few uses you'll get used to it and I've come to really like the taste. I drink so much more water now than I did before, thanks to MiO!

column9: Not even remotely tasting like sweet tea
column10: Okay, this sounded like a cool idea and it is the first MiO liquid I have ever tasted.  I love sweet tea, so if I could enjoy it calorie free, what's not to love...  Well unfortunately, this product did not live up to my expectations, even remotely.One squirt into an 8 oz glass of cold water, tasted like slightly sweet cold water.Two squirts into an 8 oz glass of cold water, tasted like even sweeter cold water, with a vague tea after taste.Three squirts into an 8 oz glass of cold water, tasted like very sweet cold water, with a nasty aftertaste.I understand the other flavors are quite good, based on the reviews.  This one is not.

column9: YUCK! NOT SWEET! NOT SWEET TEA --  Just light citrus flavor and hint of  tea. Do not expect any real tea flavor.
column10: This is just plain awful. It tastes like you went to a self serve bar in buffet and filled you cup with 1 tea to 3 waters. It has a slight hint of citrus / lemon flavor, and you have to stretch your taste bud imagination to even get a  hint of tea.  Even after putting 10 of the MIO it still had hardly any tea taste. We much prefer the mango MIO Liquid Peach Tea, 1.62-Ounce, (Pack of 4) OR MIO Mango Peach, 1.62 Ounce (Pack of 4)

column9: Busted open, dyed my hands, mostly chemicals
column10: When I received my container of Mio Sweet Tea water enhancer, I opened the envelop and the container had been cracked during shipping. When I pulled it out of the padded envelope, the Mio fluid got on my hands. I couldn't get the dye off my hands after washing them twice! This prompted me to check the ingredients, where I then saw it was full of dyes and chemicals:Water, Malic Acid, PROPYLENE GLYCOL, Citric Acid, Sucrolose & ACESULFAME potassium, potassium citrate, RED 40, POLYSORBATE 60, and POTASSIUM SORBATE (preservative).OK people, you can make a tea concentrate using these crazy ingredients called TEA LEAVES & a sweetener! Why all these freak ingredients?I had to try it so I could write a fair review... it tasted like it's ingredients: mysterious chemicals. This was no enhancer, but really a "water detractor".Stay away from this Franken-Tea unless you crave bizarre chemicals & dyes.

column9: Contains Chinese Meds For Thrombosis Cardiovascular Diseases!
column10: I would not worry about the other ingredients everyone seems concerned about. but you should worry about this:Acesulfame K is 180-200 times sweeter than sucrose (table sugar) and has not been fully studied. It is believed to be carcinogenic. More studies are needed.Since this is so sweet and leaves nasty bitter aftertaste Kraft Foods invented a way to help mask the bitterness by getting a patent on this drug Sodium ferulate which is in this drink. Sodium ferulate (SF), the sodium salt of ferulic acid, is a drug used in traditional Chinese medicine for treatment of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases and to prevent thrombosis.Save yourself the worry and nasty taste. Go out and get a sack of sugar and box of tea bags for the same price and enjoy it that much more. At least real tea is safe and has health benefits and is full of antioxidants.

I gave this product a 1-star for its packaging because if I were ever concerned about being able to have iced tea wherever I went, then Mio Sweet Tea mix would be handy to have.Having said that, I thought the taste was a little flat, and I suppose if I were traveling I would buy tea in a restaurant or store.  If you are going camping, this might be good to have but I don't know if I would choose it over Crystal Light flavor packs.  That's my preference.  You can try yourself to see.

I've been curious about these little bottles for a while now, since water can sometimes get a bit boring and I try to avoid soda. When I saw the opportunity to try them as a Vine member, I was excited!They're definitely convenient little objects, and if you really wanted to, you could fit one in your purse to carry with you. The way it works is you're supposed to squeeze in a drop at a time until you've reached the flavor you want. Firstly, there are no drops. I had to squeeze the thing with a kung fu grip before anything came out, and when it did, it shot out in a little jet stream. I tried a couple of times, but couldn't get it to just drip. That said, it takes far more than a few drops to get any flavor! I ended up putting in a teaspoon or so before the color was finally tea-like and there was some sort of flavor. The flavor was seriously watered down, like a super weak glass of iced tea.Both my cousin and I tried the sweet tea MIO, and we were both rather disgusted by the flavor. Hopefully the other flavors are better!

I love sweet tea.  LOVE it.  It's hard being in Ohio and having an immense love for sweet tea... as it's not common around these parts.  Luckily it's become more popular lately but rarely is the sweet tea served southern style.  When I saw this flavor I was pretty excited to give it a whirl.My first try I thought I put too much in as it was overly syrupy.  The second try I didn't think I had enough.  On and on and on I tried and I've yet to find a happy medium for this product.  It's either bland or ick.So sad :(

I like tea, and thought that maybe this would be something great to jazz up my bottled water at work. As I put the drops in the bottle, I was a little surprised at how vividly colored this stuff is; I'm sure colorless liquid would be less exciting but this tiny bottle of flavoring packs a TON of color!The flavor effect fell flat; I could not add enough to get the flavor I expected, it just got sweeter and sweeter, to the point of being unable to drink it. I would like to suggest to the MIO maker that if they just took out the higher concentration of color and replaced that with a higher percentage of flavoring, that would go a long way in improving this product. It has an aftertaste that is even more pronounced than Crystal Light, and another side effect that is not refreshing. After dumping my bottle, I then had to get another bottle of plain water to wash the weird icky feeling out of my mouth. My mouth felt like I'd imagine Astroglide would act if you drank it; it had this weird slippery aftereffect and my mouth felt like it just wasn't hydrated with the water, as if I needed to keep on drinking. Bleh!Not a purchase or even a recommendation for me.

I thought I would really like this product.  I love sweet tea, but try to avoid calorie laden beverages.  However, it just tastes bad.  Way too artificial, and with a really bad aftertaste.  It didn't really taste like tea at all, just a kinda sweet, but very artificial tasting water.  Even when I doubled the amount suggested on the bottle, it still tasted off and nothing like tea.I might try some of the other MIO flavors, but I won't be buying this one anytime soon.

Do your research on this... the main ingredients are chemicals, ie propylene glycol. I got my 4 bottles from Amazon... opened one bottle, squirted some into a tall glass of ice cold water and could not wait... well... EEKKKKK... so gross. It tasted like pure sugar water with a weird aftertaste, squirted some more and finally got the "hint" of tea taste...  You have to squirt A LOT to even taste a hint of tea and when the main ingredients are chemicals (excluding water of course) it tastes like what it is.. A CHEMICAL. I immediately put the bottle back into the box from Amazon, along with the 3 unopened bottles and tossed them in the garbage. While I hated to spend $12+ of my money for NOTHING.. it's my fault, I should have done reviews FIRST. Here's just one I found: [...]The cute bottle and the 0 calories in the commercials were enough to entice me and I am sure this product will make millions from idiots like me who fell for this, but trust me people, SAVE YOUR MONEY. I don't write much reviews, but I just had to come on here because I am trying to go green and avoid as many chemicals as I can for my own body and home and this is just one big giant chemical hidden in a cute bottle with a great commercial. Look up the ingredients, which are NOT on Amazon and do your own research.  Pour a glass of water, squeeze some lemons and add stevia for some lemonade with no chemicals.... Or brew some tea bags, put in pitcher, refrigerate, add stevia for some sweet tea... it will be better for you and taste better than this crap. Lesson learned... Now choose for yourself, if you buy it... remember I warned you ;)

I don't normally drink diet but I wanted a portable way to carry sweet tea.  The problem with this is the water tastes sweet but I can't taste tea.  I just taste like sweet water.  I think I may try the fruit punch, it may be better but I won't be buying the Sweet Tea again.
I never ever review products on Amazon. This is my first. I love MIO Fruit Punch. This was so foul- I actually threw it away after 1 drink. It doesn't taste like sweet tea at all.

I WAS NOT IMPRESSED WITH THIS WATER ADDITIVE. IT TOOK MORE THAN THE RECOMENDED QUANITY AND EVEN THEN IT WAS NOT A GOOD FLAVOR. LEFT A METALIC TASED.THE IDEA IS GOOD BUT NEEDS QUALITY AND RESEARCH TO IMPROVE.
Taste great and already slightly sweet so you don't even need to add any sweetner. I like it cause its small enough to fit in your purse or not take up much space in your desk at work.

One of our disappointments in traveling last year to Costa Rica--and other countries over the years--was the absence of iced tea. Sorry folks---we've been hooked on iced tea for 50 years! Anyway, we don't drink wine or beer, and water/carbonated beverages got old in the tropics. In Germany, for three years we longed for having iced tea with our schnitzel! This year we tried taking a few small bottles of MIO in Peach Tea and Sweet Tea flavors. Outstanding! Made a LOT of difference, whether at meals or just drinking bottled water. Advantage over powdered flavorings is that you can adjust the strength of the mixture a squirt at a time. (What would you do with a glass of water, but with an envelope of powdered flavoring for a quart of water?) And, for those concerned about passing airport security,  these contain only 1.6oz.  Use 'em at the office for drinks during the day. Very convenient.

After reading the ingredients, I can't drink this tea.  I do love tea, but these ingredients sound a bit too harsh for me.  Also, I read some bad things about this tea when reading the reviews.  I refuse to drink this tea.  I am a bit on the sensitive side, and I get reactions from most things that I cannot pronounce or have never heard of.  I will stick with the natural tea that I've been drinking.  I am a tea-drinker, but not this tea.Also, I couldn't drink this tea anyway, even if I wanted to, because the product was all over the outside of the bottle when I took it out of the mailer.  The packaging of this product must not be very good; it seems to have leaked through.

column9: It's Like Drinking A Sharpie Permanent Marker
column10: Are you familiar with the chemical smell that emanates from the tip of a Sharpie? That's what your water will smell like when you put this in it. No matter how much of this concoction I mixed into my water, it failed to taste like sweet tea. It did have a tea-like taste but I'd put it somewhere between Snapple peach and raspberry teas. If you're a fan of sweet tea just go buy some from the store or make your own; stay far, far away from this stuff.
It was rather disgusting. If I tried a single squirt or 3 big squirts, it tasted horrible. Don't buy Sweet Tea, try their Fruit Punch first.

column9: just enough sweet for me and perfect for work!
column10: I really like these, no calorie water flavorings that are small (fit in the palm of your hand) to use at home or on the go.  I took this one to work and am sweetening my water up at the office.  I like all of the flavors I have tried so far, peach mango, watermelon strawberry and this one, sweet tea.  It has just the right mix of tea taste and sweetness.  I drink diet drinks sometimes so I don't have an aversion to a little aftertaste, but I really can't make one out with any of the flavors I have tried.  I have since purchased another flavor after testing these and would recommend if you think water is "boring" but need to get your ounces in.  I would definitely recommend to others.

They've changed the description since I first purchased Mio.  I'm not sure I would have purchased "sweet tea".  The flavors I ordered were some kind of berry (purple) and strawberry (red).  I had been spending a fortune on the new Vitamin Waters and was thrilled to get virtually the same product that I could use with my own water.  Less expensive, fewer trips to the store and no having to drag cases of bottles home.  The strawberry wasn't the best, but the purple is great!  Delicious.
I would give this one a 5 star, but no one seems to be able to make a natural sweet tea flavor. Other than that it is quite good!

For those looking for a review, and not a debate on additives that are good for us:I have to say I really enjoy MiO.  I posted my review on the Sweet Tea flavor because out of all the ones I've tried, I like it the best.  I'm a big fan of sweet tea, and when I'm out and about and can't make my own, this is a great substitute.  It is easy to change the amount to your taste (I often like a weaker flavor, just enough to help the water go down).In my opinion this product is superior to most of the dry products on the market today - a lot because it is so easy to change the concentration, and how portable it is.  I was a fan of the crystal light singles for a while, but a lot of their flavors were way too strong for me.  This solves it all, and I can get 24+ drinks out of every bottle!

column9: OK, kind of a funny taste
column10: I like this Mio the least of all of the flavors -- to me it has kind of an odd taste.  It's ok, but if you're a real iced tea lover, this probably isn't going to cut it for you!

column9: Great Idea, but Too Much Aftertaste
column10: In theory, Mio is a great idea.  The bottles look cool, and offer a chance to drink water without, you know, having it taste like water.In practice, unfortunately, I prefer water to Mio's sweet tea flavor.  Your taste may vary, particularly if you are a big fan of lemony sweet tea, but this didn't work for me.  It's a challenge to come up with a sugar free drink as sweet as sweet tea that still tastes natural.  This definitely has some caramel-y tea flavor, but the strongest flavor is probably lemon, followed by a chemical "artificial sweetener" aftertaste.IMHO, this is worth a try if you love sweet tea, but I wouldn't invest in a package of four until you were sure you liked it.

This is all right as something to add just a small amount of flavor to water if you really can't stand plain water. It has a fairly strong chemical edge to its flavor, though. It's nice in that the little bottle lends itself well to being able to add however much you want compared to the little packets of powdered flavoring made by other companies that you can't reseal.On the whole, the flavor of the sweet tea version just isn't to the point where I could see myself deliberately seeking this out over other flavoring options.

column9: I have a hard time getting the right flavor for this.
column10: I've used MIO products before.  I was so excited to see a sweet tea option but I cannot get the correct amount squeezed in to make my water taste anything but nasty.I've tried the suggested serving amount and I've used trial and error.  I'm more apt to drink the more watered down experiments as there is a horrible after taste when using too much of the sweet tea.I would purchase this if I could actually get the correct mixture to taste anywhere near sweet tea.

I started with 5 squirts of the tea and that did nothing but color the water a smirky brown.  I added 5 more squirts and it tasted like watered-down day old McDonald's sweet tea.  It was just too lemony without having a true sweet taste.  I wouldn't purchase again and don't recommend either.

I wasn't too thrilled with this at all. The first thing that scared me off was the long list of ingredients in the product. I can't imagine anything good being in such a condensed form.The taste was okay, except I wasn't convinced it was authentic sweet tea. It really did taste too artificial.I won't be trying any other flavors.

I thought the concept of this was awesome.  The packaging seemed prefect for portability; small with a spill-free pop-top.  It is available in nine flavors - Berry Pomegranate, Sweet Tea, Peach Tea, Mango Peach, Orange Tangerine, Fruit Punch, Strawberry Watermelon, Black Cherry and Green Thunder.  Just a squirt or 2 and I would have favor-enhanced water on the go.The reality was slightly different.  Although the packaging is small, the spill-free pop-top LEAKS.  I received the Sweet Tea flavor to sample.  The flavor was very inconsistent - sometimes a squirt would be enough for an 8 oz. glass; other times 2 or more squirts were needed.  It was almost like a science experiment (LOL).  Often I would have to pour it out and start over; once I had added too much the taste would be overwhelmed with an artificial chemical-like sweetener taste. YUCK!!!!!
